<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{theo-covertime}
For some finite random variable $X_\star>0$ and any fixed $z\in \mathbb{R}$,
\begin{align}
\lim_{\varepsilon \to 0} \mathbb{P} \big( \sqrt{\mathcal{C}^\star_{\varepsilon,\mathbb{T}^2}}  \le \overline{\mathsf{m}}_\varepsilon + z  \big)
=  \mathbb{E} \(\exp\{-X_\star \mathrm{e}^{-2 z}\} \) :=  \mathbb{P}(Y_\star \leq z) \,.
\label{ct2.25b}
\end{align}
where
$Y_\star\stackrel{d}{=} (W_\star-\log X_\star)/2$.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
\label{rem:int-effects}
The attentive reader must have realized that our tiling of the inner cities by extended blocks
requires in addition to $\sqrt{\mathsf {M}}=e^{\mathsf {K}_{0}}$ integer, also
that $(1-6 \mathsf{\delta_\star}) e^{-\mathsf {K}_{0}}$ be an integer multiple of $\varepsilon e^{\mathsf {K}_{5}}$. We take 
care of this integer effect by adjusting $\mathsf{\delta_\star}$ to some $\varepsilon$-dependent 
$\mathsf{\delta_\star}(\varepsilon)$ which is within $\frac{1}{6} \varepsilon e^{\mathsf {K}_{0}+\mathsf {K}_{5}}$ of $\mathsf{\delta_\star}$. As this does
not impact any of our arguments, we stay with $\mathsf{\delta_\star}$ for the sake of keeping compact notation.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
\label{rem:unif-ic}
Some of our proofs, starting with Lemma \ref{lem-claim1}, 
are simplified by our standing assumption that the Brownian motion starts at a 
uniformly chosen point on $\mathbb{T}^2$. However, we achieve the exact
same effect for any other initial law (at any value of $\varepsilon$), by 
introducing an additional uniform random shift of our tiling of $\mathbb{T}^2$
by cities, and thereby blocks, which is further 
independent of the Brownian path and the original tiling.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
Starting the Brownian path uniformly on $\mathbb{T}^2$,
\label{lem-claim1} 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:removal}
\lim_{\mathsf{\delta_\star} \to 0} \sup_{\mathsf {K}_{0},\mathsf {K}_{5}}
\varlimsup_{\varepsilon \to 0} \mathbb{P}({\widehat \mathcal{C}}_{\varepsilon,\mathsf{\delta_\star}} \ne \mathcal{C}^\star_{\varepsilon,\mathbb{T}^2} ) = 0 \,.
\end{equation}
Further, in evaluating the asymptotics of $\sqrt{
\smash[b]{{\widehat \mathcal{C}}_{\varepsilon,\mathsf{\delta_\star}}}}-\overline{\mathsf{m}}_\varepsilon$ we may instead
{\sc\lowercase{wlog}} start the Brownian path 
         
with
any initial law on $\partial \mathbb{C}=\cup_u \partial \mathbb{A}_u$.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
We first establish (\ref{eq:removal}). To this end, 
note that ${\widehat \mathcal{C}}_{\varepsilon,\mathsf{\delta_\star}} \le {\widehat \mathcal{C}}_{\varepsilon,0}$ with equality unless the 
last $\varepsilon$-ball within $\mathbb{T}^2$ to intersect the Brownian path, either intersects some city boundary 
zone, or some block boundary zone. Starting our Brownian motion uniformly over $\mathbb{T}^2$ results 
by symmetry, with  a uniform distribution for the center of this (random) $\varepsilon$-ball. Thus, per 
choice of $\mathsf{\delta_\star}$ and $\varepsilon$ the probability in question is precisely the 
             
area of the
$\varepsilon$-blowup of the union of all city and block boundary zones. 
                                          
Upon taking $\varepsilon \to 0$, the latter area goes down to zero as $\mathsf{\delta_\star} \to 0$,  uniformly in
$\mathsf {K}_{0}$ and $\mathsf {K}_{5}$. 

Next, let $\mathcal{C}^{(+)}_{\varepsilon,\mathsf{\delta_\star}}$ denote the modified $\varepsilon$-cover 
time in case covering starts at the random path location at time $T_0$
(instead of time $0$), with 
$\mathcal{C}^{(-)}_{\varepsilon,\mathsf{\delta_\star}}$ standing for the modified $\varepsilon$-cover time 
where if the path starts within some $\mathbb{A}_u \setminus \partial \mathbb{A}_u$
we ignore
                                    
also the whole city $\mathbb{A}_u$. Clearly, we then have that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:pm-bound}
\mathcal{C}^{(-)}_{\varepsilon,\mathsf{\delta_\star}} \le {\widehat \mathcal{C}}_{\varepsilon,\mathsf{\delta_\star}} \le T_0 + \mathcal{C}^{(+)}_{\varepsilon,\mathsf{\delta_\star}} 
\end{equation}
(with equality on the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} whenever $\mathsf{z}_{01} \notin \cup_u \mathbb{A}_u$).
By definition, the path in $[0,T_0]$ does not contribute to the modified $\varepsilon$-covers 
$\mathcal{C}^{(\pm)}_{\varepsilon,\mathsf{\delta_\star}}$ (beyond the law of the initial position), with 
$\mathcal{C}^{(-)}_{\varepsilon,\mathsf{\delta_\star}} \ne \mathcal{C}^{(+)}_{\varepsilon,\mathsf{\delta_\star}}$  
only if the last $\varepsilon$-ball to be considered in $\mathcal{C}^{(+)}_{\varepsilon,\mathsf{\delta_\star}}$ intersects the
city within which the path started at time zero.  {The probability of the latter 
event is at most the probability of such an event for a uniformly chosen
city (independently of the path), } which by symmetry is $\mathsf {M}^{-1} \to 0$
as $\mathsf {K}_{0} \to \infty$. With $\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon \to \infty$ and $T_0$ independent of $\varepsilon$, we
thus deduce from (\ref{eq:pm-bound}) that the asymptotic of 
$\sqrt{\smash[b]{{\widehat \mathcal{C}}_{\varepsilon,\mathsf{\delta_\star}}}}-\overline{\mathsf{m}}_\varepsilon$ matches that of $\sqrt{\smash[b]{\mathcal{C}^{(+)}_{\varepsilon,\mathsf{\delta_\star}}}}-\overline{\mathsf{m}}_\varepsilon$,
as claimed.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
\label{rem:bad-cities} The same reasoning as in the proof of Lemma \ref{lem-claim1} 
extends to 
the $\varepsilon$-cover time of any sets
$\mathbb{M}_\mathsf{\delta_\star} \subset \mathbb{T}^2$ that are chosen independently of the Brownian path,
provided  that the 
area of the closure of $(\mathbb{M}_\mathsf{\delta_\star})^\complement$ decays to zero
with $\mathsf{\delta_\star} \to 0$ (for example, one may in addition remove $\mathsf {M}_\mathsf{\delta_\star}$ 
cities, provided $\mathsf {M}_\mathsf{\delta_\star}/\mathsf {M} \to 0$ when $\mathsf {K}_{0} \to \infty$ 
followed by $\mathsf{\delta_\star} \to 0$).
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:conc}
Fixing $\mathsf{\delta_\star}>0$ and $\mathsf {K}_{0}$,  let $\mathsf{t}_1 := \mathsf{t}_1(\mathsf {K}_{0},\mathsf{\delta_\star}) =  \mathbb{E}_{\mu_\mathsf{e}} [T_1]$.
The sequence $\big\{ \sqrt{S_k} - \sqrt{k\, \mathsf{t}_1}\big\}$ converges as $k \to \infty$
to a normal variable of zero mean,  whose finite variance $\mathsf{v}_\mathsf{e}/(2\mathsf{t}_1) \to 0$
when $\mathsf {K}_{0} \to \infty$.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
By the preceding reasoning, and in particular, the uniform bound on
$\mathbb{E}[e^{c T_j}|\mathsf{z}_{(j-1)2}]$, the ergodic 
        
chain $\{(\mathsf{z}_{(j-1)2},T_j), j \ge 1\}$, is further $V$-uniformly ergodic 
for $V(z,t)=e^{ct}$ and some $c>0$ (see \cite[(16.2)]{Meyn-Tweedie}).
By the {\sc\lowercase{clt}} for such chains (e.g. \cite[Theorem 17.0.1]{Meyn-Tweedie}), 
we have that, regardless of $\mathsf{z}_{02} \in \partial \mathbb{C}$,
the sequence $(S_k - k \mathsf{t}_1)/\sqrt{k}$ converges in law to a normal variable 
of zero mean and the finite variance 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:var-erg}
\mathsf{v}_\mathsf{e} :=
\lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{1}{k} \mathbb{E}_{\mu_{\mathsf{e}}} \Big[ (S_k - k \mathsf{t}_1)^2 \Big] = 
{\sf var}_{\mu_\mathsf{e}} (T_1) + 2 \sum_{j=2}^\infty {\sf cov}_{\mu_\mathsf{e}} (T_j,T_1)\,,
\end{equation}
where ${\sf cov}_{\mu_\mathsf{e}}(\cdot,\cdot)$ denotes the covariance under 
                  
$\mu_\mathsf{e}$.  It thus remains only to show that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq-amirswriteup}
\mathsf{v}_\mathsf{e} = o_{\mathsf {K}_{0}}( \mathbb{E}_{\mu_\mathsf{e}} [T_1] ) \,.
\end{equation}
To see (\ref{eq-amirswriteup}), let $W_t$ denote the Brownian motion on $\mathbb{T}^2$ 
equipped with a coordinate system so $(0,0)$ is a left-lower corner of the 
extended city $\mathbb{A}^\mathsf{e}_{1}$.  Recall from our tiling that $e^{\mathsf {K}_{0}} \in \mathbb{Z}_+$,
hence the process 
$Y_t = W_t \!\!\! \mod \!\! (e^{-\mathsf {K}_{0}})$ is a Brownian motion on 
a torus $
         
\mathbb{A}^\mathsf{e}_1$ of edge-length $e^{-\mathsf {K}_{0}}$. By  
the invariance of $\partial \mathbb{C}$ and $\partial \mathbb{C}^\mathsf{e}$ to $(e^{-\mathsf {K}_{0}} \mathbb{Z})^2$-translations 
on $\mathbb{T}^2$, the sequence $\{T_j$, $j \ge 1\}$ merely records the successive 
times it takes $\{Y_t\}$ to get from $\partial \mathbb{A}_1$ to $\partial \mathbb{A}^\mathsf{e}_1$ 
and back to $\partial \mathbb{A}_1$, while our folding of $\mathbb{T}^2$ 
              
maps $\mu_\mathsf{e}$ to the joint distribution of such $T_1$ (for $Y_t$), and the unique
invariant hitting measure of $\partial \mathbb{A}_1$ 
associated with the preceding excursions. By the scale invariance of Brownian motion, 
it thus follows that $\mathsf{v}_\mathsf{e}$ of (\ref{eq:var-erg}) scales as
$e^{-4\mathsf {K}_{0}}$, whereas $\mathsf{t}_1 = \mathbb{E}_{\mu_\mathsf{e}} [T_1]$ scales as $e^{-2\mathsf {K}_{0}}$, 
thereby establishing (\ref{eq-amirswriteup}).
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop-apriori}
For large $\kappa_\star$ and small $\widetilde{c}$,  $r_0$,  fixing $z \in \mathbb{R}$,  $\mathsf{\delta_\star}>0$ and ${\kappa_o},{\kappa_1},{\kappa'},{\kappa''}$
as in (\ref{dfn:aux-par}),
\begin{align}\label{eq:U-minus}
 \varlimsup_{\mathsf {K}_{6},\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon} & \; \mathbb{P} \Big(
\bigcup_\beta \big\{ \mathcal{U}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\beta,[z]} \setminus \mathcal{U}^{(+,\varepsilon)}_{\beta,[z]}  \big\} 
                 
 \Big) = 0 \,.
\end{align}
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
\label{rem:more-int-effects} 
To define $\mathcal{U}^{(+,\varepsilon)}_{\beta,[z]}$ we set $\varepsilon$-dependent levels 
$\mathsf {K}_{\mathsf{a}}:=(21 \log n_\varepsilon)^{1/{\kappa_o}}$,  $\mathsf {K}_{2}:=\mathsf {K}_{1} + 2 (21 \log n_\varepsilon)^{1/{\kappa_o}}$
and $\mathsf {K}_{3}:=\mathsf {K}_{2}+ 5 \log n_\varepsilon$.  Our proofs are essentially unaffected 
by inserting an integer part in our specifications of $\mathsf {K}_{1}$,  $\mathsf {K}_{\mathsf{a}}-\mathsf {K}_{1}$,  
$\mathsf {K}_{2}-\mathsf {K}_{1}$,  $\mathsf {K}_{3}-\mathsf {K}_{2}$ and $\mathsf {K}_{4}-\mathsf {K}_{5}$ (thereby yielding integer
$\mathsf {K}_{\mathsf{a}}$ and $\mathsf {K}_i$, $1 \le i \le 5$),  and for a lighter notation we proceed without doing so. 
Indeed,  all our arguments rely only on having gaps of suitable order between 
$\mathsf {K}_{0}<\mathsf {K}_{1} < \mathsf {K}_{\mathsf{a}}<\mathsf {K}_{2}<\mathsf {K}_{3}$ and between $\mathsf {K}_{4} >\mathsf {K}_{5} > \mathsf {K}_{6}$, while taking first 
$\mathsf {K}_{0} \to \infty$ before $\mathsf {K}_{5} \to \infty$, and only at the very end considering $\mathsf {K}_{6} \to \infty$.
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{rem:nominal}
Using the notation of (\ref{eq:norm-exc}),  we set for $j \ge 0$ and $y \in \mathbb{R}$, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:nominal}
 \mathsf{s}_j (y)  :=  \frac{1}{2} ( \gamma_0(j)  + y)^2
\end{equation}
(so $\mathsf{s}_1(y)=\bar \mathsf{s}_\varepsilon(y)$ of (\ref{dfn:bar-svep})).
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
\label{def:ex-cnt}
For $z \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{T}^2$,  let $\eta_{\mathsf{v},j}^{[z]} := \sqrt{\smash[b]{2T_{\mathsf{v},j}^{[z]}}}$ for the count 
\begin{align}
T_{\mathsf{v},j}^{[z]} := \#\{ &  \mbox{\rm excursions from } \partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{v},r_j) \;\; \mbox{\rm to } 
\partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{v},r_{j-1}) \;\;  
\nonumber \\
\; & \mbox{\rm during the first } \mathsf{k}_\varepsilon(z) \mbox{\rm inter-city excursions} \}.
\end{align}
Similarly,  for any block $\beta$,  $y \in \mathbb{R}$ 
and $\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F}^\beta$ set $\eta_{\mathsf{v},j}^{\beta,(y)} := \sqrt{\smash[b]{2 T_{\mathsf{v},j}^{\beta,(y)}}}$ for the count
\begin{align}
T_{\mathsf{v},j}^{\beta,(y)} := \#\{ & 
    
\mbox{\rm
                                                 
excursions from } \partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{v},r_j) \;\;
\mbox{\rm  to } \partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{v},r_{j-1})  
\nonumber \\
\; & \mbox{\rm during  the}
 \;\; [\mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}(y)] \; \mbox{\rm first 
$\mathsf {K}_{1}$-level excursions of block $\beta$} \}.
 \label{Tjvdef}
\end{align}
We further consider the corresponding "excess excursion counts"
\begin{align}\label{eq:eta-centered}
\widehat{\eta}_{\mathsf{v},j}^{\,[z]} := \eta_{\mathsf{v},j}^{[z]} - \gamma_0(j) \quad \rm{and} \quad \widehat{\eta}_{\mathsf{v},j}^{\beta,(y)}=\eta_{\mathsf{v},j}^{\beta,(y)}-\gamma_0(j) \,.
\end{align} 
In case $\mathsf{v}=\mathsf{v}_\beta$,  we shall use the shorthand $T_{\beta,j}^{[z]}$, $\eta_{\beta,j}^{[z]}$ and $\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,j}^{\,[z]}$ 
for  $T_{\mathsf{v},j}^{[z]}$,  $\eta_{\mathsf{v},j}^{[z]}$ and $\widehat{\eta}_{\mathsf{v},j}^{\,[z]}$,  likewise using the notations $T_{\beta,j}^{(y)}=T_{\mathsf{v},j}^{\beta,(y)}$,
$\eta_{\beta,j}^{(y)}=\eta_{\mathsf{v},j}^{\beta,(y)}$ and $\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,j}^{\,(y)}=\widehat{\eta}_{\mathsf{v},j}^{\beta,(y)}$ when $\mathsf{v}=\mathsf{v}_\beta$.
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- remark-5: body_md -->
\label{rem:y-to-z}
In view of  (\ref{eq:nominal}) and (\ref{eq:eta-centered})
the path completes within the first $\mathsf{k}_\varepsilon(z)$ inter-city excursions
precisely $\mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}} (\widehat{\eta}^{\,[z]}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}})$ of the $\mathsf {K}_{1}$-level excursions to block $\beta$.
Hence,  for $\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F}^\beta$ each $T_{\mathsf{v},j}^{[z]}$ count equals $T_{\mathsf{v},j}^{\beta,(y)}$ at $y=\widehat{\eta}^{\,[z]}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}$.
<!-- end remark-5 -->
<!-- remark-6: body_md -->
\label{rem:alt-UU}
 Note that for any $z$ and $\beta$,  
\begin{equation}\label{dfn:UU-alt}
\mathcal{U}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\beta,[z]} \subseteq \Big\{ \min_{\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F}^\beta} \{ T_{\mathsf{v},n_\varepsilon+1}^{[z]} \} = 0  \Big\} := \widehat{\mathcal{U}}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\beta,[z]} \,.
\end{equation}
Thus,  $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{U}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\beta,[z]} \cap \mathcal{A}) \le \mathbb{P}(\widehat{\mathcal{U}}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\beta,[z]} \cap \mathcal{A})$ for any event $\mathcal{A}$ of interest.  In 
particular,  we can and shall replace $\mathcal{U}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\beta,[z]}$ by $\widehat{\mathcal{U}}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\beta,[z]}$ throughout our proof of (\ref{eq:U-minus}).
<!-- end remark-6 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:end-game}
Fix $z$,  $\mathsf{\delta_\star}$ and $\mathsf {K}_{6}$.  For some $\overline X$ 
whose law depends on $\mathsf{\delta_\star}$,  $\mathsf {K}_{0}$,  $\mathsf {K}_{5}$,  $\mathsf {K}_{6}$,  but not on $\varepsilon$ or $z$,
\begin{align}
{\mathop{\underline{\overline{\lim }}}_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon}}\,\,
 \mathbb{E} \Big[   \prod_{u=1}^{\mathsf {M}}  (1-  \widetilde{Q}^{(1,\varepsilon)}_{u,z})_+ \Big] 
    
= {\mathop{\underline{\overline{\lim }}}_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon}}\,\,
\mathbb{E} \Big[  \exp\big(-\sum_{u=1}^{\mathsf {M}} \widetilde{Q}^{(1,\varepsilon)}_{u,z}\big)  \Big] 
               
& = {\mathop{\underline{\overline{\lim }}}_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{0}}}\,
\mathbb{E} \Big[ \exp( - \overline X e^{-2 z} ) \Big]  \,.
\label{eq:end-game}
\end{align}
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
\label{dfn:ggi-barsi}
For $i=1,2,3$ let $\mathsf{I}^{\star}_i$ denote
the subset of $y \in \bar{\mathsf I}_{\mathsf {K}_i}$ for which $\mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}_i}(y) \in \mathbb{N}$ and
 \begin{equation}\label{dfn:ggi}
g_i(y):={\bf 1}_{\mathsf{I}^{\star}_i} (y) y e^{-2 y},   \qquad i=1,2,3.
\end{equation}
{We similarly} denote by $\mathsf{I}^{\star}_i$,  $i=4,5$,  those $y \in  \bar{\mathsf I}_{n^{(i)}_\varepsilon}$ for which
\begin{equation}\label{eq:nominalno-vep}
 \bar \mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}_i} (y)  :=  \frac{1}{2} (2\,  \mathsf {K}_i  + y)^2 \in \mathbb{N} \,.
\end{equation}
We denote by $\underline{\mathsf{x}} := \{ (\mathsf{x}_{q1},\mathsf{x}_{q2}), q=1,\ldots,[\mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}} (y)] \}$,
the ordered collection of start and end points of the first $\mathsf {K}_{1}$-level excursions 
of block $\beta$ {and isolate}
the `large scale' constraints part of (\ref{eq:good-cover-y}),  {see \Cref{fig-scales},}
\begin{align}
\label{eq:BW-K12}
\mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}^{(\varepsilon),(y)}_{\beta,[\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]} & :=  \mathcal{W}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\beta}(y) 
\bigcap_{j \in [\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]} \big\{ \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,j}^{\,(y)} \in \bar{\mathsf I}_j  \big\}  \,.
\end{align}
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:angle-diff}
For 
                                                        
some $0<\underline \alpha(\mathsf {K}_{6})<\bar \alpha(\mathsf {K}_{6})<\infty$
and $o_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\varepsilon} (1) \to 0$ (as $\varepsilon \to 0$,  then $\mathsf {K}_{5} \to \infty$),  uniformly in $\beta$, $\underline{\mathsf{x}}$ 
and $y$,  
\begin{equation}\label{eq:good-cover}
e^{2 (n_\varepsilon^{(5)}-\mathsf {K}_{3})} \, \mathbb{P}(\mathcal{U}^{(+,\varepsilon)}_{\beta}(y) | \underline{\mathsf{x}}) = \big( \alpha(\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6})+o_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\varepsilon} (1) \big)
\, \mathbb{E} \big[ g_3(\widehat{\eta}^{\,(y)}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{3}});  \mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}^{(\varepsilon),(y)}_{\beta,[\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]}  \,| L_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{(y)}\big]  \,,
\end{equation}
where $\alpha(\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6}) \in [\underline \alpha(\mathsf {K}_{6}), \bar \alpha(\mathsf {K}_{6})]$ for all $\mathsf {K}_{6}$ large enough.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- remark-7: body_md -->
\label{rmk:no-vep-inJs}
We assume hereafter that $\varepsilon$ is small enough 
so for all $j \in [n_\varepsilon^{(4)},n_\varepsilon]$ replacing $\boldsymbol{\rho}_\varepsilon$ by its limit does not change  
$\{ \mathsf{s}_{j} (y) : y \in \bar{\mathsf I}_{j} \} \cap \mathbb{Z}$,  nor which integers exceed $\frac{1}{2} \gamma_{-1}(j)^2$.
Since $\mathsf {K}_{6} \gg 1$ we also freely re-adjust (\ref{eq:norm-exc}) and (\ref{eq:eta-centered}) to 
have $\gamma_{b}(n_\varepsilon-\ell):=2 \ell + b \ell^{{\kappa_o}}$ whenever $n_\varepsilon - \ell \in \mathsf {J}_\star$ 
(by slightly changing ${\kappa_o}>0$).
Similarly,  
                                                                                                  
we may {\sc\lowercase{wlog}} change to non-strict inequalities in (\ref{eq:barrier-event-z}) and (\ref{def:res-u-z})
(e.g.,  when referring to \cite{BRZ,BRZ2}).
<!-- end remark-7 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:proxy-good-cover}
Let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:g-def}
g_o (y,v) := y e^{-2 y} e^{- 2 v} 
\,,
\qquad \mathsf {b} := \frac{1}{2} (2 \bar{c})^2 {\rm var}_{\bar\mu}(\theta) \,,
\end{equation}
for $\bar{c}$ and $\bar\mu$ of (\ref{dfn:Poiss}).  Then, 
for large $\kappa_\star$ and some $o_{\mathsf {K}_1,\varepsilon} (1) \to 0$ (as $\varepsilon \to 0$ followed by 
$\mathsf {K}_1 \to \infty$),  
\begin{align}\label{eq:K1-to-K3}
[r_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}/r_{\mathsf {K}_{3}}]^2\,  
\, \mathbb{E} \big[ g_3(\widehat{\eta}^{\,(y)}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{3}});  \mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}^{(\varepsilon),(y)}_{\beta,[\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]}  \,| L_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{(y)}\big]  
&=  (1+o_{\mathsf {K}_{1},\varepsilon} (1)) e^{-\mathsf {b}} g_o (y,h^{\measuredangle}_{\varepsilon}(L_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{(y)}))\, ,
\end{align}
                                  
uniformly in $\beta$ and uniformly 
{\sc\lowercase{wrt}} all $(y,L_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{(y)}) \in \mathbb{I}_\star^{(\varepsilon)}$.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:UUpy}
For some non-random 
$o_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon}(1) \to 0$ as $\varepsilon \to 0$ then $\mathsf {K}_{0} \to \infty$ followed by $\mathsf {K}_{5} \to \infty$,
uniformly in $\beta$ and $\underline{\mathsf{x}}$ such that $(y,L_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{(y)}) \in \mathbb{I}_\star^{(\varepsilon)}$
\begin{equation}\label{UUpy-asymp}
\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{U}^{(+,\varepsilon)}_{\beta}(y) | \underline{\mathsf{x}}) =  \big(1+o_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon} (1) \big) 
                                
\big[\varepsilon e^{\mathsf {K}_{5}}/r_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}\big]^2
\alpha(\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6}) e^{-\mathsf {b}} g_o (y,h^{\measuredangle}_{\varepsilon}(L_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{(y)})) \,.
\end{equation}
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
\label{def:Fvjs}
Let $\mathcal{G}^\tau$ denote the $\sigma$-algebra generated by the Brownian motion up to the stopping time $\tau$,  
denoting by  $\mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}, \tau}_j$ the $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal{G}^\tau$
augmented by all the Brownian excursions from $\partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d} (\mathsf{v}, r_{j-1})$ 
to $\partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{v},r_j)$.  In particular,  $\mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}, \tau}_j$ contains the start and end points of all 
excursions from $\partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{v},r_j)$ to  $\partial\mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{v},r_{j-1})$.
We further use $\mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_j$ for $\mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v},\tau}_j$ with $\tau$ the Brownian entrance time of 
$\mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d} (\mathsf{v},r_{j-1})$.
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- remark-8: body_md -->
\label{rmk:z-a-vep}
The value of each $Q^{(+,\varepsilon)}_{u,z}$,  $\widetilde{Q}^{(1,\varepsilon)}_{u,z}$ or $\widetilde{Q}^{(2,\varepsilon)}_{u,z}$ is 
unaffected if one replaces in their definition $\mathcal{F}^{\varepsilon}_{u,z}$ with the  $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal{H}_{\mathsf{k}_\varepsilon(z)}$ 
                                                       
or even with the larger $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal{H}^\star_u$ {(see (\ref{eq:FF-to-HH}))}.  
Similarly,  the joint law of $\{ (\widehat{\eta}^{\,[z]}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}},L_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{[z]}) \}_{\beta \in u}$ 
conditional on $\mathcal{F}^{\varepsilon}_{u,z}$ coincides with their joint law conditional on $\mathcal{H}^\star_u$.
<!-- end remark-8 -->
<!-- remark-9: body_md -->
\label{rmk:free-kappas}
For convenience we have set in (\ref{dfn:windows})
the same parameters ${\kappa_1}$ and ${\kappa'}$ for all
our narrow windows (namely,  throughout $\partial \mathsf {J}$),  but our arguments 
allow for different choices at each such window (provided they all satisfy (\ref{dfn:aux-par})).
For example,  we ease our task of proving Propositions \ref{prop:angle-diff} and \ref{prop:proxy-good-cover} 
by reducing ${\kappa_1}$ and increasing ${\kappa'}$ at $j=\mathsf {K}_{3}$ (thereby making
$\bar{\mathsf I}_{\mathsf {K}_{3}}$ much wider than $\bar{\mathsf I}_{\mathsf {K}_{2}}$),  and apply similar devices also when proving 
Propositions \ref{lem:good-cover-end} and \ref{prop:2nd-moment}.
<!-- end remark-9 -->
<!-- remark-10: body_md -->
\label{rmk:first-mom}
{\Cref{prop-apriori},  \Cref{cor:UUpy} and their proofs
apply} for any parameters satisfying (\ref{dfn:aux-par}) with $\kappa_\star$ large.  Also,  
while we have set $\mathsf {K}_{3} = \mathsf {K}_{2} + 5 \log n_\varepsilon$,   $\mathsf {K}_{2} = \mathsf {K}_{1} + 2 \mathsf {K}_{\mathsf{a}}$ and 
$\mathsf {K}_{\mathsf{a}} = (21 \log n_\varepsilon)^{1/{\kappa_o}}$,  
                                 
our proof of (\ref{UUpy-asymp}) works verbatim as soon as for some $C<\infty$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:flex-Ki}
C (\log n_\varepsilon)^{1/{\kappa_o}} \ge \mathsf {K}_{3} \ge  \mathsf {K}_{2} + 2 \log (5 n_\varepsilon^2),  \quad 
  \mathsf {K}_{2} \ge \frac{1}{C} (\log n_\varepsilon)^{1/{\kappa_o}},  \quad \mathsf {K}_{2} \ge 2 \mathsf {K}_{\mathsf{a}} \,.
\end{equation}
The same applies for (\ref{eq:wtQ1-bd}).
<!-- end remark-10 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:good-cover-end}
{For $\bar b_{\mathsf {K}_{0}}$ of (\ref{def:bar-bKz}) and $\alpha(\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6})$ of \Cref{prop:angle-diff} consider}
the random variables 
\begin{align}
\mathsf {X}^{(\varepsilon)}_{u,z}  &:=  \alpha (\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6}) \bar b_{\mathsf {K}_{0}} 
\,  \operatorname*{\mathrlap{\hspace{.2ex}\rotatebox[origin=c]{20}{\bf---}}{\sum}}_{\beta \in u} \mathbb{E} \Big[ g_\star \big( \widehat{\eta}^{\,[z]}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}} -z,V^{[z]}_{\beta} \big)  
\,\big|\,  \mathcal{H}_{\mathsf{k}_\varepsilon(z)}\Big]\,,
\label{def:X-eps}
\end{align}
where {
 \begin{align}\label{eq:g-def-alt}
g_\star (y,v) &:=  g_o (y,v) \big( 1- \inf\{  |y-y'|+|v-v'| : (y',v') \in \bar{\mathsf I}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}} \times \mathsf{I}_{\measuredangle} \} \big)_+ \,.
\end{align}
                                                           
Then,  there exist random variables $0 \le \bar Q^{(1,\varepsilon)}_{u,z} \le \mathsf {X}^{(\varepsilon)}_{u,z} e^{-2 z}$ such that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:wX-small}
\varlimsup_{\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon} \mathbb{P} \Big[ \sum_{u=1}^{\mathsf {M}}  \big(\mathsf {X}^{(\varepsilon)}_{u,z} e^{-2 z} 
- \bar Q^{(1,\varepsilon)}_{u,z} \big)  > \delta \Big] = 0 \qquad \forall \delta >0,
\end{equation}
and} for $\widetilde{Q}_{u,z}^{(1,\varepsilon)}$ of (\ref{dfn:wt-Q}),  we have that uniformly in $u$,
\begin{align}\label{eq:eqv-wt-Q}
                              
                                   
                           
                            
\widetilde{Q}_{u,z}^{(1,\varepsilon)} = \big(1+o_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon}(1)\big) \bar Q^{(1,\varepsilon)}_{u,z} 
\,.
\end{align}
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- remark-11: body_md -->
\label{rmk:Xu-cnv-zero}
Clearly,  $\| g_\star \|_\infty \le e^{-c\,  \mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa_1}}}$ for some universal $c>0$ {(as 
                                                                                  
$y \ge \mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa_1}}-1$ and $v \ge -\kappa_\star \log \mathsf {K}_{1}-1$} throughout the support of $g_\star(\cdot)$).
Hence,  our choice of 
$\mathsf {K}_{1}-\mathsf {K}_{0} = 5 \log \mathsf {K}_{0}$ implies that for any $z$ fixed,  
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Xu-small}
\lim_{\mathsf {K}_{0} \to \infty} \sup_{\varepsilon, u} \{ \bar Q^{(1,\varepsilon)}_{u,z}
 \} = 0  \,.
\end{equation}
<!-- end remark-11 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{prop:Gauss-field-continuity}
Fix 
         
$\mathsf{\delta_\star}$, $z$  and $\mathsf {K}_{0}$ large.  As $\varepsilon \to 0$
the random vectors $\{ \mathsf {X}^{(\varepsilon)}_{u,z},  u \in [1,\mathsf {M}] \}$
of (\ref{def:X-eps}) converge in law to some $\{ \mathsf {X}_{u},  u \in [1,\mathsf {M}] \}$ which is
                                                                                                           
independent of $z$.
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Fixing $z$,  $\mathsf{\delta_\star}$ and $\mathsf {K}_{6}$,  consider the variable  
\begin{equation}\label{dfn:Xstar-K}
\overline X :=  \sum_{u=1}^{\mathsf {M}}  \mathsf {X}_u 
\end{equation}
whose law depends only on $\mathsf{\delta_\star}$, 
         
$\mathsf {K}_{0}$, $\mathsf {K}_{5}$ and $\mathsf {K}_{6}$.
                            
By \Cref{prop:Gauss-field-continuity},  we have that {as $\varepsilon \to 0$, 
                               
\begin{align*}
\sum_{u=1}^{\mathsf {M}} X^{(\varepsilon)}_{u,z} e^{-2 z} 
 \overset{\rm dist}{\Longrightarrow}  \overline X e^{-2 z} \,.
\end{align*}
By (\ref{eq:wX-small}),  taking $\varepsilon \to 0$ then $\mathsf {K}_{0} \to \infty$,  yields the same weak limit points
for $\sum_{u} \bar Q^{(1,\varepsilon)}_{u,z}$.  In particular, } 
\begin{align}
 {\mathop{\underline{\overline{\lim }}}_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon}}\,\,
\mathbb{E} \Big[  \exp\big(-\sum_{u=1}^{\mathsf {M}} \bar Q^{(1,\varepsilon)}_{u,z}\big)  \Big] 
& = {\mathop{\underline{\overline{\lim }}}_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{0}}}\,
\mathbb{E} \Big[ \exp( - \overline X e^{-2 z} ) \Big]  \,.
\label{eq:end-game1}
\end{align}
With $\bar Q^{(1,\varepsilon)}_{u,z} \ge 0$,  by the uniform in $u$ and $\varepsilon$ convergence of  (\ref{eq:Xu-small}),   
\begin{equation}\label{eq:end-game2}
{\mathop{\underline{\overline{\lim }}}_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon}}\,\,
 \mathbb{E} \Big[   \prod_{u=1}^{\mathsf {M}}  (1-  \bar Q^{(1,\varepsilon)}_{u,z})_+ \Big] 
= {\mathop{\underline{\overline{\lim }}}_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon}}\,\,
\mathbb{E} \Big[  \exp\big(-\sum_{u=1}^{\mathsf {M}} \bar Q^{(1,\varepsilon)}_{u,z}\big)  \Big] \,.
\end{equation}
Thanks to the
uniform in $u$ multiplicative bound of (\ref{eq:eqv-wt-Q}) both sides of (\ref{eq:end-game2}) 
are unchanged when replacing 
$\bar Q^{(1,\varepsilon)}_{u,z}$ by  $\widetilde{Q}_{u,z}^{(1,\varepsilon)}$,
thereby concluding our proof of (\ref{eq:end-game}).
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:2nd-moment}
Fix $\mathsf{\delta_\star}$,  $\mathsf {K}_{6}$ and parameters as in (\ref{dfn:aux-par}). 
There exists $\xi=\xi(\mathsf {K}_{0},\mathsf {K}_{5}) \ge 0$ such that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:C-star-good}   
\varlimsup_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{0}} \xi(\mathsf {K}_{0},\mathsf {K}_{5}) = 0 
\end{equation}
and for any fixed $z$,
\begin{equation}
\varlimsup_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon} \mathbb{P} \Big( \sum_{u=1}^{\mathsf {M}} \widetilde Q^{(2,\varepsilon)}_{u,z} 
\ge \xi + \xi \sum_{u=1}^{\mathsf {M}} \widetilde Q^{(1,\varepsilon)}_{u,z}   \Big) = 0 \,.
\label{eq:sec-mom-bd}
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
\label{prop:tight}
The collection $\Big\{\sqrt{\mathcal{C}^\star_{\varepsilon,\mathbb{T}^2}} -\overline{\mathsf{m}}_\varepsilon, \; \varepsilon>0\Big\}$ is 
           
tight.
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
In view of \Cref{prop:tight},  the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} of (\ref{ct2.25b-new}) coincides with the {\sc\lowercase{cdf}} 
of a finite-valued random variable $Y_\star$.  {By Helly's selection theorem} 
                       
the laws of $\overline X_\star$ converge vaguely along some sub-sequence 
(of $\mathsf {K}_{0}$, $\mathsf {K}_{5}$, $\mathsf {K}_{6}$,
         
$\mathsf{\delta_\star}$), 
                        
{hence} such convergence must also hold weakly {and} 
to some $(0,\infty)$-valued limit in law $X_\star$.
                                                    
In particular, the Laplace transforms of $\overline X_\star$ 
converge pointwise along such sub-sequence to the Laplace transform of $X_\star$. In view
of (\ref{ct2.25b-new}) the latter does not depend on the chosen sub-sequence, thereby 
establishing (\ref{ct2.25b}).
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem-bend1} For $0 \le s < t \le n$ and ${\kappa_o} \in (0,\frac{2}{3}]$,  
\begin{equation}
s^{ {\kappa_o}}_{n}+\(t_n^{{\kappa_o}}-s^{ {\kappa_o}}_{n}\)\frac{l-s}{t-s}+\(l-s\)_{t-s}^{{\kappa_o}} 
\ge l_{n}^{{\kappa_o}},\qquad 
\forall l \in [s, t].\label{bent.1}
\end{equation}
Further,  if $t \le n/2$ or $s \ge n/2$,  then the inequality (\ref{bent.1}) holds for all ${\kappa_o} \in (0,1]$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:bend1}
Recall the curved lines $\gamma_{b}(\cdot)$ of (\ref{eq:norm-exc}).
                                                   
For any $J=[s,t]\subset [0,n_\varepsilon]$,  introduce the curves
\begin{equation}\label{dfn:gamma-J}
\gamma_{b}^{J} (l {+1}) := \gamma_{b} (s {+1}) +
(s-l) \boldsymbol{\rho}_\varepsilon^{J,b} + b (l-s)_{t-s}^{\kappa_o} \,, \quad 
\boldsymbol{\rho}_\varepsilon^{J,b} := \boldsymbol{\rho}_\varepsilon + b \frac{s_{n_\varepsilon}^{\kappa_o}-t_{n_\varepsilon}^{\kappa_o}}{t-s} \,.
\end{equation}
                                    
                                                               
                          
Then,  
\begin{equation}\label{gamma-J-dom}
\mbox{\rm sign}(b)\gamma_{b}^J(\cdot) \ge \mbox{\rm sign}(b) \gamma_{b}(\cdot) \quad \mbox{\rm on $J$}.
                                            
\end{equation}
Further,  (\ref{gamma-J-dom}) remains true if $\boldsymbol{\rho}_\varepsilon$ in  both  definitions of $\gamma_b$ and $\gamma_b^J$ is replaced by 
an arbitrary slope $\boldsymbol{\rho}$.
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Let $a:=s/n$, $b:=(t-s)/n>0$ and $c:=(n- t)/n < 1-a$.  Dividing 
(\ref{bent.1})  by $n^{\kappa_o}$ and expressing it via $a, b, c$ and 
$x:=(l-s)/(t-s) \in [0,1]$,  we see that  (\ref{bent.1}) is a consequence of 
\begin{equation}
f (x) :=  (c)_1^{\kappa_o} x + (a)_1^{\kappa_o} (1-x) + b^{\kappa_o}  (x)_1^{\kappa_o} - (a+b x)_1^{\kappa_o} \ge 0 \,, \quad \forall x \in [0,1]\,.
\label{bent.1-sc}
\end{equation}
We proceed to prove (\ref{bent.1-sc}),  first for $0 \le c \le a < x_\star := \frac{1}{2}$.  In that case,  setting  
$x_o \in [0,x_\star]$ such that $b x_o = x_\star - a$,  
it is not hard to see that for ${\kappa_o} \in (0,1]$,  the continuous function $f(\cdot)$ is concave in each 
of the intervals $I_1=(0,x_o)$,  $I_2=(x_o,x_\star)$ and $I_3=(x_\star,1)$ (where we rely on $b \le 1-a$ 
and on having also $2 b x \le b
         
$ throughout $I_2$).
               
                                                                                                      
                                                                                                       
                                                                                                      
             
Thus,  $\min_{I_j} f(x)$ must be at one of the ends of $I_j$,  for $j=1,2,3$.  Noting that 
$f (0)=f (1)=0$,  it remains only to check that 
\begin{align*}
f(x_o) =   a^{\kappa_o} + ( b  x_o)^{\kappa_o} - (a+b x_o)^{\kappa_o} - (a^{\kappa_o} - c^{\kappa_o}) x_o &\ge 0 \,,  \\
f(x_\star)= c^{\kappa_o} + (b x_\star)^{\kappa_o} - (1-a-b x_\star)^{\kappa_o}  + (a^{\kappa_o}-c^{\kappa_o}) x_\star &\ge 0 \,.
\end{align*}
Having ${\kappa_o} \le 1$,  $a \ge c$ and $1-a-b x_\star = c + b x_\star$,  implies that $f(x_\star) \ge 0$,  leaving only the task 
of verifying that $f(x_o) \ge 0$,  or equivalently,  to show that for each $a \in [0, x_\star]$,  the concave function 
\[
g_a(c) :=  (1-a-c) [ a^{\kappa_o} + (x_\star - a)^{\kappa_o} - x_\star^{\kappa_o}] - (a^{\kappa_o} - c^{\kappa_o}) (x_\star-a) \,,
\]
is non-negative on $[0,a]$.  
With $g_a (a) = (1-2a) [ a^{\kappa_o} + (x_\star - a)^{\kappa_o} - x_\star^{\kappa_o}] \ge 0$,  it thus 
suffices to check that $g_a (0) \ge 0$.  Setting $v:=(1-2a)^{1/3}$ and recalling that $2x_\star =1$,  this is equivalent to 
showing that
\begin{equation}\label{bent.2}
h_{\kappa_o}(v) := (1-v^3)^{{\kappa_o}} - (1+v^3) (1-v^{3{\kappa_o}}) \ge 0 \,,  \qquad \forall v \in [0,1]\,.
\end{equation}
As ${\kappa_o} \mapsto h_{\kappa_o}(v)$ decreases monotonically (for $v \in [0,1]$),  it suffices to establish (\ref{bent.2})
at ${\kappa_o}=\frac{2}{3}$.  To this end,  it is not hard to verify that the polynomial 
$p(v):=[(1-v^3)^2-(1+v^3)^3(1-v^2)^3]/v^2(1-v)^2$
                                              
is non-negative on $[0,1]$.  Thus,  $(1-v^3)^{\frac{2}{3}} \ge (1+v^3)(1-v^2)$ for any $v \in [0,1]$.
This is equivalent to (\ref{bent.2}) at ${\kappa_o}=\frac{2}{3}$,  thereby 
completing the proof of (\ref{bent.1}) in case $n \le s+t$,  $s < n/2$.

Note that $a+bx+c+b(1-x)=1$,  hence the value of $f(\cdot)$ is unaffected by 
exchanging both $a \leftrightarrow c$ and $x \leftrightarrow (1-x)$.  The preceding proof
thus also establishes (\ref{bent.1-sc}) for  $0 \le a \le c < x_\star$ and ${\kappa_o} \in (0,\frac{2}{3}]$,
thereby extending the scope of (\ref{bent.1}) to all $t>n/2>s$.

We next move to $x_\star \le c < 1-a$,  in which case 
$a+bx \le \frac{1}{2}$ for any $x \in [0,1]$.  Yet again $f(0)=f(1)=0$ and $f(\cdot)$ is now concave
in $I_1=(0,x_\star)$ and in $I_2=(x_\star,1)$.  With $2x_\star=1$,  it thus suffices in this case to check that  
\begin{equation}\label{bent.2-sc}
f(x_\star) = [(1-c)^{\kappa_o}- a^{\kappa_o}] x_\star + [(2a)^{\kappa_o} + b^{\kappa_o} - (b+2a)^{\kappa_o}] x_\star^{\kappa_o} \ge 0 \,.
\end{equation}
To establish (\ref{bent.2-sc}) and thereby also (\ref{bent.1}),  note that for any 
${\kappa_o} \in [0,1]$,  the left bracket in (\ref{bent.2-sc}) is non-negative since $1-c > a$,  
with its right bracket non-negative by the concavity of $x \mapsto x^{\kappa_o}$.  We are done,  as 
exchanging $a \leftrightarrow c$ and $x \leftrightarrow (1-x)$ extends  the latter reasoning 
to apply also for $x_\star \le a < 1-c$.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:easy-off}
Fix non-negative $\rho$,  $d_\star$,  $r$,  $R$,  $\ell' < \infty$ and $\mathsf{z}, \mathsf{u},\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{R}^2$ such that 
\begin{align}\label{eq:par-rt}
\frac{r}{R} & \le d_\star (1-\rho) \le 1- \rho \,,  \quad  \rho \le e^{-1} \\
|\mathsf{u}-\mathsf{v}| &\le \rho R \quad {\rm and} \quad |\,   |\mathsf{z}-\mathsf{v}| - d_\star R | \le \rho d_\star R \,.
\label{eq:par-uy}
\end{align}
Denoting by
$\widetilde{A}_k \in \mathcal{N}_{\mathsf{v},r,\ell'}$ the event of having $k$ excursions from $\partial \mathbb{B}(\mathsf{v}, r)$ 
to $\partial \mathbb{B}(\mathsf{v}, r/e)$,  for some $c<\infty$,  any $k \ge 0$ and such parameters,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:off1-center-bd}
 (1+c \rho)^{-(k+1)} \, \mathbb{P}_R^{d_\star} (A) \le 
\mathbb{P}_R^{\mathsf{z},\mathsf{u}}(A) \le (1+c \rho)^{(k+1)} \, \mathbb{P}_{R}^{d_\star}(A) \qquad \forall A \in \mathcal{N}_{\mathsf{v}, r,\ell'},   A \subseteq \widetilde{A}_k \,.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- remark-12: body_md -->
\label{rmk:off-center} If $\rho=0$ then $\mathsf{u}=\mathsf{v}$ where by radial symmetry
$\mathsf{z} \mapsto \mathbb{P}_R^{\mathsf{z},\mathsf{v}}(A)$ depends 
only on $|\mathsf{z}-\mathsf{v}|=d_\star R$ when $A \in \mathcal{N}_{\mathsf{v},r,\ell'}$.  It is further
also invariant under translation $(\mathsf{z},\mathsf{v}) \to  (\mathsf{z}-\mathsf{v},{\bf 0})$ 
sending $\mathcal{N}_{\mathsf{v},r,\ell'} \mapsto \mathcal{N}_{{\bf 0},r,\ell'}$,  motivating 
our short-hand notation $\mathbb{P}^{d_\star}_{R}$.  By the same reasoning,  it suffices to prove
\Cref{lem:easy-off} for $\mathsf{v}={\bf 0}$ (translating also $\mathsf{u} \to \mathsf{u}-\mathsf{v}$).  Having done so,  since for 
any $a>0$ the law $\mathbb{P}_a^{a \mathsf{z},a \mathsf{u}}$ on $\mathcal{N}_{{\bf 0},a r,\ell'}$ matches 
                     
that of 
$\mathbb{P}_1^{\mathsf{z},\mathsf{u}}$ on $\mathcal{N}_{{\bf 0},r,\ell'}$,  we can also fix $R=1$ when proving \Cref{lem:easy-off}.
<!-- end remark-12 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label{cor:easy-off}
Fix parameters as in (\ref{eq:par-rt}) for $R \le e^{-2}$ and $\mathsf{z},\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{T}^2$ such that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:z1-v-cond}
\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}) \le \rho R
 \quad {\rm and}  \quad 
 |\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{z},\mathsf{v}) - d_\star R| \le \rho \,d_\star  R \,.
\end{equation}
Then,  (\ref{eq:off1-center-bd}) holds for the Brownian motion on $\mathbb{T}^2$.
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
Recalling \Cref{rmk:off-center},  we set $\mathsf{v}={\bf 0}$,  $R=1$ and 
fix $\rho$,  $r$ and $d_\star$ satisfying (\ref{eq:par-rt}).  Considering  
a Brownian path from $\mathsf{z}=t \mathsf{y}$ with $|\mathsf{y}|=d_\star$,  stopped upon first exiting $\mathbb{B}(\mathsf{u},e)$, 
we are to show that for some $c$ finite,  any $\rho \le e^{-1}$ and $k \ge 0$,  
\begin{equation}\label{eq:off-center1}
(1  + c \rho)^{-(k+1)} \mathbb{P}_1^{\mathsf{y},{\bf 0}} (A) \le \mathbb{P}_1^{\,  t \,  \mathsf{y},\mathsf{u}} (A) \le 
(1+ c \rho)^{k+1} \mathbb{P}_1^{\mathsf{y},{\bf 0}}(A)  \qquad \forall A \in \mathcal{N}_{{\bf 0},r},  A \subseteq \widetilde{A}_k,
 |\mathsf{u}| \le \rho,  |\mathsf{y}| = d_\star \,,
\end{equation}
which in view of (\ref{eq:par-rt})-(\ref{eq:par-uy}) should hold for any choice of
\begin{equation}\label{eq:par-rho}
|t-1| \le \rho,  \quad  
r \le d_\star (1-\rho) \le 1-\rho \,.
\end{equation}
Setting $B_1 := \mathbb{B}({\bf 0},  r/e) \subset \mathbb{B}({\bf 0},r):= B_0$ and $B^{\pm}:=\mathbb{B}({\bf 0},e \pm \rho)$ 
we have that for any such $\mathsf{u}$,  $\mathsf{y}$,  $\rho$,  $t$,  $d_\star$,  $r$,  
\[
 B_1 \subset B_0 \subset B^- 
 \subset \mathbb{B}(\mathsf{u},e)  \subset B^+ 
\quad {\rm and} \quad  
t \,  \mathsf{y} \in B^- \setminus B_0 \,.
\]
Further,  any $A \in \mathcal{N}_{{\bf 0},r}$,  $A \subset \widetilde{A}_k$ specifies having 
exactly $k$ excursions from $\partial B_0$ to $\partial B_1$,  hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cont-off}
\mathbb{P}_{-,k}^{ t \,  d_\star}(A) \le \mathbb{P}_1^{\,  t \,  \mathsf{y},\mathsf{u}} (A) \le  \mathbb{P}_{+,k}^{t \,  d_\star}(A) \,,
\end{equation}
where $\mathbb{P}_{\pm, k}^{d}(A)$ stand for the probability that starting at $\partial \mathbb{B}({\bf 0},d)$,
the excursion counts specified by 
$A \in \mathcal{N}_{{\bf 0},r}$ occur during $k$ excursions from $\partial B_0$ to $\partial B_1$ 
that do not exit $B^{\pm}$ and upon returning to $\partial B_0$ at the end of the $k$-th such 
excursion,  the path exits $B^{\mp}$ before re-entering $B_1$.  In particular,  
(\ref{eq:cont-off}) holds for $\mathbb{P}_1^{\mathsf{y},{\bf 0}}(A)$ and 
we get (\ref{eq:off-center1}) upon showing that for $c$ finite and all relevant $r$,  $d_\star$,  $\rho$,  $k$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cnt-sym}
\sup_{|t-1| \le \rho} \{  \mathbb{P}_{+,k}^{ t \,  d_\star}(A) \} \le (1+c \rho)^{k+1} \inf_{|t-1| \le \rho} \{ \mathbb{P}_{-,k}^{t \,  d_\star}(A) \} 
\qquad \forall A \in \mathcal{N}_{{\bf 0},r},  A \subseteq \widetilde{A}_k \,.
\end{equation}
                                                                                      
With $\mathbb{P}_{\pm,k}^{d}(A)$ concerning only the joint law of excursion counts between concentric circles,  we have 
by the Markov property of such counts that $\mathbb{P}_{+,k}^{t \, d_\star}(A|\widetilde{A}_k)=\mathbb{P}_{-,k}^{t \, d_\star}(A|\widetilde{A}_k)$
is further independent of $t \in [1-\rho,1+\rho]$.  It thus suffices to establish (\ref{eq:cnt-sym}) only for 
$A=\widetilde{A}_k$.  To this end,  recall that a Brownian path starting at $\partial \mathbb{B}({\bf 0},d)$ 
with  $\frac{r}{e} \le d \le e-\rho$,  enters $B_1$ before exiting $B^\pm$,  with probability
\begin{equation}\label{eq:nom-q}
q_\pm(d)=\frac{\log(e \pm \rho)-\log (d)}{\log (e \pm \rho )-\log (r /e)}
\end{equation}
(see e.g. \cite[(2.1)]{BRZ2}),  hence by definition 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:off-bd}
\mathbb{P}_{\pm,0}^{d}(\widetilde{A}_0) = 1-q_\mp(d), \qquad
\mathbb{P}_{\pm,k}^{d}(\widetilde{A}_{k}) = q_\pm(d) q_\pm(r)^{k-1} (1-q_\mp(r)), \quad k \ge 1 \,.
\end{equation}
By (\ref{eq:off-bd}),  the extremes in (\ref{eq:cnt-sym}) occur at $t = 1 \pm \rho$ 
and setting $p(\pm \rho):=q_{\pm}(r)$,  $s(\pm \rho):=q_{\pm} (d_\star (1 \mp \rho))$,
it suffices to show that for some $c$,  
all $\rho \le  e^{-1}$,  $d_\star \le 1$ and $r$ as specified,   
\begin{equation}\label{eq:calc-bd}
\max\Big\{  \frac{1-s(-\rho)}{1-s(\rho)},  \frac{s(\rho)}{s(-\rho)},   \frac{p(\rho)}{p(-\rho)},  \frac{1-p(-\rho)}{1-p(\rho)} 
\Big\} \le 1+c\rho \,.
\end{equation}
Setting $b:=\log(e/r) \ge \log(e/d_\star) := b_\star \ge 1$, 
note that $1-p(0) = \frac{1}{b+1} \le \frac{1}{2}$ while $s(0)=\frac{b_\star}{b+1} \in [1-p(0),p(0)]$, 
with (\ref{eq:calc-bd}) holding if $b |p'(x)|$ and $b |s'(x)|$ are bounded,  uniformly in $|x| \le e^{-1}$ 
and $b \ge b_\star \ge 1$.  To verify the latter property,  check that 
\[
p(x)=1-\frac{1}{1+b+f_1(x)}\,,   \qquad s(x)=1 + \frac{f_2(x)+b_\star-1-b}{1+b+f_1(x)} \,,
\]
where $f_1(x):=\log(1+x/e)$ and $f_2(x):=-\log(1-x)$.
Consequently,  with $f_i(0)=0$,  $f_1(x) \ge -1$ and $f_i'(x)$,  $i=1,2$ uniformly bounded on $|x| \le e^{-1}$, 
the same applies for $b|p'(x)|$ and $b|s'(x)|$,  which by the preceding completes the proof of the lemma.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lem-off-center-applies} 
Fix $\mathsf{u} \in \mathbb{T}^2$,  $m,\mathsf{s},\mathsf{L} \ge 1$, 
strictly decreasing $R_i$,  $0 \le i \le \mathsf{L}$ with {$R_0=e R_1 \le e^{-1}$},  $R:=R_{\mathsf{L}}=R_{\mathsf{L}-1}/e$
and $\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{u},\rho R)$,  $\rho \le e^{-1}$,  $r \le (1-\rho)R$.
Let
 $\mathcal{A}^{(m)}$ denote an event involving only the excursion 
counts between $\partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}} (\mathsf{u},R_i)$ and
$\partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}} (\mathsf{u},R_{i-1})$,  $2 \le i \le \mathsf{L}$,  with precisely $m$ excursions {specified for}
$i=\mathsf{L}$.  Then,  for $c$ of \Cref{lem:easy-off} and any $k \ge 0$, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:off-center-bd} 
 (1+c \rho)^{-(k+m)} \, (\mathbb{P}_R^{1})^m (\Gamma) \le 
\mathbb{Q}_{R_1}^{\mathsf{s},\mathsf{u}}(\Gamma|\mathcal{A}^{(m)}) 
\le (1+c \rho)^{(k+m)} \,  (\mathbb{P}_R^{1})^m (\Gamma) \qquad \forall \Gamma \in \mathcal{N}_{\mathsf{v},r, m,k} \,,
\end{equation}
{where in the term $\mathbb{Q}_{R_1}^{\mathsf{s},\mathsf{u}}(\Gamma|\mathcal{A}^{(m)}) $, we consider for the event $\Gamma$ the excursion counts induced by the  $m$ excursions  between $\partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}} (\mathsf{u},R_\mathsf{L})$ and
$\partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}} (\mathsf{u},R_{\mathsf{L}-1})$.}
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
It suffices to consider $\mathsf{L} \ge 2$ and assume {\sc\lowercase{wlog}} 
that for some non-random 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:mi-s}
0 = m_0  \le m_1 \le \cdots \le m_{\mathsf{s}} := m,
\end{equation}
the event $\mathcal{A}^{(m)}$ dictates having precisely $m_i$ of our inner excursions completed by the end of the $i$-th 
outer excursion (e.g.  \Cref{fig:village1} has $\mathsf{s}=2$,  $m_1=0$ and $m=m_2=3$).
The proof is based on a path decomposition.
Using throughout our running convention,  of viewing 
the path as a directed curve up to time re-parametrization,  we proceed to decompose the first $\mathsf{s}$ 
outer excursions,  between circles of radii $R_1$ and $R_0$ into outer segments 
$\mathcal{R}_0$ till first entering $\mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{u},R_1)$ at some $\mathsf{x}_1$ (the 
dashed red curve in \Cref{fig:village1}),  followed by 
$\mathcal{R}_i$ from some $\mathsf{w}_i \in \partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{u},R_0)$ to some 
$\mathsf{x}_{i+1} \in \partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{u},R_1)$ (marked there by solid red),  interlaced 
between out-connecting segments $\mathcal{C}_i$ (within $\mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{u},R_0)$,  marked in blue),
that lead from $\mathsf{x}_i$ to $\mathsf{w}_i$ if $m_{i}=m_{i-1}$,  or otherwise
end at $\mathsf{z}_{m_{i-1}+1} \in \partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{u},R_{\mathsf{L}})$
(with a dashed line in former case and a solid one in the latter).  In case $m_{i+1}>m_i$ we further decompose
the remainder of the $i$-th outer excursion (between $\mathcal{C}_i$ and $\mathcal{R}_{i}$),  to its inner parts 
$\mathcal{B}_{j}$,   $j \in (m_{i-1},m_{i}]$,  from $\mathsf{z}_j \in \partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{u},R_{\mathsf{L}})$ to 
$\mathsf{y}_j \in \partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{u},R_{\mathsf{L}-1})$ staying within $\mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{u},R_{\mathsf{L}-1})$
(marked black in \Cref{fig:village1}),  interlaced between the in-connecting paths 
$\mathcal{G}_{j}$,  $j \in (m_{i-1}, m_i]$ which stay outside $\mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{u},R_{\mathsf{L}})$,
leading from $\mathsf{y}_j$ to $\mathsf{z}_{j+1}$ (as solid green lines),  except for $\mathcal{G}_{m_i}$
which goes out,  ending at $\mathsf{w}_i$ (marked by a green dashed line).  This decomposition is uniquely 
specified by the parameters of (\ref{eq:mi-s}),  where for illustration,  the case
depicted in  \Cref{fig:village1} corresponds to having 
\[
\mathcal{R}_0,  \mathcal{C}_1,\mathcal{R}_1,\mathcal{C}_2,\mathcal{B}_1,\mathcal{G}_1,\mathcal{B}_2,\mathcal{G}_2,\mathcal{B}_3,\mathcal{G}_3,\mathcal{R}_2\,.
\] 
Note that $\Gamma \in \sigma(\mathcal{B}_j,j \le m)$ and $\mathcal{A}^{(m)} \in \sigma(\mathcal{C}_i,\mathcal{G}_j, j \le m, i \le \mathsf{s})$.  In particular, 
$\Gamma \in \mathcal{N}_{\mathsf{v},r,m,k}$ is a countable union of disjoint sets of the form $\Gamma_1 \times \cdots \times \Gamma_m$,  for $\Gamma_j \in \mathcal{N}_{\mathsf{v},r}$ such that $\Gamma_j \subset \widetilde{A}_{k_j}$,  $\sum_j k_j \le k$ 
specifying the relevant excursion counts (around $\mathsf{v}$),  during the segment $\mathcal{B}_j$.  Likewise,  
$\mathcal{A}^{(m)}$ is a countable disjoint union of product sets $\mathcal{A}_0 \times \mathcal{A}_1 \cdots \times \mathcal{A}_m$ 
where $\mathcal{A}_0$ specifies the excursion counts between balls around $\mathsf{u}$,
of radii $R_i$ and $R_{i-1}$,  $2 \le i < \mathsf{L}$,  
                             
up to the start of the segment $\mathcal{B}_1$,  with $\mathcal{A}_j$,  $j \ge 1$ specifying such excursion counts 
                                               
that occur from the end of $\mathcal{B}_{j}$ to the start of $\mathcal{B}_{j+1}$.
By the law of total probability,  it thus suffices to establish 
(\ref{eq:off-center-bd}) for $\Gamma=\Gamma_1 \times \cdots \times \Gamma_m$ 
and $\mathcal{A}^{(m)}=\mathcal{A}_0 \times \cdots \times \mathcal{A}_m$
(excluding all choices $\mathcal{A}_j$ and $\Gamma_j$ of zero probability,  or which are inconsistent 
with the given $\{m_i\}$).
                                                                                                  
                                               
Fixing such $\{\Gamma_j\}$ and $\{\mathcal{A}_j\}$,  the stated bound follows from having for any $1 \le j \le m$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:off-center-prod}
(1+c \rho)^{-(k_j+1)} \, \mathbb{P}_R^{1} (\Gamma_j)  \le 
\frac{\mathbb{Q}_{R_1}^{\mathsf{s},\mathsf{u}}(\Gamma_1 \times \cdots \times \Gamma_j\,|\, \mathcal{A}_0 \times\cdots \times \mathcal{A}_j)}
{\mathbb{Q}_{R_1}^{\mathsf{s},\mathsf{u}}(\Gamma_1 \times \cdots \times \Gamma_{j-1}\,|\, \mathcal{A}_0 \times\cdots \times \mathcal{A}_{j-1})} \le
 (1+c \rho)^{(k_j+1)} \mathbb{P}_R^{1} (\Gamma_j)  \,.
\end{equation}
Indeed,  applying (\ref{eq:off-center-prod}) backwards from $j=m$ to $j=1$ establishes (\ref{eq:off-center-bd})
for such product sets.  

We thus turn to proving (\ref{eq:off-center-prod}). The ratio of probabilities in the middle of
                                                                                
                            
(\ref{eq:off-center-prod}) equals
\begin{equation}
\label{eq-ofernew300926a}
                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                 
                                                                         
\mathbb{Q}_{R_1}^{\mathsf{s},\mathsf{u}} (\Gamma_j \, | \, \mathcal{A}_0 \times\cdots \times \mathcal{A}_{j-1}, \Gamma_1 \times \cdots \times \Gamma_{j-1})
\frac{\mathbb{Q}_{R_1}^{\mathsf{s},\mathsf{u}}(\mathcal{A}_j \,|\,  \Gamma_1 \times \cdots \times \Gamma_{j},\mathcal{A}_0 \times\cdots \times \mathcal{A}_{j-1})}
{\mathbb{Q}_{R_1}^{\mathsf{s},\mathsf{u}}(\mathcal{A}_j \,|\, \mathcal{A}_0 \times\cdots \times \mathcal{A}_{j-1})} \,.
\end{equation}
{Denoting by} $\mathcal{P}_j$ the $\sigma$-algebra generated by the path up to the start of the segment 
$\mathcal{B}_{j}$, 
 and by 
$\mathcal{P}_{j}^+$ the $\sigma$-algebra generated by the path up to the end of the segment $\mathcal{B}_j$
for $1 \le j \le m$, we {will show} that
\begin{align}\label{eq:radial-eq}
& \mathbb{Q}_{R_1}^{\mathsf{s},\mathsf{u}}(\mathcal{A}_j \,|\,  \mathcal{P}_j^+)= \mathbb{Q}_{R_1}^{\mathsf{s},\mathsf{u}}(\mathcal{A}_j ),\\
(1+c \rho)^{-(k_j+1)} \, \mathbb{P}_R^{1} (\Gamma_j) \le
& \mathbb{Q}_{R_1}^{\mathsf{s},\mathsf{u}}(\Gamma_j \, | \, \mathcal{P}_j)
 \le(1+c \rho)^{(k_j+1)} \mathbb{P}_R^{1} (\Gamma_j)  \,.
\label{eq:bd-Gammaj}
\end{align}
{Since the} conditioning events in the ratio of probabilities in (\ref{eq-ofernew300926a}) are $\mathcal{P}_j^+$ measurable,  by (\ref{eq:radial-eq}) that ratio must equal one,  whereby (\ref{eq:bd-Gammaj}) together 
with the $\mathcal{P}_j$-measurability of $ \mathcal{A}_0 \times\cdots \times \mathcal{A}_{j-1}, \Gamma_1 \times \cdots \times \Gamma_{j-1}$ would yield (\ref{eq:off-center-prod}).
Turning to show (\ref{eq:radial-eq}), 
note that by the strong Markov property,  
                           
the conditioning on $\mathcal{P}_j^+$ can only affect the probability of the event $\mathcal{A}_j$ 
                                                                                                 
               
via the $\mathcal{P}_j^+$-measurable value of $\mathsf{y}_j$. 
                                    
But $\mathcal{A}_j$ involves only 
excursion counts between concentric circles centered at $\mathsf{u}$,  so its
conditional 
probability 
does not depend on the specific value of $\mathsf{y}_j \in \partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{u},R_{\mathsf{L}-1})$,
yielding
               
the identity (\ref{eq:radial-eq}).  In (\ref{eq:bd-Gammaj}) we have 
the conditional probability of the event $\Gamma_j \in \mathcal{N}_{\mathsf{v},r}$ occurring 
during our $j$-th inner part $\mathcal{B}_j$ given $\mathcal{P}_j$, 
which  
by the above reasoning is between the minimum and maximum,
over $\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{z},\mathsf{u})=R$,
of $\mathbb{P}_R^{\mathsf{z},\mathsf{u}}(\Gamma_j)$ of \Cref{cor:easy-off}.
Setting $d_\star=1$,  our assumptions on $r$ and $\rho$ match (\ref{eq:par-rt}), 
with (\ref{eq:z1-v-cond}) holding by the triangle inequality.  Thus,    
applying (\ref{eq:off1-center-bd}) for $A=\Gamma_{j} \subset \widetilde{A}_{k_j}$ we
verify (\ref{eq:bd-Gammaj}) and thereupon complete our proof of (\ref{eq:off-center-bd}).
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- remark-13: body_md -->
\label{rmk:off-center-applies}
Our proof of \Cref{lem-off-center-applies} is easily adapted to handle 
$\mathsf{s}$ independent planar Brownian paths from $\partial \mathbb{B}(\mathsf{u},R_1)$ to  
$\partial \mathbb{B} (\mathsf{u},R_0)$ (conditioned on $\mathcal{A}^{(m)}$ of the form specified in the lemma).
                                   
                                                                                                
                                         
In particular,  taking $\mathsf{L}=1$ and $\mathsf{s}=m$ 
then corresponds to $m$ {\sc\lowercase{iid}} Brownian paths,  each stopped at its first 
exit from $\partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{u},e R_\mathsf{L})$.
<!-- end remark-13 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lem-xyN}
For some $C'$, 
          
all $\mathsf {K}_{5}$ large and $\mathsf{u} \in \mathbb{T}^2$, 
if $j \ge \mathsf {K}_{5}+ \log \mathsf{\delta_\star} + 2$,  $\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}') \in [e^{j-1}\varepsilon ,e^{j}\varepsilon]$,  $\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},\mathsf{u}) \le e^{\mathsf {K}_{5}} \varepsilon$, 
$\ell=j+6\log j$ and $y \in [0, \ell]$,  then for $R=e^{\ell} \varepsilon$ and  
$m=\frac{1}{2} (2 \ell+y)^2$ paths as 
in  \Cref{lem-off-center-applies},  
                
\begin{align}
\sup_{\varepsilon}  \{ \mathbb{Q}_{R_1}^{\mathsf{s},\mathsf{u}}\big(\Gamma^{(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}',1} \times \cdots \times \Gamma^{(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}',m}
\,|\,\mathcal{A}^{(m)}\big) \}
\leq & C' e^{-4j} e^{-3y} 
                                           
\,, 
\label{xyN.2}
                                                                                                                                                                                    
\end{align}
where 
                                              
$\Gamma^{(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}',j}$ is the event of the $j$-th path
avoiding $\mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},\varepsilon/e) \cup \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x}',\varepsilon/e)$.
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
The path decomposition in our proof of \Cref{lem-off-center-applies} yields 
                                                                                  
that 
\[
                               
\mathbb{Q}_{R_1}^{\mathsf{s},\mathsf{u}}\big(\Gamma^{(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}',1} \times \cdots \times \Gamma^{(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}',m}
\,|\,\mathcal{A}^{(m)}\big) 
\le \sup_{\mathsf{z} \in \partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{u},R)} \big( 1- q^{\mathsf{z},\mathsf{u}}_{\ell,\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'} \big)^m
 \qquad {\rm for} \qquad 
q^{\mathsf{z},\mathsf{u}}_{\ell,\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'} := \mathbb{P}_R^{\mathsf{z},\mathsf{u}} \Big(({\Gamma^{(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'}})^\complement\Big) \,.
\]
With $4 \ge \frac{m}{\ell^{2}}  \ge 2 + 2 \frac{y}{\ell}
                      
$ 
                               
and $4 j \ge 3 \ell$ for all $\mathsf {K}_{5}$ large enough,  utilizing that $1-q \le e^{-q}$
we get (\ref{xyN.2}) upon showing 
that for $C$ finite and all $\mathsf{z} \in \partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{u},R)$,
\begin{eqnarray}\label{ver.16-new}
q^{\mathsf{z},\mathsf{u}}_{\ell,\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'} \ge 2 \,  \frac{(j-C)}{\ell^2} \,.
                                   
\end{eqnarray}
To this end,  note that the event $({\Gamma^{(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'}})^\complement$ of our 
(stopped) path 
                                            
entering $\mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},\varepsilon/e) \cup \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x}',\varepsilon/e)$
                                        
contains the event of hitting one of these (small) balls 
                                       
and thereafter 
                            
missing the other ball.   Setting $r=e^{-\ell}$ consider
the latter two disjoint events,  where by the strong Markov property upon first hitting 
the relevant ball of radius $\varepsilon/e$ (say,  at location $\mathsf{z}'$),  
\begin{equation}\label{eq:lbd-union-2-balls}
q^{\mathsf{z},\mathsf{u}}_{\ell,\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'} \ge q^{\mathsf{z},\mathsf{u}}_{r,\mathsf{x}} \inf_{\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{z}',\mathsf{x})=\varepsilon/e} \{ 1- q^{\mathsf{z}',\mathsf{u}}_{r,\mathsf{x}'} \} 
+ q^{\mathsf{z},\mathsf{u}}_{r,\mathsf{x}'}  \inf_{\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{z}',\mathsf{x}')=\varepsilon/e} \{ 1- q^{\mathsf{z}',\mathsf{u}}_{r,\mathsf{x}}\}  
\end{equation}
(see \Cref{angle-off-m1} {depicting a sample from the first event considered on the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}})}.
Setting $d_\star=1$ for the first term in each product in (\ref{eq:lbd-union-2-balls}) 
while $d_\star =\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}')/R$ for the second term in each product,  we get from 
(\ref{eq:pv-u}) the lower bound $\frac{1-c\rho}{\ell+2} (\frac{j}{\ell+2}-c\rho)$ for each product.
In our setting $\rho \to 0$ as $\mathsf {K}_{5} \to \infty$,  with uniformly bounded
$$
(\ell+2) \rho \le (\ell+2) \max(e^{-j}, e^{-\ell} (e^j + e^{\mathsf {K}_{5}}))\,.
$$
Thus,  each of the two terms we add on the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} of (\ref{eq:lbd-union-2-balls}) is at least
$\frac{j-(C-8)}{(\ell+2)^{2}} \ge \frac{j-C}{\ell^2}$ and (\ref{ver.16-new}) follows. 
\begin{comment}
                                            
                                                                                                         
  
                                                                                                                       
  
                                      
                                                                                            
  
                                                                                               
  
                                                                                                  
                                                                    
                                                                              
                                                                                          
\end{comment}
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{lem:g4-bds} 
For some $0<c(\mathsf {K}_{6})<C(\mathsf {K}_{6})<\infty$ and all $\mathsf {K}_{5}$ large enough 
\begin{align}\label{ubd2-g4}
g_{\mathsf {K}_{4}}(z) &\le  C(\mathsf {K}_{6})\frac{z}{\mathsf {K}_{4}}   e^{- 2 z}  e^{-\frac{z^2}{8 \mathsf {K}_{4}}} \,,\\
\label{eq:lbd-alpha}
g_{\mathsf {K}_{4}}(z) &\ge c(\mathsf {K}_{6}) \frac{z}{\mathsf {K}_{4}} e^{-2 z}\,, 
\qquad \forall z \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_4 \cap  [2 \sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}}, 4 \sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}}]\,.
\end{align}
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- definition-5: body_md -->
\label{dfn:Markov}
Under $\bar \mathbb{P}^{(\star)}_z$,  let $q^{(u)}_{\ell',\ell}(x',x)=q^{(u)}_{\ell-\ell'}(x',x)$ for  $u \ge 0$,  $\ell \ge \ell'$, 
be the probability that during $\frac{(x')^2}{2}$ excursions at level $\ell'$ around ${\bf 0}$,
the path completed exactly $\frac{x^2}{2}$ excursions at level $\ell$ and at least 
$\frac{1}{2}(x' \wedge x - u)^2$ such excursions at levels $j \in (\ell,\ell')$,  using
$q_{\ell-\ell'}(x',x)$ when $u=x' \wedge x$.  Similarly,  denote by
$q^{(\ge)}_{\mathsf {J}^\star}(x',x)$ the probability that in addition to completing exactly $\frac{x^2}{2}$ 
excursions at level $\mathsf {L}_o+\mathsf {L}_1$ during $\frac{(x')^2}{2}$ such excursions at level $\mathsf {L}_o$,  for all
$j \in \mathsf {J}^\star$ the $j$-th level excursion count around ${\bf 0}$ exceeds $\frac{1}{2} \gamma^{\mathsf {J}^\star}_{-1}(j)^2$
and by $q^{\Cap}_{\mathsf {J}^\star}(x',x)$ the probability that for each $j \in \mathsf {J}^\star$
the number of such excursions 
                    
is further $\frac{1}{2} y^2$ for some $y \in \mathsf{I}'_j$.
<!-- end definition-5 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{lem:g4-cnc}
Fix $0 < \kappa \le {\kappa_o} < \frac{1}{3} \wedge {\kappa_1} < \frac{1}{2} < {\kappa'} < {\kappa''} < \frac{3}{4}$.
                             
\newline
(a).  There exists $u_o<\infty$ such that for  any  $(x \wedge y)^\kappa \ge u \ge u_o$ 
and $|x-y| \le (x \wedge y)^{{\kappa''}}$, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:q3-bd}
q_3^{(u)}(x,[y,y+2)) \ge \frac{1}{4}
                                      
 q_3(x,[y,y+2)) \,.
\end{equation}
(b). Fixing $\Delta \ge 0$ and $\mathsf {K}_{6}$ large,  for some $C_{\mathsf {K}_{6}} < \infty$,  any $\mathsf {K}_{5}$ large and 
$z \in (\mathsf {K}_{4}^{{\kappa_1}},  \mathsf {K}_{4}^{{\kappa'}})$ with $\bar \mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}_{4}}(z) \in \mathbb{N}$,
\begin{align}\label{ubd-wQ}
 \bar \mathbb{P}^{(\star)}_{z} ( \widehat{\mathcal{Q}}_{{\bf 0}}) &\le C_{\mathsf {K}_{6}} \frac{z}{\mathsf {K}_{4}} e^{-2 \mathsf {K}_{4}} e^{- 2z}  e^{-z^2/(8 \mathsf {K}_{4})} \,,\\
 \label{ubd-Aell}
 \bar \mathbb{P}^{(\star)}_{z} (\mathcal{A}_{{\bf 0},\ell}) &\le C_{\mathsf {K}_{6}} \frac{z}{\mathsf {K}_{4}} e^{-2 \mathsf {K}_{4}} e^{- 2z}  e^{-z^2/(8 \mathsf {K}_{4})}\,, 
 \qquad \quad \forall \ell \in \mathsf {J}^\star \,.
\end{align}
(c).  There exist $c_{\mathsf {K}_{6}} >0$ so if in addition $z \in [2 \sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}}, 4\sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}}]$,  then for $\mathcal{A}_{{\bf 0}}$ of (\ref{def:whcI}),
\begin{align}\label{eq:mom-bd-cent}
\bar \mathbb{P}^{(\star)}_z(\mathcal{A}_{{\bf 0}}) &\ge c_{\mathsf {K}_{6}}  \frac{z}{\mathsf {K}_{4}}  e^{-2 \mathsf {K}_{4}} e^{-2 z} \,.
\end{align}
(d).  The preceding applies 
                                                     
also for   
$\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}_{\mathsf{v}}$,  $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v}}$ and $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v},\ell}$,  uniformly in $\| \mathsf{v}\| \le \mathsf {K}_{5}^{-5}$.
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
(a).  We show (\ref{eq:q3-bd}) by bounding above the value of 
$q_3(x,[y,y+2))-q_3^{(u)}(x,[y,y+2))$.  Specifically,  setting $z:=x \wedge y - u$,  
by our definition of $q_3^{(u)}(x,\cdot)$,  the Markov property and the monotonicity 
of $z' \mapsto q_j(z',[y,\infty))$,  it suffices to show that 
\[
q_1(x,(0, z]) q_2 (z,[y,\infty)) + q_2(x,(0,z]) q_1(z,[y,\infty)) \le \frac{3}{4} q_3(x,[y,y+2)) \,.
\]
Setting $m:=\frac{x^2}{2}$,  $\widetilde{m}=\frac{z^2}{2}$,  $m':=\frac{y^2}{2}$ and 
$I_{m'}:=[0, 2(\sqrt{2m'}+1))$,  this amounts in turn to
\begin{equation}\label{eq:q3-bd-alt}
\mathbb{P}(S^{(1)}_m \le \widetilde{m}) \mathbb{P}(S^{(2)}_{\widetilde{m}} \ge m') + 
\mathbb{P}(S^{(2)}_m \le \widetilde{m}) \mathbb{P}(S^{(1)}_{\widetilde{m}} \ge m')  \le \frac{3}{4} \mathbb{P}(S^{(3)}_m -m' \in I_{m'})\,,
\end{equation}
where $S^{(j)}_m$ denote the sum of $m$ 
{\sc\lowercase{iid}} non-negative integer variables $\{\mathsf {G}'_i\}$ of the form 
\begin{equation}\label{dfn:GJp}
\mathbb{P}(\mathsf {G}'_i=0)=1-q  \quad \text{and} \quad \mathbb{P}(\mathsf {G}'_i=k)=q^2 (1-q)^{k-1},  \qquad \forall k \ge 1
\end{equation}
for the parameter $q:=\frac{1}{j+1}$ (see \cite[(2.1)]{BRZ2}).  It is easy to verify that 
\begin{equation}\label{def:q-cgf}
\Lambda_q(\lambda) :=\log \mathbb{E}[e^{-\lambda \mathsf {G}_i'}] = 
\log \Big( 1 - \frac{q (e^{\lambda}-1)}{q+e^{\lambda}-1} \Big)  \qquad \forall \lambda \ge 0 \,,
\end{equation}
whereby $\mathsf {G}'_i$ has finite {\sc\lowercase{mgf}} up to $\lambda=\log(1-q)$,  with   
\begin{equation}\label{eq:GJp-var}
\mathbb{E}[\mathsf {G}'_i]=-\Lambda_q'(0)=1 \qquad \hbox{and} \qquad \hbox{var}(\mathsf {G}_i')=\Lambda_q''(0)=\frac{2}{q} (1-q) \,.
\end{equation}
In particular,  
$\widehat{S}^{(j)}_m :=(S^{(j)}_m-m)/\sqrt{2jm}$ have mean zero and variance one.  Under our
assumptions on $x$ and $y$,  {\sc\lowercase{wlog}} $I_{m'} \supset [0,\sqrt{6 m})$.  Moreover,  for 
$m':=m+t \sqrt{m}$,  $t_+:=t \vee 0$ and any $u \in [u_o, (2 (m \wedge m'))^{\kappa/2}]$,
\[
\widetilde{m} - m  = - (-t)_+ \sqrt{m} - u \sqrt{2(m \wedge m')} + \frac{1}{2} u^{2}  \le - (u+ (-t)_+) \sqrt{m} 
\]
provided $u_o$ is large enough (recall that $\sqrt{2 (m \wedge m')} -\sqrt{2 m} 
= - (x-y)_+ 
\ge - (x \wedge y)^{{\kappa''}}$).  We thus replace (\ref{eq:q3-bd-alt}) by the stronger requirement 
\begin{align}\label{eq:q3-new}
\mathbb{P}\Big(\widehat{S}^{(1)}_m \le -\frac{u+(-t)_+}{\sqrt{2}}\Big) \mathbb{P}\Big(\widehat{S}^{(2)}_{\widetilde{m}} \ge \frac{u+t_+}{2}\Big) &+ 
\mathbb{P}\Big(\widehat{S}^{(2)}_m \le -\frac{u+(-t)_+}{2}\Big) \mathbb{P}\Big( \widehat{S}^{(1)}_{\widetilde{m}} \ge \frac{u+t_+}{\sqrt{2}}\Big) 
 \nonumber \\
&\le \frac{3}{4} \Big[ \mathbb{P}\big(\widehat{S}^{(3)}_m \ge \frac{t}{\sqrt 6} +1 \big) -
\mathbb{P}\big(\widehat{S}^{(3)}_m \ge \frac{t}{\sqrt 6} \big) \Big] \,.
\end{align}
Denoting by $\Phi(\cdot)$ the standard normal {\sc\lowercase{cdf}},  we have that for some $u_o$ finite, 
any $u \ge u_o$ and all $t$,
\begin{align}\label{eq:q3-Gauss}
e^{\frac{t^2}{25}} \Big[ \Phi\big(-\frac{u+(-t)_+}{\sqrt{2}}\big) \Big(1-\Phi\big(\frac{u+t_+}{2}\big)\Big) &+ \Phi\big( -\frac{u+(-t)_+}{2}\big) \Big(1-\Phi\big(\frac{u+t_+}{\sqrt{2}}\big)\Big) \Big] \nonumber \\
&\le \frac{3}{5} \Big(\Phi\big(\frac{t}{\sqrt{6}}+1 \big) - \Phi\big(\frac{t}{\sqrt{6}}\big) \Big) \,.
\end{align}
Indeed,  as (\ref{eq:q3-Gauss}) is of the form $f_2(t,u) \le f_1(t)$ for continuous $f_1,f_2 >0$, 
with $\sup_u \frac{f_2(t,u)}{f_1(t)} \to 0$ as $|t| \to \infty$ and {$\sup_{|t| \le b} f_2(t,u) \to 0$ as $u \to \infty$,  
for fixed $b$},
                                                                                                                                                                                                  
it holds for all $t$ and $u \ge u_0$,  provided $u_o$ is large enough.

Now,  fixing $\xi<\frac{1}{6}$ and increasing $u_o$ as needed,  the normal approximation of 
\cite[Thm. ~VIII.2.1]{Petrov} yields (\ref{eq:q3-new}) for $u_o \le u \le 2 m^{\kappa/2}$,  
$|t| 
                                               
\le m^{\xi}$.  To deal with larger $|t|$ first 
note that our assumptions on $x$ and $y$ imply for large $u_o$ that $|t| \le 2 m^{{\kappa''}/2} \le m^{3/8}$,  
with the {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of (\ref{eq:q3-new}) still uniformly bounded by the {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of (\ref{eq:q3-Gauss}) 
(increasing  $u_o$,  hence $m \wedge m'$,  so the factors $\frac{\pm t}{\sqrt m} \lambda(\frac{\pm t}{\sqrt m})$ 
in \cite[Thm.~VIII.2.1]{Petrov} be accommodated by the left-most
exponential factor in (\ref{eq:q3-Gauss})).  Moreover,  mimicking the derivation of \cite[Thm. ~VIII.2.8]{Petrov},  
apply \cite[Thm.~VIII.2.1]{Petrov} for each term on the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} of 
(\ref{eq:q3-new}) then plug the tail asymptotic of $1-\Phi(\cdot)$ to deduce that their difference 
                                 
is at least $\frac{2}{3} \mathbb{P}\big(\widehat{S}^{(3)}_m \ge t' \big)$ for 
$t':=|\frac{t}{\sqrt 6}| \wedge |\frac{t}{\sqrt 6}+1|$,  any
$|t| \in [m^{\xi},m^{3/8}]$ and $m \ge m_0$.  To complete the proof recall \cite[Thm.~VIII.2.1]{Petrov}
that the latter quantity is in turn bounded below by the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} of (\ref{eq:q3-Gauss}),  up to another 
multiplicative factor,  embedded within the factor $\exp(\frac{t^2}{25})$ of (\ref{eq:q3-Gauss}).
\newline
(b). Clearly,  the probability $q_\ell(y,0)$ of missing a concentric inner ball during 
$\frac{y^2}{2}$ excursions is 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:miss-ball}
q_{\ell}(y,0) =\Big(1-\frac{1}{\ell+1}\Big)^{y^2/2} \le e^{-\frac{y^2}{2 \ell +2}} \,.
\end{equation}
Considering $\ell=\mathsf {K}_{6}+1$,  we ignore hereafter the negligible contribution to $\bar \mathbb{P}^{(\star)}_{z} ( \widehat{\mathcal{Q}}_{{\bf 0}})$
from $y \ge \mathsf {K}_{6} \sqrt{6 \mathsf {K}_{4}}$.  Now,  bounding $q^{(\ge)}_{\mathsf {J}^\star}(\cdot)$ by $q_{\mathsf {L}}(\cdot)$
and summing over $y$ leads to $\bar \mathbb{P}^{(\star)}_{z} ( \widehat{\mathcal{Q}}_{{\bf 0}}) \le \sum_x q_{\widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5}+1}(x,0)$,  
so by the preceding reasoning we further restrict the sum in (\ref{eq:decom-p0}) to 
$x \le a':= 2 \widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5} + (\widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5})^{{\kappa''}}$.  Note that by \cite[Theorem 1.1(a)]{BRZ} we have 
for some $C<\infty$ and any $x \ge a := 2\widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5}-(\widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5})^{\kappa_o}$ and $y \ge b := 2\mathsf {K}_{6}-\mathsf {K}_{6}^{\kappa_o}$ as above,  
\begin{equation}\label{eq:BRZ-1.1a}
q^{(\ge)}_{\mathsf {J}^\star}(x,[y,y+2)) \le C  \frac{(1+x-a)(1+y-b)}{\mathsf {L}_1}\sqrt{\frac{x}{y\mathsf {L}_1}} e^{-\frac{(x-y)^2}{2\mathsf {L}_1}} \,.
\end{equation}
One may further adapt the proof of  \cite[(1.10)]{BRZ} (taking there $L=\mathsf {L}_o$),  to have for
some $C$, $c$ finite,  upon setting $\mathsf {L}_o':=\mathsf {L}_o+c$,  that for $z \in (\mathsf {K}_{4}^{{\kappa_1}},  \mathsf {K}_{4}^{{\kappa'}})$ 
and any such $x$,  
\begin{equation}\label{eq:BRZ-1.10m}
q_{\, \mathsf {L}_o} (2\mathsf {K}_{4}+z,[x,x+2)) \le \frac{C}{\sqrt{4\pi \mathsf {L}_o'}} e^{-\frac{(2\mathsf {K}_{4}+z-x)^2}{2\mathsf {L}_o'}} \,.
\end{equation}
                                                                                                     
                                                                                                         
                                                                     
Indeed,  \cite[(1.10)]{BRZ} bounds $q_{\ell}(x',[x,x+2))$ in case $\max(x',x) \le c' \ell$; That restriction is only used in evaluating the last expression in the display after \cite[(4.1),  page 140]{BRZ}.  But its conclusion 
applies as long as $|x'-x| \le c' \ell$,  since combining the sub-Gaussian tails of $w=\sqrt{2\mathcal{L}_1}-x'$ and 
the expansion of \cite{BRZ},  yields the bound on \cite[(1.10)]{BRZ},  up to the uniformly bounded multiplicative factor    
$\int_\mathbb{R} dw \sqrt{1+|w|/x'} e^{-c w^2} \int_0^2 e^{(x-x')(w-t)/\ell} dt$.
When $|x-x'|>c' \ell$ one gets,  by comparing the law of $(\sqrt{2\mathcal{L}_1}-x')/\sqrt{2}$ 
there to the standard Gaussian law,  an extra error term of the type 
$e^{c(|x'-x|/\ell^2}$ (for some $c \ge \frac{1}{2}$),  which is absorbed by changing to $2(\ell+c)$ in the exponent in the bound,  
                                                   
as we have done. 
                                                                                          
                                        

To help appreciate the following,  we point out that for large $\mathsf {K}_{5}$ we have $\mathsf {L}_1=(1+o(1)) \mathsf {K}_{5}$
and $\mathsf {L}_o' = O(\log \mathsf {K}_{5})$.  Plugging the bounds (\ref{eq:miss-ball})-(\ref{eq:BRZ-1.10m}) into (\ref{eq:decom-p0}) 
we thus find that for some $C'$ finite and any $\mathsf {K}_{4}$ large enough, 
\[  
\bar \mathbb{P}^{(\star)}_{z} ( \widehat{\mathcal{Q}}_{{\bf 0}}) 
\le \frac{C'}{\mathsf {K}_{4}} \sum_{x=a}^{a'}  \frac{(1+x-a)}{\sqrt{4\pi \mathsf {L}_o'}} e^{-\frac{(2\mathsf {K}_{4}+z-x)^2}{2\mathsf {L}_o'}}
\sum_{y=0}^\infty e^{-\frac{(x-y)^2}{2\mathsf {L}_1}} \sqrt{y} e^{-y^2/(2 \mathsf {K}_{6}+4)},
\]
where now the sums in $x,y$ go over even integers,  and we have used the fact that 
per value of $\mathsf {K}_{6}$,  the ratio $x/\mathsf {L}_1 \le a'/\mathsf {L}_1$ is bounded 
uniformly in $\widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5}$.  Using this again,  we see that the preceding sum over $y$ is at most 
$C'_{\mathsf {K}_{6}} e^{-x^2/(2\mathsf {L}_1)}$ for 
some $C'_{\mathsf {K}_{6}}$ finite,  resulting with 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:temp-bd}
\bar \mathbb{P}^{(\star)}_{z} ( \widehat{\mathcal{Q}}_{{\bf 0}}) 
\le \frac{C_{\mathsf {K}_{6}}}{3 \mathsf {K}_{4}} \sum_{x=a}^{a'}  \frac{(2c+x-a)}{\sqrt{4\pi \mathsf {L}_o'}} e^{-\frac{(2\mathsf {K}_{4}+z-x)^2}{2\mathsf {L}_o'}} e^{-\frac{x^2}{2\mathsf {L}_1}} \,.
\end{equation}
Now using $(A+B)^{2}\geq A^2/2-B^2$ twice,  we have for any $z,w,v$ and $\mathsf {L} \ge \mathsf {K}_{6} - c \ge  0$,  that 
 \[
 2 ( \mathsf {K}_{6} - c) + \frac{(z+w-v+2\mathsf {K}_{6}-2c)^2}{2\mathsf {L}} \ge \frac{(z+w-v)^2}{4\mathsf {L}} 
 \ge  \frac{z^2}{8\mathsf {L}} - \frac{(w-v)^2}{4\mathsf {L}} \,.
\]
Thus,  with $\mathsf {K}_{4}-\mathsf {L}_o'
           
=\mathsf {L}_1+\mathsf {K}_{6}-c$,  setting $x=2\mathsf {K}_{4} - 2\mathsf {L}_o' -v+w+z$,  we get that for $\mathsf {L}_1 \ge \mathsf {L}_o'$,  
                      
\begin{align}
   
\frac{(2\mathsf {K}_{4}+z-x)^2}{2\mathsf {L}_o'} + \frac{x^2}{2\mathsf {L}_1}  
             
=& \frac{(2\mathsf {L}_o'+v-w)^2}{2\mathsf {L}_o'} + \frac{(2\mathsf {L}_1+2\mathsf {K}_{6}-2c-v+w+z)^2}{2\mathsf {L}_1} \nonumber \\
 = & 2\mathsf {K}_{4} + 2z + 2 (\mathsf {K}_{6} - c) + \frac{(v-w)^2}{2\mathsf {L}_o'}  + \frac{(z+w-v+2\mathsf {K}_{6}-2c)^2}{2\mathsf {L}_1} 
                         
 \nonumber \\
 \ge & 2\mathsf {K}_{4} + 2 z + \frac{(w-v)^2}{4\mathsf {L}_o'} + \frac{z^2}{8\mathsf {L}_1} \,.
\label{eq:quad-ineq}
\end{align}
Now,  setting $v:=(\widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5})^{\kappa_o}$,  or alternatively $x=a-2c+w+z$,  combining (\ref{eq:temp-bd}) with (\ref{eq:quad-ineq}),  results with
\begin{equation}\label{eq:riemann-sum}
\bar \mathbb{P}^{(\star)}_{z} ( \widehat{\mathcal{Q}}_{{\bf 0}}) 
\le \frac{C_{\mathsf {K}_{6}}}{3 \mathsf {K}_{4}} e^{-2\mathsf {K}_{4}} e^{-2z} e^{-\frac{z^2}{8\mathsf {K}_{4}}}
 \sum_{w} \frac{e^{-\frac{(w-v)^2}{4\mathsf {L}_o'}}}{\sqrt{4\pi \mathsf {L}_o'}} (w+z)  \,,
\end{equation}
where the sum is over all $w+z \in 2 \mathbb{Z}_+$.   For $\mathsf {L}_o' \gg 1$,  the sum in (\ref{eq:riemann-sum}) is
the Riemann sum approximation of
the expectation of $(W+z)_+$ for $W$ a $N(v,2\mathsf {L}_o')$ variable.  Since for $v,z \ge 0$ the latter expectation 
is at most $v+z+\sqrt{2\mathsf {L}_o'} \le 2z$ (since $z \ge \mathsf {K}_{4}^{{\kappa_1}} \ge \sqrt{2\mathsf {L}_o'} + (\widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5})^{\kappa_o}$),   
this completes the proof of (\ref{ubd-wQ}).

Turning to (\ref{ubd-Aell}),  increasing $\Delta$ by two has no effect on the bound (\ref{ubd-wQ}),  so 
             
we may and shall assume that  
                                                                        
$\ell \ge \mathsf {L}_o+\Delta+3$.  Then,  (\ref{ubd-wQ}) holds,  uniformly in $\ell$,  when replacing 
$\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}_{{\bf 0}}$ with 
\[
\mathcal{A}_{{\bf 0},\ell} \cap \{\eta_{{\bf 0},\ell-i} > \gamma_{-1}(\ell-i), i=1,2 \}
\subset \widehat{\mathcal{Q}}_{{\bf 0}} \,,
\] 
so by the Markov property of $j \mapsto \eta_{{\bf 0},j}$,  the bound (\ref{ubd-Aell}) follows upon showing 
that for $\mathsf {K}_{6}$ large,  all $\ell \in [\mathsf {L}_o+3,\mathsf {L}_o+\mathsf {L}_1]$ and $x^2, y^2 \in 2\mathbb{N}$,
\begin{align}
 \bar \mathbb{P}^{(\star)} \big( \eta_{{\bf 0},\ell-i} > \gamma_{-1}(\ell-i), i=1,2,
\eta_{{\bf 0},\ell}=y\,\big|\,
\eta_{{\bf 0},\ell-3}=x\big)
& \ge \frac{1}{4}  \,  q_3 (x,y) \, \quad  \forall x \in \mathsf{I}'_{\ell-3},  y \in \mathsf{I}'_\ell \,.
\label{eq:drop2-bar}
\end{align}
With $\mathsf {K}_{4}-\ell \ge \mathsf {K}_{6}$ large,   as in our proof of (\ref{ubd-wQ}) we can replace on 
both sides the point estimates at $y$,  by the interval $[y,y+2)$ and restrict to $y \in 2 \mathbb{N}$.   
Having done so,  here $\gamma_{-1}(\ell-1) \le \gamma_{-1}(\ell-2) < x \wedge y- u$
for $u=(x \wedge y)^{{\kappa_o}}$ (compare (\ref{dfn:gam}) and (\ref{dfn:Ip-sfJs})),  with the 
conditional probability on the {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} 
thus being at least $q_3^{(u)}(x,[y,y+2))$.  With $\mathsf {K}_{4}-\ell \ge \mathsf {K}_{6}$ large,  having both
$x \in \mathsf{I}'_{\ell-3}$ and $y \in \mathsf{I}'_\ell$ implies that $|x-y| \le (x \wedge y)^{{\kappa''}}$ and 
$u \ge u_o$ of part (a),  hence (\ref{eq:q3-bd}) yields the desired conclusion.

\noindent
(c).  Aiming at (\ref{eq:mom-bd-cent}),  we 
                                                                          
                                                                                                
                                                                                         
restrict (\ref{eq:new-p0}) hereafter to $x^2,y^2 \in 2 \mathbb{Z}_+$ such that 
$\frac{x-2 \widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5}}{\sqrt{\mathsf {L}_1}} \in [1,6]$ and
$\frac{y - 2\mathsf {K}_{6}}{\sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{6}}} \in [1,2]$,  whereby 
$q_{\mathsf {K}_{6}}(y,0) \ge c'_{\mathsf {K}_{6}} >0$ (see (\ref{eq:miss-ball})).
Recall from (\ref{dfn:Ip-sfJs}) and \Cref{dfn:Markov} that $q^{\Cap}_{\mathsf {J}^\star}(x,y)$ specifies having 
\begin{equation}\label{dfn:capq}
2 (\widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5} -\ell) + (\widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5}-\ell)^{{\kappa_o}} \le \eta_{{\bf 0},\mathsf {L}_o+\ell} \le
2 (\widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5} -\ell) + (\widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5}-\ell)^{{\kappa''}} \qquad \forall \ell \in [0,\mathsf {L}_1] \,.
\end{equation}
In the sequel we bound $q^{\Cap}_{\mathsf {J}^\star}(x,y)$ below,  using \cite[Theorem 1.1]{BRZ} 
                             
after showing that
\begin{align}\label{eq:fab-bd}
2 ( \widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5}-\ell) + (\widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5}-\ell)^{{\kappa_o}} &\le f_{a,b}(\ell;\mathsf {L}_1) +  \ell_{\mathsf {L}_1}^{{\kappa_o}}   \qquad \qquad \quad \forall \ell \in [0,\mathsf {L}_1] \,,
\end{align}
where $f_{a,b}(\ell;\mathsf {L}_1):=a+(b-a)\ell/\mathsf {L}_1$
                                                 
for $a:=2\widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5}+\widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5}^{{\kappa_o}}$,  $b:=2\mathsf {K}_{6} + \mathsf {K}_{6}^{{\kappa_o}} \gg 1$,  and further
(see \Cref{fig:EnlandFnl2}),  showing that for any $x,y$ as above,  
\begin{align}
 f_{x,y}(\ell;\mathsf {L}_1) + \widetilde{C} \ell_{\mathsf {L}_1}^{{\kappa'}} &\le 2(\widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5}-\ell)+(\widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5}-\ell)^{{\kappa''}}  \qquad \forall \ell \in [0,\mathsf {L}_1] \,.
\label{eq:fxy-bd}
\end{align}
To get (\ref{eq:fab-bd})-(\ref{eq:fxy-bd}),  first note that for $0<{\kappa_o}<\frac{1}{2}<{\kappa''}<1$ and all $\lambda,\varphi\in [0,1]$, 
\begin{align}\label{eq:fab-norm-bd}
(\varphi+\lambda)^{{\kappa_o}} &\le \lambda (\varphi+1)^{{\kappa_o}} + (1-\lambda) \varphi^{{\kappa_o}} +  (\lambda \wedge (1-\lambda))^{{\kappa_o}}\,,\\
\lambda + (1-\lambda) \varphi^{{\kappa''}} &\le (\varphi+\lambda)^{{\kappa''}} 
\label{eq:fxy-norm-bd}
\end{align}
(indeed $\lambda ( (\varphi+1)^{{\kappa_o}} - \varphi^{{\kappa_o}}) \ge 0$ and 
$(\varphi+\lambda)^{{\kappa_o}} \le \varphi^{\kappa_o} + \lambda^{\kappa_o}$ settle (\ref{eq:fab-norm-bd})
when $\lambda \le \frac{1}{2}$; otherwise increase its {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} to
$(\varphi+1)^{{\kappa_o}}$ and note that $(1-\lambda) ( (\varphi+1)^{{\kappa_o}} - \varphi^{{\kappa_o}}) 
\le (1-\lambda) \le (1-\lambda)^{{\kappa_o}})$.  Now,  fixing $\frac{1}{2} < {\kappa'} < (1-{\kappa_o}) \wedge {\kappa''}$,
