we get (\ref{eq:fab-bd}) after substituting $\varphi=\mathsf {K}_{6}/\mathsf {L}_1$,  $\lambda = 1-\ell/\mathsf {L}_1$ in (\ref{eq:fab-norm-bd}). 
Next,

consider (\ref{eq:fxy-bd}) for our largest
$x=2 \widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5} + 6 \sqrt{\mathsf {L}_1}$,  $y=2 \mathsf {K}_{6} + 2 \sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{6}}$ and
assuming $\mathsf {K}_{6}^{{\kappa''}-{\kappa'}} \ge \widetilde{C}+6$,  increase its {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} by noting that 
$\widetilde{C} \ell_{\mathsf {L}_1}^{{\kappa'}} \le \xi (\widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5}-\ell)^{{\kappa''}}$ for $\xi := \widetilde{C} \mathsf {K}_{6}^{{\kappa'}-{\kappa''}} \in (0,1)$. 
                                 
Subtract $\xi (\widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5}-\ell)^{{\kappa''}}$ from both sides,  using $2 \sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{6}} 
                     
\le 
(1-\xi) \mathsf {K}_{6}^{{\kappa''}}$ and $6 \sqrt{\mathsf {L}_1} 
                      
\le (1-\xi) \mathsf {L}_1^{{\kappa''}}$ 
and some calculations to reduce  (\ref{eq:fxy-bd}) to (\ref{eq:fxy-norm-bd}) 
with $\varphi=\mathsf {K}_{6}/\mathsf {L}_1$,  $\lambda = 1-\ell/\mathsf {L}_1$.

In view of (\ref{dfn:capq})-(\ref{eq:fxy-bd}),  
\[
q^{\Cap}_{\mathsf {J}^\star}(x,y) \ge \bar \mathbb{P}^{(\star)} \Big( \{ \eta_{{\bf 0},\mathsf {L}_o+\mathsf {L}_1}=y \}
\bigcap_{\ell \in [0,\mathsf {L}_1]} \{ 
 f_{a,b}(\ell;\mathsf {L}_1) +  \ell_{\mathsf {L}_1}^{{\kappa_o}} 
\le \eta_{{\bf 0},\mathsf {L}_o+\ell} \le
 f_{x,y}(\ell;\mathsf {L}_1) + \widetilde{C} \ell_{\mathsf {L}_1}^{{\kappa'}} \}
  \,  \big| \, \eta_{{\bf 0},\mathsf {L}_o}=x\Big) 
\]
and summing over the possible values of $y$,  we deduce from 
\cite[(1.2)]{BRZ} (at $\eta=3$, $C=\delta=1$, $\varepsilon={\kappa'}-\frac{1}{2}$ and $\widetilde{C}$ as needed),
that for some $c>0$,
                                      
\begin{equation}\label{eq:BRZ-1.2}
\sum_y q^{\Cap}_{\mathsf {J}^\star}(x,y) \ge
6 \,  c  \sum_y \frac{(1+x-a)(1+y-b)}{\mathsf {L}_1}\sqrt{\frac{x}{y \mathsf {L}_1}} e^{-\frac{(x-y)^2}{2\mathsf {L}_1}} 
\ge \frac{c\,  z}{\mathsf {K}_{4}} e^{-\frac{x^2}{2\mathsf {L}_1}} 
\end{equation}
(indeed $\mathsf {L}_1^{-1/2} \ge \mathsf {K}_{4}^{-1/2} \ge \frac{z}{3 \mathsf {K}_{4}}$ and 
for $\mathsf {K}_{6}$ large,  our $x,y$ satisfy
$x \in [2\mathsf {L}_1,3\mathsf {L}_1]$,  $y -b \ge \frac{\sqrt{y}}{\sqrt{3}}$,  $x -a \ge \frac{\sqrt{\mathsf {L}_1}}{2}$).  
Similarly to (\ref{eq:q3-bd-alt}),  note that $q_{\, \mathsf {L}_o}(2\mathsf {K}_{4}+z,x)= \mathbb{P}(S_m = x^2/2)$
for the sum $S_m=S^{(\mathsf {L}_o)}_m$ of $m:=\frac{1}{2}(2\mathsf {K}_{4}+z)^2$ {\sc\lowercase{iid}} variables $\{\mathsf {G}'_i\}$
as in (\ref{dfn:GJp}),  having here $q:=\frac{1}{\mathsf {L}_o+1}$.  It thus follows from 
(\ref{eq:new-p0}) and the range of $x$ for which we derived (\ref{eq:BRZ-1.2}) that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:pre-pz}
\bar \mathbb{P}^{(\star)}_z(\mathcal{A}_{{\bf 0}}) \ge c'_{\mathsf {K}_{6}}  \frac{c z}{\mathsf {K}_{4}}  
\mathbb{E} \Big[ e^{-S_m/\mathsf {L}_1}; \sqrt{\mathsf {L}_1} \le \sqrt{2 S_m} - 2\widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5} \le 6 \sqrt{\mathsf {L}_1} \,  \Big] \,.
\end{equation}
Now,  for all large $\mathsf {K}_{5}$ and $2 \sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}} \le z \le 4\sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}}$,
\[
\frac{m}{\mathsf {L}_1+\mathsf {L}_o} = \frac{(2\mathsf {K}_{4}+z)^2}{2(\mathsf {K}_{4}-\mathsf {K}_{6})} 
= 2 \mathsf {K}_{4} + 2z + 2 \mathsf {K}_{6} + \frac{(z+2\mathsf {K}_{6})^2}{2(\mathsf {K}_{4}-\mathsf {K}_{6})}\,,
\]
with the right-most term uniformly bounded,  and in addition
\[
\Big[ \sqrt{2m - m^{3/4}},\sqrt{2m+m^{3/4}}\,\Big] \subset 
\Big[\sqrt{2m} - \frac{m^{1/4}}{\sqrt{2}},\sqrt{2m} + \frac{m^{1/4}}{\sqrt{2}}\Big]
\subset \big[2 \widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5} + \sqrt{\mathsf {L}_1}, 2\widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5} + 6 \sqrt{\mathsf {L}_1} \,  \big] \,.
\]
Thus,  in view of (\ref{eq:pre-pz}),  we get (\ref{eq:mom-bd-cent}) upon showing that for some  
$c>0$ and all $\mathsf {K}_{5}$ large,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:pz-alt}
\mathbb{E} \Big[ e^{-S_m/\mathsf {L}_1}; |S_m - m| \le  \frac{1}{2} m^{3/4} \Big] \ge c \,  e^{-m/(\mathsf {L}_1+\mathsf {L}_o)} \,.
\end{equation}
Turning to (\ref{eq:pz-alt}),  with $\Lambda_q(\lambda)$ as in (\ref{def:q-cgf}) and 
$\widetilde{S}_m$ the partial sum of the {\sc\lowercase{iid}} variables $\{\widetilde{\mathsf {G}}_i\}$ such that 
\[
\mathbb{P}(\widetilde{\mathsf {G}}_i=k) = e^{-k/\mathsf {L}_1} e^{-\Lambda_q(1/\mathsf {L}_1)} \mathbb{P}(\mathsf {G}'_i = k),  \qquad \forall k \ge 0 \,,
\]
we have by Radon-Nikodym theorem that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rnd}
\mathbb{E} \Big[ e^{-S_m/\mathsf {L}_1}; |S_m - m| \le  \frac{1}{2} m^{3/4} \Big] = 
\mathbb{P}\Big( |\widetilde{S}_m - m| \le  \frac{1}{2} m^{3/4} \Big) e^{m \Lambda_q(1/\mathsf {L}_1)} 
\end{equation}
With $\widetilde{\mathsf {L}}:=(1-e^{-1/\mathsf {L}_1})^{-1} \ge \mathsf {L}_1$,  substituting $q^{-1}=\mathsf {L}_o+1$
in (\ref{def:q-cgf}),  we find that for $\mathsf {L}_1,\mathsf {L}_o \ge 1$, 
\[
m \Lambda_q(1/\mathsf {L}_1) = m \log \Big( 1 - \frac{1}{\widetilde{\mathsf {L}}+ \mathsf {L}_o} \Big)  \ge  m \log \Big( 1 - \frac{1}{\mathsf {L}_1 + \mathsf {L}_o} \Big) \ge 
-\frac{m}{\mathsf {L}_1+\mathsf {L}_o} - \frac{m}{(\mathsf {L}_1+\mathsf {L}_o)^2} \,.
\]
The right-most term is at least $-8$ when $\mathsf {K}_{4} \ge 4+ 8 \mathsf {K}_{6}$,  so by 
(\ref{eq:rnd}) it suffices for (\ref{eq:pz-alt}) to show that 
\[
\mathbb{P}\Big( |\widetilde{S}_m - m| >  \frac{1}{2} m^{3/4} \Big) \le \frac{1}{2} \,,
\]
which by Markov's inequality is a consequence of having
\begin{equation}\label{eq:var-mean-wtG}
{\rm var}[\widetilde{\mathsf {G}}_i]  
= \Lambda_q''(\frac{1}{\mathsf {L}_1}) 
= O(\mathsf {L}_o) 
\le \frac{1}{16} \sqrt{m} \quad \text{and} \quad 
1- \mathbb{E} [\widetilde{\mathsf {G}}_i] = \Lambda'_q(1/\mathsf {L}_1) - \Lambda_q'(0) = O(\mathsf {L}_o/\mathsf {L}_1) 
                                                                   
\le \frac{1}{4} m^{-1/4} \,.
\end{equation}
           
(d).  With $I_x:=[x,x+1)$,  we have that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:wQs-off}
\bar \mathbb{P}^{(\star)}_{z} ( \widehat{\mathcal{Q}}_{\mathsf{v}}) = \sum_{x=0}^\infty
\bar \mathbb{P}^{(\star)}_{z} ( \widehat{\mathcal{Q}}_{\mathsf{v}},  \eta_{\mathsf{v},\mathsf {L}_o} \in I_x) 
:= \sum_{x=0}^{\infty} p_\mathsf{v}(z,x).
\end{equation} 
By rotation symmetry, 
$p_{\mathsf{v}}(z,x) = p_{\rho}(z,x)$ depends only on 
$\rho:= \|\mathsf{v}\| \le \mathsf {K}_{5}^{-5}$.  
                                      
We are in the unconditional setting of \Cref{rmk:off-center-applies} for $R_1=R=e^{-2}$ and 
$\mathsf{s}=m=\bar \mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}_{4}}(z) \le 3 \mathsf {K}_{4}^2$ independent planar Brownian excursions.
The event we consider 
                               
$\Gamma:=\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}_{\mathsf{v}} \cap \{ \eta_{\mathsf{v},\mathsf {L}_o} \in I_x \}$ is in $\mathcal{N}_{\mathsf{v},r,m,k}$ 
for $r=e^{-(\mathsf {L}_o+3)}$ and $k=\frac{1}{2} (x+1)^2$.  
                                                                           
We thus have by 
(\ref{eq:off-center-bd}),  that for all large enough $\mathsf {K}_{5}$ and $x \le \mathsf {K}_{5}^{2}$ 
the joint probability $\mathbb{Q}_R^{m,{\bf 0}} (\Gamma)$ 
is at most $2 (\mathbb{P}_R^{1})^m(\Gamma)$ (regardless of the starting points of our excursions),
and hence $p_\rho(z,x) \le 2 p_0(z,x)$ for any such $x$.
Further,  the probability of hitting a ball of radius $r_{\mathsf {K}_{4}+1}$ 
during one Brownian excursion between concentric balls of radii 
$r_{\mathsf {L}_o}$ and $r_{\mathsf {L}_o-1}$ is,  uniformly in the starting and ending points of such excursion,  
at least $2c/\mathsf {K}_{5}$ for some $c=c(\Delta)>0$.
The probability that at least $\frac{1}{2} (\mathsf {K}_{5}^2)^2$ such excursions miss this small ball
is thus at most $e^{-c \,  \mathsf {K}_{5}^3}$,  resulting in view of (\ref{eq:wQs-off}) with 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bd-hQv}
\bar \mathbb{P}^{(\star)}_{z} ( \widehat{\mathcal{Q}}_{\mathsf{v}}) \le  2 \sum_{x=0}^{\infty} p_0 (z,x) + e^{-c \,  \mathsf {K}_{5}^3} = 
2 \bar \mathbb{P}^{(\star)}_{z} ( \widehat{\mathcal{Q}}_{{\bf 0}}) + e^{-c \,  \mathsf {K}_{5}^3} \,,
\end{equation}
thereby extending the validity of (\ref{ubd-wQ}) to all $\|\mathsf{v}\| \le \mathsf {K}_{5}^{-5}$.  Applying such 
reasoning with $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v},\ell}$ instead of $\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}_{\mathsf{v}}$
extends (\ref{ubd-Aell}) from $\mathcal{A}_{{\bf 0},\ell}$ 
to $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v},\ell}$ (uniformly in $\mathsf{v}$ and $\ell \in \mathsf {J}^\star$),  while considering 
instead $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v}}$ shows that the much larger than 
$e^{-c \mathsf {K}_{5}^3}$ lower bound of (\ref{eq:mom-bd-cent}) extends to  
$\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v}}$,  uniformly over $\|\mathsf{v}\| \le \mathsf {K}_{5}^{-5}$.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
Here $\|\mathsf{v}\| \le r_{\mathsf {L}} \le \mathsf {K}_{5}^{-5}$,  so with $|\mathbb{F}^{\bf 0}| = |\mathbb{F}^{\star}| \le e^{2\mathsf {K}_{5}}/(2 \widetilde{c}^2)$,  it
follows from (\ref{dfn:g4-alt}),  (\ref{eq:A-RU-Q-hatQ}),
the union bound and \Cref{lem:g4-cnc},  that for any $z \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_4$
\[
g_{\mathsf {K}_{4}}(z) \le  \frac{e^{2 \mathsf {K}_{4}}}{2 \, \widetilde{c}^2}  \max\big\{ \bar \mathbb{P}^{(\star)}_{z} ( \widehat{\mathcal{Q}}_{\mathsf{v}}) \,:\,
\| \mathsf{v} \|  \le \mathsf {K}_{5}^{-5} \big\} 
\le   C(\mathsf {K}_{6}) \frac{z}{\mathsf {K}_{4}} e^{- 2 z}  e^{-\frac{z^2}{8 \mathsf {K}_{4}}} 
\]
as stated in (\ref{ubd2-g4}).  

Next,  consider the sub-lattice $\mathbb{F}' \subset \mathbb{F}^{{\bf 0}}$ obtained when up-scaling the cell-size parameter $\widetilde{c}$ of
$\mathbb{F}^\star$,  see (\ref{dfn:F-star}),  to be $\widetilde{c} := \sqrt{2} e e^{\mathsf {K}'_{6}}$ for some $\mathsf {K}'_{6}  \ge \mathsf {K}_{6} + 6 \log \mathsf {K}_{6}$,
denoting by $N_z$ the number of events $\{\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v}},  \mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F}'\}$ of (\ref{def:whcI}) that occur 
under $\bar \mathbb{P}^{(\star)}_z$ when defining $\mathsf {J}^\star$ with $\Delta=0$.  
Recall (\ref{eq:A-RU-Q-hatQ}) that $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v}}\subset \mathcal{R}\mathcal{U}^{(\star)}_\mathsf{v}$ so fixing $z \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_4$ 
with $z \in [2 \sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}},4 \sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}}]$,  it suffices for (\ref{eq:lbd-alpha}),  see (\ref{dfn:g4-alt}),  to show that both
\begin{equation}\label{eq:lbd-Av}
\mathbb{P}(N_z \ge 1) \ge c(\mathsf {K}_{6}) \frac{z}{\mathsf {K}_{4}} e^{-2 \mathsf {L}} e^{-2 z} 
\end{equation}
and for some $c>0$, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ubd-eta-L}
\bar \mathbb{P}^{(\star)}_{z} (\eta_{{\bf 0},\mathsf {L}} \ge 3 \mathsf {K}_{5}) \le e^{-c \,  \mathsf {K}_{5}} 
\end{equation}
(uniformly in $\mathsf {K}_{5}$ and $z$ as above).  To this end,  first note that the {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of (\ref{eq:ubd-eta-L}) is 
precisely the probability that the sum $S_m^{(\mathsf {L})}$ of $m \le 3 \mathsf {K}_{5}^2$ {\sc\lowercase{iid}} variables $\mathsf {G}'_i$
of the form (\ref{dfn:GJp}) at $q=\frac{1}{\mathsf {L}+1}$,  exceeds $\frac{9}{2} \mathsf {K}_{5}^2$.  Now, 
from  (\ref{def:q-cgf}) we get by elementary algebra that for any $\mathsf {L} \ge 1$ and 
$0 \le \lambda \le \frac{1}{2 \mathsf {L}}$,  
\[
\log \mathbb{E}\Big[e^{\lambda \big(S_m^{(\mathsf {L})}-m\big)}\Big] 
= m \big( \Lambda_q(-\lambda) - \lambda \big) \le 3 \lambda^2 \mathsf {L}  m \,.
\]
The probability in (\ref{eq:ubd-eta-L}) is thus at most $\exp(-\frac{c}{\mathsf {L}} \, \mathsf {K}_{5}^2)$ for some $c>0$
($\lambda=\frac{1}{12 \mathsf {L}}$ gives $c=\frac{1}{16}$),   as claimed.  

Turning to (\ref{eq:lbd-Av}),  compare $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v},\ell}$ of (\ref{def:Aell}) with 
\begin{align}\label{def:A-ell-ellp} 
\bar \mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v},\ell'} &:= \{ \eta_{\mathsf{v},\ell'} \in \mathsf{I}'_{\ell'},  \eta_{\mathsf{v},\mathsf {K}_{4}} = 0 \} \,,   \qquad \ell':=\ell+5 \log (\mathsf {K}_{4}-\ell) \,, 
\end{align}
noting that 
\[
\ell \in [\mathsf {L}+2,\mathsf {K}_{4}-\mathsf {K}'_{6}] \quad \Longrightarrow  \quad \ell' \in \mathsf {J}^\star,  \quad \text{hence}
\quad \mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v}} \subset \mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v},\ell} \subset  \bar \mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v},\ell'}  \quad \forall \mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F}' \,.
\]
Further,  by construction
\begin{equation}\label{def:Gell}
\mathbb{G}'_{\ell}  :=  \left\{ (\mathsf{v},\mathsf{v}') \in (\mathbb{F}')^2 : 0 < 2 r_{\ell-1} \le \mathsf{d}(\mathsf{v},\mathsf{v}') < 2 r_{\ell-2}\right\}
\end{equation}
is empty except for $\ell \in [\mathsf {L} +2, \mathsf {K}_{4}-\mathsf {K}'_{6}]$,  so we establish 
(\ref{eq:lbd-Av}) by utilizing the bound
\begin{align}
\mathbb{P}(N_z \ge 1) &\ge \;\;\;\;  \mathbb{E}[N_z] \quad  \; - \;  \mathbb{E}[N_z (N_z-1)] \nonumber \\
 \ge |\mathbb{F}'| & \inf_{\mathsf{v} \in  \mathbb{F}'} \{ \bar \mathbb{P}^{(\star)}_{z} (\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v}}) \}
- \sum_{\ell=\mathsf {L}+2}^{\mathsf {K}_{4}-\mathsf {K}'_{6}} |\mathbb{G}'_\ell| \sup_{(\mathsf{v},\mathsf{v}') \in \mathbb{G}_\ell} \{ \bar \mathbb{P}^{(\star)}_z 
(\bar \mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v},\ell'} \cap \mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v}',\ell}) \} 
\label{eq:lbd-Ny}
\end{align}
(with $\mathbb{G}_\ell$ as in (\ref{def:Gell}),  except for considering all $\mathsf{v},\mathsf{v}' \in \mathbb{F}^{\bf 0}$).
Indeed,  in the sequel we show that for large $\mathsf {K}_{6}$,  some $C_1(\mathsf {K}_{6})<\infty$,  all $\mathsf {K}_{5} \gg \mathsf {K}_{6}$ 
                                                                        
and $z$,  $\ell$ as above,  
                                                                            
                                                                        
\begin{align}\label{eq:2mom-ubd}
e^{2 (\mathsf {K}_{4}-\ell)} 
\sup_{(\mathsf{v},  \mathsf{v}') \in \mathbb{G}_\ell} \big\{ \bar \mathbb{P}_z^{(\star)} (\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v}',\ell} \cap  \bar \mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v},\ell'} ) \big\} & \le 
C_1(\mathsf {K}_{6}) \frac{z}{\mathsf {K}_{4}} e^{-2 \mathsf {K}_{4}} e^{-2 z}  e^{-\frac{1}{4}(\mathsf {K}_{4}-\ell)^{{\kappa_o}}}\,.
\end{align}
Further,  $|\mathbb{F}'| \ge c\,  e^{2 (\mathsf {K}_{5}-\mathsf {K}'_{6})}$ and $|\mathbb{G}'_{\ell}| \le c^{-1} e^{2 (\mathsf {K}_{5}-\mathsf {K}'_{6})} e^{2 (\mathsf {K}_{4}-\ell-\mathsf {K}'_{6})}$ 
for some $c>0$ (with at most $c' e^{2 (\mathsf {K}_{4}-\mathsf {K}'_{6})}$ points of $\mathbb{F}'$ per unit area,  clearly 
$\sup_{\mathsf{v}} | \mathbb{F}' \cap \mathbb{B}(\mathsf{v},  2 r_{\ell-2})| \le c^{-1}  e^{2 (\mathsf {K}_{4}- \mathsf {K}'_{6})} r_{\ell-2}^{2}$).  
Plugging in (\ref{eq:lbd-Ny}) those estimates, 
the lower bound (\ref{eq:mom-bd-cent}) (which holds throuhgout $\mathbb{F}'$,  see \Cref{lem:g4-cnc}(d)),  
and the upper bound of (\ref{eq:2mom-ubd}),  we get (\ref{eq:lbd-Av}) 
upon considering $\mathsf {K}'_{6}$ large enough.




Turning to show (\ref{eq:2mom-ubd}),  recalling the $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_\ell$ 
which excludes only the 
                                       
excursions from $\partial \mathbb{B}(\mathsf{v},r_\ell)$ to $\partial\mathbb{B} (\mathsf{v},r_{\ell-1})$ (see \Cref{def:Fvjs}),
we claim that for some $C<\infty$,  any relevant $\ell$ and $\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F}^{\bf 0}$, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Jay-alpha}
\mathbb{P}(\bar \mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v},\ell'} \, |\, \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_\ell) \le C e^{-2 (\mathsf {K}_{4}-\ell')} e^{-(\mathsf {K}_{4}-\ell')^{{\kappa_o}}} 
\le C e^{-2 (\mathsf {K}_{4}-\ell)} e^{-\frac{1}{2}(\mathsf {K}_{4}-\ell)^{{\kappa_o}}} \,.
\end{equation}
Indeed,  for $\mathsf {K}_{6} \ge c_{{\kappa_o}}$ the second inequality is a trivial consequence of having 
$\ell'-\ell=5 \log (\mathsf {K}_{4}-\ell)$ and $\mathsf {K}_{4} -\ell \ge \mathsf {K}_{4}-\ell' \ge \mathsf {K}_{6}$.  For the first inequality,  
we set $T_{\ell'}^{\mathsf{v},\ell,\widetilde{m}}$
                                                                          
for the number of traversals $\partial \mathbb{B} (\mathsf{v}, r_{\ell'})\to\partial \mathbb{B} (\mathsf{v},r_{\ell'-1})$ 
accumulated within the first $\widetilde{m}$ such traversals $\partial \mathbb{B} (\mathsf{v}, r_{\ell-1})\to\partial \mathbb{B} (\mathsf{v},r_{\ell})$,
with $T_{\mathsf {K}_{4}}^{\mathsf{v},\ell',m'}$ defined analogously (see also \Cref{def-trav}).   Equipped with this 
notation and that of (\ref{def:why}),  we re-write the events of (\ref{def:A-ell-ellp}),  as
\begin{align*}
\bar \mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v},\ell'}
& =
\! \bigcup_{\widetilde{m}} \! \bigcup_{m' \in \mathsf{I}^{\mathsf {T}}_{\ell'}} \! \{ \ensuremath{T_{\mathsf{v},r_{\ell}\to r_{\ell-1}}^{{\bf 0},e^{-2}\overset{m}{\to}e^{-1}} }
                                    
 = \widetilde{m}, 
  T_{\ell'}^{\mathsf{v},\ell,\widetilde{m}} = m',   T_{\mathsf {K}_{4}}^{\mathsf{v},\ell',m'} = 0  \},
\end{align*} 
where $\mathsf{I}^{\mathsf {T}}_j :=\{ m' \in \mathbb{N}: \sqrt{2m'} \in \mathsf{I}'_j \}$.  Here
                                
$(1+ 50 (\ell'-\ell) e^{-(\ell'-\ell)})^{m'}
\le C$ for some $C<\infty$ and all $m' \in \mathsf{I}^{\mathsf {T}}_{\ell'}$ (by our choice of $\ell$,  $\ell'$).  Noting that 
$\ensuremath{T_{\mathsf{v},r_{\ell}\to r_{\ell-1}}^{{\bf 0},e^{-2}\overset{m}{\to}e^{-1}} }$ and the start and end points of all excursions from 
$\partial \mathbb{B}(\mathsf{v},r_{\ell})$ to $\partial \mathbb{B}(\mathsf{v},r_{\ell-1})$,  are 
measurable on $\mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_\ell$,  we thus deduce in view of \cite[Lemma 9.1]{BRZ2},  that 
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{P}(\bar \mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v},\ell'} \, |\, \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_\ell)
                                                                                          
                                                                                                                              
& \le C 
\sum_{\widetilde{m}} {\bf 1}_{\{\ensuremath{T_{\mathsf{v},r_{\ell}\to r_{\ell-1}}^{{\bf 0},e^{-2}\overset{m}{\to}e^{-1}} }=\widetilde{m}\}} 
\sum_{m' \in \mathsf{I}^{\mathsf {T}}_{\ell'}} \mathbb{P}(T_{\ell'}^{\mathsf{v},\ell,\widetilde{m}} = m'  \, |\, \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_\ell) \mathbb{P}(T_{\mathsf {K}_{4}}^{\mathsf{v},\ell',m'} = 0 ) \\
&\le C \sup_{m' \in \mathsf{I}^{\mathsf {T}}_{\ell'}} \{ \mathbb{P}(T_{\mathsf {K}_{4}}^{\mathsf{v},\ell',m'} = 0 ) \} = C \sup_{m' \in \mathsf{I}^{\mathsf {T}}_{\ell'}}
\big(1-\frac{1}{\mathsf {K}_{4}-\ell'+1}\big)^{m'}.
\end{align*}
Since any $m' \in \mathsf{I}^{\mathsf {T}}_{\ell'}$ is at least $\frac{1}{2} (2 (\mathsf {K}_{4}-\ell') + (\mathsf {K}_{4}-\ell')^{{\kappa_o}})^2$,  
the first inequality of (\ref{eq:Jay-alpha}) follows by elementary algebra.
Further,  for any $(\mathsf{v},\mathsf{v}') \in \mathbb{G}_\ell$, 
\[
\mathbb{B}(\mathsf{v},r_{\ell-1}) \subset \mathbb{B}(\mathsf{v}',r_{\ell-3}) 
\setminus \mathbb{B}(\mathsf{v}',r_{\ell-1}) \subset \mathbb{B}({\bf 0},1),
\] 
hence $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v}',\ell}$ is measurable on $\mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\ell}$.  In particular,  
\[
\bar \mathbb{P}_z^{(\star)} (\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v}',\ell} \cap  \bar \mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v},\ell'} ) = 
\bar \mathbb{E}_z^{(\star)} \big[ \mathbb{P}( \bar \mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v},\ell'} | \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\ell} ) ; \mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v}',\ell} \big] \le 
\| \mathbb{P}( \bar \mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v},\ell'} | \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\ell} ) \|_\infty \bar \mathbb{P}_z^{(\star)} (\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v}',\ell} )
\]
and we get (\ref{eq:2mom-ubd}) by combining (\ref{eq:Jay-alpha}) with 
our uniform bound on $\bar \mathbb{P}_z^{(\star)} (\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{v}',\ell} )$ (see \Cref{lem:g4-cnc}(d)).
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{lem:angle-diff} 
Fix $\mu \in M_1([-\pi,\pi))$ such that $\frac{d \mu}{d\theta} \ge c^{-1}$ for some $c$ finite.  Then
for any $\nu \in M_1([-\pi,\pi))$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:quantiles}
\mathsf{d}_\infty(\nu,\mu) \le c\,  \mathsf{d}_{\rm KS}(\nu,\mu),  \quad {\rm where}
 \quad \mathsf{d}_{\rm KS}(\nu,\mu):= \|\nu([-\pi,\cdot])-\mu([-\pi,\cdot])\|_\infty 
\end{equation}
{denotes the Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance}.  In particular,  {for discrete quantile measures}
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ds-emp}
                  
L_m^\mu := \frac{1}{m} \sum_{q=1}^m \delta_{\mu^{-1}(q/m)} \in \mathbb{B}^{\infty}_{\mu}(c/m) ,
\end{equation}
and we have that for the empirical measure $L_{\mu}(\mathsf{s})$ of $\mathsf{s} \ge 1$ {\sc\lowercase{iid}} samples from $\mu$,
\begin{equation}\label{lbl:d-inf-bd}
\mathbb{P} \big( \mathsf{d}_\infty (\mu, L_{\mu}(\mathsf{s})) > \frac{c u}{\sqrt{\mathsf{s}}} \big) \le 2 e^{-2 u^2} \,, 
\qquad \forall u > 0 \,.
\end{equation}
Moreover,  for such $\mu$,  any $\boldsymbol{\eta},\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\eta}} \ge 0$,  $\widetilde{m} -m  \in [0, \widetilde{\boldsymbol{\eta}} \,  m]$ and
$\{\theta_q,  {1 \le q \le \widetilde{m}} \} \subset [-\pi,\pi)$, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:dinf-comp}
L_{m} := \frac{1}{m} \sum_{q=1}^m \delta_{\theta_q} 
 \in  \mathbb{B}^{\infty}_{\mu}(\boldsymbol{\eta})
\;\; \Longrightarrow \;\; L_{\widetilde{m}} \in \mathbb{B}^{\infty}_{\mu}\big(\boldsymbol{\eta}+ c \,  \widetilde{\boldsymbol{\eta}} \big) \,.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
With $\frac{d \mu}{d\theta} \ge c^{-1}$,  setting $h =c \,  \mathsf{d}_{\rm KS}(\nu,\mu)$ yields by the definition 
of $\mathsf{d}_{\rm KS}(\cdot)$,  that for any $\theta \in [-\pi,\pi)$,
\begin{align*}
 \mu([-\pi,\theta-h])  
                                                                    
 \le  \mu([-\pi,\theta]) - \mathsf{d}_{\rm KS}(\nu,\mu)  \le \nu([-\pi,\theta]) 
                            
 &\le  \mu([-\pi,\theta]) + \mathsf{d}_{\rm KS}(\nu,\mu) 
                                                                   
 \le \mu([-\pi,\theta+h]) \,.
\end{align*}
This implies that $\mathsf{d}_\infty(\nu,\mu) \le h$  (see  \cite[Thm. 2.12]{BL19}),  as stated in (\ref{eq:quantiles}).
By definition,  $\mathsf{d}_{\rm KS}(L_m^\mu,\mu) \le \frac{1}{m}$,  so plugging 
$\nu = L_m^\mu$ in (\ref{eq:quantiles}) results with (\ref{eq:ds-emp}).  Moreover, 
applying (\ref{eq:quantiles}) for $\nu=L_{\mu}(\mathsf{s})$,  we see that (\ref{lbl:d-inf-bd}) 
follows from the Dvoretsky-Kiefer-Wolfowitz inequality
\begin{equation}\label{eq:dkw}
\mathbb{P} \big( \mathsf{d}_{\rm KS} (\mu, L_{\mu}(\mathsf{s})) > \frac{u}{\sqrt{\mathsf{s}}} \big) \le 2 e^{-2 u^2} 
\qquad \forall u > 0 
\end{equation}
(see \cite{Massart} for a proof of (\ref{eq:dkw})). 

Next,  with $\widetilde{m}\geq m$, let $\theta_{(i)}$, $i=1,\ldots,m$  and $\widetilde{\theta}_{(i)}$, $i=1,\ldots,\widetilde{m}$
denote the order statistics of
$\{\theta_q\}_{q\in [m]}$ and  $\{\theta_q\}_{q\in[\widetilde{m}]}$,  that is $\{\theta_q\}_{q\in[m]}=\{\theta_{(q)}\}_{q\in [m]}$
and
 $\{\theta_q\}_{q\in[\widetilde{m}]}=\{\widetilde{\theta}_{(q)}\}_{q\in [\widetilde{m}]}$,  with
\[
                              
 \{ \theta_{(0)} \le \cdots \le \theta_{(m)} \} \,,  \quad
                                     
\{ \widetilde{\theta}_{(0)} \le  \cdots \le \widetilde{\theta}_{(\widetilde{m})} \} \,,
                                                                                  
                                                                                                 
\]
where for convenience we set  $\theta_{(0)}=\widetilde{\theta}_{(0)}=-\pi$.  {Adopting the convention 
of $\theta_{(q)}=\pm \,  \pi$ when $q>m$ or $q<0$,  respectively,  necessarily}
$\theta_{(q-(\widetilde{m}-m))} \le \widetilde{\theta}_{(q)} \le \theta_{(q)}$ for all $q \in [\widetilde{m}]$.  Taking
$q = [t \widetilde{m}]$ and noting that $1 \le \frac{\widetilde{m}}{m} \le  1+ \widetilde{\boldsymbol{\eta}}$,  {this} implies that for all $t \in [0,1]$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:order-th}
(L_{m})^{-1}(t-\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\eta}}) \le (L_m)^{-1}(\frac{q}{m} - \widetilde{\boldsymbol{\eta}}) \le (L_{\widetilde m})^{-1}(t) \le (L_m)^{-1}(\frac{q}{m})
\le (L_{m})^{-1}(t+\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\eta}}) \,.
\end{equation}
Since $\| \mu^{-1} \|_{\rm Lip} \le c$,  see \cite[{display following} (5.7) \& Cor.5.12(d)]{BL19},  
combine (\ref{eq:order-th}) with our assumption {in (\ref{eq:dinf-comp})} that $\mathsf{d}_\infty(L_{m},\mu) \le \boldsymbol{\eta}$,  to get
in view of  (\ref{dfn:dsup}),  that for all $t \in [0,1]$
\[
-\boldsymbol{\eta} - c\,  \widetilde{\boldsymbol{\eta}} + \mu^{-1} (t) \le 
-\boldsymbol{\eta} + \mu^{-1}(t-\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\eta}}) \le (L_{\widetilde m})^{-1}(t) \le \boldsymbol{\eta} + \mu^{-1}(t+\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\eta}}) \le 
\boldsymbol{\eta} + c \,  \widetilde{\boldsymbol{\eta}} + \mu^{-1}(t)
\,,
\]
as claimed in (\ref{eq:dinf-comp}).
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{lem-coupb}
For some $C<\infty$,  any $r<e^{-1}$,  $|\mathsf{u}|=e r$,  $\mathsf{z}'=r e^{i \theta'}$ and 
$\mathsf{z} = r e^{i \theta} \in \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{z}',r/(2e))$,
\[
\mathsf{d}_{\rm TV}(\zeta_{\mathsf{z}},\zeta_{\mathsf{z}'}) \le \frac{C}{r} |\mathsf{z}-\mathsf{z}'| \le C |\theta - \theta'| \,,
\]
where $\zeta_{\mathsf{z}}$ denotes the first hitting point on $\partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{z}',r/e)$ 
by a Brownian path started at $\mathsf{z}$ and conditioned to exit $\mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}({\bf 0},e \, r)$ 
at the given point $\mathsf{u}$ (with $\zeta_{\mathsf{z}'}$ corresponding to $\mathsf{z}=\mathsf{z}'$).
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
The right-inequality being trivial,
                                                                                  
we only prove the left one.  Further,
being confined to $\mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}({\bf 0},1)$, we can replace {\sc\lowercase{wlog}} the unit torus 
$\mathbb{T}^2$ by $\mathbb{R}^2$ and thereby, using Brownian scaling, fix {\sc\lowercase{wlog}} $r=1$. 
Having done so, we abbreviate $\mathbb{B}:=\mathbb{B}(\mathsf{z}',1/e)$ and
let $f_{\mathsf{z}}(\cdot)$ and $f_{\mathsf{z}'}(\cdot)$ denote the normalized densities 
of $\zeta_{\mathsf{z}}$ and $\zeta_{\mathsf{z}'}$ with respect to a unit surface measure on $\partial \mathbb{B}$. 
Denoting by $q$ the Poisson kernel for the exit density of $\mathbb{B}$ 
and by $p$ the corresponding kernel for
exit density of $\mathbb{B}({\bf 0}, e)$, we have that   
\begin{equation}\label{10.11}
f_{\mathsf{z}'}(\mathsf{x})=\frac{q (\mathsf{z}',\mathsf{x})\, p (\mathsf{x},\mathsf{u})}{p (\mathsf{z}',\mathsf{u})}\,, \qquad
f_{\mathsf{z}}(\mathsf{x})=\frac{q(\mathsf{z},\mathsf{x}) p (\mathsf{x},\mathsf{u})}{p(\mathsf{z},\mathsf{u})} \,.
\end{equation}
From these identities we get that
\begin{align}\label{10.12new}
 \mathsf{d}_{\rm TV}(\zeta_{\mathsf{z}},\zeta_{\mathsf{z}'})
 &= \frac{1}{2} \int_{\partial \mathbb{B}} | f_{\mathsf{z}'}(\mathsf{x}) - f_{\mathsf{z}}(\mathsf{x}) | d\mathsf{x} \nonumber \\
& \le \frac{1}{2} \int_{\partial \mathbb{B}} \big|  \frac{p (\mathsf{z}',\mathsf{u})}{p (\mathsf{z},\mathsf{u})} - 1 \big| f_{\mathsf{z}'} (\mathsf{x}) d\mathsf{x} 
+ \int_{\partial \mathbb{B}} \big| 1 - \frac{q(\mathsf{z}',\mathsf{x})}{q(\mathsf{z},\mathsf{x})} \big|  f_{\mathsf{z}} (\mathsf{x}) d\mathsf{x} \nonumber \\
 & \le  \frac{1}{2} \Big|  \frac{p (\mathsf{z}',\mathsf{u})}{p (\mathsf{z},\mathsf{u})} - 1 \Big| + \frac{1}{2} \sup_{\mathsf{x} \in \partial \mathbb{B}}
\Big| 1 - \frac{q(\mathsf{z}',\mathsf{x})}{q(\mathsf{z},\mathsf{x})} \Big| \,.
\end{align}
Now, since $|\mathsf{z}|=|\mathsf{z}'|$, we have from (\ref{dfn:Poiss}) that 
\begin{equation}
\frac{p (\mathsf{z}',\mathsf{u})}{p (\mathsf{z},\mathsf{u})} - 1 = \frac{ |\mathsf{z}-\mathsf{u}|^{2}}{|\mathsf{z}'-\mathsf{u}|^{2}} - 1 =
2 \Re\Big\{ \frac{\mathsf{z}-\mathsf{z}'}{|\mathsf{z}'-\mathsf{u}|}\frac{\bar\mathsf{z}'-\bar\mathsf{u}}{|\mathsf{z}'-\mathsf{u}|} \Big\}
+ \frac{ |\mathsf{z}-\mathsf{z}'|^{2}}{|\mathsf{z}'-\mathsf{u}|^{2}} \,.
 \label{10.12r2}
\end{equation}
Further, as $|\mathsf{z}-\mathsf{z}'| \le 2|\mathsf{z}'-\mathsf{u}|/(e-1)$ and $|\mathsf{z}'-\mathsf{u}| \ge e-1$,
we deduce from (\ref{10.12r2}) that the 
first term on the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} of (\ref{10.12new}) is at most
\[
\big(1 + \frac{1}{e-1} \big) \frac{|\mathsf{z}-\mathsf{z}'|}{|\mathsf{z}'-\mathsf{u}|} \le C_1 |\mathsf{z}-\mathsf{z}'| 
                                               
\]
(with $C_1
                                               
= e/(e-1)^2$). Next, note that by symmetry $q(\mathsf{z}',\cdot)=1$, with
\begin{equation}
1- \frac{1}{q (\mathsf{z},\mathsf{x})} = 1 - \frac{|\mathsf{z}-\mathsf{x}|^{2}}{|\mathsf{z}'-\mathsf{x}|^{2}-|\mathsf{z}'-\mathsf{z}|^{2}}
= \frac{2\Re\{(\mathsf{z}'-\mathsf{z})(\bar \mathsf{z} - \bar \mathsf{x})\}}{|\mathsf{z}'-\mathsf{x}|^{2}-|\mathsf{z}'-\mathsf{z}|^{2}} \,.
\label{10.12r4}
 \end{equation}
Since $|\mathsf{z}'-\mathsf{z}| \le |\mathsf{z}'-\mathsf{x}|/2=1/(2e)$, the second term on the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} of 
(\ref{10.12new}) is bounded by 
\[
\frac{4}{3} \frac{|\mathsf{z}'-\mathsf{z}| |\mathsf{z} - \mathsf{x}|}{|\mathsf{z}'-\mathsf{x}|^2} \le 2\frac{|\mathsf{z}'-\mathsf{z}|}{|\mathsf{z}'-\mathsf{x}|} \le 
2 e  |\mathsf{z}-\mathsf{z}'|  \,,
\] 
 yielding the stated result.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{lem:emp}
For any $\kappa>0$ let
\begin{align}\label{dfn:Thetak}
\Theta_\kappa := \big\{ m,k,r \in \mathbb{Z}_+, b \in \mathbb{R} : \; & \;  
k \ge \kappa^{-3} \,, \;
\frac{|b|}{\sqrt{m}} \le  \frac{k \vee r}{\kappa} \le \frac{\log m}{\kappa^2}   \big\} \,.
\end{align}
Consider $\{ \widetilde{L}_j,  j \le m\}$ and $\{\widehat{L}_j, j \le \widehat{m}\}$ 
of laws $\mathbb{Q}^{(k)}_{m,b}$ and $\mathbb{Q}^{(k)}_{\widehat{m},\widehat{b}}$, respectively
(for the same unconditional marginal law of $L^{(k)}$ satisfying (\ref{eq:mean-var})--(\ref{eq:qi-spread})).
Extending with zeros the shorter among these two sequences, 
there exists a coupling of $\{ \widetilde{L}_j\}$ and $\{\widehat{L}_j\}$
such that for small $\kappa>0$ and any $C_1$ finite,
\begin{align}\label{cond-pre-a}
\sup_{\Theta_\kappa} \sup_{(\widehat{m},\widehat{b}) \in \Gamma} \, \Big\{ \frac{e^r}{k} 
\mathbb{P} \big( \, \bar{\Delta}_{(m,b),(\widehat{m},\widehat{b})} \ge 5  r \kappa \sqrt{m}\, \big) \Big\} < \infty \,, 
\end{align}
where
\begin{align}
\!\!\!\Gamma\!=\!\Gamma^{{(\mu)}}_{m,k,r,b} \!:= \!\{ (\widehat{m},\widehat{b}) : \widehat{m}, \mu \widehat{m} + \widehat{b} \in \mathbb{Z}_+,\,  | \mu m + b - \mu \widehat{m} - \widehat{b}| \le C_1 r k ,\,
                           
|\mu \widehat{m} - \mu m - b |  \le C_1 \sqrt{m  r \mathsf{v}_k}\}
\label{dfn:Gamma}
\end{align}
and
\begin{equation}\label{dfn:bar-Del}
\bar{\Delta}_{(m,b),(\widehat{m},\widehat{b})} := \sum_{j=1}^{m \vee \widehat{m}} {\bf 1}_{\{\widetilde{L}_j \ne \widehat{L}_j\}} \,.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
Fixing $\kappa>0$, as (\ref{cond-pre-a}) trivially holds for $r \le r_o + \log k$ and any 
$r_o=r_o(\kappa)$ finite, it must also hold when $m \le m_o$, for any finite $m_o(\kappa)$.
We thus consider hereafter only the asymptotics,  within $\Theta_\kappa$, of the
probability on the {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of (\ref{cond-pre-a}),  when $\widehat{m} < 2m$ and
both $m \to \infty$ and $r - \log k \to \infty$. 
Further, setting $t_m:=C k \log m$ and for some $C=C(\kappa)$ finite,
we can and shall intersect the event on the {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of (\ref{cond-pre-a}) with the event 
\begin{align}\label{eq:E0}
\mathcal{E}_o &:= \{ \max_{j \le m} \{\widetilde{L}_j\} \vee \max_{j \le \widehat{m}} \{\widehat{L}_j\} \le t_m \}\,.
\end{align}
Indeed, $\mathbb{P}(L_j > t_m,$ some $j \le 3m) \le 
                         
C_0 m^{-C'}$,
for $C' = c \, C -1$ with $c$ as on the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} of (\ref{eq:Ber-Geo}),  
some $C_0$ finite and all $k \ge 1$. In the sequel, after (\ref{eq:bd-whb}),  we show that 
$\mathbb{P}(S_{\widehat{m}} = \mu \widehat{m} + \widehat{b}) \ge O(m^{-s/2})$ for some finite $s=s(\kappa,c)$,
uniformly over $(\widehat{m},\widehat{b}) \in \Gamma$, as well as for $(m,b) \in \Theta_\kappa$.
Consequently, $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{E}_o^{\complement}) \le O(m^{-C'+s/2})$ which for $C=C(\kappa)$ large enough, and 
$r \le \frac{1}{\kappa} \log m$ is at most $e^{-r}$, as claimed.
We proceed to control the difference between the profiles 
\begin{equation}\label{dfn:Nmb}
N_i^{(m,b)} := \sum_{j=1}^m {\bf 1}_{\{L_j=i\}} \,, \qquad i \ge 1 \,,
\end{equation}
and $\{N^{(\widehat{m},\widehat{b})}_i \}$ induced by $\mathbb{Q}_{m,b}$ and $\mathbb{Q}_{\widehat{m},\widehat{b}}$ 
on the \emph{un-ordered counts of the corresponding} $\{L_j\}$, 
uniformly over $(m,b)$, $(\widehat{m},\widehat{b})$ as in the statement of the lemma.
Specifically, we claim that 
there exist $C=C(\kappa)$ finite, sub-probability weights $\{\varphi_i\}$ and some 
$n_i=n_i^{(m,b)}$, $\widehat{n}_i = n_i^{(\widehat{m},\widehat{b})}$ 
                          
such that for all $(\widehat{m},\widehat{b}) \in \Gamma$ {as well as for}
           
$(\widehat{m},\widehat{b})=(m,b)$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:main-est}
\sum_{i=1}^{t_m} \mathbb{Q}_{\widehat{m},\widehat{b}} ( N_i^{(\widehat{m},\widehat{b})} \notin \mathcal{I}_i ) \le C k e^{-r}  \,,
\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^{t_m} |n_i-\widehat{n}_i| \le h \,,
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal{I}_i=\mathcal{I}_i^{(\widehat{m},\widehat{b})} :=(\widehat{n}_i-\varphi_i \widehat{h},\widehat{n}_i+\varphi_i \widehat{h})$,
$\widehat{h}:=r \kappa \sqrt{\widehat{m}}
                      
$ and $h:=r \kappa \sqrt{m}$. To this end, first note that
for any $i,\widehat{m} \ge 1$, $\ell \ge 0$ and $\widehat{b} \in \mathbb{Z}$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:basic-bd}
\mathbb{Q}_{\widehat{m},\widehat{b}} (N_i^{(\widehat{m},\widehat{b})}=\ell) = \mathbb{P}(N_i^{(\widehat{m})}=\ell) \frac{\mathbb{P}(S^{[i]}_{\widehat{m}-\ell}=
\mu \widehat{m}+ \widehat{b}-\ell i)}{\mathbb{P}(S_{\widehat{m}}=\mu \widehat{m}+\widehat{b})} \,,
\end{equation}
with $N_i^{(\widehat{m})}$ a Binomial$(\widehat{m},q_i)$ and
$S^{[i]}_{\widehat{m}}$ denoting the partial sums of {\sc\lowercase{iid}} variables $L_j^{[i]}  \overset{\rm dist}{=} (L_j | \{L_j \ne i\})$,
that is, $\mathbb{P}(L_1^{[i]}=j)=\frac{q_j}{1-q_i} {\bf 1}_{j \ne i}$ for $j \in \mathbb{Z}_+$.
                                                                         
                                   
                                                                                           
            
                                                    
                                               
            
Setting hereafter for any $i \ge 1$,
\[
\mu^{[i]} := \mathbb{E} L_1^{[i]} \,, \qquad \mathsf{v}^{[i]} := {\sf var}(L_1^{[i]}) \,, \qquad u_i = q_i (1-q_i) \,,
\]
and recalling that $\mathbb{E} L_1 =\mu$, it is easy to check that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:mu-i}
(1-q_i) \mu^{[i]} + i q_i = \mu \qquad \& \qquad 
\mathsf{v}_k = (1-q_i) \mathsf{v}^{[i]} + (i-\mu^{[i]})^2 u_i \,.
\end{equation}
In choosing $\{\widehat{n}_i\}$ we are guided by the normal approximation 
$\bar \mathbb{Q}_{\widehat{m},\widehat{b}}$ for the conditional law of
 $N_i^{(\widehat{m},\widehat{b})}$ given $S_{\widehat m}= \mu \widehat{m}+\widehat{b}$,
where we replace the Binomial $N_i^{(\widehat{m})}$ with a gaussian $\bar N_i^{(\widehat{m})}$ 
of mean $\widehat{m} q_i$ and variance $\widehat{m} u_i$, which is independent of
the gaussian $\bar S^{[i]}_{\widehat{m} - \widehat{m} q_i}$ of mean zero and
variance $\widehat{m} (1-q_i) \mathsf{v}^{[i]}$. The gaussian law thus induced on 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bar-Sn-def}
\bar S_{\widehat m} := \, i \bar N^{(\widehat{m})}_i + (\widehat{m}-\bar N_i^{(\widehat{m})}) \mu^{[i]} 
+ \bar S^{[i]}_{\widehat{m} - \widehat{m} q_i} 
\end{equation}
has thanks to (\ref{eq:mu-i}),  the same mean $\mu \widehat{m}$ and variance $\widehat{m} \mathsf{v}_k$ as 
$S_{\widehat m}$.
Further, 
with ${\sf cov}(\bar N_i^{(\widehat{m})},\bar S_{\widehat{m}})=(i-\mu^{[i]}) \widehat{m}\, u_i$, we have that
                                 
               
                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                   
              
                                                     
                                                        
under $\bar \mathbb{Q}_{\widehat{m},\widehat{b}}$ the law of $\bar N_i^{(\widehat{m})}$ 
given the event $\{\bar S_{\widehat{m}}= \mu \widehat{m} + \widehat{b}\}$,
is gaussian of mean and variance
\begin{align}\label{eq:ci-def}
n_i^{(\widehat{m},\widehat{b})} := \mathbb{E}[\bar N_i^{(\widehat{m})}|\bar S_{\widehat{m}}=\mu \widehat{m}+\widehat{b}]  &= \widehat{m} q_i + 
u_i  (i-\mu^{[i]}) \widehat{b}/\mathsf{v}_k \,, \\
{\sf var} (\bar N^{(\widehat{m})}_i|\bar S_{\widehat{m}}=\mu \widehat{m}+\widehat{b}) 
                
&\le  
{\sf var} (\bar N^{(\widehat{m})}_i) \le \widehat{m} q_i \,.
\label{eq:cond-var-bd}
\end{align}
Setting $\phi(x):=(2\pi)^{-1/2} e^{-x^2/2}$ and 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ofer-xyz}
x_{\widehat b}:=\frac{{\widehat b}}{\sqrt{\mathsf{v}_k \widehat{m}}}, \qquad 
z_\ell:=\frac{\ell-\widehat{m}q_i}{\sqrt{u_i \widehat{m}}}\,, \qquad 
y_\ell:=\frac{\widehat{b} - (i-\mu^{[i]}) (\ell-\widehat{m}q_i)}{\sqrt{\mathsf{v}^{[i]} (1-q_i) \widehat{m}}} \,,
\end{equation}
it follows from (\ref{eq:bar-Sn-def}) that for some $C=C(\kappa)$ finite and all $r$ large enough 
\begin{align}\label{eq:gaussian1}
\bar \mathbb{Q}_{\widehat{m},\widehat{b}} (\bar N_i^{(\widehat{m})}  \notin \mathcal{I}_i \,  | \, \bar{S}_{\widehat m} = \mu \widehat m + \widehat b ) &=
\frac{\sqrt{\mathsf{v}_k \widehat{m}}}{\phi(x_{\widehat{b}})} \int_{\mathcal{I}_i^{\complement}}
\frac{\phi(z_\ell)}{\sqrt{u_i \widehat{m}}} \frac{\phi(y_\ell)}{\sqrt{\mathsf{v}^{[i]} (1-q_i)\widehat{m}}} d\ell 
\nonumber \\
& \le C \exp\big(-(\varphi_i \widehat{h})^2/(2 \widehat{m}q_i) \big)
\end{align}
(with the  inequality due to the usual tail bounds for centered gaussian of variance at most
$\widehat{m} q_i$, see (\ref{eq:cond-var-bd})). 
Note from (\ref{eq:Ber-Geo}) that for $q_i=q_i^{(k)}$ of (\ref{eq:qi-spread}),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:exp-tail}
\sup_k \Big\{ k \sum_{i=1}^\infty q_i e^{c i/k} \Big\} < \infty \,,
\end{equation}
whereby it follows that 
\begin{equation}\label{var:ubd}
k^{-1} \mathsf{v}_k \le  k \sum_{i=1}^\infty q_i (i/k)^2
\end{equation}
is also uniformly bounded above. 
Proceeding to take $\varphi_i := \delta e^{c i/(4k)} \sqrt{q_i}$, by Cauchy-Schwarz and (\ref{eq:exp-tail}),
\[
\sum_{i=1}^\infty \varphi_i  \le \delta \Big(k \sum_{i=1}^\infty q_i e^{c i/k} \Big)^{1/2}
\Big( \sum_{i=1}^\infty \frac{1}{k} e^{-c i/(2k)} \Big)^{1/2} \le c' \delta \,,
\]
so some $\delta(c)>0$ results with $\sum_i \varphi_i \le 1$ 
for all values of $k$ considered here. With such a choice of $\varphi_i$ and having
$\widehat{h}=r \kappa \sqrt{\widehat{m}}$, it follows from (\ref{eq:gaussian1}) that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gaussian2}
\bar \mathbb{Q}_{\widehat{m},\widehat{b}} (\bar N_i^{(\widehat{m})}  \notin \mathcal{I}_i \,  | \, \bar{S}_{\widehat m} = \mu \widehat m + \widehat b ) 
\le C \exp(-(r \kappa \delta)^2 e^{ci/(2k)}/2) \,.
\end{equation}
Consequently, up to the 
use of $\bar \mathbb{Q}_{\widehat{m},\widehat{b}}$ instead of $\mathbb{Q}_{\widehat{m},\widehat{b}}$,  the
{\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of (\ref{eq:main-est}) follows upon summing 
(\ref{eq:gaussian2}) over $i \le t_m$.

We next justify the preceding move from $\mathbb{Q}_{\widehat{m},\widehat{b}}$ to $\bar \mathbb{Q}_{\widehat{m},\widehat{b}}$ by 
using the local {\sc\lowercase{CLT}} of \cite[Thm. VII.3.16]{Petrov} for sums 
of integer valued {\sc\lowercase{iid}} in approximating the terms involving $S^{[i]}_{\widehat{m}}$ and $S_{\widehat{m}}$ in  
(\ref{eq:basic-bd}). 
Specifically, from the second part of (\ref{dfn:Gamma}) we know that $\widehat{m} \in [m/2,2m]$ whereas by
(\ref{dfn:Gamma}) and our restrictions on $r$ and $k$, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bd-whb}
|\widehat{b}|  \le C_1 (r k + \sqrt{m r \mathsf{v}_k}) \le 2 C_1 \sqrt{\widehat{m} r \mathsf{v}_k} \le \frac{\sqrt{m r k}}{\kappa}  
\end{equation}
(provided $\kappa \le \kappa_0(C_1)$ is small enough). In particular, the standardized argument 
$x_{\widehat{b}}$ of (\ref{eq:ofer-xyz}) in the normal approximation 
for $\mathbb{P}(S_{\widehat{m}}=\mu \widehat{m}+\widehat{b})$ is by (\ref{eq:bd-whb}) 
such that $|x_{\widehat b}| \le 2\sqrt{r}/(\kappa \sqrt{c})$. Thanks to 
(\ref{eq:Ber-Geo}), the $\rho$-th cumulant of the law of $L_j = L_j^{(k)}$ 
scales at most as $k^\rho$, with the multiplicative correction terms 
in the normal approximation of \cite[Thm. VII.3.16]{Petrov} are thus $o(1)$ as long as 
$k |x_{\widehat{b}}| = o(\widehat{m}^{1/6})$, which applies under our restriction to $k \vee r=O(\log m)$. 
Further, in view of (\ref{var:ubd}), the leading term $(\mathsf{v}_k \widehat{m})^{-1/2} \phi(x)$ is for $x=x_{\widehat b}$
then at least $O(m^{-s/2})$ for some finite $s=s(\kappa,c)$. Examining how 
the bounds on $I_1$-$I_4$ of \cite[(VII.3.7)]{Petrov} depend on the law of $L_1^{(k)}$, 
we thus deduce that upon taking the expansion in \cite[Thm. VII.3.16]{Petrov} up to the $s$-th level, 
                                                                
the resulting additive error be negligible, 
uniformly in the range of $\widehat{m},\widehat{b},m,b,k$ we consider. 
Proceeding to show that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:pre-gaussian}
\sum_{i=1}^{t_m} \sum_{\ell \notin \mathcal{I}_i}
\mathbb{P}(N_i^{(\widehat m)}=\ell) \mathbb{P}(S^{[i]}_{\widehat m-\ell}=\mu \widehat m+\widehat b-\ell i) \le C \frac{k e^{-r}}{\sqrt{\mathsf{v}_k \widehat m}} \phi(x_{\widehat b}) \,,
\end{equation}
recall that the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} is at least $O(m^{2-s'/2})$ for some finite $s'=s'(\kappa,c)$.
Summing over at most $\widehat{m} t_m = o(m^{3/2})$ terms on the {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of (\ref{eq:pre-gaussian}), 
thanks to the sub-gaussian tails of the Binomial $N_i^{(\widehat m)}$ of mean $\widehat m q_i$ and variance 
$\widehat m u_i$ we may and shall restrict, for some 
$c'=c'(s')$ finite, the inner sum in (\ref{eq:pre-gaussian}) to $\mathcal{I}_i^{\complement} \cap \mathcal{J}_i$ for the interval 
$\mathcal{J}_i$ of width $2 c' \sqrt{\widehat m q_i \log m}$ centered at $\widehat m q_i$. In particular, 
thanks to (\ref{eq:Ber-Geo}) we know that $1-q_i \ge q_0$ is bounded away from zero
uniformly in $k$ and $i \ge 1$, which within the interval $\mathcal{J}_i$ 
applies also for $(\widehat m-\ell)/\widehat m$. By the same reasoning, 
                                                              
it follows from (\ref{eq:qi-spread}) that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:mu-i-bd}
                                                 
\mathsf{v}^{[i]} \ge q_0 (\mu^{[i]})^2 \ge q_0 (\mu-i q_i)^2 \ge O(k^{-2/c}) \,.
\end{equation}
With $\mathsf{v}^{[i]}$ 
decaying at most polynomially in $k \le O(\log m)$, applying \cite[Thm. VII.3.16]{Petrov} 
to each of the terms $\mathbb{P}(S^{[i]}_{\widehat m-\ell}=\mu \widehat m+ \widehat b -\ell i)$ with an expansion up to the $s'$-th level,
                                                                                                         
results with a negligible additive error. Further, thanks to the {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of 
(\ref{eq:mu-i}), the standardized argument in such a normal approximation 
is $\widetilde{y}_\ell = y_\ell \sqrt{(1-q_i)/(1-\ell/\widehat m)}$ for $y_\ell$ of (\ref{eq:ofer-xyz}),
where
for some $C=C(\kappa)$, uniformly over $\ell \in \mathcal{J}_i$ 
and $\widehat b,\widehat m, k$ satisfying our restrictions, 
\[
|\widetilde{y}_\ell| \le C k^{1/c}   [ \sqrt{r k}  + c' \sqrt{\mathsf{v}_k \log m} ]  \le C^2 (\log m)^{1+1/c} \,.
\]
The {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} of (\ref{eq:Ber-Geo}) implies a similar bound on the {\sc\lowercase{mgf}} of 
$L_1^{[i]}/k$, uniformly in $i \ge 1$ and $k$, hence the same $k^{\rho}$ growth 
rate of the $\rho$-th cumulant of its law. This in turn yields a uniformly $o(1)$ 
multiplicative correction terms in the preceding normal approximation throughout 
the interval $\mathcal{J}_i$ of $\ell$ values of interest here (where $k |\widetilde{y}_\ell|$ stays uniformly
bounded by $(\log m)^{2+1/c}$). Finally,  
$|y_\ell^2-\widetilde{y}_\ell^2| 
                                        
= o(1)$, uniformly over $\mathcal{J}_i$, allowing us to replace $\phi(\widetilde y_\ell)$ by $\phi(y_\ell)$
in the leading term of the approximation. 
Upon utilizing also the normal approximation 
for the Binomial $N_i^{(\widehat m)}$, at the standardized argument $z_\ell$ of (\ref{eq:ofer-xyz}),
we deduce that it suffices for (\ref{eq:pre-gaussian}), to show that 
\[
\sum_{i=1}^{t_m} \frac{\sqrt{\mathsf{v}_k \widehat m}}{\phi(x_{\widehat b})} \sum_{\ell \notin \mathcal{I}_i} 
\frac{\phi(z_\ell)}{\sqrt{u_i \widehat m}} \frac{\phi(y_\ell)}{\sqrt{\mathsf{v}^{[i]} (1-q_i) \widehat m}} \le C k e^{-r} \,.
\]
As $m \to \infty$, the inner discrete sum over 
$\ell \notin \mathcal{I}_i$ is bounded, up to some universal constant $C=C(\kappa)$ by the corresponding
integral over $d\ell$. With the latter integral being precisely the conditional gaussian computation
that led to (\ref{eq:gaussian1}), we thus arrive at the {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of (\ref{eq:main-est}).

Next, recall the {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of (\ref{eq:mu-i}) that $u_i |i -\mu^{[i]}| = q_i |i-\mu|$. Since  
$\sum_{i} (i-\mu) q_i =0$ (see (\ref{eq:mean-var})), also
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ui-sum-bd}
\sum_{i \ne 0} u_i |i-\mu^{[i]}| \le 2 \sum_{i} q_i (\mu-i)_+ \le 2 \mu \,.
\end{equation}
Our choice (\ref{eq:ci-def}) for $\{n_i, \widehat{n}_i\}$ thus results for some $C=C(\mu)$ finite, with 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:mean-bd}
\sum_{i=1}^{\infty} |n_i -\widehat{n}_i| \le |\widehat{m}-m| (1-q_0) + 2 \mu \frac{|\widehat{b}- b|}{\mathsf{v}_k} \le 
\frac{C \sqrt{m}}{\kappa} ((r/k) \vee 1) \,,
\end{equation}
where we have used here the lower bound (\ref{eq:mean-var}) on $k^{-1} \mathsf{v}_k$, the upper 
bounds (\ref{eq:bd-whb}) on $|\widehat{b}|, |b|$, and (\ref{eq:Ber-Geo}) on $(1-q_0)$, as well as the bound
\begin{equation}\label{bd:m-diff}
|\widehat{m}-m| \le \mu^{-1} [\, |b| + C_1 \sqrt{m r \mathsf{v}_k}\, ] \le \frac{2 (r \vee k) \sqrt{m}}{\mu \kappa} \,,
\end{equation}
due to the second part of (\ref{dfn:Gamma}) and the right-inequality in (\ref{eq:bd-whb}). Since 
$(C/\kappa) \sqrt{m} ((r/k) \vee 1) \le h$ 
for all $r$ large enough, any $k \ge \kappa^{-3}$ and $\kappa \le \kappa_0(C)$,
we thus arrive at the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} of (\ref{eq:main-est}). Now, setting 
\[
\widehat{\Delta}_{(m,b),(\widehat{m},\widehat{b})} := \sum_{i \ge 1} | N_i^{(m,b)} - N^{(\widehat{m},\widehat{b})}_i | \,,
\]
for the independent collections $\{N_i^{(m,b)}\}$, $\{N^{(\widehat{m},\widehat{b})}_i \}$, note that under
the event $\mathcal{E}_o$ of (\ref{eq:E0}),
\[
\widehat{\Delta}_{(m,b),(\widehat{m},\widehat{b})} 
                                                          
\le \sum_{i=1}^{t_m} |N_i^{(m,b)} - n_i| 
 + \sum_{i=1}^{t_m} |\widehat{N}_i^{(\widehat{m},\widehat{b})} -\widehat{n}_i| + \sum_{i=1}^{t_m} |\widehat{n}_i - n_i| 
\]
and therefore the bounds of (\ref{eq:main-est}) yield that for any $\kappa>0$ as above
\begin{align}\label{cond-pre-b}
\sup_{\Theta_\kappa, \; (\widehat{m},\widehat{b}) \in \Gamma} \, \Big\{ \frac{e^r}{k} 
\mathbb{P} \big( \widehat{\Delta}_{(m,b),(\widehat{m},\widehat{b})} \ge 4 r \kappa \sqrt{m} \big) \Big\} < \infty \,.
\end{align}
Assuming hereafter, for the sake of definiteness, that $\widehat{m} \le m$, setting 
$\widehat{L}_j \equiv 0$ for all $\widehat{m} < j \le m$ results with  
\begin{equation}\label{bd:N0-diff}
| N_0^{(\widehat{m},\widehat{b})} - N_0^{(m,b)} | = \big| \sum_{i \ge 1} (N_i^{(m,b)} - N_i^{(\widehat{m},\widehat{b})} ) \big| 
\le \widehat{\Delta}_{(m,b),(\widehat{m},\widehat{b})} \,.
\end{equation}
Now, conditional upon the independently generated $\{N^{(m,b)}_i\}$ and $\{N^{(\widehat{m},\widehat{b})}_i \}$, 
the pairs $\{(\widetilde{L}_j, \widehat{L}_j), j \le m \}$, can and will be aligned so that $\widetilde{L}_j = \widehat{L}_j$ for  
$\sum_{i \ge 0} (N_i^{(m,b)} \wedge N_i^{(\widehat{m},\widehat{b})} )$ indices. Applying a uniformly chosen 
permutation of $\{1,\ldots,m\}$ to these $m$ pairs, attains the marginal 
law $\mathbb{Q}_{m,b}$ of $\{\widetilde{L}_j, j \le m \}$ and we
thereafter recover the marginal law $\mathbb{Q}_{\widehat{m},\widehat{b}}$ of the shorter sequence by
exchanging the set $\{\widehat{L}_j  \ne 0 : \widehat{m} < j \le m \}$ whose size we denote by $V$,
with a uniformly chosen subset of the same size from $\{ \widehat{L}_j =0 : j \le \widehat{m} \}$.
In view of (\ref{bd:N0-diff}), this coupling guarantees having 
\[
\bar{\Delta}_{(m,b),(\widehat{m},\widehat{b})} \le V + 
\frac{1}{2} \sum_{i \ge 0} |N_i^{(m,b)} - N_i^{(\widehat{m},\widehat{b})}| \le  
V + \widehat{\Delta}_{(m,b),(\widehat{m},\widehat{b})} \,,
\]
which in view of (\ref{cond-pre-b}) results with the desired statement (\ref{cond-pre-a}) provided that
\begin{equation}\label{bd:V}
\sup_{\Theta_\kappa, \; (\widehat{m},\widehat{b}) \in \Gamma} \, \Big\{ \frac{e^r}{k} 
\mathbb{P} \big( V \ge r \kappa \sqrt{m} \big) \Big\} < \infty \,, 
\end{equation}
for any $\kappa>0$ small enough. 
Turning to establish (\ref{bd:V}), note that given $\{N_i^{(\widehat{m},\widehat{b})} \}$, the variable 
$V$ counts how many of the $N_{\ge 1} =\sum_{i \ge 1} N_i^{(\widehat{m},\widehat{b})}$ items
which are uniformly distributed among the given $m$ bins, falls within the last $m-\widehat{m}$ bins.
As such, conditioned on $N_{\ge 1}=\ell$, the variable $V$ is stochastically dominated by 
the variable $\bar V$ of Binomial($\ell,\frac{m-\widehat{m}}{m-\ell}$) law. Turning to bound 
the upper tail of $\bar V$,
in view of (\ref{eq:main-est}) we can {\sc\lowercase{wlog}} replace the random value of $N_{\ge 1}$ by 
\[
\ell := \widehat{h}+ \sum_{i \ge 1} \widehat{n}_i \le h + m (1-q_0) + 2 \mu |\widehat{b}| / \mathsf{v}_k 
\le r \kappa \sqrt{m} + \frac{m}{ck}  + 2 \mu \frac{(r/k) \vee 1)}{\kappa c} \sqrt{m} \,,
\]
where we relied on having $\widehat{m} \le m$ as well as 
(\ref{eq:ci-def}) and (\ref{eq:ui-sum-bd}) to arrive at the first inequality,
and on our choice of $h$, the {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of (\ref{eq:Ber-Geo}), (\ref{eq:bd-whb}) and 
(\ref{eq:mean-var}) for the second inequality. The latter bound applies also when setting
$\ell = h + \sum_{i \ge 1} n_i$ in case $m \le \widehat{m}$,
and assuming {\sc\lowercase{wlog}} that $\sqrt{m}/(ck) \ge r \kappa + 2 \mu r/(\kappa c)$,
we see that that regardless of the sign of $m-\widehat{m}$,  we can replace $N_{\ge 1}$, 
by $\bar{\ell}=\lceil 2 m/(ck) \rceil$. Upon doing so, we have thanks to (\ref{bd:m-diff}), that 
for $\kappa>0$ small enough and $r \ge r_o(\kappa)$, 
                                       
\[
\mathbb{E} [\bar V] = \frac{|m-\widehat{m}| \bar{\ell}}{m-\bar{\ell}} \le \frac{8 ((r/k) \vee 1)}{c \mu \kappa} \sqrt{m}
\le \frac{r \kappa}{2} \sqrt{m}\,.
\]
We thus get that (\ref{bd:V}) holds 
                                                                     
by the exponential upper tails of Binomial variables such as $\bar V$.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\label{lem:coupling} 
{For $L^{(k)}$ distributed as (\ref{dfn:GJpL}),}
                                                                                                    
                                              
                                                            
        
               
                                 
                                              
                                                     
   
consider
$\{ \widetilde{L}_i,  i \le m\}$ of law $\mathbb{Q}_{m,b}$ and $\{ L_{i}^\star, i \le \tau_{m'} \}$ of law
                          
$\mathbb{Q}^\star_{m'}$, $m'=m+b$. Choose 
independently of both sequences,  {\sc\lowercase{iid}} Geometric($1/c')$ random variables $\{\chi_j, j \ge 0\}$   and 
construct the corresponding blocks $\{\widetilde{\mathcal{L}}_j, j \in [0,M_m] \}$ and $\{\mathcal{L}^\star_j, j \in [0,M_{\tau_{m'}}] \}$ by 
summing consecutive $\chi_j$ entries from the finite sequences $\{\widetilde{L}_i\}$ and $\{L^\star_i\}$ 
(cutting short the last sum as needed). For small $\kappa>0$ and any $(m,b,k,r)$ in $\Theta_\kappa$,
there exists some $\mathcal{J} \subseteq [1,M_{m \wedge \tau_{m'}})$ with 
$\widetilde{\mathcal{L}}_j=\mathcal{L}_j^\star$ when $j \in \mathcal{J}$, and
\begin{align}\label{cond-a}
\sup_{\Theta_\kappa} \, \Big\{ \frac{e^r}{k} 
\mathbb{P} \big( \bar \Delta_{m,b} \ge 6  r c' \kappa \sqrt{m} \big) \Big\} < \infty \,,
\end{align}
where $\bar \Delta_{m,b}$ count the total number of $\widetilde{L}_i \ge 1$ and $L^\star_i \ge 1$ which are
from within the collection $\bar \mathcal{U}_{m,b}$, of non-matched blocks $j \notin \mathcal{J}$ (including 
the first and last blocks in each sequence, which we do not aim to match).
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
Recall, as in the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:emp},
that it suffices to consider only the asymptotic, within $\Theta_\kappa$, of the
probability on the {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of (\ref{cond-a}),  when  both $m \to \infty$, 
$r - \log k \to \infty$. 
Setting $\widehat{M}:=\tau_{m'}-1$ and $\widehat{B} := S_{\widehat{M}}-\widehat{M}$, 
note that $\{L_j^\star, \, j \le \widehat{M} \}$ is distributed according to a mixture of $\mathbb{Q}_{\widehat{m},\widehat{b}}$, 
                                                         
for non-negative integers $\widehat{m}+\widehat{b} < m + b$ and mixture coefficients 
\begin{align}
\mathbb{Q}^\star_{m'} (\, \widehat M=\widehat m, \, \widehat B = \widehat b\, )  
               
 =
\mathbb{P}(S_{\widehat{m}}= \widehat{m}+\widehat{b}\,)\, \mathbb{P}(L_1 \ge  m+b- \widehat{m}-\widehat{b}) \,.
\label{eq:mixture}
\end{align} 
In view of (\ref{eq:mixture}), 
$\mathbb{Q}_{m'}^\star\big(\, (\widehat{M}, \widehat{B}) \notin \Gamma\big) \to 0$ faster than $k e^{-r}$
for $\Gamma$ of (\ref{dfn:Gamma}), with $\mu=1$, and some $C_1$ finite
(indeed, this follows by the exponential tails as in the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} of (\ref{eq:Ber-Geo})  
for our $L_1$, and the sub-gaussian tail of $\widehat{M}$ up to  $O(\log m)$ standard deviations). 
Thus, restricting hereafter the mixture in (\ref{eq:mixture}) to $(\widehat{m},\widehat{b}) \in \Gamma$,
                                                   
we deduce that for $\kappa>0$ small enough as in this application of Lemma \ref{lem:emp},
\begin{align}\label{cond-star}
\sup_{\Theta_\kappa} \, \Big\{ \frac{e^r}{k} 
\mathbb{P} \big( \bar{\Delta}^\star \ge 5  r \kappa \sqrt{m} \big) \Big\} < \infty \,, 
\end{align}
where upon extending with zeros the shorter of the two sequences, 
\[
\bar{\Delta}^\star := \sum_{i=1}^{m \vee \widehat{M}} {\bf 1}_{\{\widetilde{L}_i \ne L^\star_i\}} \,.
\]
Note that each $i \ge 1$ for which $\widetilde{L}_i \ne L^\star_i$, contributes at most the 
corresponding block length $\chi_j$ to $\bar{\Delta}_{m,b}$.  Since the {\sc\lowercase{iid}} $\{\chi_j\}$ are independent 
of the collection $\{\widetilde{L}_i,L_i^\star, i \ge 1 \}$, this in turn results with the conditional law of
$\bar{\Delta}_{m,b}$ given $\bar{\Delta}^\star=\ell$ being stochastically dominated 
by $\sum_{j=1}^{\ell+2} \chi_j$. In view of (\ref{cond-star}), we thus get (\ref{cond-a}) 
(utilizing the exponential tails of the {\sc\lowercase{iid}} $\chi_j$ of mean $c'$).
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- definition-6: body_md -->
\label{def-trav} For any $0<r < R \le \tilde{r}<\tilde{R}$, integer $m \ge 1$
and $\mathsf{v},\mathsf{x} \in \mathbb{T}^2$ such that $\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},\tilde{r}-R)$,
	let $\ensuremath{T_{\mathsf{v},r\to R}^{\mathsf{x},\tilde r\overset{m}{\to}\tilde R} }$ be the number of
	traversals  
	$\partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{v}, r)\to\partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{v},R)$
	during $m$ excursions $\partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{x},\tilde{r})\to\partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{x},\tilde{R})$.
These traversals are interlaced with the traversals $\partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{v}, R)\to\partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{v},r)$,  so we set 
$\ensuremath{T_{\mathsf{v},R\to r}^{\mathsf{x},\tilde r\overset{m}{\to}\tilde R} }=\ensuremath{T_{\mathsf{v},r\to R}^{\mathsf{x},\tilde r\overset{m}{\to}\tilde R} }$.  
	For $j > k \ge 1$ we often use the abbreviations 
\begin{equation}
                   
\label{eq-calgary}
 T_{\mathsf{v},j}^{\mathsf{x},m}:= \ensuremath{T_{\mathsf{v},r_j\to r_{j-1}}^{\mathsf{x},r_1\overset{m}{\to}r_0} }, \quad
                   
  T_{j}^{\mathsf{x},k,m} 
  :=\ensuremath{T_{\mathsf{x},r_{j}\to r_{j-1}}^{\mathsf{x},r_{k}\overset{m}{\to}r_{k-1}} }\,,
 \quad T^{\mathsf{x},m}_j := T^{\mathsf{x},1,m}_j = T^{\mathsf{x},m}_{\mathsf{x},j} 
\end{equation}
(also with the roles of $r_j$ and $r_{j-1}$ reversed).  
More generally,  for Brownian stopping times $\tau$ and $\tau'$,  denote by $T^{[\tau,\tau']}_{\mathsf{v},j}$ the number 
of traversals $\partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{v}, r_j)\to\partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{v},r_{j-1})$ during 
$[\tau, \tau']$,  with $T^{[\tau,\tau']}_{\mathsf{v},j} \equiv 0$ if $\tau' \le \tau$. 

We also consider the following approximation of $\mathsf{s}_1(\cdot)$ of (\ref{eq:nominal}),
\begin{equation}\label{clt.2}
\widetilde \mathsf{s} (y) = \widetilde \mathsf{s}_{n_\varepsilon}(y) := n_\varepsilon( 2 n_\varepsilon  - \log n_\varepsilon + y) = \mathsf{s}_1(y/2) +  O((\log n_\varepsilon)^2) \,,
\end{equation}
and keep track of the time it takes the Brownian motion to complete a prescribed
number of excursions.  Specifically,  for $0<r<r'$, $m \ge 1$,  we set
\begin{align}
  \tau_{\mathsf{v},r,r'} (m)=&
  \mbox{\rm 
  time it takes the Brownian motion to complete $m$ excursions} \nonumber 
  \\
  &\mbox{\rm from  
$\partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{v},r)$ to $\partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{v},r')$},
 \label{eq-tauab}
\\
\tau_{\mathsf{v}}(m) :=&\tau_{\mathsf{v},r_1,r_0}(m) \,.
\label{eq-taux}
\end{align}
<!-- end definition-6 -->
<!-- remark-14: body_md -->
Note the compatibility property 
\begin{equation}
\{ T_{j}^{\mathsf{x},k,m}=T_{j}^{\mathsf{x},t}, \;\; \forall  j > k\}, \mbox{\,\; on the event \; }\left\{ T_{k}^{\mathsf{x},t} = m  \right\}.\label{eq:TkandTCompatability}
\end{equation}
Further,  with ${GW}_j(m)$ denoting the {branching process of a}
                                                                          
Geometric(1/2) offspring distribution,  started at $GW_1(m)=m$,  we have the identity in law
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Jay1.12}
\{T_j^{\mathsf{x},m}\}_j  \overset{\rm dist}{=} \{{GW}_j(m)\}_j\,.
\end{equation}
<!-- end remark-14 -->
<!-- remark-15: body_md -->
\label{rmk:z-lz-adjust}
From \Cref{lem-claim1} we have the Brownian path starting hereafter in $\partial \mathbb{C}$ and in particular,  when showing
(\ref{eq:U-plus}) we start outside $\mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{v}_\beta,r_{\mathsf {K}_{1}-4})$,  regardless of $\beta$.  Moreover,  
                                    
we monitor $\{\eta_{\mathsf{v},j}^{\beta,\langle z \rangle}\}_{j,\mathsf{v}}$ only \emph{after first hitting} $\partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{v}_\beta,r_1)$,  see 
(\ref{eq-calgary}).  Hence,  in \Cref{sec:Jay-26} and all other 
arguments involving $\{\eta_{\mathsf{v},j}^{\beta,\langle z \rangle}\}_{j,\mathsf{v}}$,  we can assume that the path started outside 
$\mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{v}_\beta,r_1)$.
<!-- end remark-15 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
\label{Thm4.1+4.2-Jay}
For $\widetilde{\mathcal{R}}_{\mathsf{k}}^{\langle z \rangle}$ of (\ref{def:Jay-Thm4.2}),  $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k}}^{[z]}$ of (\ref{def:Jay-Thm4.1}),  small $\widetilde{c}$, $r_0$,  there exists $C<\infty$ such that for
                 
                         
     
any $z\in \mathbb{R}$ and $\mathsf{k} \ge 1$, 
\begin{align}
\varliminf_{\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon} \mathbb{P}(\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k}}^{[z]}) \ge 1-  C \mathsf{k}^{-4}  \quad \text{\rm and,  if $11 z \ge - \mathsf{k}^{{\kappa_o}}$, then} \quad 
\varliminf_{\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon}
\mathbb{P}\big(\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k}}^{[z]} \cap \widetilde{\mathcal{R}}_{\mathsf{k}}^{\langle z' \rangle}  \big) &\ge 1-  C \mathsf{k}^{-4}\,.
                                                              
\label{eq:Jay-Thm-4.2}
\end{align}
