<!-- proposition-9: body_md -->
\label{theo-pre220} Fix parameters as in (\ref{dfn:aux-par}),  with 
$\widetilde{c},  r_0,  \mathsf{\delta_\star}$  small and $\kappa_\star$ large.  Set
\begin{equation}\label{def:UUpk}
\widehat{\mathcal{U}}^{(\varepsilon),\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\beta}:= \bigcup_{\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F}^\beta} \mathcal{U}^{(\varepsilon),\beta,\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\mathsf{v}} = \mathcal{R}^{o,\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\beta} \cap \widehat{\mathcal{U}}^{(\varepsilon),\langle z \rangle}_{\beta}  \quad \text{where} \quad  
\widehat{\mathcal{U}}^{(\varepsilon),\langle z \rangle}_{\beta} :=\bigcup_{\mathsf{v}\in \mathbb{F}^\beta} 
\Big\{ \mathcal{R}^{\beta,\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\mathsf{v}},  \eta_{\mathsf{v},n_\varepsilon+1}^{\beta,\langle z \rangle} = 0\Big\}
                                                           
\,.
 \end{equation}
Further,   {recall $n_\varepsilon^{(i)}=n_\varepsilon-\mathsf {K}_i$ of (\ref{def.n-vep-i}), 
setting for} $\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,j}^{\,\langle z \rangle}:=\eta_{\beta,j}^{\langle z \rangle}-\gamma_0(j)$ {the events}
\begin{align}
\!\!\!\! \mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}_{\beta}^{\,\langle z \rangle}  \!\!  &:= \! \bigcap_{j\in \mathsf {J}'_\mathsf{a}}  \!  \{ L_{\beta,j}^{\langle z \rangle} \in \mathbb{B}^\infty_{\bar \mu} (\boldsymbol{\eta}^{(\varepsilon)}_j) \}
\bigcap_{j \in \mathsf {J}_\mathsf{e}} \! \{ \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,j}^{\,\langle z \rangle} \in \mathsf{I}'_j  \} \,,
 \label{dfn:bw-Jay}
\end{align} 
where $\mathsf {J}_\mathsf{e}:=[\mathsf {K}_{1}-3,n_\varepsilon^{(4)}] \cup \{n_\varepsilon^{(5)}\}$ and we have replaced (\ref{dfn:windows}) by the narrower
restrictions of 
\begin{equation}\label{dfn:windows-alt}
\mathsf{I}'_j := \left\{\!\!\!\begin{array}{cll}
& (-\infty,\frac{1}{2} \mathsf {K}_{5}), & \qquad j = n_\varepsilon^{(5)} \,, \\
& (\mathsf {K}_{4}^{{\kappa_1}},  \frac{1}{2} \mathsf {K}_{4}^{{\kappa'}}),  & \qquad j=n_\varepsilon^{(4)},   \\
& (2 j^{{\kappa_1}},  \frac{1}{2} j^{{\kappa'}}),  & \qquad j \le \mathsf {K}_{1},  j = \mathsf {K}_{2},  j=\mathsf {K}_{3} \,,  \\
&(2 j_{n_\varepsilon}^{\kappa_o}, \frac{1}{2} j_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa''}}),  & \qquad  j \in (\mathsf {K}_{1},n_\varepsilon^{(4)})\,,  j \ne \mathsf {K}_{2},\mathsf {K}_{3} \,.
\end{array}
\right.
\end{equation}
Then,  for some $C_{\mathsf{k}}<\infty$,  all large enough $\mathsf {K}_{5}$ and any fixed $z$,  $\mathsf{k}$,
\begin{align}
\varlimsup_{\varepsilon \to 0} \Big\{ e^{2 n_\varepsilon} \sup_{\beta,\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F}^{\beta}} 
\mathbb{P} \big( \mathcal{U}^{(\varepsilon),\beta,\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\mathsf{v}},  \widehat{\eta}^{\,\langle z \rangle}_{\beta,n_\varepsilon^{(4)}} \in (\mathsf {K}_{4}^{{\kappa_1}},\mathsf {K}_{4}^{{\kappa'}})
                                   
 \big)  \Big\} & \le C_{\mathsf{k}}  (1+z_{+}) e^{-2z},  \label{atot-new}
\\
\varlimsup_{\varepsilon \to 0} \Big\{ e^{2 n_\varepsilon^{(5)}} \sup_\beta \mathbb{P} \big( \widehat{\mathcal{U}}^{(\varepsilon),\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\beta} \setminus \mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}_{\beta}^{\,\langle z \rangle}
 \big)  \Big\} &=o_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{0}}(1)  (1+z_{+}) e^{-2z}\,.
\label{atot}
\end{align}
<!-- end proposition-9 -->
<!-- proposition-10: body_md -->
\label{Jay-4.3-4.3rev}
Recall the stopping times $\tau_{\mathsf{x}}(a)$ of (\ref{eq-taux}) and the various $\sigma$-algebras of \Cref{def:Fvjs}.
                            
For $\delta \in (0,1)$,  some $c=c(\delta)>0$,  any $b>a$ and all $\mathsf{x}$, 
\begin{equation}\label{A.2-n}
\mathbb{P} \big( T_j^{\mathsf{x}, b}  - T_j^{\mathsf{x},a} \ge \ell \,|\,  \mathcal{G}^{\tau_{\mathsf{x}}(a)} \,\big) \le e^{-c \, \ell/j},  \qquad 
\forall j \ge 1,  \;\; \ell \ge (1+2 \delta) (b-a) \,.
\end{equation}
                               
 
                                                                                                   
                                                                                          
                                                            
Further,  there exist $c>0$,  so if $j \le  n_\varepsilon$ and $T^{[\tau,\tau']}_{\mathsf{x},j}$ is $\mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{x}, \tau}_j$-measurable,
then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Jay4.14-n}
\sup_{\mathsf{v} \in  \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x}, r_j)}
\mathbb{P}( T^{[\tau,\tau']}_{\mathsf{v},n_\varepsilon+1}=0 \;\big| \; \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{x},\tau}_j,  T^{[\tau,\tau']}_{\mathsf{x},j} \ge \ell )
 \le e^{-c \,  \ell/(n_\varepsilon-j)} \,,   \qquad \forall \ell \ge 1 \,.
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-10 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{lem:adjust-AUz}
For some $c_\star=c_\star(\kappa_\star)>0$,  large enough $\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{0}$,  small enough $\varepsilon$,  and all
$\beta$,  $\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F}^\beta$, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:U-plus-event}
              
\mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}_{\beta}^{\,\langle z' \rangle} \cap \mathcal{A}\, \mathcal{U}_{\mathsf{k},\mathsf{v}}^{(\varepsilon),\beta,[z]} \subset 
\{\tau' \ge \tau \} \cap  
\{ T_{\mathsf{v},n_\varepsilon+1}^{[\tau,\tau']} = 0 \big\} \cap \Big\{  \bigcup_{j \in \mathsf {J}'_\mathsf{a}} \mathcal{W}^\star_{\mathsf{x},j} \bigcup_{j \in \mathsf {J}} \mathcal{B}^\star_{\mathsf{x},j} \Big\} \,,
\end{equation}
where 
$\tau' := S_{\mathsf{k}_\varepsilon(z)}$,
                                                         
$\tau:=\tau_\mathsf{x}(a)$, $\mathsf{x}:=\mathsf{v}_\beta$,
$a:=\mathsf{s}_1(z')$,  $b:=\mathsf{s}_1(z'')$ and
\begin{equation}\label{dfn:bb-extra-i}
\mathcal{W}^\star_{\mathsf{x},j} :=   \{ T_{j}^{\mathsf{x},b} - T_{j}^{\mathsf{x},a} \ge c_\star n_\varepsilon \log j \}\,, \qquad
\mathcal{B}_{\mathsf{x},j}^\star := \{  T_{\mathsf{x},j}^{[\tau,\tau']} \ge \ell_j\}\,,\qquad \ell_j:=\frac{1}{3} (n_\varepsilon-j) j_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa'}}  \,.
                                                                          
                                                                                     
                    
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
By \Cref{lem:adjust-AUz} and the union bound,  we get 
(\ref{eq:U-plus-alt}) upon showing that for $\mathsf{x}=\mathsf{v}_\beta$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:U-plus-123}
\varlimsup_{\varepsilon \to 0}
\Big\{ e^{2 n_\varepsilon} \sum_{j=\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\mathsf {K}_{\mathsf{a}}} \sup_{\beta,\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F}^\beta} \mathbb{P} \Big( \mathcal{U}^{(\varepsilon),\beta,\langle z' \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\mathsf{v}} \cap \mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}_{\beta}^{\,\langle z' \rangle} ,
T^{\mathsf{x},b}_{j} -T^{\mathsf{x},a}_{j} \ge c_\star n_\varepsilon \log j
 \Big) \Big\} = 0 \,,
\end{equation}
as soon as $\mathsf {K}_{0}$ is large enough (in terms of $\mathsf{k}$ and $z$),  while for $\tau=\tau_\mathsf{x}(a) \le \tau' = S_{\mathsf{k}_\varepsilon (z)}$,
                                                           
\begin{equation}\label{eq:U-plus-45}
\varlimsup_{\varepsilon \to 0}
\Big\{ e^{2 n_\varepsilon} \sum_{j \in \mathsf {J}}\sup_{\beta,\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F}^\beta} \mathbb{P} \Big( \mathcal{U}^{(\varepsilon),\beta,\langle z' \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\mathsf{v}} \cap \mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}_{\beta}^{\,\langle z' \rangle} ,  \tau' \ge \tau,
T_{\mathsf{v},n_\varepsilon+1}^{[\tau,\tau']} = 0,  T^{[\tau,\tau']}_{\mathsf{x},j} \ge \ell_j \Big) \Big\}  = o_{\mathsf {K}_{0},\mathsf {K}_{5}} (1) \,.
\end{equation}
Starting with (\ref{eq:U-plus-123}),  note that for some $C_{\mathsf{k}}$ finite,  any  $j \in \mathsf {J}'_\mathsf{a}=[\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{\mathsf{a}}]$ and 
$z =o(n_\varepsilon)$,  
\begin{equation}\label{eq:b-a-bd}
2(b-a)=2(\mathsf{s}_1(z'')-\mathsf{s}_1(z')) = 2 (z''-z') (\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon+z)
\le C_{\mathsf{k}} n_\varepsilon \le c_\star n_\varepsilon \log j
\end{equation}
provided $\mathsf {K}_{0}$ is large enough.  In that case we deduce from (\ref{A.2-n}) that as $\mathsf {K}_{\mathsf{a}} = o(n_\varepsilon)$,  
\begin{equation}\label{eq:step1-123}
\sum_{j=\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\mathsf {K}_{\mathsf{a}}} 
\sup_{\beta} \mathbb{P}\Big( T^{\mathsf{x},b}_{j} -T^{\mathsf{x},a}_{j} \ge c_\star n_\varepsilon \log j \,\big|\, \mathcal{G}^{\tau} \Big) \le 
\mathsf {K}_{\mathsf{a}} e^{-c \, c_\star n_\varepsilon \log \mathsf {K}_{\mathsf{a}}/\mathsf {K}_{\mathsf{a}}} = o_\varepsilon(1) \,.
\end{equation}
Further,  in view of (\ref{atot-new}),  for some other finite $C_{\mathsf{k},z}$, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:step2-123}
\varlimsup_{\varepsilon \to 0} \Big\{ e^{2 n_\varepsilon} \sup_{\beta,\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F}^{\beta}} 
\mathbb{P} \big( \mathcal{U}^{(\varepsilon),\beta,\langle z' \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\mathsf{v}} \cap \mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}_{\beta}^{\,\langle z' \rangle} \big)  \Big\} \le C_{\mathsf{k},z} 
\end{equation}
and as $\mathcal{U}^{(\varepsilon),\beta,\langle z' \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\mathsf{v}} \cap \mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}_{\beta}^{\,\langle z' \rangle}$ is measurable on $\mathcal{G}^{\tau}$ we get (\ref{eq:U-plus-123}) 
upon combining (\ref{eq:step1-123}) and (\ref{eq:step2-123}).

For (\ref{eq:U-plus-45}) we use instead (\ref{eq:Jay4.14-n}) at levels $j \in \mathsf {J}$. 
Indeed,  $\mathbb{F}^\beta \subset \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},r_{n_\varepsilon^{(5)}})$ and since the part of the Brownian path 
(after $\tau$) that is not measurable on  $\mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{x}, \tau}_j$  is contained within $\mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},r_{j-1})$,
the excursion counts $T^{[\tau,\tau']}_{\mathsf{x},j}$ can be read off the {path,  after $\tau$}, 
outside $\mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},r_{j-1})$ and therefore these counts are $\mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{x}, \tau}_j$-measurable
(even though the time $\tau'=S_{\mathsf{k}_\varepsilon(z)}$ is not,  since it depends on the time spent by the Brownian 
motion inside $\mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},r_{j-1})$).
                                  
Applying the tail bound (\ref{eq:Jay4.14-n}) in this setting,  we thus deduce that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:step1-45}
\sum_{j=\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{n_\varepsilon-\mathsf {K}_{5}}
\sup_{\beta,\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F}^\beta} 
\mathbb{P}\Big( T_{\mathsf{v},n_\varepsilon+1}^{[\tau,\tau']} = 0\,|\, \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{x},\tau}_{j}, 
T^{[\tau,\tau']}_{j} \ge \ell_j  \Big) \le \sum_{j=\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{n_\varepsilon-\mathsf {K}_{5}} 
e^{- c \, j_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa'}}/3} = o_{\mathsf {K}_{0},\mathsf {K}_{5}}(1) \,.
\end{equation}
As before,  combining (\ref{eq:step2-123}) and  (\ref{eq:step1-45}) yields (\ref{eq:U-plus-45}),
thereby completing the proof.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
For $\tau'=S_{\mathsf{k}_\varepsilon}(z)$ and  $\tau=\tau_{\mathsf{v}_\beta}(\mathsf{s}_1(z'))$,   the event $\{\tau' \ge \tau\}$ is part of  the
conditions in $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k},\beta}^{[z]}$ (see (\ref{def:Jay-Thm4.1})).  In that case we also have that 
$T_{\mathsf{v},n_\varepsilon+1}^{[\tau,\tau']} \le T_{\mathsf{v},n_\varepsilon+1}^{[z]}$ and recall  (\ref{def:AUvz}) that 
$\{ T_{\mathsf{v},n_\varepsilon+1}^{[z]} = 0\}$ is part of $\mathcal{A}\, \mathcal{U}_{\mathsf{k},\mathsf{v}}^{(\varepsilon),\beta,[z]}$.  Next,  
recall (\ref{def:Jay-Thm4.1-cons}) 
that $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k},\beta}^{[z]}$ implies having $\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,j}^{\,[z]} \in [\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,j}^{\,\langle z' \rangle},\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,j}^{\,\langle z'' \rangle}]$ for all $j$.  Thus,  setting 
\begin{align*}
\mathcal{W}'_{\beta,j}:= \Big\{ \mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k},\beta}^{[z]}, \mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}_{\beta}^{\,\langle z' \rangle},  L_{\beta,j}^{[z]} \notin \mathbb{B}^{\infty}_{\bar \mu} (2\boldsymbol{\eta}^{(\varepsilon)}_j) \Big\}\,,&
\qquad
\mathcal{B}'_{\beta,j} := \Big\{  \mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k},\beta}^{[z]}, \mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}_{\beta}^{\,\langle z' \rangle},  \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,j}^{\,[z]} \ge j_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa'}} \Big\}
                                                                                                   
                                                                                
\end{align*}
upon comparing (\ref{dfn:bw}) at $z$ with (\ref{dfn:bw-Jay}) at $z'$,   
and recalling (\ref{dfn:J-intervals}),  (\ref{dfn:windows}),  it follows that 
\begin{align}
 \mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k},\beta}^{[z]} \cap \mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}_{\beta}^{\,\langle z' \rangle} \setminus  \mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}_{\beta}^{[z]} &\subset \bigcup_{j \in \mathsf {J}'_\mathsf{a}}  \mathcal{W}'_{\beta,j} \bigcup_{j \in \mathsf {J}} 
 \mathcal{B}'_{\beta,j} \,.
\label{dfn:bb-extra}
\end{align}
In view of (\ref{dfn:bb-extra}) we conclude the proof upon showing that 
$\mathcal{W}'_{\beta,j} \subset \mathcal{W}^\star_{\mathsf{v}_\beta,j}$ and $\mathcal{B}'_{\beta,j} \subset \mathcal{B}^\star_{\mathsf{v}_\beta,j}$.  
To this end,   recall that $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k},\beta}^{[z]}$ implies that
                                 
$\tau' \in [\tau_{\mathsf{v}}(a),\tau_{\mathsf{v}}(b)]$ and $\mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}_{\beta}^{\,\langle z' \rangle}$ 
implies that  $L_{\beta,j}^{\langle z' \rangle} \in \mathbb{B}^{\infty}_{\bar \mu} \big(\boldsymbol{\eta}^{(\varepsilon)}_j \big)$.  Hence by 
(\ref{dfn:emp-ang}),  (\ref{dfn:Poiss}) 
 and (\ref{eq:dinf-comp}) 
(at $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\eta}}=c^{-1} \,  \boldsymbol{\eta}^{(\varepsilon)}_j$,  $c := 2\pi (\sqrt{1+\bar{c}^2} + \bar c)$),  if in addition 
$L_{\beta,j}^{[z]} \notin \mathbb{B}^{\infty}_{\bar \mu} (2 \boldsymbol{\eta}^{(\varepsilon)}_j)$ then necessarily 
$ T_{\beta,j}^{[z]} \ge (1 + c^{-1} \,  \boldsymbol{\eta}^{(\varepsilon)}_j) T_{j}^{\mathsf{v}_\beta,a}$,  which under $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k},\beta}^{[z]} \cap \mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}_{\beta}^{\,\langle z' \rangle}$ yields
for $c_\star := \frac{\kappa_\star}{2c}$,  any $\varepsilon$ small enough and all $j \in \big[\mathsf{k},\mathsf {K}_{\mathsf{a}}]$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Tb-Ta-W}
T_{j}^{\mathsf{v}_\beta,b} - T_{j}^{\mathsf{v}_\beta,a} \ge T_{\beta,j}^{[z]} -  T_{j}^{\mathsf{v}_\beta,a} \ge  c^{-1} \,  \boldsymbol{\eta}^{(\varepsilon)}_j T_{j}^{\mathsf{v}_\beta,a} \ge 
\frac{\gamma_0(\mathsf {K}_{\mathsf{a}})^2}{\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon} c_\star  \log j \ge c_\star n_\varepsilon \log j 
\end{equation}
(recall (\ref{def:mn-alt}),  (\ref{def.nvep}),   (\ref{eq:norm-exc}),  (\ref{dfn:bw-Jay}),
(\ref{dfn:windows-alt}) and $\mathsf {K}_{\mathsf{a}}=o(n_\varepsilon)$).  That is,  $\mathcal{W}'_{\beta,j} \subset \mathcal{W}^\star_{\mathsf{v}_\beta,j}$ as claimed.
Similarly,  for any  $j \in \mathsf {J}$,  having in $\mathcal{B}'_{\beta,j}$ 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:diff-hateta}
\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,j}^{\,[z]} \ge j_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa'}} \quad \text{and} \quad \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,j}^{\,\langle z' \rangle} \le \frac{1}{2} j_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa'}} \,,  
\end{equation}
implies that for $\mathsf{v}=\mathsf{v}_\beta$ and all $\varepsilon$ small enough 
                          
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Tb-Ta-nvf}
T_{\mathsf{v},j}^{[\tau_{\mathsf{v}}(a),\tau']}=T_{\mathsf{v},j}^{[z]} - T_{j}^{\mathsf{v},a} \ge \frac{1}{2} \gamma_0(j)
(\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,j}^{\,[z]}-\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,j}^{\,\langle z' \rangle})
\ge \frac{1}{4} \gamma_0(j) j_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa'}}  
\ge  \frac{1}{3} (n_\varepsilon-j) j_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa'}} \,.
\end{equation}
That is,  $\mathcal{B}'_{\beta,j} \subset \mathcal{B}^\star_{\mathsf{v}_\beta,j}$,  which concludes the proof of the lemma.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- proposition-11: body_md -->
\label{theo-etrt} For small $\widetilde{c}, r_0>0$ there exist finite $
   
c(r_0,\widetilde{c})$ and 
$
   
d(r_0,\widetilde{c})$ such that with $\widetilde\mathsf{s}(\cdot)$ of (\ref{clt.2}) and $\tau_{\mathsf{v}}(\cdot)$ of (\ref{eq-taux}), for any $\varepsilon$ sufficiently small and all $z,z_0$ satisfying $|z| \vee z_0 \leq \sqrt{n_{\varepsilon}}$, 
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{P}\( \widetilde \mathsf{s} \left(z-d\sqrt{z_{0}}\right)     \leq \pi \tau_{\mathsf{v}}\(\widetilde \mathsf{s} \left(z \right) \)\leq  \widetilde \mathsf{s} \left(z+d\sqrt{z_{0}}\right),\,\forall \mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F}
            
\)\geq 1-ce^{-4z_{0}}.\label{r1.1}
\end{equation}
Moreover,  with $\mathsf{s}_1(\cdot)$ of (\ref{eq:nominal}),  for any such $\varepsilon$ and $z$,
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{Q})\geq 1-ce^{-n_{\varepsilon}/2}, \label{g17.0b}
\end{equation} 
where 
\begin{equation*}
  \mathcal{Q}:=\{ \tau_{\mathsf{y}}\(\mathsf{s}_1(z)-10\)\leq \tau_{\mathsf{x}}\(\mathsf{s}_1(z)\)\leq \tau_{\mathsf{y}}\(\mathsf{s}_1(z)+10\),\,\forall 
  \mathsf{x},\mathsf{y} \in \mathbb{F}
              
  , \, \mathsf{d} (\mathsf{x},\mathsf{y})\leq  r_{n_{\varepsilon/2}}\}.
               
\end{equation*}
<!-- end proposition-11 -->
<!-- proposition-12: body_md -->
\label{gprop:MainGoalEasyRegime} 
For small  $\widetilde{c}$, $r_0$ and $c,d$ as in Proposition \ref{theo-etrt},  we have for any $\mathsf{k} \ge 1$,
\begin{align}
 \widetilde{q}_{\mathsf{k}}(z) :=  \varlimsup_{\varepsilon \to 0} \mathbb{P} \big( (\mathcal{R}_{\mathsf{k}}^{\langle z \rangle})^{\complement} \big)
& \leq 
c
e^{-2(z  - d  \sqrt{|z|})} e^{-\mathsf{k}^{{\kappa_o}}/5}\,.
\label{g17.0}
\end{align}
<!-- end proposition-12 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
Taking $\widetilde{c}$, $r_0$ small enough,  we have by (\ref{r1.1}) (replacing $d\sqrt{z_0}$ by $t$) that for fixed $t$,
                     
\begin{align}
\label{eq-110926b}
1 - \varliminf_{\varepsilon\to 0} \,  \inf_{|z| \le \sqrt{n_\varepsilon}} \,
\mathbb{P} \Big(\widetilde \mathsf{s} (z-t) \le \pi \tau_{\mathsf{v}} (\, \widetilde \mathsf{s} (z)) \le \widetilde \mathsf{s} (z+t),\, 
 \forall \mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F} \Big)
             
 \le c e^{-4 t^2/d} := q_{t}  \,.
\end{align}
Letting
                      
\begin{equation}\label{eq:needed-Jay2.1}
C_1=C_1(\widetilde{c},r_0):=
 4 \sup_{\mathsf{k}} \big\{ \mathsf{k}^4 q_{\, {2 \log \mathsf{k}-6}}
\big\}< \infty \,,
\end{equation}
we proceed to {establish}  the first claim in (\ref{eq:Jay-Thm-4.2}) {by showing}
that, without restriction on $z,\mathsf{k}$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Jay-Thm-4.1}
\varliminf_{\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon}
\mathbb{P}\big(\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k}}^{[z]} \cap \mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k}}^{[z-2\log \mathsf{k}]} \big) \ge 1 - C_1 \mathsf{k}^{-4} \;.
\end{equation}
To see (\ref{eq:Jay-Thm-4.1}),  recall from (\ref{dfn:bar-svep}) and the proof of \Cref{lem:conc} (see (\ref{eq-amirswriteup}))
that the time $S_\ell$ it takes
                   
to complete $\ell$ inter-city excursions is such that 
$(S_{\mathsf{k}_\varepsilon(z)} - \frac{1}{\pi} \bar \mathsf{s}_\varepsilon(z))/\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon \stackrel{p}{\to} 0$ 
                                           
as $\varepsilon \to 0$ followed by $\mathsf {K}_{0} \to \infty$.  In view of the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} of (\ref{def:Jay-Thm4.1}), 
it suffices for (\ref{eq:Jay-Thm-4.1}) to show that for any $z$,
                         
\begin{equation}
\label{eq-110926a}
\varliminf_{\varepsilon\to 0} \mathbb{P} \Big(
\tau_{\mathsf{v}} (\mathsf{s}_1 (z')) \le \frac{1}{\pi} \bar \mathsf{s}_\varepsilon(z-1) \le \frac{1}{\pi} \bar \mathsf{s}_\varepsilon(z+1) \le
\tau_{\mathsf{v}} (\mathsf{s}_1 (z'')),  \forall \mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F} \Big) \ge 1 -  \frac{1}{2} {C_1} \mathsf{k}^{-4} \,.
\end{equation}
(Indeed, if the latter hold for $z$ then it also holds when $z$ is replaced by  $z-2\log \mathsf{k}$, 
with the appropriate changes in $z'$ and $z''$.)
                                                                                         
Recall that $\bar \mathsf{s}_\varepsilon(y)=\mathsf{s}_1(y)$ and  
$\widetilde \mathsf{s} (2y-2) \le \mathsf{s}_1(y) \le \widetilde \mathsf{s}(2y+2)$ for any $y$ and all $\varepsilon \le \varepsilon_o$  
(see (\ref{clt.2})).  It thus suffices for (\ref{eq-110926a}) 
to show that for $t=2 \log \mathsf{k}-6$ and $\widehat{z} = 2 z {\pm} 2( \log \mathsf{k} -1)$, 
\[
\varliminf_{\varepsilon\to 0} \mathbb{P} \Big(
\widetilde \mathsf{s} (\hat{z}-t) \le \pi \tau_{\mathsf{v}} (\widetilde \mathsf{s} (\widehat{z})) \le \widetilde \mathsf{s}(\widehat{z}+t)  
, \;\; \forall \mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F} \Big) \ge 1 -  \frac{1}{4} C_1 \mathsf{k}^{-4} \,,
\]
which in turn follows from (\ref{eq-110926b}) and (\ref{eq:needed-Jay2.1}).
                                                         

Next,  
by (\ref{def:Jay-Thm4.1-cons}),  the event  $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k}}^{[z-2\log \mathsf{k}]}$ implies that $\mathcal{R}_{\mathsf{k}}^{\langle z - 3 \log \mathsf{k} \rangle} \subset \widetilde{\mathcal{R}}_{\mathsf{k}}^{\langle z' \rangle}$ 
and therefore 
\begin{equation}
\label{eq-120926c}
\big(\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k}}^{[z]}\cap \mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k}}^{[z-2\log \mathsf{k}]} \cap\mathcal{R}_{\mathsf{k}}^{\langle z - 3 \log \mathsf{k} \rangle}\big)\subset  \big(\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k}}^{[z]}\cap \mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k}}^{[z-2\log \mathsf{k}]} \cap\widetilde{\mathcal{R}}_{\mathsf{k}}^{\langle z' \rangle}\big)\subset \big(\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k}}^{[z]} \cap\widetilde{\mathcal{R}}_{\mathsf{k}}^{\langle z' \rangle}\big).\end{equation}
                                
We show below that,  with $\widetilde{q}_\mathsf{k}(\cdot)$ of (\ref{g17.0}),  it holds that
                                                                                                                                   
\begin{equation}\label{eq:needed-Jay2.2}
C_2=C_2(\widetilde{c},r_0) := \sup_{\mathsf{k} \ge 1} \sup_{11 z \ge - \mathsf{k}^{\kappa_o}} \{ \mathsf{k}^4 \widetilde{q}_\mathsf{k} (z-3 \log \mathsf{k}) \} < \infty \,.
\end{equation}
We then  get the second half of (\ref{eq:Jay-Thm-4.2}) with $C=C_1+C_2$  by combining (\ref{eq:Jay-Thm-4.1}),
(\ref{eq-120926c}) and \Cref{gprop:MainGoalEasyRegime} with $z$ replaced by $z-3\log \mathsf{k}$.

It remains to check (\ref{eq:needed-Jay2.2}). Since
          
$2 d \sqrt{|z-3\log \mathsf{k}|} \le 10 d^2 + (|z| +3 \log \mathsf{k})/10$,   we get from (\ref{g17.0}) that 
\[
\mathsf{k}^4 \widetilde{q}_\mathsf{k}(z-3 \log \mathsf{k}) \le c e^{10\, d^2} \mathsf{k}^{11} e^{- \frac{1}{5} \mathsf{k}^{{\kappa_o}} - 2z + \frac{|z|}{10}}
\]
which is more than enough for (\ref{eq:needed-Jay2.2}).
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{lem-clt}
Setting $\kappa_{a,b}:=\frac{1}{\pi} \log(b/a)$,  for some $c'>0$ any $0<a<b<1/2$,  
$\delta \in (0,c')$,  $m \ge 2$ and $\mathsf{v}, \mathsf{y}\in\mathbb{T}^{2}$,
\begin{align}
\mathbb{P}^{\mathsf{y}}\Big( (1-\delta) m \le 
\kappa_{a,b}^{-1} \tau_{\mathsf{v}, a,b}(m) \le (1+\delta) m \Big)& \geq 1 - e^{-c \delta^{2} m},\label{clt.1}
\end{align}
where  $c= c(a,b):=c' b (1-a/b)^{6} | \log a|^{-2}$.
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label{rlem:Continuity lemma}
                         
Fixing $r_1$,  $\widetilde{c}>0$,  there exists $a_0$,  $c$ finite,  so for any {$|z| \vee z_0 \le \sqrt{n_\varepsilon}$} 
and $n_{\varepsilon}$ large enough, 
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{P} \Big[\exists \mathsf{y} \in  \mathbb{F}_{\frac{3}{2}\log n_{\varepsilon}}\cap  \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}\left({\bf 0},\widetilde{c}\, \tilde r_{0}\right)
       
\label{req: continuity goal}
  
 \mbox{ s.t. }\left|T_{{\bf 0},\tilde{r}_{1} }^{{\bf 0},\tilde{r}_{-1},\widetilde \mathsf{s} (z)}-
T_{\mathsf{y},\tilde{r}_{1} }^{{\bf 0},\tilde{r}_{-1},\widetilde \mathsf{s} (z)}\right|\ge a_0 \sqrt{z_{0}} n_{\varepsilon} \Big]\le ce^{-4z_{0}}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
Recall that $\widetilde \mathsf{s} (z) = 2 n_\varepsilon^2 (1+o_\varepsilon (1))$,  see (\ref{clt.2}).  Hence,  
by \Cref{lem-clt} with $m=\widetilde \mathsf{s} (z)$ and $\delta=d\sqrt{z_{0}} n_\varepsilon/m$,  
we get that for all $\varepsilon$ small enough,  uniformly in $\mathsf{v}, \mathsf{y} \in\mathbb{T}^{2}$,
\begin{eqnarray}
\mathbb{P}^{\mathsf{y}} \Big( \widetilde \mathsf{s} (z-d\sqrt{z_0}) \leq  
\kappa_{a,b}^{-1} \tau_{\mathsf{v},a,b}(\widetilde \mathsf{s}(z)) \leq  \widetilde \mathsf{s} (z+d\sqrt{z_{0}}) \Big) 
\geq 1-e^{-c d^2 z_0/3}.
\label{clt.3a}
\end{eqnarray}
Taking $a=r_1$, $b=r_0$ and $d^2 c(a, b) \ge 30$ in (\ref{clt.3a}) yields 
{
\begin{equation}\label{clt.3a-new}
\inf_{\mathsf{v},\mathsf{y} \in \mathbb{T}^2}
\mathbb{P}^{\mathsf{y}} \big( \,  \widetilde \mathsf{s} \left(z-d\sqrt{z_{0}}\right)     \leq \pi \tau_{\mathsf{v}}\(\widetilde \mathsf{s} \left(z \right) \)
\leq  \widetilde \mathsf{s} \left(z+d\sqrt{z_{0}}\right) \,
            
\big) \geq 1-e^{-10 \, z_{0}} \,.
\end{equation}}
                             
                                                                                                                                                    
With $|\mathbb{F}_{n_{\varepsilon}}|$ diverging in $\varepsilon$, 
we get (\ref{r1.1}) out of (\ref{clt.3a-new}) via a chaining argument,  as in the 
derivation of \cite[Thm.  3.1]{BRZ2} out of \cite[(6.4)]{BRZ2}.  Indeed,  we
replace the factors $4$ and $\sqrt{z}$ of
\cite[(6.4)]{BRZ2} by $\frac{1}{\pi}$ and $\sqrt{z_0}$ of (\ref{clt.3a-new}),
then having here $h(r)=r$,  $L=n_\varepsilon$ and $\tilde{r}_i$ of (\ref{eq:tilde-ri}) set 
as in \cite{BRZ2},   we replace \cite[Lemma 6.2]{BRZ2}  by \Cref{rlem:Continuity lemma}.

Finally,  the direct 
proof of \cite[Thm.  3.8]{BRZ2} via a union bound (see \cite[Sec.  6]{BRZ2}),  applies
here with no change,  to yield (\ref{g17.0b}).
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{lem-sec3.3}
For $r_0, \widetilde{c}>0$ small enough,  some finite $C=C(r_0, \widetilde{c})$,  {$t=t_{\widehat z}$ of (\ref{def:tz-alpha})
and} any fixed
$\widehat z \in \mathbb{R}$,  all large enough $n_\varepsilon$,  any $l \in  (5 \log n_\varepsilon, n_{\varepsilon}]$ and $j \in [0, 12 n_\varepsilon]$,
\begin{align}\label{cb.15y}
\mathbb{P}\left(\mathcal{B}_{t,l}\,\big |\,\widetilde{\mathcal{C}}_{t,l} (j) \cap\mathcal{D}_{t,l} (j)\right)    &  \le Ce^{-4j } \,, \\
\mathbb{P}\left(\mathcal{B}_{t,l}\,\big|\, \mathcal{D}_{t,l}(   j)\right) & \leq C e^{ -4j}\,.
\label{17.1sv}
\end{align}
Further,  (\ref{17.1sv}) holds also for $l \in [\mathsf{k},5 \log n_\varepsilon]$ and $j \in [\frac{1}{4} l^{{\kappa_o}},12l]$.
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{lem:4.58m}  
For small enough $\widetilde{c}>0$,  any $d_0>0$,  some finite $j_o$,  any 
${t}, m \ge 1$,
                                 
 all $j_o \le j \le 12 n_\varepsilon$,  {$l \ge h_{l,j}+1$ of (\ref{wCdefr}) and}
$\widetilde \mathsf{y},  \mathsf{y} \in \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}\left({\bf 0},\widetilde{c}\, r_{l}\right)$ 
with $\tilde q:=\mathsf{d} \left(\mathsf{y}, \widetilde \mathsf{y}\right)/r_{l} \ge \frac{\widetilde{c}}{4} {\beta_{l,j}}$ 
{for $\beta_{l,j}$ of (\ref{BRZ2-355})},
\begin{equation}
  \label{eq-thanks4lem}
 \sup_{u\in I_{\alpha(l)+j}}
 \mathbb{P}\Big(
\big| 
\ensuremath{T_{\widetilde \mathsf{y},\widetilde r_{l-1}^+\to \widetilde r_l}^{{\bf 0},r_{l-2}\overset{u^2/2}{\to}r_{l-3}} }
 -\ensuremath{T_{\mathsf{y},\widetilde r_{l-1}^+\to \widetilde r_l}^{{\bf 0},r_{l-2}\overset{u^2/2}{\to}r_{l-3}} }
 \big| \ge \frac{d_{0}}{2} j  \, m \, 
u \sqrt{\tilde q} \,\Big|\,  \mathcal{G}^{\bf 0}_{{l-h_{i,j}}},
                      
T_{l-2}^{{\bf 0},t} = \frac{u^2}{2} \Big)
\leq  e^{-4(j+ m)}\,.
                                              
\end{equation}
The same applies without conditioning,  for any $l \in [3,n_\varepsilon]$ and $m \le 1/(j_o \beta_{l,j})$.
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
{We start by showing that (\ref{cb.15y}) holds for any $t \ge 1$}.  Recall that for 
the values of $l$,  $j$ considered here,  $\bar k := l - h_{l,j} \ge \mathsf{k}$.  Hence, 
upon replacing $\mathcal{C}_{0,t,l}$ of \cite[(3.49)]{BRZ2} by $\widetilde{\mathcal{C}}_{t,l}(j)$ 
(i.e.,  dropping part of the barrier in order to handle the conditioning without symmetry),  
and setting as in \cite[(3.58)]{BRZ2}
\begin{equation}\label{BRZ2-358}
{ k_{l,j}:=l+\log(2/\beta_{l,j}), }
\end{equation}
restricted {\sc\lowercase{wlog}} to ${k_{l,j}} \le n_\varepsilon$,
the proof of (\ref{cb.15y}) is identical to that of \cite[Lemma 3.10]{BRZ2},   apart from replacing 
\cite[Lemma 3.11]{BRZ2} by the bound of (\ref{eq-thanks4lem}),  where $d_0$ and $\widetilde \mathsf{y}$
are chosen as in \cite[(3.67)]{BRZ2}.  {Indeed,  since} $\mathsf{y},  \widetilde \mathsf{y} \in \mathbb{F}_{{k_{l,j}}}$ they are either 
the same or of distance at least $\frac{\widetilde{c}}{2}  r_{k_{l,j}} \ge \frac{\widetilde{c}}{4} \beta_{l,j} r_l$,  {while} 
the measurability of $\widetilde{\mathcal{C}}_{t,l} (j)$ on $\mathcal{G}^{\bf 0}_{\bar k}$ (of \Cref{def:Fvjs}),  allowed us to 
enlarge the conditioning in our analog of \cite[(3.72)]{BRZ2}.

Turning to prove (\ref{17.1sv}) {at $t=t_{\widehat{z}}$ and fixed $\widehat{z} \in \mathbb{R}$},
we follow the proof of \cite[Lemma 3.7]{BRZ2},  noting that {for any $t \ge 1$}
the bound of \cite[(3.66)]{BRZ2} 
applies for $\mathfrak{P}_{31}$ of \cite[(3.61)]{BRZ2} which involves concentric excursion counts.
Hence,  {setting for $\widetilde r_{l}$ of (\ref{BRZ2-355}) and $k_{l,j}$ of (\ref{BRZ2-358}) the event
\[
 \mathcal{B}_{t,l,j}:=\Big\{ \exists \mathsf{y}\in \mathbb{F}_{k_{l,j}}\cap \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}\left({\bf 0},\tilde{c}\, r_{l} \right)
 \mbox{ such that }\sqrt{2T_{\mathsf{y},\widetilde r_{l}}^{{\bf 0}, t}}\le \alpha(l)\Big\}
                  
\]
(which is $\mathcal{B}_{t,l}^{\beta,k}$ of \cite[(3.57)]{BRZ2}), 
and using the notation of} \cite[(3.60)]{BRZ2} it suffices to bound 
\begin{align}\label{eq-P3}
\mathfrak{P}_{32} & := \mathbb{P} \Big(\mathcal{B}_{t,l,j}\cap 
\Big\{\sqrt{2T_{\widetilde r_{l}}^{{\bf 0}, t }}>\alpha(l)+\frac{j}{2}\Big\}\,\big|\, \mathcal{D}_{t,l}(j) \Big) \,.
\end{align}
        
                                                                                                                                                                    
   
To this end,  for $l > 5 \log n_{\varepsilon}$ and $j \le 12 n_\varepsilon$ we proceed as before, 
apart from omitting $\mathcal{C}_{0,t,l}$,  up to the top line of \cite[(3.72)]{BRZ2}.  In this case
one has that $l > \mathsf{k} + h_{l,j}$, 
so we can again further condition on $\mathcal{G}^{\bf 0}_{\bar k}$ and utilize  (\ref{eq-thanks4lem}).  
Finally,  fixing hereafter $\widehat{z}$,  $l \in [\mathsf{k},5 \log n_\varepsilon]$ and $j \in [\frac{1}{4} l^{{\kappa_o}},12l]$,  
for {$t=t_{\widehat{z}}$ and} $\sqrt{2t'} \in I_{\alpha(l)+j}$ we
decompose the event $\mathcal{D}_{t,l}(j)$ in (\ref{eq-P3}) according to the 
value $t'$ of $T_{l-2}^{{\bf 0},t}$. 
  Thereby,  we 
condition on having precisely $t'$ of the $(l-2)$-level excursions around ${\bf 0}$ 
completed during the first $t=(\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon+\widehat{z})^2/2$ (outer)
excursions from $\partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}({\bf 0},r_1)$ to $\partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}({\bf 0},r_0)$.  These inner excursions 
thus correspond to the measure $\mathbb{P}_{t,b,b}$ of \Cref{prop:coupling} with
$R=r_1$ and at the values $k=l-3$,
                                                             
$t=t_{\widehat{z}}$ and $b:=t'-t$,  
which we then compare with the unconditional law
$\mathbb{P}^\star_{t'}$ of the $t'$ first inner excursions.  To this end, 
                        
we proceed to verify that $(t,l-3,5j,b) \in \Theta_{\kappa_0}$ of (\ref{dfn:Thetak}) for some universal $\kappa_0>0$.  Indeed,
we assume {\sc\lowercase{wlog}} that $\mathsf{k} \ge 3 + \kappa_0^{-3}$ and that $n_\varepsilon$ is large enough so that
$\sqrt{t}  \in [n_\varepsilon,2n_\varepsilon]$.  Then,  for some $\kappa_0>0$,  both 
                         
$5 j \le 60 l \le 300 \log n_\varepsilon \le \kappa_0^{-1} \log t$ and
$|b| \le (\sqrt{2t} + j) | j-\boldsymbol{\rho}_\varepsilon l-l^{{\kappa_o}}-\widehat z\,| \le  \kappa_0^{-1} (l \vee 5j) \sqrt{t}$.
With all the conditions of \Cref{prop:coupling} satisfied,  we see from  (\ref{eq:coupling}) that with  
some universal $\bar c >1$ and a single event $\mathcal{E}^{t'}_{t,l}(j)$ 
of probability at most $C l e^{-5j}$,  given that $\{T_{l-2}^{{\bf 0},t}=t'\}$,  
we match all but at most 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:N-def}
N := 35 {\bar c} \kappa_0 j \sqrt{t_{\widehat{z}}} \,,
\end{equation}
of our conditional inner excursions with the first such $t'$ unconditional inner excursions. 
Noting that,
\[
\mathfrak{P}_{32} \le C l e^{-5j} + \sup_{\sqrt{2t'} \in I_{\alpha(l)+j}} \mathbb{P}_{t,b,b} \Big(\mathcal{B}_{t,l,j}\cap 
\Big\{\sqrt{2T_{\widetilde r_{l}}^{{\bf 0}, t}}>\alpha(l)+\frac{j}{2}\Big\}\cap \mathcal{E}^{t'}_{t,l}(j)^{\complement}\,  \Big) \,,
\]
we follow the argument leading to \cite[(3.71)]{BRZ2},  now with the law
$\mathbb{P}_{t,b,b}$ instead of conditioning on $\mathcal{C}_{0,t,l} \cap \mathcal{D}_{t,l}(j)$
while intersecting each event there with $\mathcal{E}^{t'}_{t,l}(j)^{\complement}$.  With $l e^{-j}$ bounded uniformly over
$j \ge \frac{1}{4} l^{\kappa_o}$,
we arrive,  as in \cite[(3.74)]{BRZ2},  to $\mathfrak{P}_{32} \le C e^{-4j}$,  upon replacing 
\cite[Lemma 3.11]{BRZ2} by the following claim:\\
For small $\widetilde{c}>0$,  
any $m \le \log (2/{\beta_{l,j}})$,  $\sqrt{2t'} \in  I_{\alpha(l)+j}$ and
$\widetilde \mathsf{y},  \mathsf{y} \in \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}\left({\bf 0},\widetilde{c} \,  r_{l}\right)$, 
with $\tilde q:=\mathsf{d} \left(\mathsf{y}, \widetilde \mathsf{y}\right)/r_{l} \ge \frac{\widetilde{c}}{4} \beta_{l,j}$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq-mod-458}
\mathbb{P}_{t,b,b} \Big(
\big| 
\ensuremath{T_{\widetilde \mathsf{y},\widetilde r_{l-1}^+\to \widetilde r_l}^{{\bf 0},r_{l-2}\overset{t'}{\to}r_{l-3}} }
-\ensuremath{T_{\mathsf{y},\widetilde r_{l-1}^+\to \widetilde r_l}^{{\bf 0},r_{l-2}\overset{t'}{\to}r_{l-3}} }
 \big|\ge d_{0} j  \, m \, 
\sqrt{2 t' \tilde q} \,,\; \mathcal{E}^{t'}_{t,l}(j)^{\complement} \Big) \leq  3 e^{-4(j+ m)}  \,.
\end{equation}
{Turning to show (\ref{eq-mod-458}),  we set}
$\tilde{R}=r_{l-3}$,  $\tilde{r} = r_{l-2}$,  $R=\widetilde r_{l-1}^+$ and $r=\widetilde r_l$
(which satisfy (\ref{eq-ratiobounds})),  {noting}
that 
the tail bound (\ref{basicexp2}) applies for the contribution to the difference 
within (\ref{eq-mod-458}) from the $N$ possibly \emph{non-matched excursions} 
$\partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}({\bf 0},\tilde{r})\to\partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}({\bf 0},\tilde{R})$.  Thus,  using 
                     
the matching to $\mathbb{P}_{t'}^\star$ up to $N$ inner excursions
(which holds on $\mathcal{E}^{t'}_{t,l}(j)^{\complement}$),  we get (\ref{eq-mod-458}) by combining 
the unconditional version of (\ref{eq-thanks4lem}) at $u=\sqrt{2t'}$,  with the bound of 
(\ref{basicexp2}) at $\varphi= \frac{d_{0}}{2} j  \, m \,  \sqrt{2 t' \tilde q}$ and $N$ of (\ref{eq:N-def}).
Indeed,  with $\tilde q \le 2 \widetilde c$ and $t'/t_{\widehat{z}} \to 1$ for $\varepsilon \to 0$,  clearly
$\varphi \ge 2 c_3 \tilde q N$ for small enough $\widetilde c (c_3 \bar c \kappa_0/d_0)$.
                                                   
Further,  since $j,  l = o(n_\varepsilon)$ we have that $2 t' \tilde q \ge \frac{\widetilde c}{2} t' {\beta_{l,j}} = \Omega(n_\varepsilon)$,
resulting with $\varphi = \Omega (\sqrt{n_\varepsilon})$.  Similarly $N = \Omega(n_\varepsilon)$, 
while $j$ and $m$ are at most $O(\log n_\varepsilon)$,  hence $\varphi \wedge N \ge 8 (j+m)$ and 
the proof {of (\ref{eq-mod-458})} is thus complete.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
We assume {\sc\lowercase{wlog}} that $\mathsf{k}^{\kappa_o} \ge 10 z_-$ (otherwise (\ref{g17.0}) holds trivially).  Setting 
$L' := n_\varepsilon - (10 \log n_\varepsilon)^{1/{\kappa_o}}$ we first establish (\ref{g17.0}) while restricting in (\ref{eq:JayThm2.2eq})
to the ``not too large" levels $j \in [\mathsf{k}, L']$.  To this end,  
utilizing (\ref{r1.1}) allows us,  as in \cite[(3.11)]{BRZ2},  to intersect 
the event in (\ref{eq:JayThm2.2eq}) with 
\[
\mathcal{A}_{z,d \sqrt{z_0}} := \Big\{ \tau_{\mathsf{y}} (t_{z-d\sqrt{z_0}}) \le \tau_{\mathsf{x}} (t_z) \le \tau_{\mathsf{y}}(t_{z+d\sqrt{z_0}}),  \;\;
\forall \mathsf{x},\mathsf{y} \in \mathbb{F}_{n_\varepsilon} \Big\} \,,
\]
where taking here $z_0=|z|+\mathsf{k}^{{\kappa_o}}$ (instead of $z_0=z$ of \cite[(3.11)]{BRZ2}),  guarantees having 
$\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{A}_{z,d\sqrt{z_0}}^{\complement})$ much smaller than the bound of  (\ref{g17.0}).  We thus
follow the proof in \cite[Section 3.1]{BRZ2},  replacing \cite[(3.15)]{BRZ2} by 
$\widehat z := z - d \sqrt{z_0}$,  to deduce that it suffices to show  for some 
$\underline{\theta} =\underline{\theta} (l,n_\varepsilon)$,  $\bar \theta=\bar \theta (l,n_\varepsilon)$ and any $l \in [\mathsf{k},L']$,  
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{P}(\sqrt{2T_{l-2}^{{\bf 0},t_{\widehat z}}} \le \alpha(l)+\underline{\theta}) + 
\sum_{j=\underline{\theta}}^{\bar \theta-1} \mathbb{P}(\mathcal{B}_{t_{\widehat z},l} \cap \mathcal{D}_{t_{\widehat z},l}(j) )
+ \mathbb{P}(\sqrt{2T_{l-2}^{{\bf 0},t_{\widehat z}}} \ge \alpha(l)+\bar \theta) 
\label{eq:brz-331}
 \le 
c \,
             
e^{-2 \widehat z  - 2 l - l_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa_o}}}. 
\end{equation}
To this end,  we set $\underline{\theta}=\frac{1}{4} l_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa_o}}$ and $\bar{\theta}=12l$ 
up to $l=5\log n_\varepsilon$,  taking thereafter $\bar{\theta}=12 n_\varepsilon$.  Then,  using (\ref{17.1sv}) and 
bounding $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{D}_{t_{\widehat z},l}(j))$ via \cite[(3.25)-(3.26)]{BRZ2},  
we arrive at the stated bound of (\ref{eq:brz-331}),  for the sum over $j$ values.
Further,  $\sqrt{2 t_{\widehat z}} \ge \alpha(l)+\frac{1}{4} l_{n_\varepsilon}^{\kappa_o}$ 
(since by assumption $\widehat z \ge -\mathsf{k} \boldsymbol{\rho}_\varepsilon$),  with the
left-most term in (\ref{eq:brz-331}) handled as in \cite[(3.27)]{BRZ2}.  
Similarly,  with $\sqrt{2 t_{\widehat z}} \le \alpha(l) + 4 ( l \vee 5 \log n_\varepsilon)$,  the right-most term of (\ref{eq:brz-331})
is also suitably controlled,  this time by \cite[(3.26)]{BRZ2} (upon noting that 
$\frac{1}{4l} (\bar \theta-\widehat z - l_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa_o}})^2 \ge 2 \bar \theta + l$ whenever
$\bar \theta \ge 12 (l \vee \widehat z)$).

Turning to deal with the ``large levels" beyond $L'$,  consider now  as in \cite[(3.38)]{BRZ2},  the events 
\begin{equation}
  \label{defG}
{\mathcal{G}_{z,l}} :=\bigcap_{l' \in [\mathsf{k}, l]} \Big\{ \min_{\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F}_{n_{\varepsilon}}\cap \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}} \left({\bf 0},\widetilde{c}r_0 \right)}
\big\{ \sqrt{2T^{\mathsf{v}, t_z}_{l'}} \big\} \ge \alpha(l')\Big\} 
\end{equation}
(not to be confused with the $\sigma$-algebras of \Cref{def:Fvjs}).
By a union bound over the finite cover $\mathbb{F}_0$,  it suffices for (\ref{g17.0}),  to show that when  $l=n_\varepsilon-\mathsf{k}$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq-thanks1}
\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{G}_{z,l}^{\complement}) \le  c e^{-2(z-d \sqrt{|z|})} e^{-\frac{1}{5} \mathsf{k}^{{\kappa_o}}} \,.
\end{equation}
We have already proved (\ref{eq-thanks1}) for $l = L'$,  so by 
following the proof of \cite[Prop. 3.4]{BRZ2},  we complete the  proof of  \Cref{gprop:MainGoalEasyRegime},
upon establishing our next lemma (which replaces \cite[Lemma 3.9]{BRZ2}).
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\label{lem-westjet}
In the setting of \Cref{gprop:MainGoalEasyRegime},  for $\mathcal{Q}$ of (\ref{g17.0b}),  some finite $c$
and all $l \in (L', n_{\varepsilon}-\mathsf{k}]$, 
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{P}\left(\mathcal{G}_{z,l}^\complement\cap\mathcal{G}_{z,l-2}\cap\mathcal{Q} \right)\le c (1+z_+) e^{-2z} e^{-l_{n_{\varepsilon}}^{{\kappa_o}}} .
\label{Gls}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
Following the argument leading to \cite[(3.51)]{BRZ2},  it suffices to show that 
\begin{equation}\label{brz-351}
\sum_{j=0}^{8 n_\varepsilon} \mathbb{P} (\mathcal{B}_{t_z,l} \cap \widetilde \mathcal{C}_{t_z,l}(j) \cap \mathcal{D}_{t_z,l}(j) ) 
\le c (1+z_+)  e^{-2 z} e^{-2l - l_{n_{\varepsilon}}^{{\kappa_o}}}.
\end{equation}
{
To this end,  utilizing \cite{BRZ},  we have the barrier estimate (\ref{18.20srbend}),  which for 
$\mathsf{k}^{\kappa_o} \ge 10 z_-$,  $\mathsf{k} \le l_{n_\varepsilon}$ and $h_{l,j}\leq c (l_{n_{\varepsilon}}^{{\kappa_o}}+j)$, yields that}
    
                                                                                          
           
                                                                                                    
    
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{P}\left(\widetilde\mathcal{C}_{t_{z},l} (j) \cap\mathcal{D}_{t_{z},l}(j)\right)
  
                                                                                                                                                      
&
  \leq  c e^{-2l-2z-2l_{n_{\varepsilon}}^{{\kappa_o}}} e^{2j}  (1+\sqrt{l_{n_{\varepsilon}}}+z_{+} )
  \left(1+j^{2}+l_{n_{\varepsilon}}^{{\kappa_o}} \right)\,.
                   
\end{align*}
With $L' \ge 5 \log n_\varepsilon$,  the proof of (\ref{brz-351}) is completed
by combining the preceding bound with that of  (\ref{cb.15y}) and summing over $j$.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- lemma-19: body_md -->
\label{theo-win220}
Set $n'=n_\varepsilon^{(4)}$,  $n''=n_\varepsilon^{(5)}$ and fix $0<3 {\kappa_o} < {\kappa_1} < \frac{1}{4}$,  ${\kappa''} > {\kappa'} > \frac{1}{2}$.  Then,  
for $\kappa_\star$ large enough,  $z$ fixed and $g(z)= C_{\mathsf{k}} (1+z_+) e^{-2z}$ for some $C_{\mathsf{k}}$ finite, 
 \begin{align}
\varlimsup_{\varepsilon \to 0} \Big\{ e^{2 n''} \sup_{\beta} 
\mathbb{P} \big( \widehat{\mathcal{U}}^{(\varepsilon),\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\beta} \cap \boxminus^{\complement}_{\mathsf{v}_\beta,z,n'} \big) \Big\}  
&= o_{\mathsf {K}_{5}}(1) g(z)\,,
\label{agar.67a}\\
  \varlimsup_{\varepsilon \to 0} \Big\{ e^{2 n''} \sup_{\beta} 
 \mathbb{P} \big(\mathcal{R}^{o,\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\beta}  \cap \boxminus_{\mathsf{v}_\beta,z,n'} \cap \boxminus^{\complement}_{\mathsf{v}_\beta,z,n''}\big)\Big\}
 &=o_{\mathsf {K}_{5}}(1) g(z)\,, \label{win5-good}\\
 \varlimsup_{\mathsf {K}_{5}, \varepsilon} \Big\{ e^{2 n_\varepsilon} \sup_{\beta,\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F}^\beta} \mathbb{P} \big(\mathcal{U}^{(\varepsilon),\beta,\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\mathsf{v}} \cap 
\boxminus_{\beta,z,n'} \big) \Big\} & \le g(z) \,,
\label{lem-first-moment}\\
\label{lem-win1}
 \varlimsup_{\varepsilon \to 0} \Big\{ e^{2 n''} \sum_{j=\mathsf {K}_{1}-3}^{n'-1} \sup_{\beta} 
 \mathbb{P} \big( \widehat{\mathcal{U}}^{(\varepsilon),\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\beta}  \cap \boxminus_{\beta,z,n'} \cap \boxminus^{\complement}_{\mathsf{v}_\beta,z,j}
                                   
   \big) \Big\} &=  o_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{0}}(1) g(z)\,,\\
\varlimsup_{\varepsilon \to 0}  \Big\{ e^{2n''} \sum_{k=\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\mathsf {K}_{\mathsf{a}}} \sup_{\beta} \mathbb{P} \big(
\widehat{\mathcal{U}}^{(\varepsilon),\langle z \rangle}_{\beta} \cap \boxminus_{\beta,z; \mathsf {J}_\mathsf{e}^{(k)}} \cap  \{ L_{\beta,k}^{\langle z \rangle} \notin \mathbb{B}^\infty_{\bar \mu} (\boldsymbol{\eta}^{(\varepsilon)}_k) \}
                                         
 \big) \Big\} & = o_{\mathsf {K}_{0}}(1) g(z),
 \label{pawfud0.1}   
\end{align}
for the subset $\mathsf {J}_\mathsf{e}^{(k)}:=\{ k-3,[k,\mathsf {K}_{2}],[\mathsf {K}_{3},n'],n''\}$ of $\mathsf {J}_\mathsf{e}$
(and with the larger $\bar{\mathsf I}_{n'}$,  $\bar{\mathsf I}_{n''}$ of (\ref{dfn:windows}) in (\ref{lem-first-moment})).
<!-- end lemma-19 -->

We establish (\ref{agar.67a})--(\ref{pawfud0.1}), respectively,  in parts (a)--(e) below,
modifying {\sc\lowercase{wlog}} the barrier $\gamma_{-1}(j)$  
                                                         
used in the events $\mathcal{R}^{\beta,\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\mathsf{v}}$ of (\ref{a216.0}),  as explained in \Cref{rmk:no-vep-inJs}.\\
(a).  Recall (\ref{def:UUpk}) that 
\[
\widehat{\mathcal{U}}^{(\varepsilon),\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\beta} = \bigcup_{\mathsf{v}\in \mathbb{F}^\beta} \Big\{ \mathcal{R}^{\beta,\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\mathsf{v}},  \eta_{\mathsf{v},n_\varepsilon+1}^{\beta,\langle z \rangle} = 0 \Big\}
\bigcap \mathcal{R}^{o,\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\beta} \subset \bigcup_{\mathsf{v}\in \mathbb{F}^\beta} 
\Big\{ \eta_{\mathsf{v},n_\varepsilon+1}^{\beta,\langle z \rangle} = 0\Big\} \bigcap \mathcal{R}^{o,\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\beta}
\]
hence by a union bound over the $c e^{2 \mathsf {K}_{5}}$ possible values of $\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F}^\beta$,  it suffices
for (\ref{agar.67a}) to show that
\begin{equation}\label{Jay-agar.67a}
\varlimsup_{\varepsilon \to 0} \Big\{ e^{2 n_\varepsilon} \sup_{\beta,\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F}^\beta} 
\mathbb{P} \big( \{ \eta_{\mathsf{v},n_\varepsilon+1}^{\beta,\langle z \rangle} = 0 \} \cap \mathcal{R}^{o,\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\beta} \cap  \boxminus^{\complement}_{\mathsf{v}_\beta,z,n'} \big) 
\Big\}  = o_{\mathsf {K}_{5}}(1) g(z)\,.
\end{equation}
To this end,  {setting $\mathcal{A}^{\langle z \rangle}_{[\mathsf{k},n'],\beta}(m) := \{ \mathcal{R}^{o,\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\beta},  T^{\langle z \rangle}_{\beta,n'}=m\}$
we claim that for large $\mathsf {K}_{5}$ any $z$,  $\mathsf{k}$,  $\varepsilon$ and $\beta$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:pre-winx.2}
\sup_{\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F}^\beta} \mathbb{P} \(  \eta_{\mathsf{v},n_\varepsilon+1}^{\beta,\langle z \rangle} = 0  \, |\,   
\mathcal{A}^{\langle z \rangle}_{[\mathsf{k},n'],\beta}(m)  \) \leq 
 e^{-\frac{m}{\mathsf {K}_{4}} (1-\frac{2}{\mathsf {K}_{4}})} \,. 
\end{equation}
Indeed,  we are here in the setting of \Cref{lem-off-center-applies},  for $\mathsf{u}=\mathsf{v}_\beta$,  
$\mathsf{L}=n'$,  $R_i=r_i$,  $R=r_{n'}$,  $\mathsf{s}=\mathsf{s}_1(z)$,  
$\mathcal{A}^{(m)}=\mathcal{A}^{\langle z \rangle}_{[\mathsf{k},n'],\beta}(m)$ and $\rho = r_{n''}/R = \mathsf {K}_{5}^{-5}$.  
The {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of (\ref{eq:pre-winx.2}) is of the form $\mathbb{Q}_{R_1}^{\mathsf{s},\mathsf{v}_\beta} (\Gamma|\mathcal{A}^{(m)})$ for
the event $\Gamma:=\{\eta_{\mathsf{v},n_\varepsilon+1}^{\beta,\langle z \rangle} = 0\} \in \mathcal{N}_{\mathsf{v},\varepsilon,m,0}$
where our $m$ excursions from $\partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{v}_\beta,r_{n'})$ 
to $\partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{v}_\beta,r_{n'-1})$ avoid $\mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{v},\varepsilon/e)$.
Hence,  by (\ref{eq:off-center-bd}) followed by (\ref{eq:pv-u}) at $r=\varepsilon/R=e^{-\mathsf {K}_{4}}$, 
                                 
the {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of (\ref{eq:pre-winx.2}) is at most 
\[
                                                               
(1-\inf_{\mathsf{z},\mathsf{v}} \{ q^{\mathsf{z},\mathsf{v}_\beta}_{r,\mathsf{v}}\})^m 
\le  \Big(1- \frac{1- c \rho}{\mathsf {K}_{4}+2}\Big)^m \le e^{-m\frac{1-c \rho}{\mathsf {K}_{4}+2}} \le 
e^{-\frac{m}{\mathsf {K}_{4}} (1-\frac{2}{\mathsf {K}_{4}})} 
\]
(with the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} holding once $c \rho \,  \mathsf {K}_{4}^2 \le 4$).  Next,  recall \Cref{rmk:no-vep-inJs} and (\ref{a216.0}) that 
$m=\frac{1}{2}(2 \mathsf {K}_{4}+y)^{2}$ for $y=\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,n'}^{\,\langle z \rangle} \ge -\mathsf {K}_{4}^{{\kappa_o}}$.  For all $\mathsf {K}_{5}$ large enough  
\[
\inf_{y \ge -\mathsf {K}_{4}^{{\kappa_o}}} \Big\{ \frac{(2\mathsf {K}_{4}+y)^{2}}{2\mathsf {K}_{4}} (1-\frac{2}{\mathsf {K}_{4}}) 
- 2(\mathsf {K}_{4}+y) - \frac{y^2}{4\mathsf {K}_{4}} \Big\} 
\]
is uniformly bounded below,  hence (\ref{eq:pre-winx.2}) implies that for} some 
universal $C$,  all $\varepsilon$,  any $z$,  $\mathsf{k}$,  $\mathsf {K}_{5}$ and $\beta$,
 \begin{equation}
\sup_{\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F}^\beta} \mathbb{P} \(  \eta_{\mathsf{v},n_\varepsilon+1}^{\beta,\langle z \rangle} = 0  \, |\,   \mathcal{R}^{o,\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\beta},   T^{\langle z \rangle}_{\beta,n'}  \) \leq 
C  e^{-2\mathsf {K}_{4}}  e^{ -2 \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,n'}^{\,\langle z \rangle}} e^{-(\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,n'}^{\,\langle z \rangle})^2/(4 \mathsf {K}_{4})} \, .
\label{winx.2}
\end{equation} 
{Now,  in view of (\ref{14.4}) at $j=n'$ and (\ref{winx.2}),  by the union bound it suffices 
for (\ref{Jay-agar.67a}) to show} that 
\begin{align}
e^{2 n'} \!\!\!\!\!\! \sum_{y\in [-\mathsf {K}_{4}^{\kappa_o},\mathsf {K}_{4}^{{\kappa_1}}] \cup [\frac{1}{2} \mathsf {K}_{4}^{{\kappa'}},\infty)} \!\! \sup_\beta \mathbb{P} ( \mathcal{R}^{o,\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\beta},  \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,n'}^{\,\langle z \rangle} \in I_y) e^{-2 y} e^{-y^2/(4 \mathsf {K}_{4})} &= o_{\mathsf {K}_{5}}(1) g(z)\,,
\label{winx.1}
\end{align}
where $I_y=[y,y+1)$ and throughout this proof summation over $y$ in some range means the summation over $y$ integer in that range.
                                 
                                                                       
To this end,  from {(\ref{a216.0}) and} 
{\Cref{lem-bendc} at $s=\mathsf{k}$,  $k=n'$ and $v=y+\mathsf {K}_{4}^{{\kappa_o}}$, } we have that
\begin{equation}\label{agar.5old}
\mathbb{P} ( \mathcal{R}^{o,\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\beta},  \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,n'}^{\,\langle z \rangle} \in I_y) \le g(z) e^{-2 n'} \mathsf {K}_{4}^{-1/2} (1+|y|)  e^{2y} \,,
\end{equation}
which yields (\ref{winx.1}) since for ${\kappa_o} \le {\kappa_1} < \frac{1}{4}$ and ${\kappa'}>\frac{1}{2}$,
\begin{equation}\label{agar.66-67}
2 \mathsf {K}_{4}^{-1/2} \sum_{j=-\mathsf {K}_{4}^{{\kappa_o}}}^{\mathsf {K}_{4}^{{\kappa_1}}} |j|
+ \sum_{j= \frac{1}{2} \mathsf {K}_{4}^{{\kappa'}}}^\infty  j e^{-j^2/(4 \mathsf {K}_{4})} 
 = o_{\mathsf {K}_{4}}(1)\,.
\end{equation}
(b).  Recall  that excursion counts of concentric balls with a constant ratio of radii 
form a Markov chain whose transition kernels are $q_{\ell}(x',x)$ of \Cref{dfn:Markov}.
Upon using (\ref{agar.5old}) we thus arrive at (\ref{win5-good}) once we show that 
for $\mathsf {L}:=\mathsf {K}_{4}-\mathsf {K}_{5}$,
\begin{equation}\label{win5-good-alt}
\sum_{y\in \mathsf{I}'_{n'}} (1+y)  e^{2y}  
\sum_{j\geq \mathsf {K}_{5}/2} \sup_{x' \in I_{2 \mathsf {K}_{4}+y}} \{ q_{\, \mathsf {L}}(x',I_{2\mathsf {K}_{5}+j-1}) \} =o_{\mathsf {K}_{5}}(1) e^{-2 \mathsf {L}} \,. 
\end{equation}
              
                                                                     
                                                                                        
As in (\ref{eq:BRZ-1.10m}),  for some $C$ finite,  $c \ge 0$,  $\mathsf {L}'=\mathsf {L}+c$ and uniformly in 
$y,j$ appearing in the sums of (\ref{win5-good-alt})
                
                   
                                                                        
\begin{equation}\label{eq:BRZ-1.10mod}
\sup_{x' \in I_{2 \mathsf {K}_{4}+y}} \{ q_{\,\mathsf {L}}(x',I_{2\mathsf {K}_{5}+j-1}) \}
\le \frac{C}{\sqrt{\mathsf {L}'}} e^{-\frac{(j-y-2\mathsf {L}')^2}{2\mathsf {L}'}} \le \frac{C}{\sqrt{\mathsf {L}'}} e^{-2\mathsf {L}'-2y} e^{-\frac{j^2}{16\mathsf {L}'}} 
\end{equation}
(since with ${\kappa'}<1$,  once $\mathsf {K}_{5}$ is large enough we have that  $j-y \ge \frac{1}{2} j \ge 16 \mathsf {L}'$). 
                                                 
Summing the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} of (\ref{eq:BRZ-1.10mod})
over all integer $j \ge \frac{1}{2} \mathsf {K}_{5}$ and bounding by the appropriate Riemann integral 
{we get by standard tail} estimates on the Gaussian error function {that for large enough $\mathsf {K}_{5}$,}
\begin{align}\label{win5-bad}
{\sum_{j\geq \mathsf {K}_{5}/2} \sup_{x' \in I_{2 \mathsf {K}_{4}+y}} \{ q_{\, \mathsf {L}}(x',I_{2\mathsf {K}_{5}+j-1}) \} \le } 
                                                                              
8 C e^{-2\mathsf {L}-2y} e^{-\frac{\mathsf {K}_{5}^2}{128 \mathsf {L}}} \,.
\end{align}
Plugging 
            
(\ref{win5-bad}) 
                      
in (\ref{win5-good-alt}) and 
                                        
{having} $\mathsf {L} \le O(\log \mathsf {K}_{5})$,  {yields,  as claimed,  that}
the {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of (\ref{win5-good-alt}) {is at most}
             
                                                                          
\[
{8 C e^{-2\mathsf {L}} e^{-\frac{\mathsf {K}_{5}^2}{128 \mathsf {L}}} \sum_{y\in \mathsf{I}'_{n'} \cap \mathbb{Z}} (1+y) \le}   
8 C  \mathsf {K}_{4}^{\,  2 {\kappa'}} e^{-\frac{\mathsf {K}_{5}^2}{128 \mathsf {L}}}  e^{-2 \mathsf {L}} = o_{\mathsf {K}_{5}}(1) e^{-2 \mathsf {L}} \,.
\]
\noindent
(c).  In view of (\ref{def:UUvk}),  (\ref{dfn:windows-alt}) and (\ref{14.4}) we have that 
\[
\mathcal{U}^{(\varepsilon),\beta,\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\mathsf{v}} \cap \boxminus_{\beta,z,n'} \subset 
\Big\{  \mathcal{R}^{\beta,\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\mathsf{v}},  \eta_{\mathsf{v},n_\varepsilon+1}^{\beta,\langle z \rangle} = 0,
                                                 
 \mathcal{R}^{o,\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\beta},  \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,n'}^{\,\langle z \rangle} \in \bar{\mathsf I}_{n'} \Big\} \,.
\]
By (\ref{agar.5old}),  it thus suffices for (\ref{lem-first-moment}),   
to show that
\begin{align}\label{first-moment-alt}
\varlimsup_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\varepsilon} \Big\{ \frac{e^{2\mathsf {K}_{4}}}{\sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}}} \sum_{y \in \bar{\mathsf I}_{n'}\cap \mathbb{Z}} y  e^{2y} \sup \{ f_m : \sqrt{2m} \in  I_{2\mathsf {K}_{4}+y} \} \Big\}
& \le C_\mathsf{k}  \,,  
\end{align}
where {for $\mathcal{A}^{\langle z \rangle}_{[\mathsf{k},n'],\beta} (m)$ of (\ref{eq:pre-winx.2})},
                                                                                      
\begin{align}\label{dfn:f-y}
f_m & := \sup_{\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F}^\beta}   
 \mathbb{P}\Big( 
                                                   
 \mathcal{R}^{\beta,\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\mathsf{v}},  \eta_{\mathsf{v},n_\varepsilon+1}^{\beta,\langle z \rangle} = 0
   \,\big|\,  \mathcal{A}^{\langle z \rangle}_{[\mathsf{k},n'],\beta} (m) \Big)  \,.
\end{align}
{Setting $\widetilde{n}:=\tilde{n}_\varepsilon^{(5)}$,  the conditional on $\mathcal{A}^{(m)}:=\mathcal{A}^{\langle z \rangle}_{[\mathsf{k},n'],\beta}(m)$ probability 
in (\ref{dfn:f-y}) is of the form $\mathbb{Q}_{R_1}^{\mathsf{s},\mathsf{v}_\beta} (\Gamma|\mathcal{A}^{(m)})$ of \Cref{lem-off-center-applies}, 
with same values of $\mathsf{u}$,  $\mathsf{s}$,  $\mathsf{L}$,  $R_i$,  $\rho$ and $\mathcal{A}^{(m)}$ as in 
our derivation of (\ref{eq:pre-winx.2}),  while having here  
$\Gamma:=\{\eta_{\mathsf{v},n_\varepsilon+1}^{\beta,\langle z \rangle} = 0\} \cap \mathcal{R}^{\beta,\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\mathsf{v}} \in (\mathcal{N}_{\mathsf{v},r})^m$
for $r=e \,  r_{\widetilde{n}}$ (see (\ref{a216.0})).  Setting $k= \widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5}^4$,  
similarly to our derivation of (\ref{eq:bd-hQv}),  
we further split the event $\Gamma$ to the disjoint union of $\Gamma^{(k)} := \Gamma \cap \{ \eta^{\beta,\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{v},\widetilde{n}} \le \sqrt{2k} \} \in \mathcal{N}_{\mathsf{v},r,m,k}$ 
and $\Gamma \setminus \Gamma^{(k)} \subset \{T^{\mathsf{v},\widetilde{n},k}_{n_\varepsilon+1} = 0 \}$.  From 
(\ref{eq:off-center-bd}),  given our specification of $k$ and $\rho$ and having $m = O(\mathsf {K}_{4}^2)$,  it follows that  
for $\mathsf {K}_{5}$ large enough
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rem-angles}
\sup_{\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F}^\beta} \{ \mathbb{Q}_{R_1}^{\mathsf{s},\mathsf{v}_\beta} (\Gamma^{(k)}|\mathcal{A}^{(m)}) \} \le (1+c \rho)^{m+k} (\mathbb{P}^{1}_R)^m(\Gamma_k) \le 
2 (\mathbb{P}^{1}_R)^m (\Gamma) \,,
\end{equation}
where on the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} we have the probability of $\Gamma$ for $\mathsf{v}=\mathsf{v}_\beta$ and $m$ 
{\sc\lowercase{iid}} unconditioned,  stopped Brownian paths.  Setting {\sc\lowercase{wlog}} 
$\mathsf{v}={\bf 0}$ and scaling space by $e^{-2}/R$ we deduce similarly to (\ref{eq:A-RU-Q-hatQ}) that 
\[
2 (\mathbb{P}^1_R)^m(\Gamma) \le 2 \bar \mathbb{P}^{(\star)}_{u} ( \widehat{\mathcal{Q}}_{{\bf 0}}) 
\]
for $u = \sqrt{2m}-2\mathsf {K}_{4}$,  $\mathsf {K}_{6}=\mathsf{k}$ and $\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}_{\bf 0}$ of (\ref{def:QQs}).   
Further,  as in the derivation of (\ref{eq:bd-hQv}),  
the probability of hitting $\mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}} (\mathsf{v},\varepsilon/e)$ by a Brownian path
from $\partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}} (\mathsf{v},r_{\widetilde{n}})$ to $\partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}} (\mathsf{v}, e \,  r_{\widetilde{n}})$ is,  
uniformly over its starting and end points,  at least $c/\widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5}$ for some 
$c>0$.  Since $\{ T^{\mathsf{v},\widetilde{n},k}_{n_\varepsilon+1} = 0 \}$ requires that $\widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5}^4$ such paths 
all miss this ball,  we deduce from (\ref{ubd-wQ}),  that}
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sup-fm}
\sup \{ f_m : \sqrt{2m} \in  I_{2\mathsf {K}_{4}+y} \} \le  e^{-c \,  \widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5}^3} + 2 
\sup_{u \in I_y} \bar \mathbb{P}^{(\star)}_{u} ( \widehat{\mathcal{Q}}_{{\bf 0}}) 
\le c_\mathsf{k} \frac{y}{\mathsf {K}_{4}} e^{-2 \mathsf {K}_{4}} e^{- 2y}  e^{-y^2/(8 \mathsf {K}_{4})} \,.
\end{equation}
By the preceding,  the {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of (\ref{first-moment-alt}) is therefore,  as claimed,  at most 
\[
c_\mathsf{k} \sup_{\mathsf {K}_{4} \ge 1} \Big\{ \sum_{y \in \mathbb{Z}} y^2 \mathsf {K}_{4}^{-3/2}  e^{-y^2/(8 \mathsf {K}_{4})} \Big\} := C_\mathsf{k} < \infty \,.
\]
(d).  By our reasoning in part (c),  we get (\ref{lem-win1}) upon showing that for 
all large $\mathsf {K}_{0}$,  $\mathsf {K}_{5}$ and any $y \in \mathsf{I}'_{n'}$
\begin{equation}\label{eq:updn-alt}
\sup_{\beta,\varepsilon} \Big\{
 e^{2 n'} \sum_{j=\mathsf {K}_{1}-3}^{n'-1} \sum_{u \notin \mathsf{I}'_j} \mathbb{P} ( \mathcal{R}^{o,\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\beta},  \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,j}^{\,\langle z \rangle} \in I_u,
\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,n'}^{\,\langle z \rangle} \in I_y) \Big\} 
= o_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{0}}(1)  g(z) \mathsf {K}_{4}^{-1/2} y e^{2y} \,,
\end{equation}
where throughout {this} proof,  the summation is over {integer values} of $u$ in the indicated range.
Starting with $j \in [\mathsf {K}_{1}-3,\frac{1}{2} n_\varepsilon]$,  we set $b_j:=\exp((j/n_\varepsilon) \log n_\varepsilon)$
and since $z=o(\sqrt{j}\,)$,  get upon {combining \Cref{lem-bendc} for levels $[\mathsf{k},j]$ 
and heights $z$ to $v=u+j_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa_o}}$,  with \Cref{prop:BarrierSecGWPropUB} 
at levels $[j,n']$,  from $u$ to $y \in  \bar{\mathsf I}_{n'}$},  that for any $u \ge - j^{{\kappa_o}}$ and $y \gg \mathsf {K}_{4}^{{\kappa_o}}$, 
\begin{align}\label{agar.45p} 
   
e^{2 n'}  \mathbb{P} ( \mathcal{R}^{o,\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\beta},  \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,j}^{\,\langle z \rangle} \in I_u,   \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,n'}^{\,\langle z \rangle}  \in I_y)
        
& \leq g(z) 
b_j e^{-2j+2u} \,  \frac{(j^{{\kappa_o}} + u_+)}{j^{3/2}}e^{-\frac{(z-u)^{2}}{8j}} 
          
(j^{{\kappa_o}}  +u_+) b_j^{-1} e^{2j-2u} e^{2y}\,  \frac{y}{\sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}}} \nonumber\\
& \leq  g(z) \mathsf {K}_{4}^{-1/2} y e^{2y} f_{j,0}(u) \,,
\end{align}
where we set for $s \in [0,j)$ and $u \in \mathbb{Z}$, 
\begin{equation}\label{def:fjs}
f_{j,s}(u):= \frac{(j^{{\kappa_o}} +u_+)^2}{(j-s)^{3/2}} e^{- \frac{u^{2}}{16(j-s)}}.  
\end{equation}
The contribution of $j \in [\mathsf {K}_{1}-3,\mathsf {K}_{1}] \cup \{\mathsf {K}_{2},\mathsf {K}_{3}\}$ has a negligible effect on (\ref{eq:updn-alt}),  
since similarly to (\ref{agar.66-67}),  for ${\kappa_o} \le {\kappa_1} < \frac{1}{2}<{\kappa'}$ and any such $j$, 
\begin{equation}\label{agar.66-new}
\sum_{u=- j^{{\kappa_1}}}^{2 j^{{\kappa_1}}} f_{j,0}(u) + \sum_{u \ge \frac{1}{2} j^{{\kappa'}}} f_{j,0}(u) \le 
\frac{2}{j^{3/2}} \Big[ \sum_{u=0}^{2 j^{{\kappa_1}}} (j^{{\kappa_o}}+u)^2
+ \sum_{u = \frac{1}{2} j^{{\kappa'}}}^{\infty} u^2 e^{-\frac{u^2}{16j}}  \Big]  = o_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}(1)\,.
\end{equation}
The same applies to the contribution to (\ref{eq:updn-alt}) by all $j \le \frac{1}{2} n_\varepsilon$,  since for 
${\kappa_o}<\frac{1}{6}$ and ${\kappa''}>\frac{1}{2}$, 
\begin{equation}\label{agar.66-ext}
\sum_{j=\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\frac{1}{2} n_\varepsilon} \Big[
\sum_{u=- j^{{\kappa_o}}}^{2 j^{{\kappa_o}}} f_{j,0}(u) + \sum_{u \ge \frac{1}{2} j^{{\kappa''}}} f_{j,0}(u) \Big] \le 
C_{{\kappa_o},{\kappa''}}  \sum_{j=\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\infty} j^{3{\kappa_o}-3/2} = o_{\mathsf {K}_{0}}(1) \,.
\end{equation}
Since ${\kappa''} >{\kappa'}$ and ${\kappa_1}>{\kappa_o}$ we have that $2 (u-y)^2 \ge u^2 + y^2$
for any $u \notin \mathsf{I}'_j$ and $y \in \mathsf{I}'_{n'}$,  hence for $j \in [\frac{1}{2} n_\varepsilon,n')$ 
and any such integer $y$ and $u \ge - j_{n_\varepsilon}^{\kappa_o}$,  
we similarly find that
\begin{align}\label{agar.45jj} 
   
e^{2 n'} \mathbb{P} ( \mathcal{R}^{o,\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\beta},  \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,j}^{\,\langle z \rangle} \in I_u,   \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,n'}^{\,\langle z \rangle}  \in I_y)
       
& \leq 
g(z) b_{j_{n_\varepsilon}} e^{-2j+2u} \,  (j_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa_o}} + u_+)
               
\frac{(j_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa_o}}+u_+)}{(n'-j)^{3/2}} b_{j_{n_\varepsilon}}^{-1} e^{2j-2u} e^{2y}\,  \frac{y}{\sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}}} 
e^{-\frac{(u-y)^2}{8(n'-j)}} 
\nonumber\\
& \leq g(z) \mathsf {K}_{4}^{-1/2} y e^{2y} f_{j_{n_\varepsilon},\mathsf {K}_{4}}(u) 
e^{-\frac{y^2}{16(n'-j)}} \,.
\end{align}
With $f_{j,s}(\cdot) \le 4 f_{j,0}(\cdot)$ when either $j \ge 2s$ or $u \ge C \sqrt{j}$,  the aggregate contribution to 
(\ref{eq:updn-alt}) from $u \ge \frac{1}{2} j_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa''}}$ and from $|u| \le 2 j_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa_o}}$ 
and $j \leq n'-\mathsf {K}_{4}$,  be as in the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} of (\ref{agar.66-ext}) except for having $\mathsf {K}_{4}$ instead of $\mathsf {K}_{1}$.  
Moreover,  thanks to the term $\exp(-\frac{y^2}{16(n'-j)})$,  the aggregate contribution from 
$|u| \le 2 j_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa_o}}$ and $n'-j \in [1,\mathsf {K}_{4}]$ is for $y \ge \mathsf {K}_{4}^{{\kappa_1}}$ and ${\kappa_1}>3{\kappa_o}$ at most
\[
(3 \mathsf {K}_{4}^{{\kappa_o}})^3 \sum_{\ell=1}^{\mathsf {K}_{4}} \ell^{-3/2} e^{-\frac{\mathsf {K}_{4}^{2{\kappa_1}}}{16\ell}} = o_{\mathsf {K}_{5}}(1), 
\]
which thereby completes the proof of  (\ref{eq:updn-alt}).

\noindent
(e).   Enumerating the angle differences $\theta_q \in [-\pi,\pi)$ 
between the start and end-point of those excursions,  we set
\begin{equation}
\mathcal{W}^{\infty,\in m}_{\beta,k}(\mathsf{s})=\Big\{ \,  \mathsf{d}_\infty\Big(\frac{1}{\mathsf{s}} \sum_{q=1}^\mathsf{s} \delta_{\theta_q},\bar \mu\Big) 
\in   \frac{c_{0}}{2 \sqrt{\mathsf{s}}} I_m \Big\} \, .  \label{eq:LBTruncatedSumzf}
\end{equation}
Recall that $\boldsymbol{\eta}^{(\varepsilon)}_k=\frac{\kappa_\star}{\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon} \log k$,   so for any $\kappa_\star \ge c_0$,  one has that  
\begin{equation}\label{eq:inclusion}
\Big\{ \frac{1}{\mathsf{s}} \sum_{q=1}^{\mathsf{s}} \delta_{\theta_q} \notin \mathbb{B}^\infty_{\bar \mu} 
\Big(\frac{\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon}{2 \sqrt{\mathsf{s}}} \boldsymbol{\eta}^{(\varepsilon)}_k \Big)  \Big\} \subset \bigcup_{m \ge \log k} \mathcal{W}^{\infty,\in m}_{\beta,k}(\mathsf{s}) \,,
\qquad  \forall k,  \mathsf{s} \,.
\end{equation}
Let $N_{k,a}=[\mathsf{s}_k(a+1)]$ denote the largest possible number of $k$-level excursions
in case $\widehat{\eta}^{\,\langle z \rangle}_{\beta,k} \in I_a$.  In (\ref{pawfud0.1}),
$L_{\beta,k}^{\langle z \rangle}$ are the empirical measures of $\{ \theta_q\}_{q=1}^{\mathsf{s}}$,  with  
        
$\mathsf{s} \in [\mathsf{s}_k(a),N_{k,a}]$ in case $\widehat{\eta}^{\,\langle z \rangle}_{\beta,k} \in I_a$.  Since $\mathsf{s}_k(a) \ge N_{k,a}-\sqrt{2 N_{k,a}}$ and 
\[
\lim_{\varepsilon \to 0} \;\; \Big\{ \sup_{k \in [\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{\mathsf{a}}],a \in \bar{\mathsf I}_k}  \big|\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon^{-2} N_{k,a} - \frac{1}{2}\big| \Big\}  = 0 \,,
\]
it thus follows from (\ref{eq:dinf-comp}) and (\ref{eq:inclusion}) that for all $\varepsilon$ small enough 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Lkp-WNa}
\Big\{ L_{\beta,k}^{\langle z \rangle} \notin \mathbb{B}^\infty_{\bar \mu} (\boldsymbol{\eta}^{(\varepsilon)}_k) \Big\} 
\subset \bigcup_{m \ge \log k} \mathcal{W}^{\infty,\in m}_{\beta,k}(N_{k,a}) , 
\qquad \forall k \in [\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{\mathsf{a}}],  \quad \forall  a \in \mathsf{I}'_k \,.
\end{equation}
Consequently,  we control the event in (\ref{pawfud0.1}) by 
adapting the proof of \cite[(4.42)]{BRZ2}, 
                                        
though we have the event $\widehat{\mathcal{U}}^{(\varepsilon),\langle z \rangle}_{\beta}  \cap \boxminus_{\beta,z;n',n''}$ at our finer 
scales $[n',n_\varepsilon]$,  instead of the easier setting of \cite[(4.61)]{BRZ2},  where $n'=n_\varepsilon$.
Due to the angle information in the events of (\ref{eq:LBTruncatedSumzf}),
                         
we lack
the radial symmetry of the events on scales $[k,n']$,
                                    
but $\boxminus_{\beta,z;\mathsf {K}_{2},\mathsf {K}_{3}}$ implies at most $3 n_\varepsilon^2$ 
excursions at levels $\mathsf {K}_{2}$ and $\mathsf {K}_{3}$.  Hence,  with $\mathsf {K}_{3}-\mathsf {K}_{2}=5 \log n_\varepsilon$
and $\mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}_\beta}_{\mathsf {K}_{2}}$ denoting the $\sigma$-algebra of excursions 
from $\partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{v}_\beta,r_{\mathsf {K}_{2}-1})$ to $\partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{v}_\beta,r_{\mathsf {K}_{2}})$,
we get as in \cite[(4.66)]{BRZ2},  that for some $c$ finite,  uniformly in $\beta$ and 
our range of $j'$, $j''$,  $y$,   
\begin{equation}\label{eq:BRZ-466}
\mathbb{P}\Big(\boxminus_{\beta,z; [\mathsf {K}_{3},n']} \cap \{ \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,n'}^{\,\langle z \rangle} \in I_y \} \,\Big| \,  T^{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{2},s}_{\mathsf {K}_{3}},
\mathcal{G}_{\mathsf {K}_{2}}^{\mathsf{v}_\beta}  \Big) \le c \;
\mathbb{P}\Big(\boxminus_{\beta,z; [\mathsf {K}_{3},n']} \cap \{ \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,n'}^{\,\langle z \rangle} \in I_y \} \,\Big| \,  T^{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{2},s}_{\mathsf {K}_{3}} \Big) \,.
\end{equation}
With the event on the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} of (\ref{eq:BRZ-466}) having radial symmetry,  we thus 
combine the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} of (\ref{eq:sup-fm}) {with a barrier bound on the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} of (\ref{eq:BRZ-466})
from  \Cref{lem-bendc} at levels $[\mathsf {K}_{3},n']$,  similarly to (\ref{agar.5old}),  except for starting now at height 
$j''$.}
                          
Summing the resulting bound 
over $\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F}^\beta$ and $y \in \mathsf{I}'_{n'}$, 
we conclude,  analogously to \cite[(4.67)]{BRZ2},  that uniformly over $j'' \in \mathsf{I}'_{\mathsf {K}_{3}}$, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:BRZ-467}
e^{2 n''} \sup_{\beta} \mathbb{P}\Big(\widehat{\mathcal{U}}^{(\varepsilon),\langle z \rangle}_{\beta} \cap \boxminus_{\beta,z; [\mathsf {K}_{3},n'],n''} \,\Big| \,  \widehat{\eta}^{\,\langle z \rangle}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{3}} \in I_{j''}, 
\mathcal{G}_{\mathsf {K}_{2}}^{\mathsf{v}_\beta}  \Big) 
\le g(j'') 
                        
e^{2 \mathsf {K}_{3}} 
\sum_{y \in \mathsf{I}'_{n'}} \,  \frac{y^2}{\mathsf {K}_{4}^{3/2}} e^{-\frac{y^2}{8 \mathsf {K}_{4}}} = g(j'') e^{2 \mathsf {K}_{3}} \,.
\end{equation}
To complete the proof of (\ref{pawfud0.1}),  we utilize the following lemma (which is proved at the end of this section).
\begin{lemma}\label{lem:BRZ-CH4}
Fixing $z \in \mathbb{R}$,  for any $\beta$,  $k \in [\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]$,  $m \ge 0$ and integer $a$,  $j'$,  $j''$,  set 
\begin{align}\label{def:Lmpa} 
\mathcal{L}'_{k,m,a} &:=
                                       
\{ \widehat{\eta}^{\,\langle z \rangle}_{\beta,k} \in I_{a} \} \cap
\mathcal{W}^{\infty,\in m}_{\beta,k}(N_{k,a}) 
       
\\
\mathbb{B}^{j',j''}_{\beta,k+3,\mathsf {K}_{2},\mathsf {K}_{3}} &:= \bigcap_{j=k+3}^{\mathsf {K}_{2}-1} \{ \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,j}^{\,\langle z \rangle} \ge 2 j^{\kappa_o} \}
                                    
\cap \{ \widehat{\eta}^{\,\langle z \rangle}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{2}} \in I_{j'} \} \cap \{ \widehat{\eta}^{\,\langle z \rangle}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{3}} \in I_{j''} \} \,,
\label{def:Bjp-jpp}
\end{align}
where $I_y=[y,y+1)$.
Then,  for some $c'>0$,  $C<\infty$,  all $\varepsilon$ small enough,  any $k \in \mathsf {J}'_\mathsf{a}$,  $m \ge \log k$ and $\beta$, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:BRZ-top}
\sum_{j''}  g(j'') \mathbb{P}(\bigcup_{p,a,j'} \mathcal{L}'_{k,m,a}  \cap \mathbb{B}^{j',j''}_{\beta,k+3,\mathsf {K}_{2},\mathsf {K}_{3}} ) \le C (1+z_+) e^{-2z} 
e^{-2 \mathsf {K}_{3}} e^{-c' m^2}  \,,
\end{equation}
where the union is over 
                        
$a \in \mathsf{I}'_k$,  $j' \in \mathsf{I}'_{\mathsf {K}_{2}}$ and the sum 
over $j'' \in \mathsf{I}'_{\mathsf {K}_{3}}$.
\end{lemma}
Indeed,  we consider which of the events in (\ref{def:Lmpa}) and (\ref{def:Bjp-jpp}) occur in
$\boxminus_{\beta,z; \mathsf {J}_\mathsf{e}^{(k)}} \cap  \{ L_{\beta,k}^{\langle z \rangle} \notin \mathbb{B}^\infty_{\bar \mu} (\boldsymbol{\eta}^{(\varepsilon)}_k) \}$
(compare with \cite[(4.55) \& (4.69)]{BRZ2}),  and 
                                     
combine (\ref{eq:BRZ-467}) with (\ref{eq:BRZ-top}),  then 
sum over $m \ge \log k$ and $k \in \mathsf {J}'_\mathsf{a}$ to arrive at (\ref{pawfud0.1}).
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- lemma-20: body_md -->
\label{lem:BRZ-CH4}
Fixing $z \in \mathbb{R}$,  for any $\beta$,  $k \in [\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]$,  $m \ge 0$ and integer $a$,  $j'$,  $j''$,  set 
\begin{align}\label{def:Lmpa} 
\mathcal{L}'_{k,m,a} &:=
                                       
\{ \widehat{\eta}^{\,\langle z \rangle}_{\beta,k} \in I_{a} \} \cap
\mathcal{W}^{\infty,\in m}_{\beta,k}(N_{k,a}) 
       
\\
\mathbb{B}^{j',j''}_{\beta,k+3,\mathsf {K}_{2},\mathsf {K}_{3}} &:= \bigcap_{j=k+3}^{\mathsf {K}_{2}-1} \{ \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,j}^{\,\langle z \rangle} \ge 2 j^{\kappa_o} \}
                                    
\cap \{ \widehat{\eta}^{\,\langle z \rangle}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{2}} \in I_{j'} \} \cap \{ \widehat{\eta}^{\,\langle z \rangle}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{3}} \in I_{j''} \} \,,
\label{def:Bjp-jpp}
\end{align}
where $I_y=[y,y+1)$.
Then,  for some $c'>0$,  $C<\infty$,  all $\varepsilon$ small enough,  any $k \in \mathsf {J}'_\mathsf{a}$,  $m \ge \log k$ and $\beta$, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:BRZ-top}
\sum_{j''}  g(j'') \mathbb{P}(\bigcup_{p,a,j'} \mathcal{L}'_{k,m,a}  \cap \mathbb{B}^{j',j''}_{\beta,k+3,\mathsf {K}_{2},\mathsf {K}_{3}} ) \le C (1+z_+) e^{-2z} 
e^{-2 \mathsf {K}_{3}} e^{-c' m^2}  \,,
\end{equation}
where the union is over 
                        
$a \in \mathsf{I}'_k$,  $j' \in \mathsf{I}'_{\mathsf {K}_{2}}$ and the sum 
over $j'' \in \mathsf{I}'_{\mathsf {K}_{3}}$.
<!-- end lemma-20 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
Even conditional upon 
                          
$\widehat{\eta}^{\,\langle z \rangle}_{\beta,k}$,   the $\{\theta_q\}$ in (\ref{eq:LBTruncatedSumzf}) are {\sc\lowercase{IID}} 
from a law $\bar \mu$ whose density is bounded below (see (\ref{dfn:Poiss})).  
By (\ref{lbl:d-inf-bd}) we thus have,  analogously to \cite[(4.54)]{BRZ2},  the estimate 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:BRZ-454}
\mathbb{P}\Big( \mathcal{W}^{\infty,\in m}_{\beta,k}(N_{k,a}) | \widehat{\eta}^{\,\langle z \rangle}_{\beta,k} \Big) \le 2 e^{-m^2/4}    
\end{equation}
(provided $c_0 \ge 6 \sqrt{2} \,  c$,   $c = \sqrt{1+\bar c^2}+\bar c$). 
Combining (\ref{eq:BRZ-454}) and \cite[(4.56)]{BRZ2} (at $k$),  yields that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:BRZ-455}
\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{L}'_{k,m,a}) \le c_1 e^{-2k} e^{-2(z-a)} e^{-(z-a)^2/(4k)} e^{-m^2/4} \,,
\end{equation}
for some $c_1$ finite,  fixed $z$ and all $k \in [\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]$,  $a \in \mathsf{I}'_k$ and $m \ge \log k$.
                                         
By our choice of $\mathsf {K}_{3}$, 
for some $C<\infty$ the bound (\ref{eq:BRZ-454}) already implies (\ref{eq:BRZ-top}) unless
$m \le C (\log n_\varepsilon)^{1/(2 {\kappa_o})}$,  which we thus assume hereafter.  Moreover, 
as $\mathsf{d}_\mathsf{w}(\cdot,\cdot)  \le \mathsf{d}_\infty(\cdot,\cdot)$ (see (\ref{dfn:dw})),  our events 
$\mathcal{W}^{\infty,\in \log k}_{\beta,k}(\mathsf{s})$ imply the events $\mathcal{W}_{\mathsf{v}_\beta,k}(\mathsf{s})$ of \cite[(4.19)]{BRZ2}
and replacing $\log k$ by $m$ throughout \cite[Sec.  4.5]{BRZ2},  we see that 
\cite[Lemmas 4.7 \& 4.8]{BRZ2} hold here as well\footnote{Throughout \cite{BRZ2} one has the barrier
$\gamma_1(\cdot)$ with parameter ${\kappa_o}=\frac{1}{4}$ (see \cite[(4.14)]{BRZ2}),  
whereas we must use ${\kappa_o}<\frac{1}{12}$ (e.g.  part (d) relies on it).  However,    
one can check that all the proofs in \cite[Sec.  4.5]{BRZ2} work for such choice of ${\kappa_o}$,
namely,  the height parameters $a,j',j''$ can start at a lower power exponent than in \cite{BRZ2},
at the cost of having a power $\widetilde{c}=\widetilde{c}({\kappa_o}) > \frac{5}{2}$ in (\ref{eq:BRZ-471})}
with the event $\mathcal{L}'_{k,m,a}$ of (\ref{def:Lmpa}) instead of $\mathcal{L}'_{k,m,p,a}$ of \cite[(4.53)]{BRZ2},
except that unlike
\cite[(4.59)]{BRZ2},  since here  $\mathsf {K}_{3}-\mathsf {K}_{2} \ne \mathsf {K}_{2} - k$ we do not use the 
simplification step from \cite[(4.134)]{BRZ2} to \cite[(4.135)]{BRZ2}.  As  
a result the expressions in \cite[(4.71),(4.74)]{BRZ2} are respectively,  replaced by$^{1}$
\begin{align}\label{eq:BRZ-471}
G_{k,a,j',j''}(m) &=  (a+m^{\widetilde{c}}) e^{-2a} e^{-2 (\mathsf {K}_{3}-k)}
\!\!\!\!\! \sum_{\stackrel{\{\bar j' : |\bar j' - j' | \le 2 M_0 m\}}{\{\bar j'' : |\bar j'' - j'' | \le 2 M_0 m}\}}\!\!\!\!\!
\frac{\bar j'}{(\mathsf {K}_{2}-k)^{3/2}} e^{-\frac{(\bar j'-a)^2}{4(\mathsf {K}_{2}-k)}} \frac{e^{2 \bar j''}}{\sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{3}-\mathsf {K}_{2}}}
 e^{-\frac{(\bar j''-\bar j')^2}{2(\mathsf {K}_{3}-\mathsf {K}_{2})}} \,,
\\
H_{k,a,j',j''}(m) &= e^{-2a} e^{-2 (\mathsf {K}_{3}-k)}
\!\!\!\!\! \sum_{\stackrel{\{\bar j' : |\bar j' - j' | \le 2 M_0 m\}}{\{\bar j'' : |\bar j'' - j'' | \le 2 M_0 m}\}}\!\!\!\!\!
\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{2}-k}} e^{-\frac{(\bar j'-a)^2}{2(\mathsf {K}_{2}-k)}} \frac{e^{2 \bar j''}}{\sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{3}-\mathsf {K}_{2}}}
 e^{-\frac{(\bar j''-\bar j')^2}{2(\mathsf {K}_{3}-\mathsf {K}_{2})}} \,.
\label{eq:BRZ-474}
\end{align}
Here $k \in \mathsf {J}'_\mathsf{a}=[\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{\mathsf{a}}]$,  hence $\mathsf {K}_{2} - k  \ge \frac{1}{2} \mathsf {K}_{2} \gg a \vee (\mathsf {K}_{3}-\mathsf {K}_{2})$
and $a \wedge (\mathsf {K}_{3}-\mathsf {K}_{2}) \gg 1$.  It is then easy to check that for some finite $c$,  $C=C(M_0,\widetilde{c})$,
                                                                                                          
and independent $\bar j' \sim N(a,2(\mathsf {K}_{2}-k))$,  $\bar j'' -\bar j' \sim N(0,\mathsf {K}_{3}-\mathsf {K}_{2})$,
\begin{align}
\sum_{j',j''} G_{k,a,j',j''}(m)  g(j'') e^{2 \mathsf {K}_{3}} & \le c \, e^{C m} \,  a e^{-2a}  e^{2 k} 
\frac{1}{\mathsf {K}_{2}-k}  \mathbb{E} [ (1+|\bar j'|)(1+ |\bar j''|) ] 
\nonumber \\ & 
\le c^2 e^{C m} \,  a \big(1+ \frac{a^2}{\mathsf {K}_{2}}\big) e^{-2a} e^{2 k} \,, 
\label{eq:BRZ-472}\\
\label{eq:BRZ-473}
\sum_{j',j''} H_{k,a,j',j''} (m) g(j'') e^{2 \mathsf {K}_{3}} & \le c e^{C m} e^{-2a} e^{2 k} 
 \mathbb{E} [ (1+|\bar j''| )] \le c^2 e^{C m} (a + \sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{2}}) e^{-2a} e^{2 k} \,.
\end{align}
Combining (\ref{eq:BRZ-455}) and (\ref{eq:BRZ-472}),  we find that for some 
$c<\infty$,  $z$ fixed,  any $k \in \mathsf {J}'_\mathsf{a}$ and $m \ge \log k$,  
                                     
\begin{align}
\sum_{a,j',j''} G_{k,a,j',j''} (m) \mathbb{P}(\mathcal{L}'_{k,m,a}) g(j'') e^{2 \mathsf {K}_{3}} &\le c^3  e^{-2z} e^{-m^2/5}
\sum_a   a \big(1+ \frac{a^2}{\mathsf {K}_{2}}\big) e^{-(z-a)^2/(4k)} \nonumber \\
& \le c^4 \sqrt{k} (\sqrt{k}+z_+) \big(1+\frac{k+z^2}{\mathsf {K}_{2}} \big) e^{-2z} e^{-m^2/6} \le g(z) e^{-m^2/8} \,.
\label{eq:BRZ-452}
\end{align}
                                                                                    
The same bound applies with $H_{k,a,j',j''}(m)$ instead of $G_{k,a,j',j''}(m)$,  provided $m \ge 4 (\log \mathsf {K}_{3})^{1/2}$.
Thus,  analogously to \cite[(4.52)]{BRZ2},  we conclude that (\ref{eq:BRZ-top}) holds for 
for some $c'>0$,  $C<\infty$,  all $\varepsilon$ small enough,  any $k \in \mathsf {J}'_\mathsf{a}$, $m \ge \log k$ and $\beta$.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- lemma-21: body_md -->
\label{Jay-Lemma4.3}
For $\delta \in (0,1)$,  some $c=c(\delta)>0$,  any $b>a$ and all $\mathsf{x}$, 
\begin{equation}\label{A.2}
\mathbb{P} \big( T_j^{\mathsf{x}, b}  - T_j^{\mathsf{x},a} \ge \ell \,|\,  \mathcal{G}^{\tau_{\mathsf{x}}(a)} \,\big) \le e^{-c \, \ell/j},  \qquad 
\forall j \ge 1,  \;\; \ell \ge (1+2 \delta) (b-a) \,.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-21 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
By the strong Markov property of the Brownian motion at the time $\tau_{\mathsf{x}}(a)$ it took to 
complete $a$ excursions from $\partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},r_1)$ to $\partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},r_0)$,  the law of
$T_j^{\mathsf{x}, b}  - T_j^{\mathsf{x},a}$,  given $\mathcal{G}^{\tau_{\mathsf{x}}(a)}$,  matches that of $T_j^{\mathsf{x},b-a}$,  which
by radial symmetry,  is the sum of $b-a$ {\sc\lowercase{iid}} copies of $T_j^{\mathsf{x},1}$.  Noting that  
$\mathbb{P}(T_j^{\mathsf{x},1}=i)=j^{-2} (1-\frac{1}{j})^{i-1}$ for $i \ge 1$,  we deduce that $\mathbb{E}[T_j^{\mathsf{x},1}]=1$ with
$\mathbb{E}[e^{\lambda T_j^{\mathsf{x},1}/j}] \le e^{\lambda(1+\delta)/j}$ for small $\lambda>0$ and any $j \ge 1$.
By Markov's inequality,  we arrive at (\ref{A.2}) (for $c=\frac{\lambda \delta}{1+2\delta}$).
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- lemma-22: body_md -->
\label{Jay-Lemma4.3-rev}
                                                                                                   
                                                                                          
                                                            
There exist $c>0$,  so if $j \le  n_\varepsilon$ and $T^{[\tau,\tau']}_{\mathsf{x},j}$ is $\mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{x}, \tau}_j$-measurable,
then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Jay4.14}
\sup_{\mathsf{v} \in  \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x}, r_j)}
\mathbb{P}( T^{[\tau,\tau']}_{\mathsf{v},n_\varepsilon+1}=0 \;\big| \; \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{x},\tau}_j,  T^{[\tau,\tau']}_{\mathsf{x},j} \ge \ell )
 \le e^{-c \,  \ell/(n_\varepsilon-j)} \,,   \qquad \forall \ell \ge 1 \,.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-22 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
Given $\mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{x}, \tau}_j$ we know the starting points $\mathsf{w}_i \in \partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d} (\mathsf{x}, r_{j-1})$ 
and ending points $\mathsf{z}_i \in \partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d} (\mathsf{x}, r_{j})$ of the outer part of all 
excursions at level $j$ around $\mathsf{x}$,  which occur during $[\tau,\infty)$.  Since
$T:= T^{[\tau,\tau']}_{\mathsf{x},j}$ is $\mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{x}, \tau}_j$-measurable,  we have no information
about the inner parts of the subset of those excursions which are completed during $[\tau,\tau']$,  
beyond the number $T$ of such excursions and their corresponding starting and ending points.  
Setting $\rho_j:=e^{-(n_\varepsilon-j+1)}$,  the {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of (\ref{eq:Jay4.14}) is thus bounded above by the probability 
that $\ell$ independent Brownian path from $\partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},r_j)$ to $\partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},r_{j-1})$, 
with starting and ending points $(\mathsf{z}_i,\mathsf{w}_{i+1})$, 
miss $B_1 := \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{v}, \rho_j r_j)$.  Set $B_2 := \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{v}, e^{-1} r_j)$ and $B_3:= \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{v}, r_j)$,
noting that $B_1 \subseteq B_2 \subset B_3 \subset \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},2 r_j)$.  
Let $q^{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf{z},\mathsf{w}}(j)$ denote the probability of the event $\Gamma$ 
that a Brownian path starting at $\mathsf{z} \in \partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d} (\mathsf{x},r_j)$ and ending at 
$\mathsf{w} \in \partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d} (\mathsf{x},r_{j-1})$ visits $\partial B_2$ before $\partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d} (\mathsf{x}, 2 r_j)$
and thereafter enters $B_1$ before exiting $B_3$,  using $q^{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf{z}}(j)$ for such probability when 
               
$\mathsf{w}$ is not specified.  Since a Brownian path from $\mathsf{y} \in \partial B_2$ enters $B_1$ before exiting $B_3$ 
with probability
 \[
q (j) := \frac{1}{n_\varepsilon-j+1}\,,
\]
we get (\ref{eq:Jay4.14}) (with $c=\frac{1}{2} c_1 c_2$),  upon finding $c_i>0$ for $i=1,2$,  such that 
uniformly over $\mathsf{z}$,  $\mathsf{w}$,  $\mathsf{x}$,  $\mathsf{v}$ and $j$, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:unif-bd}
