q^{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf{z},\mathsf{w}} (j) \ge c_1 \,  q^{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf{z}}(j) \,, \qquad 
q^{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf{z}}(j) \ge c_2 \, q (j) \,.
\end{equation}
The quantities in (\ref{eq:unif-bd}) are about planar Brownian motion,  so by 
translation invariance and Brownian scaling we can fix hereafter $\mathsf{x}={\bf 0}$ and $r_j=1$.  
Doing so,  the probabilities $q^{\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf{z}}$ that the
                  
path from $\mathsf{z}$ hits $\partial \mathbb{B}(\mathsf{v},e^{-1})$ before exiting $\mathbb{B}({\bf 0},2)$,  are continuous 
in $(\mathsf{z},\mathsf{v})$ and positive for $\|\mathsf{z}\|=1$ and $\|\mathsf{v}\| \le 1$.  Hence,
\[
c_2 := \inf_{\stackrel{\|\mathsf{z}\|=1}{\|\mathsf{v}\| \le 1}}  \{ q^{\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf{z}} \} > 0 \,,
\] 
and the right-side of (\ref{eq:unif-bd}) follows,  since by strong Markov
$q_{\mathsf{z}}^{{\bf 0},\mathsf{v}}(j) \ge q_\mathsf{z}^\mathsf{v} \,  q (j)$.  Next,  the Poisson kernel $p(\mathsf{y},\mathsf{w})$  
for the exit measure of $\mathbb{B}({\bf 0},e)$ is such that 
\[
c_1 := \inf_{\stackrel{\|\mathsf{z}_i\|=2}{\|\mathsf{w}\|=e}}  \;\;\; \Big\{ \frac{p(\mathsf{z}_1,\mathsf{w})}{p(\mathsf{z}_2,\mathsf{w})} \Big\} > 0 \,.
\]
With $\Gamma$ measurable on the Brownian path up to its first exit from $\mathbb{B}({\bf 0},2)$,  
restricted to $\sigma(\Gamma)$,  the Radon-Nikodym derivative 
                                  
due to conditioning on exiting $\mathbb{B}({\bf 0},e)$ at $\mathsf{w}$,  is at least $c_1$,  implying the
left-side of (\ref{eq:unif-bd}).
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
From (\ref{eq:g-def}) we have that uniformly on $\bar{\mathsf I}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}} \times \mathsf{I}_{\measuredangle}$,  
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gstb-z}
g_o(y,v)=(1+o_{\mathsf {K}_{0}}(1)) g_o(y-z,v) e^{-2 z} \,.
\end{equation}
Setting the non-negative
\begin{equation}\label{def:X-eps-pre}
\bar Q^{(1,\varepsilon)}_{u,z} := 
\,  \alpha (\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6}) \bar b_{\mathsf {K}_{0}} \,  e^{-2 z}
\operatorname*{\mathrlap{\hspace{.2ex}\rotatebox[origin=c]{20}{\bf---}}{\sum}}_{\beta  \in u} \mathbb{E} \Big[ g_o \big( \widehat{\eta}^{\,[z]}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}-z, V^{[z]}_{\beta} \big) ; \widehat{\eta}^{\,[z]}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}} \in \bar{\mathsf I}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}},
L_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{[z]} \in \mathbb{B}^\infty_{\bar \mu} ( \boldsymbol{\eta}^{\star,(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}) 
\,\big|\,  \mathcal{H}_{\mathsf{k}_\varepsilon(z)}  \Big] \,,
\end{equation}
we deduce,  in view of (\ref{eq:wtQ1-bd}) and (\ref{eq:gstb-z}), 
that as claimed in (\ref{eq:eqv-wt-Q}),  
\[
\widetilde{Q}^{(1,\varepsilon)}_{u,z}
                                                            
                                                                                    
                                                                     
    
= 
(1+o_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon}(1)) \bar Q^{(1,\varepsilon)}_{u,z} \,.
\]
In view of (\ref{eq:Ball-to-angle}),  only $V^{[z]}_{\beta} \in \mathsf{I}_{\measuredangle}$ can contribute to $ \bar Q^{(1,\varepsilon)}_{u,z}$,
so comparing (\ref{def:X-eps}) with (\ref{def:X-eps-pre}) we deduce that
$\bar Q^{(1,\varepsilon)}_{u,z} \le \mathsf {X}^{(\varepsilon)}_{u,z} e^{-2 z}$ 
(since the indicator on $\bar{\mathsf I}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}} \times \mathsf{I}_{\measuredangle}$ is bounded above by $g_\star(\cdot)$ of (\ref{eq:g-def-alt})).
The proof of \Cref{lem:good-cover-end} is thus concluded upon establishing (\ref{eq:wX-small}).  To this end,
note that $g_\star(\cdot) \le g_o(\cdot)$ with equality on $\bar{\mathsf I}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}} \times \mathsf{I}_{\measuredangle}$ and fixing 
${\kappa_1^-} < {\kappa_1}$,  ${\kappa'_+} > {\kappa'}$,  $\kappa_\star$ and $z$,  for all large enough $\mathsf {K}_{1}$, 
\[
g_\star(y-z,v) >0 \quad \Longrightarrow \quad 
g_o(y-z,v) e^{-2 z} \le 2 g_o(y,v) \,,
                                           
\] 
while $g_\star(\cdot)$ is zero outside 
                                                                                      
\begin{equation}
\label{def:DI}
\mathsf{I}^{\mathsf{e}}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}} \times \mathsf{I}^{\mathsf{e}}_{\measuredangle} := [\mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa_1^-}},\mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa'_+}}] \times[-3\kappa_\star \log \mathsf {K}_{1},3\kappa_\star \log \mathsf {K}_{1}] \,.
                                                          
\end{equation}
For such $\mathsf {K}_{1}$,  we thus have that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bd-wX}
\mathsf {X}^{(\varepsilon)}_{u,z} e^{-2 z} - \bar Q^{(1,\varepsilon)}_{u,z} 
\le 2 \alpha (\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6}) \bar b_{\mathsf {K}_{0}} \Big[   
\operatorname*{\mathrlap{\hspace{.2ex}\rotatebox[origin=c]{20}{\bf---}}{\sum}}_{\beta  \in u} \widehat{\mathsf {X}}^{(\varepsilon,\measuredangle)}_{\beta,z} + \operatorname*{\mathrlap{\hspace{.2ex}\rotatebox[origin=c]{20}{\bf---}}{\sum}}_{\beta \in u} \widehat{\mathsf {X}}^{(\varepsilon,\Cap)}_{\beta,z} \Big]\,,
\end{equation}
where for any $\beta \in u$,  
\begin{align}
\widehat{\mathsf {X}}^{(\measuredangle)}_{\beta,z} &:= 
\mathbb{E} \Big[ g_o \big( \widehat{\eta}^{\,[z]}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}, V^{[z]}_{\beta} \big); 
\widehat{\eta}^{\,[z]}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}} \in \bar{\mathsf I}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}},
V^{[z]}_{\beta} \in \mathsf{I}^{\mathsf{e}}_{\measuredangle},
L_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{[z]} \notin \mathbb{B}^\infty_{\bar \mu} ( \boldsymbol{\eta}^{\star,(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}) 
\,\big|\, 
 \mathcal{H}^\star_u 
\Big] \,,
\nonumber
                   
\\
                   
\widehat{\mathsf {X}}^{(\varepsilon,\Cap)}_{\beta,z} &:= \mathbb{E} \Big[ g_o \big( \widehat{\eta}^{\,[z]}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}, V^{[z]}_{\beta} \big); \widehat{\eta}^{\,[z]}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}} \in \mathsf{I}^{\mathsf{e}}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}} \setminus \bar{\mathsf I}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}},
V^{[z]}_{\beta} \in \mathsf{I}^{\mathsf{e}}_{\measuredangle}
\,\big|\,  
 \mathcal{H}^\star_u
 \Big] 
\end{align}
(and utilizing \Cref{rmk:z-a-vep},  we have changed to conditioning on the larger $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal{H}^\star_u$).
In view of (\ref{def:bar-bKz}),  it thus suffices to fix $\delta>0$ and show that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:wX-small-alt}
\varlimsup_{\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon} 
\mathbb{P} \Big[
\operatorname*{\mathrlap{\hspace{.2ex}\rotatebox[origin=c]{20}{\bf---}}{\sum}}_{\beta} \widehat{\mathsf {X}}^{(\varepsilon,\measuredangle)}_{\beta,z} > \delta e^{-2 \mathsf {K}_{1}} \Big] = 0 \,, 
\qquad 
\varlimsup_{\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon} \mathbb{P} \Big[
\operatorname*{\mathrlap{\hspace{.2ex}\rotatebox[origin=c]{20}{\bf---}}{\sum}}_{\beta} \widehat{\mathsf {X}}^{(\varepsilon,\Cap)}_{\beta,z} 
  > \delta e^{-2 \mathsf {K}_{1}} \Big] = 0 \,,
\end{equation}
where now we average over all blocks.
Moreover,  by \Cref{Thm4.1+4.2-Jay} we can and shall intersect the variables in (\ref{eq:wX-small-alt}) 
with the events $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k},\beta}^{[z]}$ of (\ref{def:Jay-Thm4.1}),  which are measurable on $\mathcal{H}^\star_u$ when $\beta \in u$.
Upon doing so,  by Markov's inequality,  (\ref{eq:wX-small-alt}) follows from having that for any fixed
$\mathsf{k}$,
\begin{align}\label{eq:wX-sfw-small}
\varlimsup_{\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon} 
 e^{2 \mathsf {K}_{1}} \sup_{\beta} 
& \mathbb{E} \Big[ g_o\big(\widehat{\eta}^{\,[z]}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}},V^{[z]}_{\beta}\big); \mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k},\beta}^{[z]},  \widehat{\eta}^{\,[z]}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}} \in \bar{\mathsf I}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}},V^{[z]}_{\beta} \in \mathsf{I}^{\mathsf{e}}_{\measuredangle},
L_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{[z]} \notin \mathbb{B}^\infty_{\bar \mu} ( \boldsymbol{\eta}^{\star,(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}})  
\Big] = 0 \,,\\
\varlimsup_{\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon} 
 e^{2 \mathsf {K}_{1}} \sup_{\beta} 
& \mathbb{E} \Big[ g_o \big( \widehat{\eta}^{\,[z]}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}, V^{[z]}_{\beta} \big); \mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k},\beta}^{[z]},  \widehat{\eta}^{\,[z]}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}} \in \mathsf{I}^{\mathsf{e}}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}} \setminus \bar{\mathsf I}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}},  V^{[z]}_{\beta} \in \mathsf{I}^{\mathsf{e}}_{\measuredangle} \Big] = 0 \,. 
 \label{eq:wX-Cap-small}
\end{align}
Recall (\ref{def:Jay-Thm4.1-cons}) that $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k},\beta}^{[z]}$ implies having for $z'=z-\log \mathsf{k}$ and $z''=z+\log \mathsf{k}$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Akbz-cons}
T_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\mathsf{v}_\beta,\mathsf{s}_1(z')} \le T_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{[z]} \le  T_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\mathsf{v}_\beta,\mathsf{s}_1(z'')} \quad \text{and} \quad \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,\langle z' \rangle} \le \widehat{\eta}^{\,[z]}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}} \le \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,\langle z'' \rangle}\,.
\end{equation}
In addition,  $2(\mathsf{s}_1(z'')-\mathsf{s}_1(z')) \le C_{\mathsf{k}} n_\varepsilon$
for $C_\mathsf{k}$ finite,  all $\mathsf {K}_{0}$ large and any $\varepsilon$ (see (\ref{eq:b-a-bd})),  whereupon by (\ref{A.2-n})
\begin{equation}\label{A.2-alt}
\sup_{\beta} \mathbb{P}\big( T_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\mathsf{v}_\beta,\mathsf{s}_1(z'')} - T_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\mathsf{v}_\beta,\mathsf{s}_1(z')} \ge C_\mathsf{k} n_\varepsilon 
                                    
\big) \le 
e^{-c \, C_\mathsf{k} n_\varepsilon/\mathsf {K}_{1}} = o_\varepsilon(1) \,.
\end{equation}
We set $V^{\langle z' \rangle}_{\beta}  =  h^{\measuredangle}_{\varepsilon}(L_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\langle z' \rangle})$ for $h^{\measuredangle}_{\varepsilon}(\cdot)$ of (\ref{dfn:hat-L-alpha}).  Then,  noting that for some 
$c'=c'({\kappa'},\kappa_\star)$ finite
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bd-gstb}
g_o(y,v) \le \mathsf {K}_{1}^{c'} e^{-2y} \le \mathsf {K}_{1}^{c'}  \qquad \forall y \in \mathsf{I}^{\mathsf{e}}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}},  v \in \mathsf{I}^{\mathsf{e}}_{\measuredangle} \,,
\end{equation}
by (\ref{eq:Akbz-cons})--(\ref{eq:bd-gstb}),  we can and will
replace the event $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k},\beta}^{[z]}$ on the {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of (\ref{eq:wX-sfw-small})-(\ref{eq:wX-Cap-small}) by 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Akbz-alt}
n_\varepsilon^{-1} \big( T_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{[z]} - T_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\mathsf{v}_\beta,\mathsf{s}_1(z')} \big) \in [0, C_{\mathsf{k}}]\,,   \quad 
\widehat{\eta}^{\,[z]}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}} - \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,\langle z' \rangle} \in [0, \frac{1}{2} C_{\mathsf{k}}]\,,
                                                         
                                                                                                    
                   
\quad 
|V^{[z]}_{\beta}  - V^{\langle z' \rangle}_{\beta}| 
                                                                          
                                                                    
\le 2 \bar c \, C_{\mathsf{k}}  \,.
\end{equation}
Under (\ref{eq:Akbz-alt}),  for large $\mathsf {K}_{0}$ it follows from (\ref{eq:dinf-comp}) 
(similarly to our reasoning for (\ref{dfn:bb-extra})),  that also
\begin{align*}
\{ \widehat{\eta}^{\,[z]}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}} \in \bar{\mathsf I}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}},  L_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{[z]} \notin \mathbb{B}^\infty_{\bar \mu} ( \boldsymbol{\eta}^{\star,(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}) \}  &\subset 
\{ \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,\langle z' \rangle} \in \mathsf{I}^{\mathsf{e}}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}},  L_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\langle z' \rangle} \notin \mathbb{B}^\infty_{\bar \mu} (\boldsymbol{\eta}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}) \} \,.
\end{align*}
Further,  then having $\widehat{\eta}^{\,[z]}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}} \in \mathsf{I}^{\mathsf{e}}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}} \setminus \bar{\mathsf I}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}$ implies the same for $\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,\langle z' \rangle}$
upon slightly reducing the parameters ${\kappa_1^-}$ and ${\kappa'}$.
Finally,  with $y \mapsto g_o(y,v)$ 
decreasing on $\bar{\mathsf I}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}$ (for all large enough $\mathsf {K}_{0}$),  we further 
replace $g_o(\widehat{\eta}^{\,[z]}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}},V^{[z]}_{\beta})$ in (\ref{eq:wX-Cap-small}) by $g_o(\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,\langle z' \rangle},V^{\langle z' \rangle}_{\beta})$ and in
(\ref{eq:wX-sfw-small}) utilize (\ref{eq:bd-gstb}) to replace it instead by 
$\mathsf {K}_{1}^{c'} e^{-2 \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,\langle z' \rangle}}$.  

Implementing all those modifications,  our claims (\ref{eq:wX-sfw-small})-(\ref{eq:wX-Cap-small}) are 
a direct consequence of 
\begin{align}\label{eq:wX-sfw-alt}
\varlimsup_{\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon} 
\mathsf {K}_{1}^{c'} e^{2 \mathsf {K}_{1}} 
& \mathbb{E} \Big[ e^{-2  \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,\langle z' \rangle}};  \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,\langle z' \rangle} \in \mathsf{I}^{\mathsf{e}}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}},
L_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\langle z' \rangle} \notin \mathbb{B}^\infty_{\bar \mu} (\boldsymbol{\eta}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}})  
\Big] = 0 \,,\\
\varlimsup_{\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon} 
 e^{2 \mathsf {K}_{1}} 
& \mathbb{E} \Big[  \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,\langle z' \rangle} e^{-2 \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,\langle z' \rangle}} e^{-2 V^{\langle z' \rangle}_{\beta}}; \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,\langle z' \rangle} \in \mathsf{I}^{\mathsf{e}}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}} \setminus \bar{\mathsf I}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}} \Big] = 0 
 \label{eq:wX-Cap-alt}
\end{align}
(and we have dropped the supremum over $\beta$,  since $(\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,\langle z' \rangle},L_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\langle z' \rangle})$ have 
the same distribution at all blocks).  

Proceeding to confirm (\ref{eq:wX-sfw-alt})-(\ref{eq:wX-Cap-alt}),  recall that 
conditional on completing precisely $\mathsf{s}' =\mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}(\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,\langle z' \rangle})$ 
excursions at level $\mathsf {K}_{1}$ during the first $\mathsf{s}_1(z')$ 
level one excursions,  $L_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\langle z' \rangle}$ is the empirical measure of $\mathsf{s}'$ {\sc\lowercase{iid}} 
samples from the law $\bar \mu$.  Thus,  similarly to (\ref{eq:BRZ-454}) we have 
for some $c>0$ any $\kappa_\star \ge c_0$ and $\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,\langle z' \rangle} \in \mathsf{I}^{\mathsf{e}}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}$
\begin{equation}\label{eq:BRZ-454-new}
\mathbb{P}\Big( 
L_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\langle z' \rangle} \notin \mathbb{B}^\infty_{\bar \mu} (\boldsymbol{\eta}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}})  \,\big|\,  \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,\langle z' \rangle} \Big) \le 2 e^{-c (\log \mathsf {K}_{1})^2} \,.
\end{equation}
Likewise,  given $\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,\langle z' \rangle}$,  the variable $2 V^{\langle z' \rangle}_{\beta}$ is the sum of $\mathsf{s}'$ centered,  $[-1,1]$-valued,  {\sc\lowercase{iid}} 
variables multiplied by the factor $\bar c \,  \mathsf{m}_{\varepsilon}/\mathsf{s}'$.  Hence,  with 
$\sup\{ \mathsf{m}_{\varepsilon}^2/\mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}(y) : y \in \mathsf{I}^{\mathsf{e}}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}} \}$
bounded uniformly in $\mathsf {K}_{0}$ large and $\varepsilon$ small,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bd-Vbp}
\mathbb{E} \Big[ e^{-2 V^{\langle z' \rangle}_{\beta}} \, \big| \,  \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,\langle z' \rangle} \Big] \le e^{(\bar c \, \mathsf{m}_{\varepsilon})^2/(2 \mathsf{s}')} \le C
\end{equation}
for some $C$ finite.
Next,  applying
the Gaussian tail bounds of \cite[Proposition  1.4]{BRZ},  for $\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,\langle z' \rangle}$
                                                                     
and $\varepsilon \to 0$,  we deduce that 
                                                                                                          
                                                                                        
                                                
for $I_u=[u,u+1)$ and some $C=C(z')$ finite, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:clt-bd-pKo}
\varlimsup_{\varepsilon \to 0} \mathbb{P}(\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,\langle z' \rangle} \in I_u) \le C \,  \mathsf {K}_{1}^{-1/2} e^{-2(\mathsf {K}_{1}-u)} e^{-u^2/(2 \mathsf {K}_{1})} \,,
                                       
\qquad \forall u \in \mathsf{I}^{\mathsf{e}}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}
\end{equation}
(as $z'=O(1)$ and $\mathsf {K}_{1} \gg 1$).  Clearly,  (\ref{eq:clt-bd-pKo}) implies having
for $2{\kappa_1} < \frac{1}{2} < {\kappa'}$ and any $c>0$,  that 
\[
\sum_{u = \mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa_1^-}}}^{\mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa'_+}}} e^{2(\mathsf {K}_{1}-u)}
 \mathbb{P}(\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,\langle z' \rangle} \in I_u)
 \Big(2 \mathsf {K}_{1}^{c'}
e^{-c (\log \mathsf {K}_{1})^2} + u {\bf 1}_{u \le \mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa_1}}} + \mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa'_+}} {\bf 1}_{u \ge \mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa'}}} 
\Big) = o_{\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon}(1)  \,.
\]
We thus conclude by covering $\mathsf{I}^{\mathsf{e}}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}$ with intervals $I_u$ of integer end-points 
and plugging in (\ref{eq:wX-sfw-alt}) and (\ref{eq:wX-Cap-alt})
our uniform bounds (\ref{eq:BRZ-454-new}) and (\ref{eq:bd-Vbp}),  respectively.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- lemma-23: body_md -->
\label{lem:2mm-star}
Fix $\mathsf{\delta_\star}$ and ${\kappa_o}$,  ${\kappa''}$ as in (\ref{dfn:aux-par}).  Then,  for any fixed $z$ and $\mathsf {K}_{5}$, 
\begin{equation}
\varlimsup_{\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon} \mathbb{P} \Big( \sum_{u=1}^{\mathsf {M}} \widetilde{Q}^{(\star,\varepsilon)}_{u,z} \ge 1 \Big) = 0 \,,
\label{eq:2mm-star}
\end{equation}
where 
\begin{equation}\label{dfn:Qst}
\widetilde{Q}^{(\star,\varepsilon)}_{u,z} :=  \operatorname*{\mathrlap{\hspace{.2ex}\rotatebox[origin=c]{20}{\bf---}}{\sum}}_{\beta \in u}
\mathbb{E} \big[ e^{-2 \widehat{\eta}^{\,[z]}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}'_{1}}}; \widehat{\eta}^{\,[z]}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}'_{1}} \in \bar{\mathsf I}_{\mathsf {K}'_{1}}  | \mathcal{F}^{\varepsilon}_{u,z} \big] \qquad \hbox{with} \qquad \mathsf {K}'_{1}=\mathsf {K}_{1}+3.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-23 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
By \Cref{Thm4.1+4.2-Jay},  the event
$\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k}}^{[z]}$ of (\ref{def:Jay-Thm4.1}) holds up to decaying probability (of $C \mathsf{k}^{-4}$),  so it suffices to establish 
(\ref{eq:2mm-star}) with $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k}}^{[z]}$ intersecting the event on its {\sc\lowercase{lhs}}.  Having done so,  since $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k}}^{[z]}$ is the intersection of events $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k},\beta}^{[z]}$ 
                              
which are $\mathcal{F}^{\varepsilon}_{u,z}$-measurable whenever $\beta \in u$,  we can and will 
replace $\widetilde{Q}^{(\star,\varepsilon)}_{u,z}$ in (\ref{eq:2mm-star}) by
\[
\operatorname*{\mathrlap{\hspace{.2ex}\rotatebox[origin=c]{20}{\bf---}}{\sum}}_{\beta \in u} \sum_{i}
                               
 e^{-2 (y_{(i)}-1)}
\mathbb{P} \big[ \mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k},\beta}^{[z]} \cap \{ \widehat{\eta}^{\,[z]}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}'_{1}} \le y_{(i)} \} | \mathcal{F}^{\varepsilon}_{u,z} \big] \,,
\]
where $\{y_{(i)}\}$ forms a uniform partition of $\bar{\mathsf I}_{\mathsf {K}'_{1}}$ to $\mathsf {K}_{1}$ points.
With $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k},\beta}^{[z]}$ implying that 
$\widehat{\eta}^{\,[z]}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}'_{1}} \ge \widehat{\eta}^{\,\langle z' \rangle}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}'_{1}}$ for $z'=z-\log \mathsf{k}$
(see (\ref{def:Jay-Thm4.1-cons})),  we further bound above this proxy for $\widetilde{Q}^{(\star,\varepsilon)}_{u,z}$ by
\[
e^{2} \operatorname*{\mathrlap{\hspace{.2ex}\rotatebox[origin=c]{20}{\bf---}}{\sum}}_{\beta \in u} \sum_{i} e^{-2 y_{(i)}} \mathbb{P} \big[  \widehat{\eta}^{\,\langle z' \rangle}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}'_{1}} \le y_{(i)}  | \mathcal{F}^{\varepsilon}_{u,z} \big] \,.
\]
Plugging this bound on $\widetilde{Q}^{(\star,\varepsilon)}_{u,z}$ into (\ref{eq:2mm-star}),  we deduce 
by Markov's inequality that the probability on the {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of (\ref{eq:2mm-star}) is at most 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:418-alt}
e^{2} \,  \mathsf {K}_{1} \,  \mathsf {M}\,  \max_{\beta,  y \in \bar{\mathsf I}_{\mathsf {K}'_{1}}} \{ e^{-2 y} \mathbb{P} (  \widehat{\eta}^{\,\langle z' \rangle}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}'_{1}} \le y ) \} \,.
\end{equation}
Next,  recall  (\ref{eq-calgary}),  that for any $z'$,  $y$ and $\beta$, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:T-eta}
\mathbb{P} \big( \widehat{\eta}^{\,\langle z' \rangle}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}'_{1}} \le y \big) = \mathbb{P}\big( T^{\mathsf{v}_\beta,\mathsf{s}_1(z')}_{\mathsf {K}'_{1}} \le \mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}'_{1}}(y) \big),
\end{equation}
where in view of (\ref{eq:Jay1.12}),  the variable $T^{\mathsf{v}_\beta,m}_{\mathsf {K}'_{1}}$ is the sum $S_m$
of $m$ {\sc\lowercase{iid}} non-negative integer variables of the form (\ref{dfn:GJp})
for the parameter $q=\frac{1}{\mathsf {K}'_{1}}$.  With $\mathsf {K}_{1} \mathsf {M}  e^{-2 \mathsf {K}'_{1}} \to 0$ 
                         
and the law of $S_m$ independent of $\beta$ and $\varepsilon$,  we deduce in view of (\ref{eq:T-eta}),
that the expression in (\ref{eq:418-alt}) decays to zero with $\mathsf {K}_{0}$,  if for some $c(z')$ finite
\begin{equation}\label{eq:amir-lem418-equiv}
\varlimsup_{\varepsilon \to 0} \mathbb{P}\big( S_{\mathsf{s}_1(z')} \le \mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}'_{1}}(y) \big)
\le c(z') e^{-2 \mathsf {K}'_{1}} e^{2y}\,,  \qquad \forall \mathsf {K}'_{1},  \;\; y \in \bar{\mathsf I}_{\mathsf {K}'_{1}} \,.
\end{equation}
Recall (\ref{eq:special-norm}) and (\ref{eq:nominal}) that $\mathsf{s}_1(z') \to \infty$ as $\varepsilon \to 0$,  and
as $\mathbb{E}[S_1]=1$,  ${\rm var}(S_1)=2(\mathsf {K}'_{1}-1)$ (see (\ref{eq:GJp-var})),  also an elementary calculation shows that
\[
\frac{ \mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}'_{1}}(y) - \mathbb{E}[S_{\mathsf{s}_1(z')}]}{\sqrt{\hbox{var}(S_{\mathsf{s}_1(z')})}} \to
\frac{y-z' -2(\mathsf {K}'_{1}-1)}{\sqrt{\mathsf {K}'_{1}-1}} := \mathsf{t} \,.
\]
Consequently,  by the {\sc\lowercase{clt}},  for any $z'$,  $y$ and $\mathsf {K}'_{1}$ (such that $\mathsf{t} \le 0$),  
\[
\varlimsup_{\varepsilon \to 0} \mathbb{P}\big( S_{\mathsf{s}_1(z')} \le \mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}'_{1}}(y) \big) = 
\Phi(\mathsf{t}) \le e^{-\frac{1}{2} \mathsf{t}^2} \le e^{-2(\mathsf {K}'_{1}-1)} e^{2(y-z')}\,,
\]
as claimed in (\ref{eq:amir-lem418-equiv}),  which thereby concludes our proof of (\ref{eq:2mm-star}).
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- lemma-24: body_md -->
\label{lem:right-tight}
The  variables $\mathcal{U}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\beta,[z]}$ of  (\ref{dfn:UUz}) are such that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:right-tight}
\lim_{z \to \infty} \varlimsup_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon} \,\mathbb{P} \big( \bigcup_{\beta} \mathcal{U}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\beta,[z]} \big) = 0 \,.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-24 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
By (\ref{dfn:UU-alt}) and  \Cref{Thm4.1+4.2-Jay},  we get (\ref{eq:right-tight}) upon showing that
for small $\widetilde{c}$,  $r_0$ and any fixed $\mathsf{k} \ge 1$,  
\begin{equation}\label{eq:81}
\lim_{z \to \infty} \varlimsup_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon} \,\mathbb{P} \big( \bigcup_{\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F}} 
\{ \eta_{\mathsf{v},n_\varepsilon+1}^{[z]} = 0,  \mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k}}^{[z]},  \widetilde{\mathcal{R}}_{\mathsf{k}}^{\langle z' \rangle} \} \big)  = 0 \,,
\end{equation}
where $z':=z-\log \mathsf{k}$ and the events $\widetilde{\mathcal{R}}_{\mathsf{k}}^{\langle z \rangle}$,  $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k}}^{[z]}$ are as
 in (\ref{def:Jay-Thm4.2}) and (\ref{def:Jay-Thm4.1}).  To this end,  from (\ref{agar.67a})-(\ref{lem-first-moment}) 
                   
and the union bound,  it follows that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:82}
\lim_{z \to \infty} \varlimsup_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\varepsilon} \,\mathbb{P} \big( \bigcup_{\beta,\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F}^\beta} \mathcal{U}^{(\varepsilon),\beta,\langle z' \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\mathsf{v}}
 \big)  \le C_\mathsf{k} \lim_{z \to \infty} (1+z'_+) e^{-2 z'} = 0 \,.
\end{equation}
Further,  recall (\ref{def:Jay-Thm4.1-cons}) and (\ref{def:UUvk}) that 
$\{ \eta_{\mathsf{v},n_\varepsilon+1}^{[z]} = 0,  \mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k}}^{[z]},  \widetilde{\mathcal{R}}_{\mathsf{k}}^{\langle z' \rangle} \} \subset \mathcal{U}^{(\varepsilon),\beta,\langle z' \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\mathsf{v}}$ for any $\mathsf{v} \in \mathbb{F}^\beta$,  
hence (\ref{eq:81}) is a consequence of (\ref{eq:82}).
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- lemma-25: body_md -->
\label{lem:clt-left-tight}
Taking  $z=z(\mathsf {K}_{1}):=-2 \mathsf {K}_{1} + \frac{1}{2} \mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa'}}$, 
\begin{align}
\varlimsup_{\mathsf {K}_{1},\varepsilon} \sup_\beta \mathbb{P} ( 
\{ L_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{[z]} \notin \mathbb{B}^\infty_{\bar \mu} (2 \boldsymbol{\eta}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}) \} \cap \{ \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,[z]}  \in \bar{\mathsf I}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}} \}) 
& = 0 \,,
\label{eq:VKo-good}
\\
\label{eq:YKo-good}
\varlimsup_{\mathsf {K}_{1},\varepsilon} \sup_\beta \mathbb{P} ( \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,[z]}  \notin \bar{\mathsf I}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}} ) & = 0\,.
\end{align}
<!-- end lemma-25 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
In view of the left-side of (\ref{eq:Jay-Thm-4.2}),  {\sc\lowercase{wlog}} we intersect the events in 
(\ref{eq:VKo-good}) and (\ref{eq:YKo-good}) with $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{k}}^{[z]}$ of (\ref{def:Jay-Thm4.1}),  thereby having 
the properties of (\ref{def:Jay-Thm4.1-cons}).  With these in place,  as in the proof of \Cref{lem:adjust-AUz},
the event in (\ref{eq:VKo-good}) implies that at $j=\mathsf {K}_{1}$,  either (\ref{eq:Tb-Ta-W}) holds,
or $L_{\beta,j}^{\langle z' \rangle} \notin \mathbb{B}^{\infty}_{\bar \mu} \big(\boldsymbol{\eta}^{(\varepsilon)}_j \big)$ and $\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,j}^{\,\langle z' \rangle} \in [\frac{1}{2} j^{{\kappa_1}},j^{{\kappa'}}]$.
Similarly,  the event of (\ref{eq:YKo-good}) then implies 
that either $\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,\langle z' \rangle} \le \mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa_1}}$
or  $\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,\langle z'' \rangle} \ge \mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa'}}$.

For $z=z(\mathsf {K}_{1})$ we still have (\ref{eq:b-a-bd}) holding at any $\mathsf {K}_{1} \ge \mathsf {K}_{1}'(\mathsf{k})$,  and thus 
deduce from (\ref{A.2-n}),  similarly to (\ref{eq:step1-123}),
that the probability of (\ref{eq:Tb-Ta-W}) holding at $j=\mathsf {K}_{1}$ remains $o_\varepsilon(1)$.
Further,  conditional on $\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,j}^{\,\langle z' \rangle}=\sqrt{2 \mathsf{s}}-\gamma_0(j)$,  we have that $L_{\beta,j}^{\langle z' \rangle}$ is 
the empirical measure of $\mathsf{s}$ {\sc\lowercase{iid}} samples from $\bar \mu$. 
Hence,  by (\ref{lbl:d-inf-bd}),  we have for $\kappa_\star \ge c_0$ 
and $j=\mathsf {K}_{1}$,  that uniformly over $\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,j}^{\,\langle z' \rangle} \in [\frac{1}{2} j^{{\kappa_1}},j^{{\kappa'}}]$
\[
\mathbb{P} \big( L_{\beta,j}^{\langle z' \rangle} \notin \mathbb{B}^{\infty}_{\bar \mu} \big(\boldsymbol{\eta}^{(\varepsilon)}_j \big) \, \big| \, 
 \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,j}^{\,\langle z' \rangle} \big) \le 2 \sum_{m \ge \log j} e^{-m^2/4} 
\]
(see (\ref{eq:Lkp-WNa}) and (\ref{eq:BRZ-454})).  With the latter bound being $o_j(1)$,  this 
concludes the proof of (\ref{eq:VKo-good}).

Next,  note that $\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,\langle z' \rangle} \le \mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa_1}}$ 
implies having at most $\mathsf{s}'=\mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}(\mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa_1}})$ excursions at level $\mathsf {K}_{1}$
within the first $\mathsf{s}=\mathsf{s}_1(z')$ excursions at level one.  Thus,  by the {\sc\lowercase{clt}} for 
$\big(\sqrt{2 T^{\mathsf{v}_\beta,\mathsf{s}}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}}-\sqrt{2\mathsf{s}}\, \big)/\sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{1}}$ (as $\mathsf{s} \to \infty$),  see  
(\ref{eq-calgary}) and (\ref{eq:Jay1.12}),  or \cite[Proposition  1.4]{BRZ},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:YKo-clt-lb}
\mathbb{P}\big( \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,\langle z' \rangle} \le \mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa_1}} \big) \le C \int_{-\infty}^{w_1} e^{-u^2/2} du \,,
\end{equation}
where by our choice of $z(\mathsf {K}_{1})$
                                      
we have that for some $\alpha>0$ and any $\mathsf {K}_{1} \ge \mathsf {K}_{1}'(\mathsf{k})$,  
\[
w_1:=\frac{\sqrt{2 \mathsf{s}'}-\sqrt{2 \mathsf{s}}}{\sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{1}}}
=\frac{- \boldsymbol{\rho}_\varepsilon \mathsf {K}_{1} + \mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa_1}}-z(\mathsf {K}_{1})+\log \mathsf{k}}{\sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{1}}} \le - \mathsf {K}_{1}^{\alpha} \,.
\]
The {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} of (\ref{eq:YKo-clt-lb}) is thus $o_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}(1)$.  
Similarly,  taking now $\mathsf{s}=\mathsf{s}_1(z'')$ and $\mathsf{s}'=\mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}(\mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa'}})$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:YKo-clt-ub}
\mathbb{P}\big( \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\,\langle z'' \rangle} \ge \mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa'}} \big) \le C \int_{w_2}^{\infty} e^{-u^2/2} du \,,
\end{equation}
where by our choice of $z(\mathsf {K}_{1})$,  for any $\mathsf {K}_{1} \ge \mathsf {K}_{1}'(\mathsf{k})$,  
\[
w_2=\frac{\sqrt{2 \mathsf{s}'}-\sqrt{2 \mathsf{s}}}{\sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{1}}}
=\frac{- \boldsymbol{\rho}_\varepsilon \mathsf {K}_{1} + \mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa'}}-z(\mathsf {K}_{1})-\log \mathsf{k}}{\sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{1}}} \ge \mathsf {K}_{1}^{\alpha} \,.
\]
Consequently,  the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} of (\ref{eq:YKo-clt-ub}) is also $o_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}(1)$,  thereby concluding the proof 
of (\ref{eq:YKo-good}).
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- definition-7: body_md -->
\label{def:Fvj}
                                                        
                                                                                                      
                                                                                             
                                                                                                
                                                                             
Denote by $\bar \mathbb{P}^{(\ell)}_{y}$ the product law of $\mathsf{s}_{\ell}(y)$ {\sc\lowercase{iid}} unconditional  
Brownian excursions from $\partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{v},r_\ell)$ to $\partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{v},r_{\ell-1})$,  
starting independently,  uniformly on $\partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d} (\mathsf{v},r_{\ell})$.  
The law it induces on the counts of  Brownian excursions at levels $j > \ell$ 
around $\mathsf{v}$ matches that of the occupation measure of the 
reflected {\sc\lowercase{srw}} on $[\ell-1,\infty)$,  during its first $\mathsf{s}_{\ell}(y)$ moves from $\ell$ to $\ell-1$.
<!-- end definition-7 -->
<!-- lemma-26: body_md -->
\label{lem:uncond-comp}  
Recall $g_3(y)={\bf 1}_{\mathsf{I}^{\star}_3} (y) y e^{-2 y}$ and set
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:alpha-tot}
 \alpha(\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6}) := \frac{\sqrt{2} \, e^{-1}}{\sqrt{\pi \mathsf {K}_{4}}} \int_0^\infty  
 \mathbb{E}\Big[g_{\mathsf {K}_{4}}\big(\sqrt{2Y_{\bar \mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}_{4}}(y)}}- 2 \mathsf {K}_{4}\big)\Big] y e^{2 y} dy \,,
\end{equation} 
with $Y_\lambda:=$Poisson$(\lambda)$ and $\bar \mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}_{4}}(\cdot)$ of (\ref{eq:nominalno-vep}).
Then,  uniformly over $y_3 \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_3$,
\begin{align}\label{eq:g3-formula}
\widehat{g}_{\mathsf {K}_{3}}^{(\varepsilon)}(y_3) 
& = (1+o_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\varepsilon} (1)) \alpha(\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6}) g_3(y_3) \,,\\
\label{eq:g3-to-wh-g3}
g_{\mathsf {K}_{3}}^{(\varepsilon)}(y_3) &=  \widehat{g}_{\mathsf {K}_{3}}^{(\varepsilon)}(y_3)+ o_{\mathsf {K}_{5}}(1) g_3(y_3) \,.
\end{align}
<!-- end lemma-26 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
Sharp asymptotics of rare event probabilities as in (\ref{eq:g3-formula})
are considered in \cite[(6.4)]{DRZ}.  To make the connection clearer we change below 
some of the notation in \cite{DRZ} to bring it in line to what we have here.  In particular, 
we write $m,n,\rho_n$ and $\ell$ of \cite{DRZ} as $\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon$,  $n_\varepsilon$,  $\boldsymbol{\rho}_\varepsilon$,  
and $\mathsf {K}_{4}$,  respectively.  With these changes,  the asymptotics for \cite[(6.4)]{DRZ} 
would apply to (\ref{eq:g3-formula}),  except for:\\
(a).  Replacing in \cite{DRZ} the correction term $\frac{\log |\log \varepsilon|}{|\log \varepsilon|}$ in the formula (\ref{def:mn}) 
for the slope $\boldsymbol{\rho}_\varepsilon$ by $\log n_\varepsilon/n_\varepsilon$.\\
(b).  Replacing $g_{\mathsf {K}_{4}}(\cdot)$ of (\ref{dfn:g4-alt}) by a function $\widehat{\gamma}_{\mathsf {K}_{4}}(\cdot)$ 
supported on smaller interval $\sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}}[(\sqrt{\log \mathsf {K}_{4}})^{-1},\sqrt{\log \mathsf {K}_{4}}]$.\\
(c).  Having in \cite{DRZ} a straight barrier (ie.  $\widehat{\eta}(j)>0$),  while (\ref{def:wh-g3}) has a curved 
one (that is,  $\widehat{\eta}(j) > j_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa_o}}$).\\
(d).  Changing in \cite{DRZ} our nominal slope value $2$ to $c_\star = \sqrt{2 \log 2}$,
having there also $\mathsf {K}_{3}=0$ and fixed $y_3$ (whose value does not grow as $n'-\mathsf {K}_{3} \to \infty$).\\
Nevertheless,  it is not difficult to adapt the proof in \cite{DRZ} to the case in hand.  Specifically:\\
(a).  Since $\log n_\varepsilon - n_\varepsilon \frac{\log |\log \varepsilon|}{|\log \varepsilon|} \to 0$ 
as $\varepsilon \to 0$ (see (\ref{def.nvep})),  the modification of the correction term in $\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon$ is irrelevant. \\
(b).  The arguments in \cite[Sec. 6]{DRZ} apply verbatim for any positive nominal slope and
any function on the larger interval $\mathsf{I}^{\star}_4$ (the key is 
        
$\sup_{y \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_4} \{ y/\mathsf {K}_{4} + y^{-1} \log \mathsf {K}_{4} \} = o_{\mathsf {K}_{4}}(1)$, see \cite[(6.39)]{DRZ} and the text following it).\\
(c).  The straight barrier event probability exceeds the one for our curved barrier.
Moreover,  \cite[(6.8) and (6.18)]{DRZ} \emph{lower bound} the former probability,  up to relative 
error $o_{\mathsf {K}_{4}}(1)$,  in terms of Brownian motion being above a barrier of the form 
$\gamma_0(j)+ 2 (h_{\mathsf {K}_{4}} +  j_{n'}^{\delta})$,  \emph{for any} $h_\ell \ge \frac{1}{2} \log \ell$.  
One then proceeds to show that the latter curving has a negligible effect when $\delta < \frac{1}{6}$ 
and $\sup_{y \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_4} \{ \mathsf {K}_{4}^{-1} y + y^{-1} h_{\mathsf {K}_{4}}  \} = o_{\mathsf {K}_{4}} (1)$ (see \cite[Lemma 6.3 and 
last display on Pg.  854]{DRZ}).  For some $c_{\kappa_o}$ finite,  
$2 c_{{\kappa_o}} \mathsf {K}_{4}^{{\kappa_o}} + 2 j_{n'}^{{\kappa_o}} \ge j_{n_\varepsilon}^{\kappa_o}$.  Hence, 
upon taking $\delta={\kappa_o}$ and $h_\ell = c_{{\kappa_o}} \ell^{{\kappa_o}}$,  the above mentioned barrier of \cite{DRZ}
exceeds our barrier $j_{n_\varepsilon}^{\kappa_o}$,  while in view of (\ref{dfn:windows}), 
having ${\kappa_1}>{\kappa_o}$ guarantees that the arguments of \cite{DRZ} apply for our
larger support of $g_{\mathsf {K}_{4}}(\cdot)$ and larger $h_{\mathsf {K}_{4}}$ value.\\
(d).  The relative $o(1)$ error in \cite[Section 6]{DRZ},  is uniform over our range of
$\frac{h_{\mathsf {K}_{4}}}{y_3} + \frac{y_3}{\sqrt{n'-\mathsf {K}_{3}}} = o_\varepsilon(1)$ (see \cite[(6.37) and derivation of (6.27)]{DRZ}).
Using the two displays above \cite[(6.26)]{DRZ} we see that the nominal slope of $c_\star$ results in
a leading exponential tail $e^{-(c_\star^2/2) (n'+1/2)}=2^{-(n'+1/2)}$ for the expectation on the 
{\sc\lowercase{rhs}} of \cite[(6.4)]{DRZ}, 
whereas our slope $2$ merely modifies it to be $e^{-(2^2/2) (n'+1/2)} = e^{-2 n'-1}
$,  if we had $\mathsf {K}_{3}=0$ as in \cite{DRZ} (this computation is also the reason for 
the additional factor $\sqrt{2}/e$ we have in (\ref{eq:alpha-tot})).
The only effect of having here $\mathsf {K}_{3} \ne 0$ such that $\mathsf {K}_{3}/n' \to 0$, 
is to modify the value of $n'$ to $n'-\mathsf {K}_{3}$ in this leading factor.  We thus 
arrive at (\ref{eq:g3-formula}) holding uniformly over $y_3 \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_3$
                                                                  
(see \cite[(6.2)]{DRZ}, and recall that $\mathsf {K}_{3} \to \infty$ as $\varepsilon \to 0$).  

Turning to (\ref{eq:g3-to-wh-g3}),  comparing (\ref{eq:alt-g3}) with (\ref{def:wh-g3}),
the bound (\ref{ubd2-g4}) on $g_{\mathsf {K}_{4}}(\cdot)$ implies that for any $z \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_3$,  
 \begin{align}\label{eq:ubd-whg3}
0 &\le \widehat{g}_{\mathsf {K}_{3}}^{(\varepsilon)}(z) -  g_{\mathsf {K}_{3}}^{(\varepsilon)}(z) 
               
\le  \frac{C(\mathsf {K}_{6})}{\mathsf {K}_{4}}  e^{2(n'-\mathsf {K}_{3})}
\sum_{j=\mathsf {K}_{3}+1}^{n'-1} \sum_{u =  j_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa''}}}^\infty
\sum_{y} 
p_j(z,u,y) y  e^{-2 y}  e^{-\frac{y^2}{8 \mathsf {K}_{4}}} 
\end{align}
where the inner-most sum is over all integer values of $y \in \bar{\mathsf I}_{n'}$ and 
\begin{align*}
p_j(z,u,y):= 
\bar{\mathbb{P}}^{(\mathsf {K}_{3})}_{z} \big( \widehat{\eta} (j) \in I_u,  \widehat{\eta}(n') \in I_y,
                                              
\widehat{\eta}(\ell)>0 \;\; \text{for all} \;\;  \mathsf {K}_{3}< \ell < n' 
     
\big) \,.
\end{align*}
Recall that $1 \ll \mathsf {K}_{3} \le C (\log n_\varepsilon)^{c}$ and as ${\kappa''} > {\kappa'}$,  here $u \gg z$ 
uniformly over $j \in (\mathsf {K}_{3}, \frac{1}{2} n_\varepsilon]$ and $z \in \bar{\mathsf I}_{\mathsf {K}_{3}}$,  while 
$u \gg y$ uniformly over $j \in [\frac{1}{2} n_\varepsilon,n')$ and $y \in \bar{\mathsf I}_{n'}$.
We thus get
as in our derivation of (\ref{agar.45p}),   {by combining \cite[(1.1)]{BRZ}
for staying above $\gamma_0(\cdot)$ during levels $[\mathsf {K}_{3},j]$,  starting at
height $z$ above it and ending at $I_u$ above the line,  with the same bound 
for staying above this line during $[j,n']$,  now starting at $u+1$ above it
and ending at $I_y$ above the line, } that for $f_{j,s}(u)$ of (\ref{def:fjs}),
some constant $c$,  any such $z,y,u$ and $j \in (\mathsf {K}_{3}, \frac{1}{2} n_\varepsilon]$, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ubd-pjzuy}
e^{2(n'-\mathsf {K}_{3})} p_j(z,u,y) \le c \,  g_3(z) \mathsf {K}_{4}^{-1/2} y e^{2 y} f_{j_{n_\varepsilon},\mathsf {K}_{3}}(u)
\end{equation}
while for $j \in [\frac{1}{2} n_\varepsilon,n')$ one merely replaces 
$\mathsf {K}_{3}$ on the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} by $\mathsf {K}_{4}$ 
(as done in (\ref{agar.45jj})).  Further,  with ${\kappa''} \ge {\kappa_o}$ and $a:=2{\kappa''} -1 >0$, 
 if $j_{n_\varepsilon}=s+\ell$ for $s,\ell \ge 1$,   then for some universal $c$, 
\[
\sum_{u = (s+\ell)^{{\kappa''}}}^\infty f_{s+\ell,s}(u) \le 4 \sum_{u=(s+\ell)^{{\kappa''}}}^\infty u^2 \, \ell^{-3/2} e^{-\frac{u^2}{16\ell }}
\le c \exp\big( -\frac{1}{18} (s+\ell)^{a} \big) 
\]
(see (\ref{def:fjs})),  and with $\mathsf {K}_{3} \ge \mathsf {K}_{4}$,   upon plugging the bounds 
of (\ref{eq:ubd-pjzuy}) into (\ref{eq:ubd-whg3}) we arrive at 
\[
\big|\,\widehat{g}_{\mathsf {K}_{3}}^{(\varepsilon)}(z) -  g_{\mathsf {K}_{3}}^{(\varepsilon)}(z)\big| \le 
C'(\mathsf {K}_{6}) g_3(z) \Big[ \sum_{y} \mathsf {K}_{4}^{-3/2} y^2 e^{-\frac{y^2}{8 \mathsf {K}_{4}}} \Big]
\sum_{\ell \ge 1} \exp \big( -\frac{1}{18} (\mathsf {K}_{4}+\ell)^{a} \big) \le C'(\mathsf {K}_{6}) \,  g_3(z) e^{- c \,  \mathsf {K}_{4}^{a}} 
\]
That is,  (\ref{eq:g3-to-wh-g3}) holds uniformly over $y_3 \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_3$.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- remark-16: body_md -->
\label{rmk:g3-formula-gen}
Setting $\bar{\mathsf I}_\ell$ of (\ref{dfn:windows}) to have parameter ${\kappa_o^+}>{\kappa_o}$,   our proof of  (\ref{eq:g3-formula}) extends to show that for 
                                                    
any $\ell=o(n')$,  uniformly over $y' \in \bar{\mathsf I}_\ell$ with $\mathsf{s}_\ell(y') \in \mathbb{N}$,  
\begin{align}\label{eq:g3-formula-ext}
\widehat{g}_{\ell}^{(\varepsilon)}(y') 
& = (1+o_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\varepsilon} (1)) \alpha(\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6}) \,  y' e^{-2 y'} 
\end{align}
and by a similar reasoning,  for some $c_1=c_1(\mathsf {K}_{5})$ finite and any $\varepsilon>0$,  
\begin{align}\label{eq:gfl-comp}
\sup \{\widehat{g}_{\ell}^{(\varepsilon)}(\widehat{\eta}(\ell)),  \widehat{\eta}(\ell) \in [b,b+2) \} \le c_1 \inf \{\widehat{g}_{\ell}^{(\varepsilon)}(\widehat{\eta}(\ell)),  \widehat{\eta}(\ell) \in [b,b+2) \} 
\quad \forall \ell \in [\mathsf {K}_{3}, n'],  \;\; b \in \bar{\mathsf I}_\ell \,.
\end{align}
<!-- end remark-16 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{cor:gK2-gK1-arg} 
Recall $g_i(y)={\bf 1}_{\mathsf{I}^{\star}_i} (y) y e^{-2 y}$,  $i=1,2$.  Then,  uniformly in $y_i \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_i$,
\begin{align}
e^{2 (\mathsf {K}_{2}-\mathsf {K}_{1})} \,  
\bar \mathbb{E}^{(\mathsf {K}_{1})}_{y_1} \Big[ g_2 \big( \widehat{\eta}(\mathsf {K}_{2})\big);  \widehat{\eta}(j) > j^{{\kappa_o}},   j \in (\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}) \Big]
&=  (1+o_{\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon} (1)) g_1 (y_1) \, .
\label{eq:K1-to-K2-u2}
\end{align}
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- remark-17: body_md -->
One can adapt \cite[Section 6]{DRZ} to fit the 
simpler setting of (\ref{eq:K1-to-K2-u2}) where the barrier length $\mathsf {K}_{2}-\mathsf {K}_{1}$ is much shorter 
than its ending nominal height $\gamma_0(\mathsf {K}_{2})$,  which is thus 
comparable to the starting barrier nominal height (and hence to $\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon$).  But,  striving for 
a shorter proof,  we instead re-use our derivation of (\ref{eq:g3-formula}) in part (a) below, 
at the cost of having to remove the obstacles of a non-integer 
$\log (r_{\mathsf {K}_{2}}/r_{\mathsf {K}_{3}})$ and $g_2(\cdot) \equiv 0$ outside $\bar{\mathsf I}_{\mathsf {K}_{2}}$
(see parts (b) and (c) below).
<!-- end remark-17 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
The proof of (\ref{eq:K1-to-K2-u2}) consists of the following three steps:\\
(a).  Our proof of (\ref{eq:g3-formula}) requires a fixed ratio of radii between consecutive levels.
Specifically,  we could leverage it to verify (\ref{eq:K1-to-K2-u2}),  if we had
 a fixed ratio of radii between consecutive levels,  and we could ignore the fact that $g_2(\cdot)$ 
is zero outside $\mathsf{I}^{\star}_2$.  
To this end,  we consider (\ref{eq:K1-to-K2-u2}) with $\varepsilon$ replaced by $\varepsilon':=\varepsilon e^{\varpi_{\varepsilon}}$,
so that by (\ref{dr.1}) and the following line we have $r_{j-1}/r_j = e$ for all $j$,
and assume that at $\varepsilon'$,  uniformly over $\mathsf{I}^{\star}_1$,
\begin{equation}\label{def:wh-g1-excess}
e^{2(n'-\mathsf {K}_{1})} \,   \bar{\mathbb{E}}^{(\mathsf {K}_{1})}_{y_1} \Big[ g_{\mathsf {K}_{4}} \big(\widehat{\eta}(n') \big); 
 \bigcap_{j \in (\mathsf {K}_{1},n')}  \{ \widehat{\eta} (j) >  j_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa_o}} \},  \widehat{\eta}(\mathsf {K}_{2}) \notin \mathsf{I}^{\star}_2 
  \Big] = o_\varepsilon(1) \,.
\end{equation}
(b).  The {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of (\ref{eq:K1-to-K2-u2}) at $\varepsilon$ amounts to the same expression at $\varepsilon'$
up to a certain non-random shift in $\widehat{\eta}(\cdot)$.  This allows us to transfer
(\ref{eq:K1-to-K2-u2}) from the special case of part (a),  to the general case.\\
(c).  By adapting the arguments in the proof of  \Cref{theo-win220}(d),  we establish (\ref{def:wh-g1-excess}).

\smallskip
\noindent
(a).  Proceeding to prove (\ref{eq:K1-to-K2-u2}) at $\varepsilon'$
                   
instead of $\varepsilon$,  note that $n_{\varepsilon'}=n_\varepsilon$ with the values of $\mathsf {K}_i \in \mathbb{N}$,  $\mathsf{I}^{\star}_i$,  $i=1,2$ and 
$r_j$,  $j \le \mathsf {K}_{2}$ also unchanged,  while the nominal barrier value $\gamma_0(j)$ for $\varepsilon$
exceeds the one for $\varepsilon'$ by 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bar-gap}
\delta(j) := \boldsymbol{\rho}_\varepsilon \varpi_{\varepsilon} + (\boldsymbol{\rho}_{\varepsilon} - \boldsymbol{\rho}_{\varepsilon'}) (n_\varepsilon-j+1 )  = 2 \varpi_{\varepsilon} + o_\varepsilon(1)
                         
 \,.
\end{equation}
With $\log(r_{\mathsf {K}_i}/\varepsilon') =  n_\varepsilon-\mathsf {K}_i \in \mathbb{N}$ we define 
$\widehat{g}^{(\varepsilon')}_{\mathsf {K}_i}(y_i)$,  $i=1,2$ analogously to (\ref{def:wh-g3}) and subject to the 
obvious notational modifications,  our proof of (\ref{eq:g3-formula}) also shows that
 for $i=1,2$,  uniformly in $y_i \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_i$,
\begin{align}\label{eq:g12-formula}
\widehat{g}^{(\varepsilon')}_{\mathsf {K}_i}(y_i) & = (1+o_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon} (1)) \alpha(\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6}) g_i(y_i) 
\end{align}
(with the relative error $o_{\mathsf {K}_{0}}(1)$ 
                                                             
when $i=1$,  in lieu
of earlier relying on $\mathsf {K}_{3} \to \infty$ when $\varepsilon \to 0$).   Further,  having assumed
(\ref{def:wh-g1-excess}),  we have (\ref{eq:g12-formula}) holding for $i=1$ 
even with the additional constraint $\widehat{\eta}(\mathsf {K}_{2}) \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_2$.  Thus,  
by the Markov property and (\ref{eq:g12-formula}),  
\[ 
 \alpha(\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6}) g_1(y_1) = (1+o_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon} (1))  \alpha(\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6})
e^{2(\mathsf {K}_{2}-\mathsf {K}_{1})} \,   \bar{\mathbb{E}}^{(\mathsf {K}_{1})}_{y_1} \Big[ {\bf 1}_{\{ \widehat{\eta} (j) >  j^{{\kappa_o}},   j \in (\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}) \}} \, 
g_2 \big(\widehat{\eta}(\mathsf {K}_{2}) \big)
\Big] \,.
\]
Dividing both sides by $\alpha(\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6})$ results with (\ref{eq:K1-to-K2-u2}),  albeit at $\varepsilon'$
(both $g_1(\cdot)$ and the {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of (\ref{eq:K1-to-K2-u2}) are independent of $\mathsf {K}_{5}$,  so 
after the fact we can remove $\mathsf {K}_{5}$ from the preceding $o_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon} (1)$ error).  

\noindent
(b).  Now,  one gets from the {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of (\ref{eq:K1-to-K2-u2}) at $\varepsilon'$ to the {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} expression at
$\varepsilon$ by changing $\widehat{\eta}(j) \to \widehat{\eta}(j)-\delta(j)$ and replacing $y_1$ by $y_1 - \delta(\mathsf {K}_{1})$
(see (\ref{eq:eta-centered})).
                                                                                               
In view of (\ref{eq:bar-gap}),  for large $\mathsf {K}_{1}$,  a slight change of the parameter ${\kappa_1}$ absorbs the shift in our 
constraints (barrier values),  whereas up to a $(1+o_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}(1))$ factor,  such shift of the arguments of 
$\widehat{g}_i(\cdot)$ merely multiplies 
both sides of (\ref{eq:K1-to-K2-u2}) by the same factor $e^{2 2 \varpi_{\varepsilon}}$ (as mentioned and used earlier, 
moving the borders of our windows $\mathsf{I}^{\star}_i$ by any constant,  or even a small power of $\mathsf {K}_i$, 
does not affect any of our statements).

\noindent
(c).  We proceed to establish (\ref{def:wh-g1-excess}) at $\varepsilon'$ and to this end,  
we will show that uniformly in $y \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_1$,
\begin{align}\label{eq:bar-gap2}
e^{2 (n''-\mathsf {K}_{1})} \mathbb{P} \big( \mathcal{R}^{o,(y)}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}} \cap \widehat{\mathcal{U}}^{(\varepsilon',y)} \cap 
\{ \widehat{\eta}(\mathsf {K}_{4}) \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_{4},  \widehat{\eta}(\mathsf {K}_{5}) \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_5,  \widehat{\eta}(\mathsf {K}_{2}) \notin \mathsf{I}^{\star}_2\} 
 \big) = o_\varepsilon(1) \,,
\end{align}
where $\widehat{\eta}(j)$ is defined using the nominal barrier $\gamma_0(\cdot)$ for $\varepsilon'$,  while 
\begin{align*}
\mathcal{R}^{o,(y)}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}} :=  \!\!\!\! \bigcap_{j \in (\mathsf {K}_{1},n')} \!\!\!\! \{ \widehat{\eta}(j) \ge  - j_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa_o}} \} 
\, \quad\text{and}\quad 
\widehat{\mathcal{U}}^{(\varepsilon',y)} &:= \bigcup_{\mathsf{v}\in \varepsilon' \mathbb{F}^\star} \Big\{ \bigcap_{j \in [\widetilde{n}_\varepsilon^{(5)},n_\varepsilon^{(6)}]}\!\!\!\!\!
\{\widehat{\eta}_{\mathsf{v}} (j) \ge  - j_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa_o}}\},  \eta_{\mathsf{v}} (n_\varepsilon+1)= 0 \Big\} \,.
\end{align*}
Thus,  assume (\ref{eq:bar-gap2}).  Recall  (\ref{eq:K3-angles}) and (\ref{def:g4}),  that uniformly 
over $\mathsf{I}^{\star}_4$  and $\mathcal{G}_{n'}^{{\bf 0}}$ the function $e^{2(n'-n'')} g_{\mathsf {K}_{4}}(\cdot)$ is within $1+o_1(\varepsilon)$ 
of $\mathbb{P} \big(\bigcup_{v} \{ \mathcal{R}\mathcal{U}^{(\varepsilon')} (v) \cap \, \mathcal{C}^{(\varepsilon')} (\cdot
, v) \} | \mathcal{G}^{{\bf 0}}_{n'} \big)$.  As the event in this conditional probability
is contained within
$\widehat{\mathcal{U}}^{(\varepsilon',y)} \cap  \{\widehat{\eta}(\mathsf {K}_{5}) \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_5\}$ (c.f.  \Cref{rem:alt-UU} or (\ref{eq:sharp-cont})),
                     
and the upward curved barrier of (\ref{def:wh-g1-excess}) 
is more restrictive than the downward curved barrier of $\mathcal{R}^{o,(y)}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}$,  clearly
(\ref{def:wh-g1-excess}) is a consequence of (\ref{eq:bar-gap2}).

It only remains to prove (\ref{eq:bar-gap2}).  Indeed,  our proof of \Cref{theo-win220}(d),  at $\mathsf{k}=\mathsf {K}_{6}$,  
shows that the contribution to (\ref{lem-win1}) from only $j=\mathsf {K}_{2}$,  is $o_{\mathsf {K}_{2}}(1) g(z)=o_\varepsilon(1)$ 
(c.f.  (\ref{agar.66-new}) and the summand for $j=\mathsf {K}_{2}$ in (\ref{agar.66-ext})).  
This argument applies verbatim with window sizes $\mathsf{I}^{\star}_i$ at $i=2,4,5$,
instead of the smaller $\mathsf{I}'_j$ of (\ref{dfn:windows-alt}).  In contrast to
(\ref{lem-win1}) where we consider also $o_{\mathsf {K}_{0}}(1)$ contributions from levels near $\mathsf {K}_{1}$,  here
with $\mathsf {K}_{1}$ and $y_1$ independent of $\varepsilon$,  our $o_\varepsilon(1)$ smallness remains even when the rough barrier
$\mathcal{R}^{o,\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\beta}$ of (\ref{a216.0})  (which is part of $\widehat{\mathcal{U}}^{(\varepsilon),\langle z \rangle}_{\mathsf{k},\beta}$ of (\ref{lem-win1})),  starts only
at $\mathsf {K}_{1}$,  instead of at $\mathsf{k}=\mathsf {K}_{6}$.  Having done so,  the preceding reasoning applies even 
when measuring the events of (\ref{lem-win1}) during the $\mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}(y_1)$ first $\mathsf {K}_{1}$-level excursions 
(instead of the first $\mathsf{s}_1(z)$ excursions at level one).  Fixing $\mathsf{v}_\beta={\bf 0}$,  omitting the index $\beta$,
unraveling the notations  (\ref{a216.0}),  (\ref{def:UUpk}),  (\ref{14.4}) and (\ref{a216.02}) within (\ref{lem-win1})
and having now all events measured during the $\mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}(y)$ level $\mathsf {K}_{1}$ excursions,  we arrive at (\ref{eq:bar-gap2}).
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- proposition-13: body_md -->
\label{lem:alpha-unif-bd}
For $\mathsf {K}_{6}$ large,  the $\alpha(\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6})$ of (\ref{eq:alpha-tot}) are bounded above and below, 
uniformly in $\mathsf {K}_{5}$.
<!-- end proposition-13 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
To show that $\alpha(\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6}) \le \bar \alpha(\mathsf {K}_{6})$,  we set
\begin{equation}\label{def:Zz}
Z:=\frac{\sqrt{2Y_{\lambda_z}}-\sqrt{2\lambda_z}}{\sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}}} \quad \text{ for } \quad 
 \lambda_z:=\bar \mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}_{4}}(\sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}}\,  z)=\frac{1}{2}\big(2 \mathsf {K}_{4}+\sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}} \,  z\big)^{2}, 
\end{equation}
and note that 
\[
\sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}}(Z+z) = \sqrt{2Y_{\lambda_z}}-\sqrt{2 \lambda_z}+\sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}}\, z = \sqrt{2Y_{\lambda_z}}-2 \mathsf {K}_{4}  \,.
\]
Thus,  setting $y=\sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}} \, z$ in (\ref{eq:alpha-tot}) results with 
\begin{equation}\label{alt:alpha-tot}
 \alpha(\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6}) = \frac{2e\sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}}}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_0^\infty  
 \mathbb{E}\Big[g_{\mathsf {K}_{4}}\big(\sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}}(Z+z)\big)\Big] z e^{2 \sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}} \,  z} \, dz \,.
\end{equation}
Plugging 
               
(\ref{ubd2-g4}) in (\ref{alt:alpha-tot}),  after some algebra
it follows that for $h(x):=x_+ e^{-x^2/8}$,
\begin{align}\label{ubd-alpha}
\alpha(\mathsf {K}_{5}, \mathsf {K}_{6}) &\leq C'( \mathsf {K}_{6})\int_{0}^{\infty} 
\mathbb{E}\Big[ h(Z+z) e^{-2\sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}} Z } \Big] z\,dz \nonumber \\
& \le  C'(\mathsf {K}_{6}) \int_0^\infty \mathbb{E} \big[ h^2(Z+z) \big]^{1/2}  \mathbb{E} \big[ e^{- 4 \sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}} Z} \big]^{1/2}  z dz\,.
\end{align}
One clearly has that 
\[
 \mathbb{E} \big[ e^{- 4 \sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}} Z} \big] \le 1 + 4 \int_0^{\sqrt{2\lambda_z}} e^{4u} \,  \mathbb{P} \big(\sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}} Z \le -u \big) du \,.
\]
Hence,  by the Poisson tail estimate of \cite[(3.8)]{BRZ},  that for some $c>0$,  
\begin{equation}\label{eq:38-brz}
\mathbb{P}(\sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}} Z \le -u) \le e^{-c u^2} \,, \qquad \forall u \in [0,\sqrt{2\lambda_z}],   z \ge  0 \,,
                                                                                                                                            
\end{equation}
we deduce  that $\mathbb{E} \big[ e^{- 4 \sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}} Z} \big]$ is bounded above,  uniformly over $\mathsf {K}_{4}$ and $z \ge 0$.
Further,  with $h^2(\cdot)$ uniformly bounded,  decreasing on $[2,\infty)$ and such that 
$h^2(x) \le (2+z)^{-6}$ for all $x \ge 5 \sqrt{\log (2+z)}$,  we get from (\ref{ubd-alpha}) that 
$\sup_{\mathsf {K}_{5}}  \alpha(\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6})$ is finite,  provided that 
\[
\sup_{\mathsf {K}_{4}} \Big\{ \int_0^\infty z  \mathbb{P}(Z \le -z + 5 \sqrt{\log (2+z)} )^{1/2} dz \Big\} < \infty \,,
\]
which in turn is also an easy consequence of the tail estimate (\ref{eq:38-brz}).

Next,  to show that $\alpha(\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6}) \ge \underline \alpha(\mathsf {K}_{6})>0$,  recall that 
$\inf_{\lambda  \ge 4} \Big\{ \mathbb{P}\Big( \sqrt{2/\lambda} ($Poisson$(\lambda) -\lambda) \in [ -1,0]\Big) \Big\} > 0$.
Thus,  $Z$ of (\ref{def:Zz}) is such that 
                    
\[
\delta:= \inf_{z \in [3,4]} \{ \mathbb{P}(0 \ge Z  \ge -1 ) \} \ge 0 \,.
\]
Restricting in the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} of (\ref{alt:alpha-tot}) to $z \in [3,4]$ and $Z \in [-1,0]$,  we  
utilize the lower bound (\ref{eq:lbd-alpha}) to arrive at
\[
 \alpha(\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6}) \ge \frac{4 e}{\sqrt{2\pi}} c(\mathsf {K}_{6})
 \inf_{z \in [3,4]} \mathbb{E} \Big( e^{-2 \sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{4}} Z} \,,  Z+z \in [2,4] \Big) \ge  \frac{4 e \delta}{\sqrt{2\pi}} c(\mathsf {K}_{6}) \,,
\]
as claimed.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- lemma-27: body_md -->
\label{lem:uncond-top}
Recalling $\bar \mathbb{P}^{(\mathsf {K}_{1})}_{y_1}$ of \Cref{def:Fvj},  for some $c_0$ and any ${\kappa_o}$,  ${\kappa_1}$,  ${\kappa'}$
as in (\ref{dfn:aux-par}),  uniformly over $\mathsf{s}$ such that $y_1 \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_1$, 
\begin{align}\label{eq:K1-to-K3-u}
\bar \mathbb{E}_{y_1}^{(\mathsf {K}_{1})} \Big[ g_3 \big( \widehat{\eta}(\mathsf {K}_{3}) \big) ;  \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon),\smallfrown}_{[\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]} \,  \Big]
=  (1+o_{\mathsf {K}_{1},\varepsilon} (1)) & [r_{\mathsf {K}_{3}}/r_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}]^2
g_o (y_1,0) \, ,\\
\bar \mathbb{E}_{y_1}^{(\mathsf {K}_{1})} \Big[ g_3 \big( \widehat{\eta}(\mathsf {K}_{3}) \big) ;  \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon),\smallfrown}_{[\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]} \, ,
\mathsf{d}_\infty (\bar \mu, L_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}) > c_0 \frac{\log \mathsf {K}_{1}}{\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon} 
          
\Big]
=  o_{\mathsf {K}_{1},\varepsilon} (1) & [r_{\mathsf {K}_{3}}/r_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}]^2\,   g_o (y_1,0) \, ,
\label{eq:K1-to-K3-trunc}
\end{align}
with $\boldsymbol{\psi} = \{\psi_q, q \le \mathsf{s}\}$ the angle-differences of our $\mathsf {K}_{1}$-level Brownian excursions.
<!-- end lemma-27 -->
<!-- lemma-28: body_md -->
\label{lem:quant-mu}
For any $\mathsf {K}_{1}$ large enough and uniformly over  $(y_1,L_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}) \in \mathbb{I}_\star^{(\varepsilon)}$,
\begin{align}
\widehat{g}_{\pm,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{(\varepsilon)}(\boldsymbol{\theta}) &= (1+o_{\varepsilon}(1))  \widehat{g}_{\pm,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{(\varepsilon)}(\boldsymbol{\bar \mu})\, e^{2 V_{\boldsymbol{\bar \mu}}}  e^{-2 V_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}} + o_\varepsilon(1) \, ,
\label{eq:coupling-bdt}\\
\label{eq:coupling-bd1}
(1+o_{\varepsilon}(1)) \widehat{g}_{-,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{(\varepsilon)}(\boldsymbol{\theta}) - o_\varepsilon(1) \le \widehat{g}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{(\varepsilon)}(\boldsymbol{\theta}) & \le (1+o_{\varepsilon}(1)) \widehat{g}_{+,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{(\varepsilon)}(\boldsymbol{\theta}) + o_\varepsilon(1) \, .
\end{align}
<!-- end lemma-28 -->
<!-- lemma-29: body_md -->
\label{lem-} 
For any $\kappa_\star$ large enough,  uniformly in $(y_1,L_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}) \in \mathbb{I}_\star^{(\varepsilon)}$
\begin{eqnarray}
[r_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}/r_{\mathsf {K}_{3}}]^2\, 
\mathbb{E} \big[ g_3 \big( \widehat{\eta}(\mathsf {K}_{3}) \big) ;  \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon),\smallfrown}_{[\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]} \setminus \mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}^{(\varepsilon),(y_1),\Cap}_{[\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]} \,| \boldsymbol{\theta} \big]  = 
o_{\mathsf {K}_{1},\varepsilon}(1) g_o (y_1,0) e^{-2 V_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}} 
                                                                      
 \,.
\label{leftgoal.1}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lemma-29 -->
<!-- lemma-30: body_md -->
\label{lem:BRZ-CH4-bary}
For $\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon),\smallfrown}_{[\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]}$ of (\ref{eq:BK12}) and integer $j'$, $j''$,  set  
\begin{align}
\mathbb{B}^{j',j''}_{\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2},\mathsf {K}_{3}} := \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon),\smallfrown}_{[\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]} \cap \{ \widehat{\eta}(\mathsf {K}_{2}) \in I_{j'} \} \cap \{ \widehat{\eta}(\mathsf {K}_{3}) \in I_{j''} \} \,.
\label{def:Bjp-jppn}
\end{align}
                                                               
Then,  for $g(y):=y e^{-2y}$,  $\mathcal{W}^{\in m}(\mathsf{s})=\mathcal{W}^{\infty,\in m}_{{\bf 0},\mathsf {K}_{1}}(\mathsf{s})$ 
of (\ref{eq:LBTruncatedSumzf}),  some finite $c_0$ and $C$,  any $y_1 \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_1$ and $m \ge \log \mathsf {K}_{1}$, 
\begin{equation}
\sum_{j''} g(j'')
\bar \mathbb{P}_{y_1}^{(\mathsf {K}_{1})} \big( \bigcup_{j'}  \{ \mathcal{W}^{\in m}(\mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}(y_1)) \cap
\mathbb{B}^{j',j''}_{\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2},\mathsf {K}_{3}} \} \big)
\le  C e^{-2 (\mathsf {K}_{3}-\mathsf {K}_{1})} y_1 e^{-2 y_1} e^{-m^2/8}  \,,
\label{eq:K13-t}
\end{equation}
where the union is over $j' \in \bar{\mathsf I}_{\mathsf {K}_{2}}$ and the sum is over $j'' \in \bar{\mathsf I}_{\mathsf {K}_{3}}$.
<!-- end lemma-30 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
Using the short hand $\mathsf{s}:=\mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}(y_1)$,  recall similarly to (\ref{eq:BRZ-454}),
that by (\ref{lbl:d-inf-bd}) we have
                                      
for some $c_0$ finite,  the uniform bounds  
\begin{equation}\label{eq:BRZ-454nn}
\bar \mathbb{P}^{(\mathsf {K}_{1})}_{y_1} \big( \mathcal{W}^{\in m} (\mathsf{s}) \big) \le 2 e^{-m^2/4} \,,   \qquad \forall y_1 \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_1,  m \ge 0 \,.
\end{equation}
With $\mathsf {K}_{3} \le 2 (22 \log n_\varepsilon)^{1/{\kappa_o}}$,  it thus remains only to prove (\ref{eq:K13-t}) for
$m \le C (\log n_\varepsilon)^{1/(2 {\kappa_o})}$ and some universal $C<\infty$.  In contrast to \Cref{lem:BRZ-CH4},
here we have a fixed number $\mathsf{s}$ of excursions at level $\mathsf {K}_{1}$ (which are further {\sc\lowercase{iid}}).
In such a setting we do not need the  counts of excursions at levels $k<\mathsf {K}_{1}$ and
\cite[Lemmas 4.7 \& 4.8]{BRZ2} hold with $\mathcal{W}^{\in m} (\mathsf{s})$ replacing $\mathcal{L}'_{\mathsf {K}_{1},m,a}$ of
(\ref{def:Lmpa}).  That is, 
uniformly over our range of $y_1,j',j'',m$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:BRZ-lem48}
\bar \mathbb{P}_{y_1}^{(\mathsf {K}_{1})} \big( \mathcal{W}^{\in m}(\mathsf{s}) \cap
\mathbb{B}^{j',j''}_{\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2},\mathsf {K}_{3}} \big)
\le c \,  H_{\mathsf {K}_{1},y_1,j',j''} (m) e^{-m^2/4} + e^{-\sqrt{n_\varepsilon}} 
\end{equation}
for $H_{\mathsf {K}_{1},a,j',j''}(m)$ of (\ref{eq:BRZ-474}),  while for $m \le 4 (\log \mathsf {K}_{3})^{1/2}$ 
we have a stronger bound,  with $H_{\mathsf {K}_{1},y_1,j',j''}(m)$ replaced in (\ref{eq:BRZ-lem48}) by 
$G_{\mathsf {K}_{1},y_1,j',j''}(m)$ of (\ref{eq:BRZ-471}).  In either case,  multiplying both sides of this bound
                        
by $g(j'')$ and summing over $j'$ and $j''$ yields (\ref{eq:K13-t}) (note that $y_1^2 =o(\mathsf {K}_{2})$ and utilize (\ref{eq:BRZ-472}) 
if $m \le 4 (\log \mathsf {K}_{3})^{1/2}$,  while if $m > 4 (\log \mathsf {K}_{3})^{1/2}$ use (\ref{eq:BRZ-473}),  
for then $\sqrt{\mathsf {K}_{2}} \le e^{m^2/32}$).
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- lemma-31: body_md -->
\label{lem:bd-hq}
Recall $\mathsf{z}_{q}=r_{\mathsf {K}_{1}} e^{-i \theta_q}$,  $\mathsf{z}'_q=r_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}e^{-i \bar \mu_q}$,
$\mathsf{u}=(r_{\mathsf {K}_{1}-1},0)$ and $\bar p_\varepsilon$ of (\ref{dfn:bar-p-vep}).   Let $T(\mathsf{z}_q)$ and $T(\mathsf{z}'_q)$
count the $\mathsf {K}_{3}$-level excursions in an $\mathsf {K}_{1}$ excursion
starting at $\mathsf{z}_q$,  or at $\mathsf{z}'_q$,  and ending at $\mathsf{u}$.   Then,   
\begin{align}\label{dfn:hq}
h^{(\varepsilon)}_{q}(\theta_q)  := \log \Big\{ 1+\frac{1}{\bar p_\varepsilon} \Big(
 \frac{\mathbb{E} \big[e^{-2 T(\mathsf{z}_q)/\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon} \big]}{\mathbb{E} \big[e^{-2 T(\mathsf{z}'_q)/\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon} \big]} -1 \Big) \Big\} \,,
\end{align}
are such that uniformly over $(y_1,L_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}) \in \mathbb{I}_\star^{(\varepsilon)}$ and all $\varepsilon$ small enough,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:hq-bd}
\sup_{q} \Big | \mathsf{m}_\varepsilon h^{(\varepsilon)}_{q}(\theta_q) - \frac{2\,  \bar c}{\bar p_\varepsilon} [ \cos(\theta_q)-\cos(\bar \mu_q) ] \Big| 
=o_\varepsilon (1) \,. 
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-31 -->
<!-- remark-18: body_md -->
\label{rmk:hq} In view of (\ref{eq:quant}) and (\ref{dfn:bar-p-vep}),  it follows from 
(\ref{eq:hq-bd}) that $\sup_q |h^{(\varepsilon)}_{q}(\theta_q)| \le C/\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon$ for some $C$ finite.   Moreover,  with 
$\mathsf{s} \,  \bar p_\varepsilon = O(\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon)$,  it follows from (\ref{dfn:Vthet}) and (\ref{eq:hq-bd}) that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:hq-sum}
| \bar p_\varepsilon \sum_{q=1}^{\mathsf{s}} h^{(\varepsilon)}_{q}(\theta_q) - 2 (V_{\boldsymbol{\bar \mu}} - V_{\boldsymbol{\theta}} ) | =o_\varepsilon(1) \,.
\end{equation}
<!-- end remark-18 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
It is easy to check that $\mathbb{E} [T(\mathsf{z}) ]$ is uniformly bounded above and below
over $|\mathsf{z}| = r_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}$ and likewise $\sup_{\mathsf{z}} \mathbb{E} [T(\mathsf{z})^3] \le C \mathsf {K}_{3}^2$.  
With $\bar p_\varepsilon \mathsf{m}_\varepsilon$ uniformly bounded in $\varepsilon$,  by the inequalities 
$|e^{-x}-(1-x + \frac{1}{2} x^2) | \le |x|^3$ and  $|\log(1+x)-x| \le x^2$ whenever $|x| \le \frac{1}{2}$,  
we thus get (\ref{eq:hq-bd}) upon showing that uniformly over $q \le \mathsf{s}$,  
\begin{align}\label{eq:bd-T-diff2}
\big| \mathbb{E}[T(\mathsf{z}_q)^2]- \mathbb{E}[T(\mathsf{z}'_q)^2] \big|  &= o_\varepsilon(1) \,,  \\
\big| \mathbb{E}[T(\mathsf{z}_q)]- \mathbb{E}[T(\mathsf{z}'_q)] - \bar c [ \cos(\bar \mu_q)-\cos(\theta_q) ] \big| & = o_\varepsilon(\bar p_\varepsilon) \,.
\label{eq:bd-T-diff1}
\end{align}
Clearly,   $\sup_{\mathsf{z}} \mathbb{E} [T(\mathsf{z})^2] \le C \mathsf {K}_{3}$ also for
$\mathsf{z} \in \Gamma_q := \partial \mathbb{B} (\mathsf{z}'_q,r_{\mathsf {K}_{1}+1})$,  with
$T(\mathsf{z}_q)=T(\zeta_{\mathsf{z}_q})$ and $T(\mathsf{z}'_q)=T(\zeta_{\mathsf{z}'_q})$ 
for the first hitting points $\zeta_{\mathsf{z}_q}$ and $\zeta_{\mathsf{z}'_q}$ 
of $\Gamma_q$ when starting at $\mathsf{z}_q$ and $\mathsf{z}'_q$ (see our justification of (\ref{eq-011025a})).
Further,  by the strong Markov property and (\ref{eq:zeta-tv-bd}),  
\[
\big| \mathbb{E}[T(\mathsf{z}_q)^2]- \mathbb{E}[T(\mathsf{z}'_q)^2] \big| = \big| \mathbb{E}[T(\zeta_{\mathsf{z}_q})^2]- \mathbb{E}[T(\zeta_{\mathsf{z}'_q})^2] \big|  
 \le \mathsf{d}_{\rm TV}(\zeta_{\mathsf{z}_q},\zeta_{\mathsf{z}'_q})  \sup_{\mathsf{z} \in \Gamma_q} \mathbb{E}[T(\mathsf{z})^2] \le 
 C \mathsf {K}_{3} \bar p_\varepsilon 
\]
yielding (\ref{eq:bd-T-diff2}).  Turning to (\ref{eq:bd-T-diff1}),  set $R:=r_{\mathsf {K}_{1}-1}$,
$\rho:=r_{\mathsf {K}_{3}-1}/r_{\mathsf {K}_{1}-1}
                      
$ and let $T'(\mathsf{x})$ count the $\mathsf {K}_{3}$-level 
excursions within a path starting at specific $\mathsf{x} \in  \partial \mathbb{B} ({\bf 0},\rho R)$ and ending at 
$\mathsf{u}=(R,0)$.  The unconditioned version of such $T'(\mathsf{x})$,  
                       
counting $\mathsf {K}_{3}$-level excursions within a path from $\partial \mathbb{B} ({\bf 0}, \rho R)$ to $\partial \mathbb{B} ({\bf 0}, R)$,
is the Geometric variable $\mathsf {G}^o$ such that $\mathbb{P}(\mathsf {G}^o=\ell)=(1-p) p^\ell$,  $\ell \ge 0$ 
for $p:=L/(L+1)$ and $L=\log (1/\rho)$,  see \cite[(2.1)]{BRZ2}.  Clearly,  $\mathbb{E}[\mathsf {G}^o]=L$.  Moreover,  we have from \cite[(9.5)]{BRZ2} 
at $h_k=R$ and $h_{k'-1}= \rho R$,  the bound 
\[
\sup_{|\mathsf{x}| = \rho R} \Big\{ \big| \mathbb{E}[T'(\mathsf{x})]  - \mathbb{E}[\mathsf {G}^o] \big| \Big\}  \le  
5 \mathsf {K}_{3} \,  \rho \,  \mathbb{E}[\mathsf {G}^o] \,.
\]
                                                                                       
                                                         
Starting at $\mathsf{z} \in \partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}({\bf 0},R/e)$ and setting 
\[
A(\mathsf{z}):=\{\text{hitting} \;\; \partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}({\bf 0},\rho R) \;\; \text{before exiting} \;\;
\mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}({\bf 0},R)  \;\;  \text{at}  \;\;  \mathsf{u} \}\,,
\]
we consequently have that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Tz-bd1}
\big| \mathbb{E}[T(\mathsf{z})] -  \mathbb{P}(A(\mathsf{z})) \mathbb{E}[\mathsf {G}^o] \big| \le \mathbb{P}(A(\mathsf{z})) 
\sup_{|\mathsf{x}| = \rho R} \big\{ | \mathbb{E}[T'(\mathsf{x})] - \mathbb{E}[\mathsf {G}^o] | \big\}
\le 5 \mathsf {K}_{3}^2 e^{-(\mathsf {K}_{3}-\mathsf {K}_{1})} = o_\varepsilon(\bar p_\varepsilon) \,.
\end{equation}
In computing $\mathbb{P}(A(\mathsf{z}))$ our Brownian path is confined to $\mathbb{B}({\bf 0},R)$,  
so {\sc\lowercase{wlog}} we set $R=1$ with a path starting at $\mathsf{z}=e^{-1} e^{-i \theta}$ and ending at $\mathsf{u}=(1,0)$
after hitting $\mathbb{B}({\bf 0},\rho)$.  Then,  similarly to (\ref{10.11}) we have by the strong Markov property,  that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Az-formula}
\mathbb{P}(A(\mathsf{z}))= \frac{1}{p(\mathsf{z},\mathsf{u})} \mathbb{E}_{\mathsf{z}} \big[ p(X_{\tau_\rho},\mathsf{u}); \tau_\rho < \tau_1 \big] \,,
\end{equation}
where $X_0=z$ with $\tau_r := \inf\{ t \ge 0 : |X_t |=r \}$ and the Poisson kernel
$p(\mathsf{x},\mathsf{u}):=(1-|\mathsf{x}|^2)/|\mathsf{x}-\mathsf{u}|^2$  for the exit density of $\mathbb{B}({\bf 0}, 1)$ is such that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Pois-bds}
\sup_{|\mathsf{x}|=\rho} | p(\mathsf{x},\mathsf{u}) -1 | \le 3 \rho \qquad \qquad \forall \rho \le \frac{1}{3} \,.
\end{equation}
Clearly,  $\inf \{ p(\mathsf{z},\mathsf{u}) : |\mathsf{z}|=1/e \} = 1/c > 0$ and $\mathbb{P}_{\mathsf{z}} (\tau_\rho < \tau_1 \big)= 1/L$
whenever $|\mathsf{z}|=1/e$ (see \cite[(2.1)]{BRZ2}),  so from (\ref{eq:Az-formula}) and (\ref{eq:Pois-bds}) we deduce that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Tz-bd2}
\big| \mathbb{P}(A(\mathsf{z})) \mathbb{E}[\mathsf {G}^o] - \frac{1}{p(\mathsf{z},\mathsf{u})} \big| \le 3 c \rho = o_\varepsilon(\bar p_\varepsilon)  \,.
\end{equation}
Finally,  note that
\[
\frac{1}{p(\mathsf{z}_q,\mathsf{u})} - \frac{1}{p(\mathsf{z}'_q,\mathsf{u})} =\frac{|\mathsf{z}_q-\mathsf{u}|^2-|\mathsf{z}'_q-\mathsf{u}|^2}{1-e^{-2}} =
 \bar c [ \cos(\bar \mu_q)-\cos(\theta_q) ] \,,
\]
which in view of (\ref{eq:Tz-bd1}) and (\ref{eq:Tz-bd2}) completes the proof of (\ref{eq:bd-T-diff1}).
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
Recall the first hitting points $\zeta_{\mathsf{z}_q}$ and $\zeta_{\mathsf{z}'_q}$ 
of $\Gamma_q := \partial \mathbb{B} (\mathsf{z}'_q,r_{\mathsf {K}_{1}+1})$ when starting at $\mathsf{z}_q$ and $\mathsf{z}'_q$,  see (\ref{dfn:coup}).
By the independence of our Brownian excursions,  we have for any $\ell \ge \mathsf {K}_{1}$ the representation 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Dlt-rep}
\Delta^{(\varepsilon)}_{\boldsymbol{\theta},\ell} = \sum_{q=1}^{\mathsf{s}} B_q T_{q,\ell}
\end{equation}
for independent variables $\{T_{q,\ell},  B_q,  q \le \mathsf{s}\}$,  where $T_{q,\ell}$ counts the number of 
$\ell$-level excursions within a single $\mathsf {K}_{1}$-level excursion that ends at $\mathsf{u}=(r_{\mathsf {K}_{1}-1},0)$  
and starts at $\xi_q \in \Gamma_q$ such that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:coup-st}
\mathbb{P}(\xi_q \in A) =  \frac{1}{\bar p_\varepsilon} \mathbb{P}(\zeta_{\mathsf{z}_q} \in A) 
- \frac{(1-\bar p_\varepsilon)}{\bar p_\varepsilon} \mathbb{P}(\zeta_{\mathsf{z}'_q} \in A) \qquad \forall A \subseteq \Gamma_q \,.
\end{equation}
With $\xi_q$ chosen according to the mixture (\ref{eq:coup-st}),  
similarly to (\ref{eq-011025a}),  we have for $T_q:=T_{q,\mathsf {K}_{3}}$ and any $j \ge 0$, 
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{P}(T_q=j)&=\mathbb{P}(T(\zeta_{\mathsf{z}'_q})=j) + \frac{1}{\bar p_\varepsilon} \big[
\mathbb{P}(T(\zeta_{\mathsf{z}_q})=j) - \mathbb{P}(T(\zeta_{\mathsf{z}'_q})=j) \big] \nonumber \\&=
\mathbb{P}(T(\mathsf{z}'_q)=j) + \frac{1}{\bar p_\varepsilon} \big[
\mathbb{P}(T(\mathsf{z}_q)=j) - \mathbb{P}(T(\mathsf{z}'_q)=j) \big] \,,
\end{align*}
from which we deduce by elementary algebra that
\begin{align}\label{dfn:hq-alt}
\mathbb{E} \big[e^{-2 T_q/\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon} \big] = e^{h^{(\varepsilon)}_{q}(\theta_q)}  \,  \mathbb{E} \big[e^{-2 T(\mathsf{z}'_q)/\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon} \big]  \,. 
\end{align}
In particular,  $h^{(\varepsilon)}_q (\bar \mu_q)=0$.
Conditionally on $\underline{B}:=(B_1,\ldots,B_{\mathsf{s}})$,  the variable $\Delta^{(\varepsilon)}_{\boldsymbol{\theta},\mathsf {K}_{3}}$ is independent 
of $\widehat{\eta}_\star(\cdot)$ and $\widehat{g}_{\pm,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{(\varepsilon)}$ depends on $\theta_q$ only via the law of $T_q$.  Thus,  setting 
\begin{align}\label{dfn:bar-g} 
\bar g^{(\varepsilon)}
         
 (\underline{B}) &:= \mathbb{E} \big[  g_3 \big( \widehat{\eta}_\star(\mathsf {K}_{3}) \big) ; \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\pm} \,| \underline{B} \big]
\prod_{\{q: B_q=1\}}  \mathbb{E} \big[e^{-2 T(\mathsf{z}'_q)/\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon} \Big] \, , \\
\bar \Delta^{(\varepsilon)}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}
         
 (\underline{B}) &:= \sum_{q=1}^{\mathsf{s}} (B_q - \bar p_\varepsilon) h^{(\varepsilon)}_{q}(\theta_q) \,,
\label{dfn:bar-Dlt}
\end{align}
plug (\ref{eq:Dlt-rep}) for $\ell=\mathsf {K}_{3}$,  within (\ref{dfn:wh-g1n}),  compute the conditional expectation 
given $\underline{B}$ and utilize (\ref{dfn:hq-alt}),  to arrive at 
\begin{align}\label{dfn:g1n-alt}
\widehat{g}_{\pm,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{(\varepsilon)}(\boldsymbol{\bar \mu}) &= [r_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}/r_{\mathsf {K}_{3}}]^2\,   \mathbb{E} \big[ \bar g^{(\varepsilon)}
         
  \big],\\
\label{dfn:g1t-alt}
\widehat{g}_{\pm,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{(\varepsilon)}(\boldsymbol{\theta}) &= [r_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}/r_{\mathsf {K}_{3}}]^2\,  \exp\big( \bar p_\varepsilon \sum_{q=1}^\mathsf{s} h^{(\varepsilon)}_{q}(\theta_q) \big) 
\mathbb{E} \big[ \bar g^{(\varepsilon)}
         
  e^{\bar \Delta^{(\varepsilon)}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}
         
}  \big] 
\end{align}
(with both expectations over the vector $\underline{B}$ of {\sc\lowercase{iid}} Bernoulli$(\bar p_\varepsilon)$ variables).
                 
                                                       
                                                                                                
                                                                     
                                                                                   
                                
                                                              
                                                      
                  
            
By (\ref{eq:hq-sum}),  (\ref{dfn:g1n-alt}),  (\ref{dfn:g1t-alt})
and the bound $|V_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}|,  |V_{\boldsymbol{\bar \mu}}| \le \kappa_\star \log \mathsf {K}_{1}$ (as in (\ref{dfn:hat-L-alpha})),  
 our claim 
(\ref{eq:coupling-bdt}) amounts to having uniformly over  $(y_1,L_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}) \in \mathbb{I}_\star^{(\varepsilon)}$
\begin{align}\label{eq:cor-Dlt}
\mathbb{E} \big[ \bar g^{(\varepsilon)}
         
 e^{\bar \Delta^{(\varepsilon)}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}
         
} \big] 
&= (1+o_{\varepsilon}(1))  \mathbb{E} \big[ \bar g^{(\varepsilon)}
         
 \big] + o_\varepsilon(e^{-2\mathsf {K}_{3}}) \,.
\end{align}
Note that $g_3(\cdot) \in [0,1]$ for all small enough $\varepsilon$ and thereby so is
$\bar g ^{(\varepsilon)}$ of (\ref{dfn:bar-g}).  Setting $\delta_\varepsilon := \bar p_\varepsilon^{1/4} \to 0$,  
we lower bound the expected value of $\bar g^{(\varepsilon)}
         
 e^{\bar \Delta^{(\varepsilon)}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}
         
}$ by restricting it to $\bar \Delta^{(\varepsilon)}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}
         
 \ge -\delta_\varepsilon$
and upper bounding it according to whether or not $\bar \Delta^{(\varepsilon)}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}
         
 \ge \delta_\varepsilon$,  
arriving at (\ref{eq:cor-Dlt}) upon showing that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Dlt-bdd-by-g}
\mathbb{E} \Big[ e^{\bar \Delta^{(\varepsilon)}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}
         
};  \bar \Delta^{(\varepsilon)}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}
         
 \ge \delta_\varepsilon \Big]
+ \mathbb{P}(\bar \Delta^{(\varepsilon)}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}
         
 \le -\delta_\varepsilon) 
= o_{\varepsilon}(e^{-2 \mathsf {K}_{3}})  \,.
\end{equation}
Further,  the centered {\sc\lowercase{cgf}} of Bernoulli$(p)$ variables are such that for any $|\lambda| \le 1$ and $p \in [0,1]$, 
\[
\Lambda_p(\lambda) := \log \big( 1 + p (e^{\lambda}-1) \,  \big) - \lambda p \le \frac{e}{2} p  \lambda^2 \,,
\]
hence it follows from (\ref{dfn:bar-Dlt}),  with $|h_q^{(\varepsilon)}| \le C/\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon$ (see  \Cref{rmk:hq}),  
$\mathsf{s} \le \frac{1}{2} \mathsf{m}_\varepsilon^2$ and $\bar p_\varepsilon \le \frac{1}{2}$,  that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Dlt-mgf}
\log \mathbb{E} \big [ e^{\lambda \bar \Delta^{(\varepsilon)}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}
         
} \big] \le \mathsf{s} \Lambda_{\bar p_\varepsilon} (C |\lambda|/\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon) 
\le C^2 \bar p_\varepsilon \lambda^2  \qquad \forall |\lambda| \le \mathsf{m}_\varepsilon/C \,.
         
\end{equation}
                                    
By Markov's inequality and (\ref{eq:Dlt-mgf}) at $\pm \lambda$, 
for $\lambda=\frac{\delta_\varepsilon}{2 C^2 \bar p_\varepsilon} \in [1, \mathsf{m}_\varepsilon/C]$, 
the {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of (\ref{eq:Dlt-bdd-by-g}) is at most
\[
                                   
e^{\delta_\varepsilon} \mathbb{E} \big[ e^{\lambda \bar \Delta^{(\varepsilon)}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}
         
}\big]  e^{-\lambda \delta_\varepsilon} + 
\mathbb{E} \big[ e^{-\lambda \bar \Delta^{(\varepsilon)}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}
         
}\big] e^{-\lambda \delta_\varepsilon} \le 4 e^{-\delta_\varepsilon^2/(4 C^2 \bar p_\varepsilon)} =
o_{\varepsilon}(e^{-2 \mathsf {K}_{3}})
\]
               
(as $\mathsf {K}_{3} \sqrt{\bar p_\varepsilon} \to 0$).
                                                                       
This yields  (\ref{eq:Dlt-bdd-by-g}) and thereby completes our proof of (\ref{eq:coupling-bdt}).
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- lemma-32: body_md -->
\label{lem:bd-Delj}
For some $C'$ finite,  any $\mathsf {K}_{1}$ and all $\varepsilon$, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bd-Delj}
\sup_{\boldsymbol{\theta}} \{ \mathbb{P}(\Delta^{(\varepsilon)}_{\boldsymbol{\theta},\ell} \ge C' \,  \bar p_\varepsilon \mathsf{s}) \} \le 2 \exp \big(-\frac{\bar p_\varepsilon \mathsf{s}}{C' (\ell-\mathsf {K}_{1}+1)} \big) \,, 
\qquad \forall y_1 \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_1,  \;\;  \ell \ge \mathsf {K}_{1} \,. 
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-32 -->
<!-- remark-19: body_md -->
\label{rmk:bd-Delj}
For $y_1 \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_1$ and our choice of $\mathsf {K}_{3} \ll n_\varepsilon$ we have that 
$\mathsf{s} \le \frac{1}{2} \mathsf{m}_\varepsilon^2 \le \gamma_0(\mathsf {K}_{3}) \mathsf{m}_\varepsilon$ and 
\[
2 \mathsf {K}_{3} e^{-\bar p_\varepsilon \mathsf{s}/(C' \mathsf {K}_{3})} = o_\varepsilon(e^{-3 \mathsf {K}_{3}}) \,.
\]
Recalling (\ref{dfn:bar-p-vep}) that $\bar p_\varepsilon = C_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}/\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon$,  we thus deduce 
from  (\ref{eq:bd-Delj})  and the union bound that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bd-Delu}
\sup_{y_1,\boldsymbol{\theta}}  \mathbb{P} \big( \Gamma_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{(\varepsilon)} \big) = o_\varepsilon(e^{-3 \mathsf {K}_{3}} ) \,,  \qquad
\Gamma_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{(\varepsilon)} := \bigcup_{\ell \in [\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{3}]} \{ \Delta^{(\varepsilon)}_{\boldsymbol{\theta},\ell} \ge C' C_{\mathsf {K}_{1}} \gamma_0(\ell) \} \,.
\end{equation}
<!-- end remark-19 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
Recall that $\Delta^{(\varepsilon)}_{\boldsymbol{\theta},\mathsf {K}_{1}} = \sum_{q} B_q$ is a Binomial($\mathsf{s},\bar p_\varepsilon$),  whose {\sc\lowercase{cgf}}
is at most $\mathsf{s} \bar p_\varepsilon (e^\lambda-1)$,  yielding 
by Markov's inequality at $\lambda=\log C_o$ that for large enough $C_o>1$,  
                                
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bd-DelKo}
\mathbb{P}\Big(\sum_{q=1}^{\mathsf{s}} B_q \ge C_o \bar p_\varepsilon \mathsf{s}\Big) \le e^{-\bar p_\varepsilon \mathsf{s}/C_o} 
\end{equation}
which is (\ref{eq:bd-Delj}) at $\ell=\mathsf {K}_{1}$.  Next,  setting $p_\ell:=1/(\ell-\mathsf {K}_{1}+1)$,
                         
recall that 
by Poisson kernel estimates 
$\mathbb{P}(T_{q,\ell} = j ) \le \frac{c}{2}\,  p_\ell^2 (1-p_\ell)^{j-1}$ for some finite $c$,  any $\ell > \mathsf {K}_{1}$,  $q,j \ge 1$ 
and $\theta_q$ (see \cite[(4.124)]{BRZ2}).  By elementary algebra it then follows that 
at $\lambda_o>0$ such that $1-e^{-\lambda_o}=\frac{1}{2} p_\ell$,  any $\ell > \mathsf {K}_{1}$ and all $q$,  $\theta_q$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Tq-cgf}
\mathbb{E} [e^{\lambda_o T_{q,\ell}}] \le 1 + \frac{c}{2}  \frac{p_\ell^2}{p_\ell - (1-e^{-\lambda_o})} = 1 + c \,  p_\ell 
\le e^{c \,  p_\ell} \;.
\end{equation}
With the representation (\ref{eq:Dlt-rep}) for independent $\{T_{q,\ell},  B_q,  q \le \mathsf{s}\}$,  we deduce
from (\ref{eq:bd-DelKo}) and Markov's inequality at $\lambda_o \ge 
                      
\frac{1}{2} p_\ell$ 
                      
of (\ref{eq:Tq-cgf}),  that for any $C'>0$ and $\ell > \mathsf {K}_{1}$,  
\begin{align*}
\sup_{\boldsymbol{\theta}} \{ \mathbb{P}(\Delta^{(\varepsilon)}_{\boldsymbol{\theta},\ell} \ge C' \,  \bar p_\varepsilon \mathsf{s}) \} &\le 
\mathbb{P}\big(\sum_{q=1}^{\mathsf{s}} B_q \ge C_o \bar p_\varepsilon \mathsf{s}\big) +
\sup_{\boldsymbol{\theta},\{q_i\}} \{ \mathbb{P}(\sum_{i=1}^{C_o \bar p_\varepsilon \mathsf{s}} T_{q_i,\ell} \ge C' \,  \bar p_\varepsilon \mathsf{s}) \} \nonumber \\
& \le \exp(-\bar p_\varepsilon \mathsf{s}/C_o) + \exp( (c \,  C_o - \frac{1}{2} C') p_\ell \,  \bar p_\varepsilon \,  \mathsf{s} ) 
\end{align*}
and taking $C'=2 C_o (c+1)$ results with (\ref{eq:bd-Delj}).
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
Comparing (\ref{dfn:wh-g1}) with (\ref{dfn:wh-g1n}),  our claim is that for $\mathsf {K}_{1}$ large,  
uniformly over $(y_1,L_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}) \in \mathbb{I}_\star^{(\varepsilon)}$
\begin{align}
e^{-o_\varepsilon(1)} \mathbb{E} \big[ \widehat{\eta}_\star(\mathsf {K}_{3}) e^{-2 \widehat{\eta}_\star(\mathsf {K}_{3}) - \frac{2}{\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon} \Delta^{(\varepsilon)}_{\boldsymbol{\theta},\mathsf {K}_{3}}} ;  \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{-} \big] 
\le \mathbb{E} \big[ \widehat{\eta}(\mathsf {K}_{3}) e^{-2 \widehat{\eta}(\mathsf {K}_{3})};  \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{o} \big] &+ o_\varepsilon(e^{-2 \mathsf {K}_{3}}) \nonumber \\
\le e^{o_\varepsilon(1)} 
\, \mathbb{E} \big[  \widehat{\eta}_\star(\mathsf {K}_{3}) e^{-2 \widehat{\eta}_\star(\mathsf {K}_{3}) - \frac{2}{\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon} \Delta^{(\varepsilon)}_{\boldsymbol{\theta},\mathsf {K}_{3}}} ;  \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{+} \big]  &+ o_\varepsilon(e^{-2 \mathsf {K}_{3}}) \,,
\label{eq:bd-gopm}
\end{align}
where in view of (\ref{eq:BK12}) and (\ref{eq:BK12n}),
for some ${\kappa'_-}<{\kappa'}$,  ${\kappa_1^-}<{\kappa_1}$,  ${\kappa_o^-} <{\kappa_o}$,  
\begin{align}
\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{-} & := \bigcap_{i=2,3} \big\{ \widehat{\eta}_\star(\mathsf {K}_i) \in (\mathsf {K}_i^{{\kappa_1}},\mathsf {K}_i^{{\kappa'_-}})  \big\}
