\!\!\! \bigcap_{\ell \in (\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2})}\!\!\! \big\{ \widehat{\eta}_\star(\ell) > \ell^{{\kappa_o}}  \big\}\,, \nonumber \\
\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{o} &:=  \bigcap_{i=2,3} \big\{ \widehat{\eta}(\mathsf {K}_i) \in (\mathsf {K}_i^{{\kappa_1}},\mathsf {K}_i^{{\kappa'}})  \big\}
\!\!\! \bigcap_{\ell \in (\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2})} \!\!\! \big\{ \widehat{\eta}(\ell) > \ell^{{\kappa_o}}  \big\} \,,  \nonumber \\
\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{+} & := \bigcap_{i=2,3} \big\{ \widehat{\eta}_\star(\mathsf {K}_i) \in (\mathsf {K}_i^{{\kappa_1^-}},\mathsf {K}_i^{{\kappa'}})  \big\}
\!\!\! \bigcap_{\ell \in (\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2})} \!\!\! \big\{ \widehat{\eta}_\star(\ell) > \ell^{{\kappa_o^-}}  \big\}\,.
\label{dfn:Bplus}
\end{align}
By definition $\widehat{\eta}(\ell) \ge \widehat{\eta}_\star(\ell)$,  $\gamma_0(\ell))+\widehat{\eta}_\star(\ell) \ge 0$ and 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Delj-alt}
\Delta^{(\varepsilon)}_{\boldsymbol{\theta},\ell} = 
\big(\,  \gamma_0(\ell) +\frac{1}{2} \widehat{\eta}(\ell) + \frac{1}{2} \widehat{\eta}_\star(\ell) \big) \big( \widehat{\eta}(\ell) -  \widehat{\eta}_\star(\ell) \big)  \,.
\end{equation}
Hence,  it is easy to see that on the events $\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{o}$ and $\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\pm}$
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bd-eta-etas}
0 \le \widehat{\eta}(\ell) - \widehat{\eta}_\star(\ell) \le 2 \Delta^{(\varepsilon)}_{\boldsymbol{\theta},\ell}/\gamma_0(\ell)  \qquad \forall \ell \in [\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}] \cup \{\mathsf {K}_{3}\} \,,
\end{equation}
from which we deduce that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Del-whes}
\begin{aligned}
2 C' C_{\mathsf {K}_{1}} \le \mathsf {K}_{2}^{{\kappa'}} - \mathsf {K}_{2}^{{\kappa'_-}} \quad &\Longrightarrow \quad
\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{-} \cap \big( \Gamma_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{(\varepsilon)}\big)^{\complement} \subset \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{o} \,, \\
2 C' C_{\mathsf {K}_{1}} \le (\mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa_o}} - \mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa_o^-}}) \wedge ( \mathsf {K}_{2}^{{\kappa_1}} - \mathsf {K}_{2}^{{\kappa_1^-}})  \quad &\Longrightarrow \quad
\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{o} \cap \big( \Gamma_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{(\varepsilon)}\big)^{\complement} \subset \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{+} \,.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
In view of (\ref{dfn:bar-p-vep}),  the {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of (\ref{eq:Del-whes}) holds for all $\mathsf {K}_{1}$ large and 
$\varepsilon$ small.  Further,  all expectations in (\ref{eq:bd-gopm}) are over $[0,1]$-valued variables,  so by
(\ref{eq:bd-Delu}) we establish (\ref{eq:bd-gopm}) upon showing that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gth-star}
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{-} \cap \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{o} \cap \big( \Gamma_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{(\varepsilon)}\big)^{\complement}  \quad &\Longrightarrow \quad 
\widehat{\eta}(\mathsf {K}_{3}) - \widehat{\eta}_\star(\mathsf {K}_{3}) \le \frac{\Delta^{(\varepsilon)}_{\boldsymbol{\theta},\mathsf {K}_{3}}}{\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon} + o_\varepsilon(1) \,,  \\
\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{+} \cap \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{o} \cap \big( \Gamma_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{(\varepsilon)}\big)^{\complement} \quad  &\Longrightarrow \quad 
o_\varepsilon(\widehat{\eta}_\star(\mathsf {K}_{3})) \ge \widehat{\eta}(\mathsf {K}_{3}) - \widehat{\eta}_\star(\mathsf {K}_{3}) \ge \frac{\Delta^{(\varepsilon)}_{\boldsymbol{\theta},\mathsf {K}_{3}}}{\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon} - o_\varepsilon(1) \,.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Note that  $0 \le \widehat{\eta}_\star(\mathsf {K}_{3}) \le \widehat{\eta}(\mathsf {K}_{3}) \le \mathsf {K}_{3}$ on $\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{o} \cap \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\pm}$.  Thus,  
substituting (\ref{eq:Delj-alt}) at $\ell=\mathsf {K}_{3}$ on the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} of (\ref{eq:gth-star})
                 
yields the top inequality since $\mathsf {K}_{3} (1- \frac{\gamma_0(\mathsf {K}_{3})}{\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon}) =  o_\varepsilon(1)$.
Moreover,  $\frac{\Delta^{(\varepsilon)}_{\boldsymbol{\theta},\mathsf {K}_{3}}}{\gamma_0(\mathsf {K}_{3})} \le C' C_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}=o_\varepsilon(\widehat{\eta}_\star(\mathsf {K}_{3}))$
on $\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{+} \cap \big( \Gamma_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{(\varepsilon)}\big)^{\complement}$,  so with $\mathsf {K}_{3}^2 = o_\varepsilon(\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon)$ 
the same reasoning yields also the bottom inequality of (\ref{eq:gth-star}).
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- proposition-14: body_md -->
\label{prop:UpperBoundz}  
For any block $\beta'$,  partition the blocks in $u(\beta')$ according to
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq-G0L}
\mathbb{G}_{\ell}  :=  \left\{ \beta\in u(\beta') : 2 r_{\ell-1} \le \mathsf{d}(\mathsf{v}_{\beta'},\mathsf{v}_{\beta}) < 2 r_{\ell-2}\right\}.
\end{eqnarray}
Then,  for some $c=c(\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6})$ finite,  any $\mathsf {K}_{6}$,  
large enough $\mathsf {K}_{0}$,  $\mathsf {K}_{5}$ and small enough $\varepsilon>0$,
\begin{align}\label{eq:UpperBoundzr}
& \sup_{\beta \in \mathbb{G}_\ell} \{ P^{(2)}_{\beta,\beta'} \} \leq  c \,  P^{(\star)}_{\beta',\mathsf {K}'_{1}}
e^{ -2(n''-\ell \vee \mathsf {K}_{1})}e^{- \frac{1}{8} (\ell \vee \mathsf {K}_{1})^{{\kappa_o}}_{n_{\varepsilon}}}\,, \qquad \forall \beta' \quad  
\forall \ell \le n_\varepsilon - \mathsf {K}_{0} + 2\,,
\end{align}
with $\mathsf {K}'_{1}=\mathsf {K}_{1}$,  except for taking $\mathsf {K}'_{1}=\mathsf {K}_{1}+3$ when $\ell \in \{\mathsf {K}_{1}+1,\mathsf {K}_{1}+2\}$.  Further,  for any block $\beta$,
\begin{align}\label{bd:Late-brch}
P^{(2,{\sf Late})}_{\beta} := \sum_{\{ \beta' : 0 < \mathsf{d}(\mathsf{v}_{\beta},\mathsf{v}_{\beta'}) \le 2 \varepsilon e^{\mathsf {K}_{0}-1} \} } \!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!
P^{(2)}_{\beta,\beta'} \le e^{-\frac{1}{3} \mathsf {K}_{5}^{\kappa_o}} 
P^{(1)}_{\beta} \,.
\end{align}
<!-- end proposition-14 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
Recall our tiling of the inner city $\mathbb{A}^{o}_{u}$ 
of edge-length $(1-6\mathsf{\delta_\star}) e^{-\mathsf {K}_{0}}$ by blocks of edge-length $\varepsilon e^{\mathsf {K}_{5}}$ each. 
It is thus easy to see that $\mathbb{G}_\ell \neq \emptyset$ only when $\ell \ge \mathsf {K}_{0}-\ell_o$,
in which case $|\mathbb{G}_\ell| \le c' e^{2(n''-\ell)}$ for some universal finite constant $c'$.
Further,  if $\beta \in \mathbb{G}_\ell$, $\ell > n_\varepsilon - \mathsf {K}_{0} + 2$ then necessarily
$\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{v}_{\beta'},\mathsf{v}_{\beta}) \le 2 \varepsilon e^{\mathsf {K}_{0}-1}$.   
Thus,  assuming {\sc\lowercase{wlog}} that $\mathsf {K}_{0} \ge \mathsf {K}_{4} + \ell_o$ and combining 
(\ref{eq:UpperBoundzr}) and (\ref{bd:Late-brch}) we find that 
\begin{align}
& P^{(2)}_{\beta'} =  \sum_{\beta\neq \beta', \beta \in u(\beta')} P^{(2)}_{\beta,\beta'}
\label{eq:SecondMomentDecomp}
\le P^{(2,{\sf Late})}_{\beta'} 
                                                                                           
+ \sum_{\ell_{n_\varepsilon} \ge \mathsf {K}_{0}-\ell_o} \sum_{\beta \in \mathbb{G}_{\ell}} P^{(2)}_{\beta,\beta'} 
\nonumber \\
& \le  e^{-\frac{1}{3} \mathsf {K}_{5}^{\kappa_o}} P^{(1)}_{\beta'} + 
 + c\, c' \Big [ \big(
 \sum_{\ell = \mathsf {K}_{0}-\ell_o}^{\mathsf {K}_{1}}  
 e^{2(\mathsf {K}_{1}-\ell)- \frac{1}{8} \mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa_o}}} 
+  \sum_{\ell = \mathsf {K}_{1}+1}^{n_\varepsilon-\mathsf {K}_{0}+2}  e^{-\frac{1}{8} \ell_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa_o}}} \Big) P^{(\star)}_{\beta',\mathsf {K}_{1}} 
+ 2  e^{-\frac{1}{8} \mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa_o}}} \,   P^{(\star)}_{\beta',\mathsf {K}_{1}+3} \Big]
 \nonumber \\
 &
 \leq e^{-\frac{1}{3} \mathsf {K}_{5}^{{\kappa_o}}} P^{(\star)}_{\beta',\mathsf {K}_{1}} 
 + c  \,  \Big[ 
 c'' \big( e^{2(\mathsf {K}_{1}-\mathsf {K}_{0})} e^{-\frac{1}{8} \mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa_o}}} +
 e^{-\frac{1}{8}\mathsf {K}_{0}^{{\kappa_o}}}  \big) P^{(\star)}_{\beta',\mathsf {K}_{1}} + 2 c' e^{-\frac{1}{8} \mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa_o}}} P^{(\star)}_{\beta',\mathsf {K}_{1}+3} \Big] 
 \end{align}
 for some $c''=c''(\ell_o)<\infty$.  Since $\mathsf {K}_{1} \to \infty$ before $\mathsf {K}_{5}$,
 and recalling that $\mathsf {K}_{1}-\mathsf {K}_{0} = o(\mathsf {K}_{1}^{\kappa_o})$,  we deduce that for any fixed $\mathsf {K}_{6}$,  uniformly in $\beta'$,
\begin{equation}
P^{(2)}_{\beta'} \leq  o_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon} (1)\,  P^{(\star)}_{\beta',\mathsf {K}_{1}} + e^{-\frac{1}{9} \mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa_o}}} P^{(\star)}_{\beta',\mathsf {K}_{1}+3} \,.
\label{glb.6}
\end{equation}
Now,  recall (\ref{dfn:wt-Q}),  (\ref{dfn:wt-Q2}) that 
\[
\widetilde{Q}^{(i,\varepsilon)}_{u,z} = \sum_{\beta' \in u} P^{(i)}_{\beta'},  \qquad i=1,2 
\]
(where we also utilized (\ref{eq:good-cover-y})).  Recall that $\sup_{\mathsf {K}_{5}} \alpha(\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6})<\infty$ 
(see \Cref{lem:alpha-unif-bd}),  and on the support of $g_\star(y,v)$ we have that 
$y e^{-2 v} \le \mathsf {K}_{1}^{\widetilde{\kappa}_\star}$ for some $\widetilde{\kappa}_\star(\kappa_\star)<\infty$.  So,  summing (\ref{glb.6}) over 
the $[(1-6\mathsf{\delta_\star}) e^{-\mathsf {K}_{0}}/(\varepsilon e^{\mathsf {K}_{5}})]^2$ blocks $\beta' \in u$,  using (\ref{eq:Po-Pm}) for 
the term at $\mathsf {K}_{1}$ and (\ref{eq:Pm-form}) for the one at $\mathsf {K}_{1}+3$, 
we have that for $\widetilde{Q}^{(\star,\varepsilon)}_{u,z}$ of (\ref{dfn:Qst}),
some $c=c(r_0,b,\mathsf {K}_{6})$ finite,  any large $\mathsf {K}_{5}$ and $\mathsf {K}_{0} \ge \mathsf {K}_{0}'(\mathsf {K}_{5})$,  
$\varepsilon$ small enough and all $u,z$, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Q2-Q1-Qs}
\widetilde{Q}^{(2,\varepsilon)}_{u,z} \le  o_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon} (1) \widetilde{Q}^{(1,\varepsilon)}_{u,z}
+ c \,  e^{-\frac{1}{10} \mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa_o}}} e^{2 (\mathsf {K}_{1}-\mathsf {K}_{0})} \,  \widetilde{Q}^{(\star,\varepsilon)}_{u,z} \,.
\end{equation}
In view of \Cref{lem:2mm-star},  summing this bound over $u$ results with  (\ref{eq:sec-mom-bd}) for 
$\xi(\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{0})$ which is the maximum of $e^{-\frac{1}{11} \mathsf {K}_{1}^{{\kappa_o}}}$,  see (\ref{eq:2mm-star}),
and twice the $\varlimsup_\varepsilon o_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{0},\varepsilon} (1)$ of (\ref{eq:Q2-Q1-Qs}).
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- lemma-33: body_md -->
\label{lem:2-levels} 
                                      
For some 
                     
                       
 $c(\mathsf {K}_{5})$ finite,  large enough $\mathsf {K}_{5}$,  $\mathsf {K}_{0}$ and any $\varepsilon$ small enough
                                                                                                
\begin{equation}\label{eq:drop2-levels}
P_{\beta,\ell}
\le c(\mathsf {K}_{5}) 
                  
\,  P^{(\star)}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}'_{1}} \qquad \forall \beta,  \ell \in (\mathsf {K}_{1},n'] \,,
\end{equation} 
where $\mathsf {K}'_{1}=\mathsf {K}_{1}$ except for $\mathsf {K}'_{1}=\mathsf {K}_{1}+3$ when $\ell \in \{\mathsf {K}_{1}+1,\mathsf {K}_{1}+2\}$.
<!-- end lemma-33 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
For any block $\beta$ and $y=\widehat{\eta}^{\,[z]}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}'_{1}}$ we set,  analogously to (\ref{dfn:Umy}),  the events
\begin{align}\label{dfn:UUpl}
\mathcal{U}^{(+,\varepsilon)}_{\beta,\ell} (y) := & 
 \{ L_{\beta,\mathsf {K}'_{1}}^{(y)} \in \mathbb{B}^\infty_{\bar \mu} ( \boldsymbol{\eta}^{\star,(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf {K}'_{1}}) \}
\bigcap_{j \in \mathsf {J}_\ell}  \{ \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,j}^{\,(y)} \in \bar{\mathsf I}_j  \} \bigcap \mathcal{R}\mathcal{U}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\beta}(y)
\end{align}
and by the argument leading to (\ref{eq:pre-precise}),  deduce that for all $\beta$ and $\ell$, 
\begin{equation}\label{dfn:Pml-alt}
P_{\beta,\ell} = (1+o_{\mathsf {K}_{5}}(1)) \mathbb{P} \big(\mathcal{U}^{(+,\varepsilon)}_{\beta,\ell} (\widehat{\eta}^{\,[z]}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}'_{1}})|\mathcal{F}\big) \,.
\end{equation}
(a) Taking $\ell \in \{\mathsf {K}_{1}+1,\mathsf {K}_{1}+2\}$,  compare
(\ref{dfn:UUpl}) with (\ref{dfn:Umy}) at $\mathsf {K}'_{1}=\mathsf {K}_{1}+3$,  to see 
that $\mathcal{U}^{(+,\varepsilon)}_{\beta,\ell} (y) \subset \mathcal{U}^{(\star,\varepsilon)}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}'_{1}} (y)$ yielding (\ref{eq:drop2-levels}) as an
immediate consequence of (\ref{dfn:Pml-alt}) and the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} of (\ref{dfn:P1-}).

We proceed with $\ell \ge \mathsf {K}_{1}+3$ where the starting level $\mathsf {K}'_{1}$ of $\mathcal{U}^{(+,\varepsilon)}_{\beta,\ell}(y)$ 
and the constraints imposed there,  match those of $\mathcal{U}^{(\star,\varepsilon)}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}(y)$.  In view of (\ref{dfn:P1-}) 
and (\ref{dfn:Pml-alt}),  it suffices to 
compare the events $\mathcal{U}^{(+,\varepsilon)}_{\beta,\ell}(y)$ and $\mathcal{U}^{(\star,\varepsilon)}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}(y)$ for fixed $\beta$ 
and {\sc\lowercase{wlog}} also $(y,L_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{(y)}) \in \mathbb{I}_\star^{(\varepsilon)}$,  as we do next.\\
(b).  $\ell \in (\mathsf {K}_{2}+2,\mathsf {K}_{3}]$.  In this range,  comparing (\ref{dfn:Umy}) with (\ref{dfn:UUpl}) 
we see that (\ref{eq:drop2-levels}) trivially holds since $\mathsf {J}_\ell=\mathsf {J}$ and $\mathcal{U}^{(+,\varepsilon)}_{\beta,\ell} (y) \subset \mathcal{U}^{(\star,\varepsilon)}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}} (y)$. \\
(c).  $\ell \in \{\mathsf {K}_{2}+1,\mathsf {K}_{2}+2,\mathsf {K}_{3}+1,\mathsf {K}_{3}+2\}$.  For $\ell =\mathsf {K}_{2}+i$,  $i=1,2$,  the removal 
of constraints at levels $\{\ell-2,\ell-1\}$ amounts to decreasing $\mathsf {K}_{2}$ by $3-i$,  
while for $\ell=\mathsf {K}_{3}+i$,  $i=1,2$,  it amounts to increasing $\mathsf {K}_{3}$ by $i$ (where
to bound $P_{\beta,\ell}$ first replace ${\kappa_o}$ by ${\kappa_o^-}$ and increase ${\kappa''}$ 
outside its new boundary levels $\mathsf {K}_{2}+i-3$,  or $\mathsf {K}_{3}+i$,   then replace ${\kappa_1}$ by 
${\kappa_o}$ and ${\kappa'}$ by ${\kappa''}$ at the remainder of $\partial \mathsf {J}$).  
Recall (\ref{eq:flex-Ki}) and \Cref{rmk:first-mom} that such adjustments of $\mathsf {K}_{2}$,  $\mathsf {K}_{3}$ 
and of our parameters do not affect the validity of (\ref{UUpy-asymp}),  so in this case
$P_{\beta,\ell} \le (1+o_\varepsilon(1)) P^{(\star)}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}$. \\
(d).  $\ell \in [\mathsf {K}_{3}+3,n']$.  As in part (c),  first enlarge in $P_{\beta,\ell}$ the windows 
$\bar{\mathsf I}_j$ to be $(j_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa_o^-}},\infty)$,  for all $j \in (\ell,n')$.  Setting $\widehat{g}_{\ell}^{(\varepsilon)}(\cdot)$ as in 
(\ref{def:wh-g3-ell}),  except for replacing ${\kappa_o}$ by ${\kappa_o^-}$ at levels $(\ell,n')$,
   
                                                                                       
                                                                                
   
note that by the Markov property of $\widehat{\eta}(j)$ under $\bar{\mathbb{P}}^{(\mathsf {K}_{3})}_{y_3}$,  it suffices for
(\ref{eq:drop2-levels}) to show that for large $\mathsf {K}_{5}$,  small $\varepsilon>0$ and all allowable $x' \in \bar{\mathsf I}_{\ell-3}$ 
                                        
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bd-drop-ell}
\bar{\mathbb{E}}^{(\ell-3)}_{x'} \Big[ \widehat{g}_{\ell}^{(\varepsilon)} \big(\widehat{\eta}(\ell)\big); \widehat{\eta}(\ell) \in \bar{\mathsf I}_\ell \Big] \le c(\mathsf {K}_{5}) 
\bar{\mathbb{E}}^{(\ell-3)}_{x'} \Big[ \widehat{g}_{\ell}^{(\varepsilon)} \big(\widehat{\eta}(\ell) \big); \widehat{\eta}(\ell) \in \bar{\mathsf I}_\ell,   
\widehat{\eta} (\ell-i) > (\ell-i)_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa_o^-}},  i=1,2 \Big] \,.
\end{equation}
By (\ref{eq:gfl-comp}) of \Cref{rmk:g3-formula-gen},  we get (\ref{eq:bd-drop-ell}) 
                                                                    
upon having,  uniformly in $\ell$,  $x' \in \bar{\mathsf I}_{\ell-3}$ and $y \in \gamma_0(\ell) + \bar{\mathsf I}_\ell$,  that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bd-d-ell-alt}
\bar{\mathbb{P}}^{(\ell-3)}_{x'} \Big[ \eta(\ell) \in [y,y+2) \Big] \le c(\mathsf {K}_{5}) 
\bar{\mathbb{P}}^{(\ell-3)}_{x'} \Big[ 
\widehat{\eta} (\ell-i) > (\ell-i)_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa_o^-}},  i=1,2,  \eta(\ell) \in [y,y+2) \Big] \,.
\end{equation}
The {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of (\ref{eq:bd-d-ell-alt}) is $q_3(x,[y,y+2))$ of \Cref{dfn:Markov}  
at $x:=\gamma_0(\ell-3)+x'$.  Here
$x \wedge y \ge \gamma_0(\ell) \ge \boldsymbol{\rho}_\varepsilon \ell_{n_\varepsilon}$ 
and $|x-y| \le (\boldsymbol{\rho}_\varepsilon \ell_{n_\varepsilon})^{{\kappa''}}$.  Further,  for 
$u_o$ of \Cref{lem:g4-cnc}(a),  the probability on the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} of (\ref{eq:bd-d-ell-alt}) 
is at least $q^{(u)}_{3}(x,[y,y+2))$ with $u = \frac{1}{2} \ell_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa_o}} \ge u_o$
once $\mathsf {K}_{5}$ is large enough,  whereby (\ref{eq:bd-d-ell-alt}) follows from 
(\ref{eq:q3-bd}).
\newline
(e).  $\ell \in [\mathsf {K}_{1}+3,\mathsf {K}_{2}]$.  Here $\mathsf {K}'_{1}=\mathsf {K}_{1}$ and for
$\boldsymbol{\theta}=\boldsymbol{\theta}(y_1)=\{\theta_{q,\beta}^{(\mathsf {K}_{1})},  q \le \mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}(y_1)\}$ with $y_1 = \widehat{\eta}^{\,[z]}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}$ we set 
$\widehat{g}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{(\varepsilon)}(\cdot)$ as in (\ref{dfn:wh-g1}),  except for replacing ${\kappa_o}$ by ${\kappa_o^-}$.
It then follows from our derivation of (\ref{eq:step2})-(\ref{eq:g3-formula}) that 
\begin{equation}\label{Pbm-hg3}
P^{(\star)}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}} = (1+o_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\varepsilon}(1)) 
\big[\varepsilon e^{\mathsf {K}_{5}}/r_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}\big]^2
 \,  \alpha(\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6}) 
\mathbb{E} \big[  \widehat{g}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{(\varepsilon)}(\boldsymbol{\theta}); (y_1,L_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}) \in \mathbb{I}_\star^{(\varepsilon)}  \,| \mathcal{F} \big] \,.
\end{equation}
Setting analogously to (\ref{dfn:wh-g1})-(\ref{eq:BK12}),
\begin{align}\label{dfn:wh-gl}
\widehat{g}_{\ell}^{(\varepsilon)}(\boldsymbol{\theta})& :=  [r_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}/r_{\mathsf {K}_{3}}]^2 \, \mathbb{E} \big[ g_3 \big( \widehat{\eta}(\mathsf {K}_{3}) \big) ;  \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_\ell  \,| \boldsymbol{\theta} \big]
\quad \text{for} \quad \boldsymbol{\theta}=\boldsymbol{\theta}(y_1) \quad \text{and} \\
\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_\ell &:=  \!\!\!\! \bigcap_{j \in (\mathsf {K}_{1},\ell-3)} \!\!\!\! \big\{ \widehat{\eta}(j) > j^{{\kappa_o^-}}  \big\} \!\!\!\!\! \bigcap_{j \in \{\ell-3,\ell\}}  
\!\!\!\!\! \big\{ \widehat{\eta}(j) \in \bar{\mathsf I}_j \big\} \!\!\!\! 
\bigcap_{j \in (\ell,\mathsf {K}_{2})} \!\!\! 
\big\{ \widehat{\eta}(j) > j^{{\kappa_o^-}}  \big\} \bigcap \big\{ \widehat{\eta}(\mathsf {K}_{2}) \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_2 \big\} \,,
\label{dfn:B-ell}
\end{align}
we enlarge $P_{\beta,\ell}$ by replacing at each $j \in (\mathsf {K}_{1},\ell-3) \cup (\ell,\mathsf {K}_{2}) \cup (\mathsf {K}_{3},n')$,  the window
$\bar{\mathsf I}_j$ by $(j_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa_o^-}},\infty)$,  to arrive,  analogously to (\ref{Pbm-hg3}) at 
\begin{equation}\label{Pbl-hg3}
P_{\beta,\ell} \le 2 \big[\varepsilon e^{\mathsf {K}_{5}}/r_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}\big]^2 \,  \alpha(\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6}) 
\mathbb{E} \big[  \widehat{g}_{\ell}^{(\varepsilon)}(\boldsymbol{\theta}); (y_1,L_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}) \in \mathbb{I}_\star^{(\varepsilon)}  \,| \mathcal{F} \big] \,.
\end{equation}
Comparing (\ref{Pbm-hg3}) with (\ref{Pbl-hg3}),   it suffices for (\ref{eq:drop2-levels}) to show 
that for some $C<\infty$,  
\begin{align*}
\widehat{g}_{\ell}^{(\varepsilon)}(\boldsymbol{\theta}) \le C\,  
 \widehat{g}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{(\varepsilon)}(\boldsymbol{\theta})  \qquad  \qquad \forall (y_1,L_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}) \in \mathbb{I}_\star^{(\varepsilon)} 
\end{align*}
and,  in view of (\ref{eq:K1-to-K3-u}) and (\ref{eq:V-tet-alt}),  for this we merely need to show that 
\begin{align}\label{eq:dr2-ell}
\widehat{g}_{\ell}^{(\varepsilon)}(\boldsymbol{\theta}) \le C\,  e^{-\mathsf {b}} e^{-2 V_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}} \,  [r_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}/r_{\mathsf {K}_{3}}]^2 \, 
\bar \mathbb{E}_{y_1}^{(\mathsf {K}_{1})} \big[  g_3\big( \widehat{\eta}(\mathsf {K}_{3}) \big) ;  \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}  \big]
\qquad  \forall (y_1,L_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}) \in \mathbb{I}_\star^{(\varepsilon)} \,.
\end{align}
To this end,  we utilize our coupling with $\boldsymbol{\bar \mu}$,  in analogy with (\ref{eq:BK12n})
to set $\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{+,\ell}$ as in (\ref{dfn:B-ell}) 
except for involving only the contributions $\widehat{\eta}_\star(j)$ from the coupled 
$\mathsf {K}_{1}$-level excursions (with $B_q=0$),  
                                                                  
while also slightly decreasing ${\kappa_o^-}$,  ${\kappa_o}$ and ${\kappa_1}$ (so $\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{+,\mathsf {K}_{1}}=\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{+}$ of (\ref{eq:BK12n})),  
and consider the following proxy for $\widehat{g}_{\ell}^{(\varepsilon)}(\cdot)$,
                      
\begin{align}\label{dfn:wt-g1n}
\widehat{g}_{+,\ell}^{(\varepsilon)} (\boldsymbol{\theta}) &:= [r_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}/r_{\mathsf {K}_{3}}]^2\,  
\, \mathbb{E} \big[  e^{-\frac{2}{\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon} \Delta^{(\varepsilon)}_{\boldsymbol{\theta},\mathsf {K}_{3}}} g_3 \big( \widehat{\eta}_\star(\mathsf {K}_{3}) \big) ;  \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{+,\ell} \big], 
\end{align}
(which at $\ell=\mathsf {K}_{1}$ matches our earlier definition (\ref{dfn:wh-g1n})).  Now 
note that a minor change in \Cref{sec:coupling}
(of deriving (\ref{eq:bd-gopm}) in terms of events $\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_\ell$ and $\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{+,\ell}$ of (\ref{dfn:B-ell})
instead of those of (\ref{dfn:Bplus})),  
yields,  similarly to (\ref{eq:coupling-bdt})-(\ref{eq:coupling-bd1}),  
\[
\widehat{g}_{\ell}^{(\varepsilon)}(\boldsymbol{\theta}) \le (1+o_{\varepsilon}(1))  \widehat{g}_{+,\ell}^{(\varepsilon)}(\boldsymbol{\theta}) + o_\varepsilon(1) = (1+o_{\varepsilon}(1)) \widehat{g}_{+,\ell}^{(\varepsilon)}(\boldsymbol{\bar \mu})\, e^{2 V_{\boldsymbol{\bar \mu}}}  
e^{-2 V_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}} + o_\varepsilon(1)  \quad  \forall (y_1,L_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}) \in \mathbb{I}_\star^{(\varepsilon)} \,.
\]
Similarly to our derivation of (\ref{eq:V-tet-alt}),  this,  
together with (\ref{eq:lim-V-psi})-(\ref{eq:lim-V-psi2}),  yield that for ordered $\boldsymbol{\psi}$ consisting 
of $
      
\mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}(y_1)$
{\sc\lowercase{iid}} samples from $\bar \mu$,   
\begin{equation}\label{eq:g-ell-bd}
\widehat{g}_{\ell}^{(\varepsilon)}(\boldsymbol{\theta}) \le (1+o_{\mathsf {K}_{1},\varepsilon}(1)) e^{-\mathsf {b}} e^{-2 V_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}} 
\mathbb{E} \big[ \widehat{g}_{+,\ell}^{(\varepsilon)}(\boldsymbol{\psi})  {\bf{1}}_{\{(y_1,L_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}) \in \mathbb{I}_\star^{(\varepsilon)}\}} \big]
                                    
+ o_\varepsilon(1) 
\qquad  \forall (y_1,L_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}) \in \mathbb{I}_\star^{(\varepsilon)} \,.
\end{equation}
Further,  denoting by $\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\star,\ell}$ the event $\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_\ell$ of (\ref{dfn:B-ell}) but with  
the smaller parameters ${\kappa_o^-}$,  ${\kappa_o}$,  ${\kappa_1}$ of $\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{+,\ell}$ and with slightly larger 
values of ${\kappa'}$,  ${\kappa''}$,  our proof of the left-inequality of (\ref{eq:bd-gopm}) can be adapted to show that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:coupling-bd2}
\mathbb{E} \big[ \widehat{g}_{+,\ell}^{(\varepsilon)}(\boldsymbol{\psi})  {\bf{1}}_{\{(y_1,L_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}) \in \mathbb{I}_\star^{(\varepsilon)}\}} \big] \le 2 \mathbb{E} \big[ \widehat{g}_{\ell}^{(\varepsilon)}(\boldsymbol{\psi}) \big] 
= 2  \,  [r_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}/r_{\mathsf {K}_{3}}]^2 \,  \bar \mathbb{E}_{y_1}^{(\mathsf {K}_{1})} \big[  g_3\big( \widehat{\eta}(\mathsf {K}_{3}) \big) ;  \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\star,\ell} \big] \,,
\end{equation}
where in $g_3(\cdot)$ on the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} we have the same ${\kappa_1}$,  ${\kappa'}$ values as in $\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\star,\ell}$.  In view of
(\ref{eq:g-ell-bd})-(\ref{eq:coupling-bd2}),  the bound (\ref{eq:dr2-ell}) is
a direct consequence of having for some $C<\infty$ and all $y_1 \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_1$, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:dr2-ell-alt}
\bar \mathbb{E}_{y_1}^{(\mathsf {K}_{1})} \big[  g_3\big( \widehat{\eta}(\mathsf {K}_{3}) \big) ;  \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\star,\ell} \big] 
\le C\, 
\bar \mathbb{E}_{y_1}^{(\mathsf {K}_{1})} \big[  g_3\big( \widehat{\eta}(\mathsf {K}_{3}) \big) ;  \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}  \big]  \,.
\end{equation}
Now,  by the same reasoning as in part (d),  the bound (\ref{eq:bd-drop-ell}) applies also for
\[
\widehat{g}_{\ell}^{(\varepsilon)}(y') = 
 \bar{\mathbb{E}}^{(\ell)}_{y'} \Big[ g_3 \big(\widehat{\eta}(\mathsf {K}_{3})\big);
\{ \widehat{\eta} (\mathsf {K}_{2}) \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_2 \} 
\!\! \bigcap_{j \in (\ell,\mathsf {K}_{2})} \!\! \{ \widehat{\eta} (j) >  j_{n_\varepsilon}^{{\kappa_o^-}} \} \Big] \,,
\]
yielding (\ref{eq:dr2-ell-alt}) (as argued at
(\ref{eq:K1-to-K3n}),  for 
                        
$\mathsf {K}_{1} \gg 1$ the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} 
of (\ref{eq:dr2-ell-alt}) 
is independent of ${\kappa_o^-}$,  ${\kappa_o}$,  ${\kappa_1}$, ${\kappa'}$,  ${\kappa''}$).
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- lemma-34: body_md -->
\label{lem:key-bd}
For some finite $c(\mathsf {K}_{6})$, uniformly over quantifiers as above, 
\begin{equation}
\label{eq-EB1}
\sum_{y_4,y_5} \alpha_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6}} (y_5)
\mathbb{P}( \widehat{\mathcal{B}}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\beta,\ell'} (y,y_4,y_5)|\mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}_\beta}_{\ell'}) \leq c(\mathsf {K}_{6}) 
e^{-2(n''-\ell)} e^{-\frac{1}{7} \ell^{{\kappa_o}}} \, .
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-34 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
For notational convenience we use hereafter $\ell \ge \mathsf {K}_{1}+3$ instead of $\ell'$.  
Note that for $\mathsf{v}:=\mathsf{v}_\beta$,  the collection 
$\underline{\mathsf{x}}_{\beta}$ of start point and endpoint of all excursions from $\partial \mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{v},r_{\ell})$ 
to $\partial\mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{v},r_{\ell-1})$ is $\mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\ell}$-measurable,  and with 
$\mathcal{F} \subseteq \mathcal{G}^\mathsf{v}_{\ell}$, the same applies for $y=\widehat{\eta}^{\,[z]}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}'_{1}}$ (as $\mathsf {K}'_{1} \le \ell$),   
$\widehat{\eta}^{(y)}_{\beta,\ell}$ and $L^{(y)}_{\beta,\ell}$.  It thus suffices to show that fixing 
any $a \in [\ell^{{\kappa_o}},\ell^{{\kappa''}}]$ such that $\mathsf{s}:=\mathsf{s}_{\ell}(a)$ of (\ref{eq:nominal}) is integer,
the bound (\ref{eq-EB1}) holds 
                                                     
when replacing $\mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}'_{1}}(y)$ by the first $\mathsf{s}$ 
of the $\ell$-level excursions between concentric circles centered at $\mathsf{v}$.  Having done that,  
the conditional probability on the {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of (\ref{eq-EB1}) now only depends 
on the angular differences $\boldsymbol{\theta} = \{\theta_{q,\beta}^{(\ell)}, q \le \mathsf{s}\}$ between the start and end 
point of those $\mathsf{s}$ 
                         
excursions.  We can further replace 
$\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,j}^{\,(y)}$ by $\widehat{\eta}_{\beta,j}^{(a)}$ that correspond to our $\mathsf{s}$ excursions 
at level $\ell$ and for $y_i$ with $\mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}_i}(y_i) \in \mathbb{N}$,  denote
by $\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},n'']} (y_4,y_5)$ and $\widehat{\mathcal{C}}^{(\varepsilon)} (y_2,y_3)$ the events analogous to   
those of (\ref{eq:B-K3}) and (\ref{eq:hat-C}),  respectively.  In this setting 
\begin{align}\label{eq:B-U}
\widehat{\mathcal{B}}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\beta,\ell} 
(y,y_4,y_5)\subset 
& \{L_{\boldsymbol{\theta}} \in \mathbb{B}^\infty_{\bar \mu} (\boldsymbol{\eta}^{\star,(\varepsilon)}_\ell)\} \bigcap \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon),(a)}_{[\ell,\mathsf {K}_{2}]} 
                                                                 
                                                                    
\bigcap
\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},n'']} (y_4,y_5) 
       
 \,,
\end{align}
for the $\mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf {K}_{2}}$-measurable events
\begin{align*}
\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon),(a)}_{[\ell,\mathsf {K}_{2}]} : =& 
                                                                 
 \!\!\!\! \bigcap_{j \in [\ell,\mathsf {K}_{2}]} \!\!\!\! \{ \widehat{\eta}^{(a)}_{\beta,j} \in \bar{\mathsf I}_j \} 
\end{align*}
and we get (\ref{eq-EB1}) upon showing that for any such $a$ and $L_{\boldsymbol{\theta}} \in \mathbb{B}^\infty_{\bar \mu} (\boldsymbol{\eta}^{\star,(\varepsilon)}_\ell)$,  
\begin{equation}\label{eq-EBa}
\sum_{y_4,y_5} \alpha_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6}} (y_5)
\mathbb{P}\big( \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon),(a)}_{[\ell,\mathsf {K}_{2}]} \cap \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},n'']} (y_4,y_5) \,|\, \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\ell}\big) 
\leq c(\mathsf {K}_{6}) 
e^{-2(n''-\ell)} e^{-\frac{1}{7} \ell^{{\kappa_o}}} \, .
\end{equation}
Proceeding to show (\ref{eq-EBa}),  with $\mathsf {K}_{3} > \mathsf {K}_{2} > \mathsf {K}_{\mathsf{a}} \ge \ell$,
applying \cite[Lemma 9.1]{BRZ2} allows us to decouple 
the events $\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},n'']} (y_4,y_5)$ (about concentric excursion counts starting at level $\mathsf {K}_{3}$),
from $\mathcal{G}^\mathsf{v}_{\mathsf {K}_{2}}$-measurable events.
Specifically,  
                                                                                                      
we have as in the
derivation of (\ref{eq:g3}),  that for some finite  $c'$, $c(\mathsf {K}_{6})$ and any $y_i \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_i$, $i=2,3$, 
\begin{align}\label{eq:barrier}
& \sum_{y_4,y_5} \alpha_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6}} (y_5)
\mathbb{P} \Big(\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},n'']}(y_4,y_5) \big| \, \widehat{\mathcal{C}}^{(\varepsilon)} (y_2,y_3), \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf {K}_{2}} \Big) \nonumber \\
& \le c' \sum_{y_4,y_5} \alpha_{\mathsf {K}_{5},\mathsf {K}_{6}} (y_5)
  \, \bar \mathbb{P}_{y_2}^{(\mathsf {K}_{2})} \Big( \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},n'']} (y_4,y_5) \big| \, \widehat{\mathcal{C}}^{(\varepsilon)} (y_2,y_3) \Big)
             
\le c(\mathsf {K}_{6}) y_3 e^{-2y_3} e^{-2(n''-\mathsf {K}_{3})} \,,
\end{align}
where the last inequality follows as in the derivation of (\ref{eq:g3-formula}) out of (\ref{eq:alt-g3})
(upon recalling that $\widehat{\eta}(\cdot)$ is distributed under $\bar{\mathbb{P}}_{y_2}^{(\mathsf {K}_{2})}$ as the 
excess occupation measures for reflected {\sc\lowercase{srw}} on $[\mathsf {K}_{3}-1,n'']$,  during its first 
$\mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}_{3}}(y_3)$ moves from $\mathsf {K}_{3}$ to $\mathsf {K}_{3}-1$).  We further condition on  $\mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf {K}_{2}} \supset 
\mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_\ell$
in the {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of (\ref{eq-EBa}),  splitting according to the value $y_2 \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_2$ of $\widehat{\eta}^{(a)}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{2}}$,  
at which point we can combine (\ref{eq:barrier}) with the elementary identity
\[
\mathbb{P} \Big( \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},n'']} (y_4,y_5) | \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf {K}_{2}} \Big) = \sum_{y_3 \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_3} 
\mathbb{P} (  \widehat{\mathcal{C}}^{(\varepsilon)} (y_2,y_3) | \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf {K}_{2}} ) \mathbb{P} (
\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},n'']} (y_4,y_5) | \widehat{\mathcal{C}}^{(\varepsilon)} (y_2,y_3),  \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf {K}_{2}}), 
\]
to deduce that (\ref{eq-EBa}) is a consequence of having that for any possible $a \in [\ell^{{\kappa_o}},\ell^{{\kappa''}}]$,  
\begin{equation}\label{eq-EB1-alt}
                  
\mathbb{E} \Big[ g_3 (\widehat{\eta}^{(a)}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{3}}) ; \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon),(a)}_{[\ell,\mathsf {K}_{2}]}
                                                                   
\, |\, \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\ell} \Big] {\bf{1}}_{\mathbb{B}^\infty_{\bar \mu} (\boldsymbol{\eta}^{\star,(\varepsilon)}_\ell)} (L_{\boldsymbol{\theta}})
\leq  
e^{-2(\mathsf {K}_{3}-\ell)} e^{-\frac{1}{7} \ell^{{\kappa_o}}} \, .
\end{equation}
Our proof of (\ref{eq-EB1-alt}) is an adaptation of the arguments in 
\cite[Section 4.4]{BRZ2}
                                                    
and we only sketch the required changes.  
Specifically,  we recall that the {\sc\lowercase{lhs}} of (\ref{eq-EB1-alt}) 
only depends on the angular differences $\boldsymbol{\theta}$ between the start and end point of our $\mathsf{s}$ excursions, 
coupling those excursions,  as in \cite[Lemma 4.10]{BRZ2},  with $\mathsf{s}$ such excursions of {\sc\lowercase{iid}} angular 
differences $\boldsymbol{\psi} = \{\psi_q, q \le \mathsf{s}\}$ from $\bar \mu$ of (\ref{dfn:Poiss}).  Hereafter we denote by $\widetilde{\mathbb{P}}$
the law on the probability space enlarged with these coupled {\sc\lowercase{iid}} angles
(analogously to \cite[(4.110)]{BRZ2},  except that here we  also average over the 
independent realization of $\boldsymbol{\psi}$).  Now,  in view of (\ref{dfn:dw}),  the event 
$\{L_{\boldsymbol{\theta}} \in \mathbb{B}^\infty_{\bar \mu} (\boldsymbol{\eta}^{\star,(\varepsilon)}_\ell)\}$ is contained (up to changing
certain universal constants),  in the $\mathcal{G}_\ell^\mathsf{v}$-measurable event 
$\mathcal{W}_{\mathsf{v},\ell}(\mathsf{s})$ of \cite[(4.19)]{BRZ2},  and the ``good coupling'' event $\Phi_{\ell,a}$ of \cite[(4.112)]{BRZ2},   
                                                          
is such that uniformly over $\ell, a$ and $\mathsf{v}$, $\varepsilon$,
\begin{align}\label{eq-EB2}
\widetilde \mathbb{P}(  \Phi_{\ell,a}^{\complement}   | \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\ell},   \mathcal{W}_{\mathsf{v},\ell}(\mathsf{s}) ) & \leq e^{-10 n_\varepsilon}
\end{align}
(see \cite[(4.108) and proof of Lemma 4.11]{BRZ2}).  
\begin{comment}
                                                    
                                                                         
                                                               
                                                     
                                
                                                                                                   
              
                            
\end{comment}
                                          
Similarly to  \cite[Lemma 4.9]{BRZ2}, 
utilizing the proof of \cite[Lemma 4.13]{BRZ2} at
               
$\mathsf {K}_{3}-\mathsf {K}_{2} \le \mathsf {K}_{2} - \ell$,  yields that in terms of $G_{\ell,a,y_2,y_3}(m)$ of (\ref{eq:BRZ-471})
(which replaces the factor
 $F_{\ell,a,y_2,y_3}$ of \cite[(4.94)]{BRZ2}),  
\[
\widetilde{\mathbb{P}} \Big(\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon),(a)}_{[\ell,\mathsf {K}_{2}]} 
                                    
\cap \Phi_{\ell,a} \bigcap_{i=2,3} \{ \widehat{\eta}^{(a)}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_i}=y_i \}    
\, |\, \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\ell} \Big) \le G_{\ell,a,y_2,y_3}(m)\,, 
\]
where $m=\log \ell$ 
due to $
                                   
\Phi_{\ell,a}$.
Similarly to (\ref{eq:BRZ-472}),  summing this bound over $y_2,y_3$ we arrive at 
\begin{align}\label{eq-EB3}
& \widetilde \mathbb{E}\Big[g_3 \big(\widehat{\eta}^{(a)}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{3}}\big) ;
\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon),(a)}_{[\ell,\mathsf {K}_{2}]} 
                                   
\cap \Phi_{\ell,a}| \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_\ell \Big] 
      
\le a \big(1+ \frac{a^2}{\mathsf {K}_{2}} \big) e^{-2a} e^{-2 (\mathsf {K}_{3}-\ell)} e^{M \log \ell} 
                                                        
                                                                  
                                               
\end{align}
for some universal $M$.  Now recall that $g_3(\cdot) \le 1$ and utilize (\ref{eq-EB2}) to eliminate
the event $\Phi_{\ell,a}$ from (\ref{eq-EB3}) in case $L_{\boldsymbol{\theta}} \in \mathbb{B}^\infty_{\bar \mu} (\boldsymbol{\eta}^{\star,(\varepsilon)}_\ell)$.  
Thereby,  we can also change from $\widetilde{\mathbb{E}}[\cdot]$ to $\mathbb{E}[\cdot]$ in (\ref{eq-EB3})
and since $a \ge \ell^{\kappa_o} \gg 1$,  conclude that 
                                                                      
(\ref{eq-EB1-alt}) holds.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- lemma-35: body_md -->
\label{lem:dec-2mm}
Fix $\mathsf{\delta_\star}>0$ and large $\mathsf {K}_{6}$.  Then,  for all $\mathsf {K}_{5}$ large enough,  
any $\beta$,  $y$ and vector $\underline{\mathsf{x}}_{\beta}$ of the start and end points of the $[\mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}(y)]$ 
first $\mathsf {K}_{1}$-level excursions of $\beta$, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bd-2mm}
\sum_{\mathsf{x} \in \mathbb{F}^{\beta}}  \sum_{j=\widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5}+2}^{\mathsf {K}_{0}+1} \;\,
\sum_{\mathsf{x}' \in \widehat{\mathbb{G}}_j}
\mathbb{P} \big[ \,  \mathcal{U}^{(\star,\varepsilon)}_{\beta,\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'}(y) \big| \underline{\mathsf{x}}_\beta \big] \le e^{-\frac{1}{3} \mathsf {K}_{5}^{\kappa_o}}  \mathbb{P}(\mathcal{U}^{(+,\varepsilon)}_{\beta}(y) | \underline{\mathsf{x}}_\beta) \,.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-35 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
Fix $\beta$,  $\mathsf{x} \in \mathbb{F}^\beta$,  $j \in [\widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5}+2,\mathsf {K}_{1}+1]$, 
$\mathsf{x}' \in \widehat{\mathbb{G}}_j$,  $y$ and the vector $\underline{\mathsf{x}}_{\beta}$ of the start and end points
of the $[\mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}(y)]$ first $\mathsf {K}_{1}$-level excursions of block $\beta$.  Set
$\widetilde{n}':=n_\varepsilon-\ell \le n'$ for $\ell:=j+6\log j$,
$\mathsf{v}:=\mathsf{v}_{\beta}$ and define the following quantities in terms of the laws $\bar \mathbb{P}^{(k)}_y$ of  \Cref{def:Fvj},
\begin{align}\label{dfn:gxxp}
g_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'}(y_2,y_3) &:=
\sum_{y_4 \in \bar{\mathsf I}_{\widetilde{n}'}
} \bar\mathbb{P}^{(\mathsf {K}_{3})}_{y_3}  \Big(\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},\widetilde{n}']} (y_3,y_4)  \Big) 
  \bar\mathbb{P}^{(\mathsf {K}_{2})}_{y_2} \Big(
  A^{\ell,\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'} 
 (y_4) \,|\,  \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},\widetilde{n}']} (y_3,y_4)  \Big) \,,\\
\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},\widetilde{n}']} (y_3,y_4) &:=  \big\{ \widehat{\eta}(\mathsf {K}_{3}) = y_3 \big \} 
\!\!\!\!
\bigcap_{k \in [\mathsf {K}_{3},\widetilde{n}']} \!\!\!\!\! \{ \widehat{\eta} (k) \in \bar{\mathsf I}_k \} \bigcap \big\{ \widehat{\eta}(\widetilde{n}') = y_4 \big \} \,,
\label{eq:B-K3n} 
\\
\label{eq:term2}
A^{\ell,\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'}(y_4) &:= \Big\{  T_{\mathsf{x},n_\varepsilon+1}^{\mathsf{v},\widetilde{n}',m} =0, 
T_{\mathsf{x}',n_\varepsilon+1}^{\mathsf{v},\widetilde{n}',m} =0,    \;\;  m=\mathsf{s}_{\widetilde{n}'} (y_4) \in \mathbb{N} \Big\},
\end{align}
where throughout this proof,  the traversal times of (\ref{eq-calgary})
and $\widehat{\eta}(k)$ are for excursions around $\mathsf{v}$ during the 
first $\mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}(y)$ such $\mathsf {K}_{1}$-level excursions.  A key step in our proof is to show that
\begin{align}
\mathbb{P} [ \,  \mathcal{U}^{(\star,\varepsilon)}_{\beta,\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'}(y) | \underline{\mathsf{x}}_\beta] \le 
4 & \sum_{y_2 \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_2,  y_3 \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_3} \mathbb{P} \Big[ \mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}^{(\varepsilon),(y)}_{\beta,[\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]} \bigcap \{ \widehat{\eta}^{\,(y)}_ {\beta,\mathsf {K}_{2}} = y_2,
\widehat{\eta}^{\,(y)}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{3}}=y_3 \}  \, \big| \,  \underline{\mathsf{x}}_\beta \Big] g_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'}(y_2,y_3) 
  \,,
\label{eq:dec-2mm}
\end{align}
where as in (\ref{eq:BW-K12}), 
\begin{align} \label{B-K1-K2n}
\mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}^{(\varepsilon),(y)}_{\beta,[\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]} & :=  \mathcal{W}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\beta}(y) 
\bigcap_{k \in [\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]} \big\{ \widehat{\eta}_{\beta,k}^{\,(y)} \in \bar{\mathsf I}_k  \big\}   \,.
\end{align}
To this end,  we 
omit from $\mathcal{U}^{(\star,\varepsilon)}_{\beta,\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'}$ the excursion constraints at levels $(\widetilde{n}',n'']$ and decompose the resulting event 
as in Steps {\bf I} and {\bf II} of \Cref{sec:angle-diff},  now with $\widetilde{n}'$ and $\widetilde{n}'':=n_\varepsilon-1-j \vee \mathsf {K}_{5}$
in lieu of $n'$ and $n''$.  Specifically,  
                                             
                                                                                    
we have in analogy to (\ref{eq:decom-U}) and (\ref{eq:B-K1-K2})-(\ref{eq:decomp})  that
\begin{align}\label{eq:decom-Un}
  \mathcal{U}^{(\star,\varepsilon)}_{\beta,\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'}(y) &\subset \bigcup_{y_2,y_3,y_4} \Big\{  \widehat{\mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]} (y_2|y) 
                                               
  \bigcap \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},\widetilde{n}']} (y_3,y_4) \bigcap 
  A^{\ell,\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'} (y_4)
 \Big\},
 \end{align}
 \begin{align}
 \label{eq:B-K1=K2}
\widehat{\mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]} (y_2|y) := \mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}^{(\varepsilon),(y)}_{\beta,[\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]} \bigcap \{ \widehat{\eta}^{\,(y)}_ {\beta,\mathsf {K}_{2}} = y_2 \} \,,
\end{align}
 and the union is over $y_2 \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_2$,  $y_3 \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_3$ and $y_4 \in \bar{\mathsf I}_{\widetilde{n}'}$.
Since the number 
                         
of $\widetilde{n}'$-level excursions around $\mathsf{v}$ and 
\[
 \widehat{\mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{1},\widetilde{n}']}(y_4|y) := 
  \bigcup_{y_2,y_3} \Big\{ \widehat{\mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]} (y_2|y) 
  \bigcap \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},\widetilde{n}']} (y_3,y_4) \Big\},
\] 
are $\mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\widetilde{n}'}$-measurable,  it follows from (\ref{eq:decom-Un}) that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cnd-at-ell}
\mathbb{P} [ \,  \mathcal{U}^{(\star,\varepsilon)}_{\beta,\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'}(y) | \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\widetilde{n}'}] \le \sum_{y_4} 
{\bf{1}}_{\widehat{\mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{1},\widetilde{n}']}(y_4|y)} \,\,
\mathbb{P}
\Big( A^{\ell,\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'} (y_4)   \, | \,  \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\widetilde{n}'} 
\Big) \,.
\end{equation}
Denoting by $\mathcal{C}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\widetilde{n}',\widetilde{n}''} (y_4,y_5)$ having precisely $\mathsf{s}_{\widetilde{n}''} (y_5)$ 
of our $\mathsf{s}_{\widetilde{n}'} (y_4)$ level $\widetilde{n}'$ excursions enter $\mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{v},r_{\widetilde{n}''})$,  we set 
\begin{equation}\label{dfn:alpha-x}
\alpha_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'} (y_5|y_2,y_3,y_4) := \bar \mathbb{P}_{y_2}^{(\mathsf {K}_{2})} \Big( A^{\ell,\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'} (y_4)
 \,  | \,  \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},\widetilde{n}']} (y_3,y_4) \bigcap 
\mathcal{C}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\widetilde{n}',\widetilde{n}''} (y_4,y_5) \Big) \, .
\end{equation}
The $\mathcal{G}^\mathsf{v}_{\widetilde{n}'}$-measurable 
event $\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},\widetilde{n}']} (y_3,y_4)$ specifies the number $m=\mathsf{s}_{\widetilde{n}'}(y_4)$ of level $\widetilde{n}'$ excursions,  with $\alpha_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'} (y_5|y_2,y_3,y_4)$ the conditional probability of event 
$A^{\ell,\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'} (y_4)$ when precisely $\mathsf{s}_{\widetilde{n}''}(y_5)$ of the  $m$ excursions reach level $\widetilde{n}''$
and the starting and end points of those $m$ excursions are chosen according to the law induced by 
$\bar \mathbb{P}_{y_2}^{(\mathsf {K}_{2})}\big(\cdot|\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},\widetilde{n}']} (y_3,y_4)\big)$.  
Here $m=\mathsf{s}_{\widetilde{n}'} (y_4)
                        
 \le 5 \ell^2$,  while $\mathsf {K}_{5}$ large guarantees 
having $\widetilde{n}''-\widetilde{n}' \ge 2 \log (5 \ell^2)$.  Further,  
                     
for $\mathsf{x}' \in \widehat{\mathbb{G}}_j$ and fixed $y_4$,  the event $A^{\ell,\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'}(y_4)$ 
is 
measurable on the path within $\mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{v},r_{\widetilde{n}''})$,  so by
\cite[Lemma 9.3]{BRZ2},  we have similarly to (\ref{eq:K3-angles}),  that for any $y_2 \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_2$,  $y_3 \in \mathsf{I}^{\star}_3$
and relevant value of $y_4$,
\begin{align}
\mathbb{P} \Big( A^{\ell,\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'} (y_4)   \, | \,  \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\widetilde{n}'} \Big) 
= \sum_{y_5}  \mathbb{P}  \big( A^{\ell,\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'} & (y_4)   \, | \,  \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\widetilde{n}'},  \mathcal{C}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\widetilde{n}',\widetilde{n}''} (y_4,y_5) 
\big) \mathbb{P} \big( \mathcal{C}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\widetilde{n}',\widetilde{n}''} (y_4,y_5)  \, | \,  \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\widetilde{n}'} ) 
\nonumber \\
&\le 2 \sum_{y_5} \alpha_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'} (y_5|y_2,y_3,y_4) \mathbb{P} \big( \mathcal{C}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\widetilde{n}',\widetilde{n}''} (y_4,y_5)  \, | \,  \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\widetilde{n}'} ) \,.
\label{BRZ-93-2mt}
\end{align}
Here we used the fact that  the conditioning on $\mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\widetilde{n}'}$ in $ \mathbb{P}  \big( A^{\ell,\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'}  (y_4)   \, | \,  \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\widetilde{n}'},  \mathcal{C}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\widetilde{n}',\widetilde{n}''} (y_4,y_5) 
\big)$ is the same as conditioning on the starting and end points of those $m$ excursions,  see the proof of \cite[Lemma 9.3]{BRZ2}.

Next,  combine (\ref{eq:cnd-at-ell}) 
and (\ref{BRZ-93-2mt}),  then evaluate the conditional expectation given 
$\mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf {K}_{2}} \subset \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\widetilde{n}'}$, 
on which $\widehat{\mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]}(y_2|y)$ 
is measurable.  Utilizing \cite[Lemma 9.1]{BRZ2} similarly to (\ref{eq:g3}),  this leads to 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cnd-at-K2}
\mathbb{P} [ \,  \mathcal{U}^{(\star,\varepsilon)}_{\beta,\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'}(y) | \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf {K}_{2}}] \le 4 \sum_{y_2,y_3} 
{\bf{1}}_{\widehat{\mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]}(y_2|y)} 
\mathbb{P} \big( \widehat{\mathcal{C}}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf {K}_{2},\mathsf {K}_{3}} (y_2,y_3) \, | \,  \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf {K}_{2}} \big) f_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'} (y_2,y_3)\,,
\end{equation}
for events $\widehat{\mathcal{C}}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf {K}_{2},\mathsf {K}_{3}}(\cdot,\cdot)$ as in (\ref{def:Cjjp}) (now in terms of our
$\mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}(y)$ first $\mathsf {K}_{1}$-excursions around $\mathsf{v}$),  and 
\begin{align}\label{dfn:fxxp}
f_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'}(y_2,y_3) := \sum_{y_4,y_5}  \alpha_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'} (y_5|y_2,y_3,y_4)
 \bar\mathbb{P}^{(\mathsf {K}_{2})}_{y_2} 
 \Big(\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},\widetilde{n}']} (y_3,y_4) \bigcap \mathcal{C}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\widetilde{n}',\widetilde{n}''} (y_4,y_5)
  \,| \,  \widehat{\mathcal{C}}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf {K}_{2},\mathsf {K}_{3}} (y_2,y_3)  \Big) \,.
 \end{align}
Note from (\ref{eq:B-K3n}) that 
$\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},\widetilde{n}']} (y_3,y_4) \subset  \widehat{\mathcal{C}}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf {K}_{2},\mathsf {K}_{3}} (y_2,y_3)$
under the law $\bar\mathbb{P}^{(\mathsf {K}_{2})}_{y_2}$,  so plugging (\ref{dfn:alpha-x}) into (\ref{dfn:fxxp}),  we arrive at
  \begin{align*}
  f_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'}(y_2,y_3)
&= \sum_{y_4,y_5}  
 \bar\mathbb{P}^{(\mathsf {K}_{2})}_{y_2} 
 \Big(\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},\widetilde{n}']} (y_3,y_4) \bigcap \mathcal{C}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\widetilde{n}',\widetilde{n}''} (y_4,y_5) \bigcap A^{\ell,\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'} 
 (y_4)
  \,| \,  \widehat{\mathcal{C}}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf {K}_{2},\mathsf {K}_{3}} (y_2,y_3) \Big) \\
  &=\sum_{y_4}  
 \bar\mathbb{P}^{(\mathsf {K}_{2})}_{y_2} 
 \Big(\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},\widetilde{n}']} (y_3,y_4) \bigcap A^{\ell,\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'} 
 (y_4)
  \,| \,  \widehat{\mathcal{C}}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf {K}_{2},\mathsf {K}_{3}} (y_2,y_3) \Big) \\
 &= \sum_{y_4}  
 \bar\mathbb{P}^{(\mathsf {K}_{2})}_{y_2} 
 \big(\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},\widetilde{n}']} (y_3,y_4)  \,| \,  \widehat{\mathcal{C}}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf {K}_{2},\mathsf {K}_{3}} (y_2,y_3) \big) 
 \bar\mathbb{P}^{(\mathsf {K}_{2})}_{y_2} \big( A^{\ell,\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'}  (y_4) \,|\,
 \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},\widetilde{n}']} (y_3,y_4) \big) \,.
\end{align*}
This is precisely  $g_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'}(y_2,y_3)$ of (\ref{dfn:gxxp}),  since 
\begin{align*} 
 \bar\mathbb{P}^{(\mathsf {K}_{2})}_{y_2} \big(
 \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},\widetilde{n}']} (y_3,y_4)  \,| \,  \widehat{\mathcal{C}}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf {K}_{2},\mathsf {K}_{3}} (y_2,y_3) \big) 
 =
   \bar\mathbb{P}^{(\mathsf {K}_{3})}_{y_3} 
 \big(\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},\widetilde{n}']} (y_3,y_4)  \big) \,,
\end{align*}
thanks to the Markov property of the concentric excursion counts around $\mathsf{v}$.  

To proceed,  replace $f_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'} (\cdot)$ by $g_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'}(\cdot)$ in (\ref{eq:cnd-at-K2})
and evaluate the conditional expectation of both sides given 
$\mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}} \subset \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf {K}_{2}}$ to find that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:pre-dec-2mm}
\mathbb{P} [ \,  \mathcal{U}^{(\star,\varepsilon)}_{\beta,\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'}(y) | \mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}] \le 4 \sum_{y_2,y_3} \mathbb{P} \Big[\widehat{\mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]}(y_2|y)
\bigcap  \widehat{\mathcal{C}}^{(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf {K}_{2},\mathsf {K}_{3}} (y_2,y_3) \, | \,  \mathcal{G}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\mathsf{v}} \Big] g_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'} (y_2,y_3)\,.
\end{equation}
This amounts to (\ref{eq:dec-2mm}),  since $\underline{\mathsf{x}}_\beta$ is $\mathcal{G}^{\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf {K}_{1}}$-measurable 
and one easily checks,  in view of (\ref{eq:B-K1=K2}),  that the conditional probabilities 
on the {\sc\lowercase{rhs}} of (\ref{eq:pre-dec-2mm}) match those on 
(\ref{eq:dec-2mm}).




Now,  $\bar\mathbb{P}^{(\mathsf {K}_{2})}_{y_2} \big(  \cdot
                                   
 \,|\,  \mathcal{A}^{(m)} \big)$,  at $\mathcal{A}^{(m)}=\mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},\widetilde{n}']} (y_3,y_4)$ 
which is determined by counts of excursions around $\mathsf{v}$
       
(for radii $R_{i+1-\mathsf {K}_{2}}=r_i$,  $i \le \widetilde{n}'$),  
puts us
                                                      
in the setting of \Cref{rmk:off-center-applies} for
$R=r_{\widetilde{n}'} = e^\ell \varepsilon$ and precisely $m=\mathsf{s}_{\widetilde{n}'}(y_4)$ paths 
from $\mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{v},R)$ to $\mathbb{B}_{\mathsf{d}}(\mathsf{v},e R)$ completed during our 
$
\mathsf{s}:=
\mathsf{s}_{\mathsf {K}_{2}}(y_2)$ {\sc\lowercase{iid}} outer Brownian excursions.   As
$A^{\ell,\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'} (y_4)$ requires avoiding 
$\mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},\varepsilon/e) \cup \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x}',\varepsilon/e)$,  the 
conditional probability 
$\bar\mathbb{P}^{(\mathsf {K}_{2})}_{y_2} \Big(  A^{\ell,\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'}  (y_4) \,|\,  \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},\widetilde{n}']} (y_3,y_4)  \Big)$ 
is of the form of 
                                                
\Cref{lem-xyN},  with $\ell=j+6 \log j$ and $\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}')$ 
as given in (\ref{dfn:tGj}).  Thus,  for $C'<\infty$ and large $\mathsf {K}_{5}$,   
                        
any such $\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}',\mathsf{v}$ and $y_2,y_3,y_4$,   we deduce from (\ref{xyN.2}) that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Axxp-bd}
 \,  \bar\mathbb{P}^{(\mathsf {K}_{2})}_{y_2} \Big(
  A^{\ell,\mathsf{v}}_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'} 
 (y_4) \,|\,  \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},\widetilde{n}']} (y_3,y_4)  \Big) \le  C' e^{-4j} e^{-3y_4} \,.
\end{equation}
In addition,  {from (\ref{18.20bend}) 
                                   
at levels $[\mathsf {K}_{3},\widetilde{n}']$ from height $y_3$ to $[b,b+1)$}  we get that  
\begin{align}\label{eq:barrier-K3-wtn}
\bar\mathbb{P}^{(\mathsf {K}_{3})}_{y_3} 
 \Big( \big\{ \widehat{\eta}(\widetilde{n}') \in [b,  b+1] \big \}  
\!\!\!\!
\bigcap_{k \in [\mathsf {K}_{3},\widetilde{n}']} \!\!\!\!\! \{ \widehat{\eta} (k) \in \bar{\mathsf I}_k \} 
\Big) \leq 
                           
b e^{2b} \, 
e^{-2(\widetilde{n}'-\mathsf {K}_{3})} \,  y_3 e^{-2y_3}  \,.
\end{align}
Since $ \bar{\mathsf I}_{\widetilde{n}'} \subset [j^{\kappa_o},\infty)$ and $j \ge \widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5} \gg 1$,  plugging (\ref{eq:Axxp-bd})
into (\ref{dfn:gxxp}) and then utilizing (\ref{eq:barrier-K3-wtn}),  yields that 
\begin{align*}
 g_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'}(y_2,y_3) &\le  C' e^{-4j} 
\sum_{b \in \bar{\mathsf I}_{\widetilde{n}'} \cap \mathbb{N}} e^{-3b} \, 
\bar\mathbb{P}^{(\mathsf {K}_{3})}_{y_3}  \big(\bigcup_{y_4 \in [b,b+1)} \mathcal{B}^{(\varepsilon)}_{[\mathsf {K}_{3},\widetilde{n}']} (y_3,y_4)  \big) \\
&\le   
  C'  e^{-4j}  e^{-2(\widetilde{n}'-\mathsf {K}_{3})} \,  y_3 e^{-2y_3} 
 \sum_{b \in  \bar{\mathsf I}_{\widetilde{n}'} \cap \mathbb{N}} b e^{-b} \le \frac{1}{4} e^{-2(\widetilde{n}'-\mathsf {K}_{3})} e^{-4j} 
 e^{-\frac{1}{2} j^{\kappa_o}}  \,  y_3 e^{-2y_3}  \,.
\end{align*}
Plugging this bound  in (\ref{eq:dec-2mm}),  yields that for $g_3(y_3):={\bf 1}_{\mathsf{I}^{\star}_3}(y_3)y_3 e^{-2 y_3}$, 
any $\mathsf{x} \in \mathbb{F}^\beta$ and $\mathsf{x}' \in \widehat{\mathbb{G}}_{j}$, 
\begin{align}\label{eq:bd-2mm-xxp}
\mathbb{P} [ \,  \mathcal{U}^{(\star,\varepsilon)}_{\beta,\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'}(y) |  \underline{\mathsf{x}}_\beta ] \le  e^{-2 (\widetilde{n}'-\mathsf {K}_{3})} e^{-4 j} e^{-\frac{1}{2} j^{\kappa_o}}
\, \mathbb{E} \big[ g_3(\widehat{\eta}^{\,(y)}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{3}});  \mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}^{(\varepsilon),(y)}_{\beta,[\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]}  \,|  \underline{\mathsf{x}}_\beta \big]  \,.
\end{align}
Now,  by the same reasoning that led to 
(\ref{eq:uux-to-emp-meas}),  for any $\beta$,  $y$ and $\underline{\mathsf{x}}_\beta$,  
\[
\mathbb{E} \big[ g_3(\widehat{\eta}^{\,(y)}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{3}});  \mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}^{(\varepsilon),(y)}_{\beta,[\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]}  \,| \underline{\mathsf{x}}_\beta \big] =
\mathbb{E} \big[ g_3(\widehat{\eta}^{\,(y)}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{3}});  \mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}^{(\varepsilon),(y)}_{\beta,[\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]}  \,| L_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{(y)}\big] \,,
\]
hence by (\ref{eq:good-cover}),  for $\mathsf {K}_{6}$ large,  some $\underline \alpha(\mathsf {K}_{6})>0$
all $\mathsf {K}_{5}$ large enough,  any $\beta$,  $y$ and $\underline{\mathsf{x}}_\beta$ 
\begin{equation}\label{bd:g-cover}
 \frac{1}{2} \underline \alpha(\mathsf {K}_{6}) e^{-2 (n''-\mathsf {K}_{3})} 
\, \mathbb{E} \big[ g_3(\widehat{\eta}^{\,(y)}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{3}});  \mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}^{(\varepsilon),(y)}_{\beta,[\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]}  \,| \underline{\mathsf{x}}_\beta \big]  \le \mathbb{P}(\mathcal{U}^{(+,\varepsilon)}_{\beta}(y) | \underline{\mathsf{x}}_\beta) \,.
\end{equation}
Next,  recall (\ref{dfn:F-beta}) and 
(\ref{dfn:tGj}) that $|\mathbb{F}^\beta| \le  c e^{2 \mathsf {K}_{5}}$ and 
$|\widehat{\mathbb{G}}_{j}| \le c e^{2j}$ for some $c(\widetilde{c})$ finite,  any $\beta$ and $j$.  Thus,   
with $\widetilde{n}'=n_\varepsilon-j-6 \log j$,  we have for any $\mathsf {K}_{6}$,  $\mathsf{\delta_\star}>0$ and all $\mathsf {K}_{5}$ large enough,    
\begin{align}
|\mathbb{F}^\beta| \sum_{j=\widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5}+2}^{\mathsf {K}_{0}+1}  \,  |\widehat{\mathbb{G}}_j| \, 
e^{-2 (\widetilde{n}'-\mathsf {K}_{3})} e^{-4 j} e^{-\frac{1}{2} j^{\kappa_o}}
&\le c^2 \,  e^{-2(n''-\mathsf {K}_{3})} 
 \sum_{j=\widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5}+2}^{\infty} j^{12} e^{-\frac{1}{2} j^{\kappa_o}} \nonumber \\
 &\le \frac{1}{2} \underline \alpha(\mathsf {K}_{6}) e^{-2 (n''-\mathsf {K}_{3})} 
 e^{-\frac{1}{3} \mathsf {K}_{5}^{\kappa_o}} \,.
 \label{eq:sum-xxp}
\end{align}
Combining  (\ref{eq:bd-2mm-xxp}) and (\ref{eq:sum-xxp}) we deduce that 
\[
                                  
\sum_{\mathsf{x} \in \mathbb{F}^{\beta}} \sum_{j=\widetilde{\mathsf {K}}_{5}+2}^{\mathsf {K}_{0}+1} \;\,
\sum_{\mathsf{x}' \in \widehat{\mathbb{G}}_j}
\mathbb{P} \big[ \,  \mathcal{U}^{(\star,\varepsilon)}_{\beta,\mathsf{x},\mathsf{x}'}(y) \big| \underline{\mathsf{x}}_\beta \big] \le  \frac{1}{2} \underline \alpha(\mathsf {K}_{6}) e^{-2 (n''-\mathsf {K}_{3})} 
 e^{-\frac{1}{3} \mathsf {K}_{5}^{\kappa_o}} 
\, \mathbb{E} \big[ g_3(\widehat{\eta}^{\,(y)}_{\beta,\mathsf {K}_{3}});  \mathcal{B}\mathcal{W}^{(\varepsilon),(y)}_{\beta,[\mathsf {K}_{1},\mathsf {K}_{2}]}  \,| \underline{\mathsf{x}}_\beta \big],
\]
which together with (\ref{bd:g-cover}) implies that (\ref{eq:bd-2mm}) holds as well.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- proposition-15: body_md -->
\label{th-heightcontinuity}
Fixing  $\mathsf{\delta_\star}, \mathsf {K}_{0}, \mathsf {K}_{5},z$,  for any $\gamma,\zeta>0$,  there exists $\delta>0$ so
\begin{align}
\limsup_{\varepsilon \to 0} \mathbb{P} \Big(\sup_{\stackrel{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{y} \in \mathbb{F}_{n_\varepsilon} \cup \widetilde{\mathbb{F}}_\varepsilon}{\mathsf{d} (\mathsf{x}, \mathsf{y}) \le \delta  }}
\|(Y^{(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf{x},[z]},V^{(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf{x},[z]})
-(Y^{(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf{y},[z]},V^{(\varepsilon)}_{\mathsf{y},[z]})\|_\infty \ge \gamma \Big) &\leq \zeta \,.
\label{hc.2a}
\end{align}
<!-- end proposition-15 -->
<!-- proposition-16: body_md -->
\label{theo-mclt}
Fix $\mathsf{\delta_\star},\mathsf {K}_{0},z$ and $\{\mathsf{x}_{i}: i \le p \} \subset  \widetilde{\mathbb{F}}_\varepsilon$,  independent of $\varepsilon$ and $z$.
For $1 \le i \le p$,  let 
\begin{align}\label{def:qin}
q_{\rm in}^{(\varepsilon)}(i) &:= \frac{1}{\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon+z} \Big(N_{\mathsf{x}_i}-\mathbb{E}\big[N_{\mathsf{x}_i}|\mathcal{H}_{\mathsf{k}_\varepsilon(z)} \big]\Big),\\
q_{\rm in}^{(\varepsilon)}(i+p) &:= \frac{1}{\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon+z}
\Big(\hat{N}^\theta_{\mathsf{x}_i}-\mathbb{E}\big[\hat{N}^\theta_{\mathsf{x}_i}|\mathcal{H}_{\mathsf{k}_\varepsilon(z)} \big]\Big), 
\label{def:qin-th}
\\
q_{\rm out}^{(\varepsilon)}(i) &:= \frac{1}{\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon+z} \Big(\mathbb{E}\big[N_{\mathsf{x}_i}|\mathcal{H}_{\mathsf{k}_\varepsilon(z)} \big]-\mathbb{E}_{\bar \mu_\mathsf{e}}\big[N_{\mathsf{x}_i}\big]\Big),
\label{def:qout}
\\
q_{\rm out}^{(\varepsilon)}(i+p) &:=\frac{1}{\mathsf{m}_\varepsilon+z}
 \Big(\mathbb{E}\big[\hat{N}^\theta_{\mathsf{x}_i}|\mathcal{H}_{\mathsf{k}_\varepsilon(z)} \big]-\mathbb{E}_{\bar \mu_\mathsf{e}}\big[\hat{N}^\theta_{\mathsf{x}_i}\big]\Big)\,.
\label{def:qout-th}
\end{align}
There are 
                 
non-negative definite matrices $\Sigma_1$,  $\Sigma_2$ independent of $z$,  such that 
\begin{align}
q_{\rm in}^{(\varepsilon)} &\overset{\rm dist}{\Longrightarrow}  N\( 0, \Sigma_{1}\),  \quad \mbox{\rm conditionally on 
$\mathcal{H}_{\mathsf{k}_\varepsilon(z)}$},\label{mCLT.03}\\
q_{\rm out}^{(\varepsilon)} &\overset{\rm dist}{\Longrightarrow}  N\( 0, \Sigma_{2}\).
                                 
\label{mCLT.04}
\end{align}
<!-- end proposition-16 -->
<!-- lemma-36: body_md -->
\label{lem-expi}
For any $\mathsf{\delta_\star}$,  large $\mathsf {K}_{1}-\mathsf {K}_{0}$ and all $\mathsf{x} \in \cup_u \mathbb{A}^o_u$,
\begin{align}
 \mathbb{E}_{\bar \mu_{\mathsf{e}}} \big[T_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\partial \mathbb{C}^\mathsf{e}(1)} \big]&=\pi {\bf  t_{1}}, \label{17.02b}\\
 \mathbb{E}_{\bar \mu_{\mathsf{e}}}\Bigg[  \sum_{j=1}^{T_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf {K}_{1}}^{\partial \mathbb{C}^\mathsf{e}(1)}}  \cos(\theta_{j,\mathsf{x}}) \Bigg]
 &=\pi {\bf  t_{1}} \langle \cos(\cdot), \bar \mu \rangle \,. \label{17.02c}
 \end{align}
<!-- end lemma-36 -->
<!-- lemma-37: body_md -->
\label{lem:D-c}
Fix $z$,  $\mathsf{\delta_\star}$, $\mathsf {K}_{0}$.  There exist $c_\zeta<\infty$ such that for $\varepsilon$ small enough,
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{P} (D_\varepsilon (c_\zeta))\geq 1-\zeta \,.
\label{ff.0}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-37 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
Let $S_k$ denote the time to complete $k$ intercity excursions.  In proving \Cref{lem:conc} 
we saw that $\frac{1}{\sqrt{k}} (S_k - k \mathsf{t}_1)$ converges in law,  as $k \to \infty$, 
to a normal variable of zero mean and finite variance.
                                      
Recalling also (\ref{dfn:bar-svep}) and (\ref{clt.2}) that 
\[
\bar \mathsf{s}_\varepsilon(z) = \pi \mathsf{k}_\varepsilon(z) \mathsf{t}_1 
                                   
 \in 
                                     
[\widetilde \mathsf{s}(2z-1),\widetilde \mathsf{s}(2z+2c+1)] \, ,
\]
we get that for some $\delta_b =\delta_b(z,\mathsf{\delta_\star},\mathsf {K}_{0}) \to 0$ as $b\to\infty$ and all $\varepsilon \le \varepsilon_o(z,b)$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb{P} \Big(  \widetilde{\mathsf{s}}(-b) \leq \pi S_{\mathsf{k}_{\varepsilon}(z)}\leq \widetilde \mathsf{s}(b) \Big) \geq 1-\delta_b \,. \label{ff.0p}
\end{equation}
Further,  by the same reasoning as in \Cref{theo-etrt},  its conclusion applies for $k$-level excursions,
at any fixed $k$,  which in view of (\ref{ff.0p}) results with (\ref{ff.0}) holding for all $c_\zeta$ large enough.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- lemma-38: body_md -->
\label{lem-kolmo}  With $\bar n_\varepsilon=2 \log (n_\varepsilon \log n_\varepsilon)$ and $\widehat{\mathbb{F}}_\varepsilon=\mathbb{F}_{n_\varepsilon}
 \cup \bar{\mathbb{F}}_{\bar{n}_\varepsilon}$,
\begin{align}\label{height.70a}
\mathbb{P} \Big(\sup_{\stackrel{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{y} \in \widehat{\mathbb{F}}_{\varepsilon} \cap \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}({\bf 0},\bar r)}{2 \mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x}, \mathsf{y}) \le 
e^{-\bar n_\varepsilon}}}
|N_\mathsf{x}-N_\mathsf{y}|  \ge \gamma n_\varepsilon;  D_\varepsilon \Big) & = o_\varepsilon(1) \,.
\end{align}
For some $\rho>0$,  $C_\gamma<\infty$ any $\varepsilon \le \varepsilon_o$ and $\delta \le \delta_o$,  
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{P} \Big(\sup_{\stackrel{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{y} \in \bar \mathbb{F}_{\bar n_\varepsilon} \cap \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}({\bf 0},\bar r)}{\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x}, \mathsf{y}) \le 2 \delta  }}
|N_\mathsf{x}-N_\mathsf{y}|  \ge \gamma n_\varepsilon;  D_\varepsilon \Big) \leq C_\gamma (2 \delta)^\rho \,.
                                                                                
                                                                                             
\label{height.74a}
\end{equation}
Moreover,  both (\ref{height.70a}) and (\ref{height.74a}) hold with $N_\mathsf{x}^\theta-N_\mathsf{y}^\theta$ instead of $N_\mathsf{x}-N_\mathsf{y}$.
<!-- end lemma-38 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
Recall that $\widetilde r =\bar r e$ and
$\mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}({\bf 0}, \widetilde  r e)$ lies inside one city,  with $\mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},\bar r) \subseteq \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}({\bf 0}, \widetilde r)$ for any $\mathsf{x}$ we are to consider.  
As in \cite[Section 5]{BRZ2},  let $A_{\mathsf{x},i}$ and $B_{\mathsf{y},i}$ count traversals from 
$\partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},\bar r)$ to $\partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},\bar r/e)$,  respectively from
$\partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{y},\bar r)$ to $\partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{y},\bar r/e)$,
during the $i$-th excursion from $\partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}({\bf 0},{\widetilde r})$ to
$\partial \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}({\bf 0},  e {\widetilde r})$,  so
\begin{equation}
N_{\mathsf{x}}-N_{\mathsf{y}}=\sum_{i=1}^{\widetilde  N_{\bf 0}}\( A_{\mathsf{x},i} -B_{\mathsf{y},i}\)\,. \label{f1.2}
\end{equation}
By a union over pairs $\mathsf{x},\mathsf{y}$ of distance at most $e^{-\bar n_\varepsilon}$,  
the sign of $N_{\mathsf{x}}-N_{\mathsf{y}}$ and the $2 c_\zeta n_\varepsilon$ possible values of $\widetilde N_{\bf 0}$ 
under $D_\varepsilon$,  it suffices for (\ref{height.70a}),  to show that 
 \begin{align}\label{height.70a28}
n_\varepsilon e^{4 n_\varepsilon} e^{- 2 \bar n_\varepsilon} 
\sup_{
\stackrel{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{y} \in \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}({\bf 0},\bar r),  2 \mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x}, \mathsf{y}) \le e^{-\bar n_\varepsilon}}{\widetilde \mathsf{s} (-c_\zeta) \le \ell \le 
\widetilde \mathsf{s}(c_\zeta)}}
\mathbb{P} \Big(  \sum_{i=1}^{\ell} (A_{\mathsf{x},i} -B_{\mathsf{y},i})   \ge \gamma n_\varepsilon \Big)  = o_\varepsilon(1) \,.
\end{align}
Now,  if $2 \mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},\mathsf{y}) \le e^{-\bar n_\varepsilon}$,  then by Chebychev's exponential inequality
and the bound (\ref{basicexp-ad}) at $\lambda=5/\gamma$,  we have for $\ell \le 2 n_\varepsilon^2$
\[
\mathbb{P} \Big(  \sum_{i=1}^{\ell} (A_{\mathsf{x},i} -B_{\mathsf{y},i})   \ge \gamma n_\varepsilon \Big)
\le e^{-5 n_\varepsilon} e^{c_3 e^{4 \pi\lambda} e^{-\bar n_\varepsilon} n_\varepsilon^2} \,,
\]
from which (\ref{height.70a28}) follows,  as $e^{-\bar n_\varepsilon} n_\varepsilon \to 0$.

As in the proof of Kolmogorov-Centsov continuity theorem (e.g.  \cite[p. 118,  solution of Problem 2.2.9]{KaS},  at
$d=2$,  $\alpha=14$,  $\beta=1$),  we get (\ref{height.74a}) for some $\rho<1/14$ upon 
showing that for $C=C(\bar r)<\infty$,  all $\varepsilon \le \varepsilon_o$ and $\mathsf{x},\mathsf{y}\in \bar \mathbb{F}_{\bar n_\varepsilon}\cap  \mathbb{B}_\mathsf{d}({\bf 0},\bar r)$ with $\mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},\mathsf{y}) \le \delta_o(\bar r)$,  
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E} \Big[ |N_\mathsf{x}-N_\mathsf{y}|^{14};  D_\varepsilon \Big] \le C n_\varepsilon^{14}  \mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},\mathsf{y})^{3} \,.
\label{kolmo.120-new}
\end{equation}
To this end,  by (\ref{f1.2}) we have on $D_\varepsilon$ that 
\begin{equation}
    \label{eq-rage1}
    N_\mathsf{x} - N_\mathsf{y} \leq 
    \sum_{i=1}^{\widetilde \mathsf{s} (-c_\zeta)} \( A_{\mathsf{x},i} -B_{\mathsf{y},i}\)+
    \sum_{i=\widetilde \mathsf{s}(-c_\zeta) +1}^{\widetilde \mathsf{s}(c_\zeta)} |A_{\mathsf{x},i}-B_{\mathsf{y},i}|=: \mathcal{A}_1+\mathcal{A}_2 
  \end{equation}
(the absolute values in $\mathcal{A}_2$ as we have 
                
in (\ref{f1.2}) some
$[\widetilde \mathsf{s}(-c_\zeta),\widetilde \mathsf{s}(c_\zeta)]$-valued random number of summands).  It thus suffices for (\ref{kolmo.120-new}) to show that 
\[
\mathbb{E} [ \mathcal{A}_1^{14} ] \le C n_\varepsilon^{14} \mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},\mathsf{y})^{3}\,,  \quad 
\mathbb{E} [ \mathcal{A}_2^{14} ] \le C n_\varepsilon^{14} \mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},\mathsf{y})^{3}\,.
\]
For $\mathcal{A}_1$ consider (\ref{eq-zav1-new}) at $\ell=\widetilde \mathsf{s}(-c_\zeta) \le 2 n_\varepsilon^2$ and
   
                                                                                          
                                                                              
   
$\lambda=n_\varepsilon^{-1} \mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},\mathsf{y})^{-3/14}$ which for
$\varepsilon \le \varepsilon_o$ and $\mathsf{x} \ne \mathsf{y} \in \bar \mathbb{F}_{\bar n_\varepsilon}$ is arbitrarily small,  to get as needed that 
\begin{equation}
\label{eq-rage2}
\frac{\mathbb{E} [\mathcal{A}_1^{14}]}{14!} \le \frac{\mathbb{E} [ \cosh(\lambda \mathcal{A}_1)]}{\lambda^{14}} \le \lambda^{-14} c^{-1} e^{c \, \mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},\mathsf{y}) \lambda^2 n_\varepsilon^2} \le 
C
                                 
\, n_\varepsilon^{14} \,  \mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},\mathsf{y})^3 \,.
\end{equation}
For $\mathcal{A}_2$ note that by  (\ref{basicexp-ad}),  for $\lambda \in [0,1]$, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq-zav2}
\mathbb{E}[e^{\lambda \mathcal{A}_2}] \le e^{2 c_\zeta c_3  \lambda \mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},\mathsf{y}) n_\varepsilon} \,.
\end{equation}
Considering as before $\lambda=n_\varepsilon^{-1} \mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},\mathsf{y})^{-3/14}$,  and having $\mathcal{A}_2 \ge 0$,  we 
find that 
\[
\frac{\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{A}_2^{14}]}{14!} \le \frac{\mathbb{E}[e^{\lambda \mathcal{A}_2}]}{\lambda^{14}} \le  
e^{2 c_\zeta c_3  \delta_o^{11/14}} \,  n_\varepsilon^{14} \mathsf{d}(\mathsf{x},\mathsf{y})^{3} \,,
\]
as needed to complete the proof of (\ref{kolmo.120-new}) and thereby of (\ref{height.74a}).
